            "text": "   - If asked about a year NOT in the facts, say: \"I don't have data for [year].\"",
            "lineNumber": 559
          },
          {
            "text": "   - DO NOT extrapolate, estimate, or guess for missing years",
            "lineNumber": 560
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Example: If facts have [2024, 2023, 2022, 2021] and user asks for 2020, say \"I don't have 2020 data\"",
            "lineNumber": 561
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 562
          },
          {
            "text": "3. DATES - Use EXACT dates from the data:",
            "lineNumber": 563
          },
          {
            "text": "   - For filings, use the exact filing_date from the facts",
            "lineNumber": 564
          },
          {
            "text": "   - For periods, use the exact period_end_date from the facts",
            "lineNumber": 565
          },
          {
            "text": "   - NEVER invent or approximate dates",
            "lineNumber": 566
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Example: If filing_date is \"2024-11-01\", say \"November 1, 2024\" not \"November 2024\"",
            "lineNumber": 567
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 568
          },
          {
            "text": "4. CITATIONS - Use EXACT filing information:",
            "lineNumber": 569
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If mentioning a filing, verify its filing_type and filing_date are in the facts",
            "lineNumber": 570
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Example: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024...\" (use exact date from data)",
            "lineNumber": 571
          },
          {
            "text": "   - NEVER reference filings not present in the facts",
            "lineNumber": 572
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 573
          },
          {
            "text": "4a. SEC FILING PASSAGES - When facts contain SEC filing content:",
            "lineNumber": 574
          },
          {
            "text": "   - The facts JSON contains \"chunk_text\" fields with actual text from SEC filings",
            "lineNumber": 575
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ⚠️ CRITICAL: READ ALL PASSAGES COMPLETELY before answering",
            "lineNumber": 576
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ⚠️ CRITICAL: Search through ALL passages for the information requested",
            "lineNumber": 577
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 578
          },
          {
            "text": "   When user asks about specific topics (e.g., \"iPhone sales\", \"risk factors\"):",
            "lineNumber": 579
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. Scan through ALL passages looking for mentions of that topic",
            "lineNumber": 580
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If you find relevant data (numbers, quotes, facts), EXTRACT IT and provide it",
            "lineNumber": 581
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. DO NOT say \"I can provide it if you want\" - JUST PROVIDE IT",
            "lineNumber": 582
          },
          {
            "text": "   4. DO NOT be overly cautious - if the data is there, use it",
            "lineNumber": 583
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 584
          },
          {
            "text": "   For DATA in tables or structured format:",
            "lineNumber": 585
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Extract the numbers and present them clearly",
            "lineNumber": 586
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Example: If passage contains \"iPhone $ 201,183 $ 200,583 $ 205,489\" with headers \"2024 2023 2022\"",
            "lineNumber": 587
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Answer: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, iPhone net sales were $201.2 billion in 2024, $200.6 billion in 2023, and $205.5 billion in 2022.\"",
            "lineNumber": 588
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 589
          },
          {
            "text": "   For QUOTES and qualitative content:",
            "lineNumber": 590
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Provide direct quotes from chunk_text that are RELEVANT",
            "lineNumber": 591
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Use quotation marks around direct quotes",
            "lineNumber": 592
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Cite the source: filing type, date, and section",
            "lineNumber": 593
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Example: According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, \"The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs...\"",
            "lineNumber": 594
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 595
          },
          {
            "text": "   Only say \"I couldn't find information\" if:",
            "lineNumber": 596
          },
          {
            "text": "   - You've read ALL passages completely",
            "lineNumber": 597
          },
          {
            "text": "   - NONE of them contain the requested information",
            "lineNumber": 598
          },
          {
            "text": "   - DO NOT say this if the data exists but you're uncertain about formatting",
            "lineNumber": 599
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 600
          },
          {
            "text": "5. UNCERTAINTY - Admit when unsure:",
            "lineNumber": 601
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If you cannot find specific data in the facts, say so clearly",
            "lineNumber": 602
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Better to say \"I don't have that information\" than to guess",
            "lineNumber": 603
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If data seems incomplete, acknowledge it",
            "lineNumber": 604
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 605
          },
          {
            "text": "6. CALCULATIONS - You MUST calculate ratios/percentages from the data when requested:",
            "lineNumber": 606
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 607
          },
          {
            "text": "   IMPORTANT: The facts JSON often includes multiple fields per row to enable ratio calculations.",
            "lineNumber": 608
          },
          {
            "text": "   For example, if the metric is \"total_liabilities\", the JSON will also include \"shareholders_equity\" and \"total_assets\".",
            "lineNumber": 609
          },
          {
            "text": "   These additional fields are provided specifically so you can calculate ratios. USE THEM.",
            "lineNumber": 610
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 611
          },
          {
            "text": "   STOCK PRICE PERFORMANCE:",
            "lineNumber": 612
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If the facts include a \"percentChange\" field, USE THAT VALUE directly (it's already calculated)",
            "lineNumber": 613
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If percentChange is NOT provided, calculate it: ((ending_price - starting_price) / starting_price) × 100",
            "lineNumber": 614
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Format: \"up X%\" or \"down X%\" with 2 decimal places",
            "lineNumber": 615
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Example: percentChange: 790.58 → \"up 790.58%\"",
            "lineNumber": 616
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Example: Start: $243.85, End: $267.93 → ((267.93 - 243.85) / 243.85) × 100 = 9.88% → \"up 9.88%\"",
            "lineNumber": 617
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 618
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ REQUIRED FORMAT FOR PRICE PERFORMANCE ANSWERS (STRICTLY ENFORCE):",
            "lineNumber": 619
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 620
          },
          {
            "text": "   SENTENCE 1 (MANDATORY): \"Over the last [timeframe], AAPL stock is up (or down) X%.\"",
            "lineNumber": 621
          },
          {
            "text": "   SENTENCE 2 (MANDATORY): \"It has gone from $X to $X.\"",
            "lineNumber": 622
          },
          {
            "text": "   SENTENCE 3 (OPTIONAL): \"During this period, the stock reached a high of $X and a low of $X.\"",
            "lineNumber": 623
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 624
          },
          {
            "text": "   Example: \"Over the last 10 years, AAPL stock is up 790.58%. It has gone from $30.14 to $268.47. During this period, the stock reached a high of $271.40 and a low of $22.59.\"",
            "lineNumber": 625
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 626
          },
          {
            "text": "   ❌ WRONG (DO NOT DO THIS): \"Over the last 7 years, the data range runs from 2018-11-08 to 2025-11-07, with a start price of $52.12...\"",
            "lineNumber": 627
          },
          {
            "text": "   ✅ CORRECT: \"Over the last 7 years, AAPL stock is up 415.15%. It has gone from $52.12 to $268.47...\"",
            "lineNumber": 628
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 629
          },
          {
            "text": "   CRITICAL: The FIRST sentence MUST state the percentage change. Do NOT start with dates, price levels, or \"the data range runs from...\"",
            "lineNumber": 630
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 631
          },
          {
            "text": "   PROFITABILITY RATIOS:",
            "lineNumber": 632
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Gross Margin = (gross_profit / revenue) × 100",
            "lineNumber": 633
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Operating Margin = (operating_income / revenue) × 100",
            "lineNumber": 634
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Net Margin = (net_income / revenue) × 100",
            "lineNumber": 635
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ROE (Return on Equity) = (net_income / shareholders_equity) × 100",
            "lineNumber": 636
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ROA (Return on Assets) = (net_income / total_assets) × 100",
            "lineNumber": 637
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 638
          },
          {
            "text": "   LEVERAGE RATIOS:",
            "lineNumber": 639
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Debt-to-Equity = total_liabilities / shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 640
          },
          {
            "text": "     * When asked for debt-to-equity, look for \"value\" (total_liabilities) and \"shareholders_equity\" in each row",
            "lineNumber": 641
          },
          {
            "text": "     * Calculate the ratio for each year: value / shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 642
          },
          {
            "text": "     * Format as a ratio with 2 decimal places: \"3.87\" not \"3.87234...\"",
            "lineNumber": 643
          },
          {
            "text": "     * Show dollar amounts in B or M format, and the calculated ratio",
            "lineNumber": 644
          },
          {
            "text": "     * Example: \"The debt-to-equity ratio in 2025 is 3.87 (total liabilities of $285.5B divided by shareholders' equity of $73.7B).\"",
            "lineNumber": 645
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Debt-to-Assets = total_liabilities / total_assets",
            "lineNumber": 646
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 647
          },
          {
            "text": "   EFFICIENCY RATIOS:",
            "lineNumber": 648
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Asset Turnover = revenue / total_assets",
            "lineNumber": 649
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Cash Flow Margin = (operating_cash_flow / revenue) × 100",
            "lineNumber": 650
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 651
          },
          {
            "text": "   - If user asks for a \"margin\" or \"ratio\", calculate it from the available data",
            "lineNumber": 652
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Show the calculation concisely with formatted numbers",
            "lineNumber": 653
          },
          {
            "text": "   - For margins (profitability), show as percentage: \"Gross margin is 46.2% ($180.7B gross profit / $391.0B revenue)\"",
            "lineNumber": 654
          },
          {
            "text": "   - For ratios (leverage, efficiency), show as decimal: \"Debt-to-equity ratio is 3.87 ($285.5B liabilities / $73.7B equity)\"",
            "lineNumber": 655
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 656
          },
          {
            "text": "7. ⚠️ CRITICAL: EXTENDED METRICS FORMATTING (from financial_metrics table):",
            "lineNumber": 657
          },
          {
            "text": "   When the facts JSON contains \"metric_name\" and \"metric_value\" fields, you MUST apply these formatting rules:",
            "lineNumber": 658
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 659
          },
          {
            "text": "   PERCENTAGE METRICS - MULTIPLY BY 100 AND ADD %:",
            "lineNumber": 660
          },
          {
            "text": "   ❌ WRONG: \"ROE is 1.52\" or \"ROE is 1.50\"",
            "lineNumber": 661
          },
          {
            "text": "   ✅ CORRECT: \"ROE is 152%\" or \"ROE is 150%\"",
            "lineNumber": 662
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 663
          },
          {
            "text": "   - returnOnEquity (ROE): If data shows 1.52, write \"152%\"",
            "lineNumber": 664
          },
          {
            "text": "   - returnOnAssets (ROA): If data shows 0.28, write \"28%\"",
            "lineNumber": 665
          },
          {
            "text": "   - returnOnCapitalEmployed (ROCE): If data shows 0.35, write \"35%\"",
            "lineNumber": 666
          },
          {
            "text": "   - grossProfitMargin: If data shows 0.46, write \"46%\"",
            "lineNumber": 667
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operatingProfitMargin, netProfitMargin: Same rule",
            "lineNumber": 668
          },
          {
            "text": "   - All metrics ending in \"Margin\", \"Growth\", \"Yield\": multiply by 100, add %",
            "lineNumber": 669
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 670
          },
          {
            "text": "   RATIO METRICS (show as decimal, 2 places, NO multiplication):",
            "lineNumber": 671
          },
          {
            "text": "   - peRatio, pbRatio, priceToSalesRatio → \"P/E ratio is 28.50\"",
            "lineNumber": 672
          },
          {
            "text": "   - currentRatio, quickRatio, cashRatio → \"Current ratio is 1.23\"",
            "lineNumber": 673
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debtEquityRatio, debtToAssets → \"Debt-to-equity is 1.87\"",
            "lineNumber": 674
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 675
          },
          {
            "text": "   CURRENCY METRICS (format with $ and B/M):",
            "lineNumber": 676
          },
          {
            "text": "   - marketCap, enterpriseValue → \"$3.5T\" or \"$350B\"",
            "lineNumber": 677
          },
          {
            "text": "   - freeCashFlow, operatingCashFlow → \"$100.5B\"",
            "lineNumber": 678
          },
          {
            "text": "   - bookValuePerShare, cashPerShare → \"$4.25\"",
            "lineNumber": 679
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 680
          },
          {
            "text": "   DAYS METRICS (show as whole number with \"days\"):",
            "lineNumber": 681
          },
          {
            "text": "   - daysOfInventoryOnHand, daysPayablesOutstanding → \"45 days\"",
            "lineNumber": 682
          },
          {
            "text": "   - cashConversionCycle → \"-35 days\" (can be negative)",
            "lineNumber": 683
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 684
          },
          {
            "text": "   ALWAYS round to 2 decimal places maximum. NEVER show raw decimal values.",
            "lineNumber": 685
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 686
          },
          {
            "text": "General Instructions:",
            "lineNumber": 687
          },
          {
            "text": "- Be concise and clear.",
            "lineNumber": 688
          },
          {
            "text": "- If the user asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (e.g., \"in 2020\", \"for 2018\"), check if that year exists in the facts:",
            "lineNumber": 689
          },
          {
            "text": "  * If the year IS in the facts → provide the data directly and clearly",
            "lineNumber": 690
          },
          {
            "text": "  * If the year is NOT in the facts → say \"I don't have data for [year].\" and stop",
            "lineNumber": 691
          },
          {
            "text": "- If the user asks for multiple years or a trend, show all relevant years.",
            "lineNumber": 692
          },
          {
            "text": "- If trend is relevant (and the user asked for it), describe it (e.g., increasing/decreasing/flat).",
            "lineNumber": 693
          },
          {
            "text": "- Do not invent numbers or sources.",
            "lineNumber": 694
          },
          {
            "text": "- Respond in plain text sentences. Do NOT use Markdown formatting (no bullet lists, bold, italics, tables, or code blocks).",
            "lineNumber": 695
          },
          {
            "text": "- When there is only ONE data point, provide a concise single-sentence answer with the year and value. Do NOT mention any chart or table.",
            "lineNumber": 696
          },
          {
            "text": "- When there are 2-4 data points AND the user did NOT explicitly ask for a chart/graph, list them briefly in your answer.",
            "lineNumber": 697
          },
          {
            "text": "- When there are 2-4 data points AND the user explicitly asked for a chart/graph/visualization, briefly mention the key values and direct them to check the chart below.",
            "lineNumber": 698
          },
          {
            "text": "- When more than four data points are relevant, do not list each one. Write at most two sentences: the first calls out the earliest year/value, latest year/value, and any notable high/low WITH the percentage change; the second describes the overall trend and tells the user to check the chart and data table below for the full yearly breakdown.",
            "lineNumber": 699
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 700
          },
          {
            "text": "Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 701
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"What was net income in 2020?\" → Answer: \"AAPL's net income in 2020 was $57.4 billion.\" (Only 2020, exact number)",
            "lineNumber": 702
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"What's the revenue trend?\" → Answer: \"Revenue increased from $274.5B in 2020 to $383.3B in 2024.\" (Show trend, exact numbers)",
            "lineNumber": 703
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"Revenue in 2020 vs 2024?\" → Answer: \"Revenue was $274.5B in 2020 and $383.3B in 2024, a 40% increase.\" (Compare as requested, exact numbers)",
            "lineNumber": 704
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"What's the gross margin?\" → Answer: \"AAPL's gross margin in 2024 is 46.2% (gross profit of $180.7B divided by revenue of $391.0B).\" (Calculate ratio from data)",
            "lineNumber": 705
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"Chart of debt to equity ratio last 5 years\" → Answer: \"The debt-to-equity ratio decreased from 2.61 in 2022 to 0.11 in 2025; check the chart below for the full trend.\" (User asked for chart, direct them to it)",
            "lineNumber": 706
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"Show year to date performance\" → Answer: \"AAPL is up 9.88% year-to-date, from $243.85 to $267.93 as of the latest date in the data. Check the data table below for the full yearly breakdown.\" (Calculate percentage, format prices with $, mention trend)",
            "lineNumber": 707
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"What did AAPL say about risk factors in their latest 10-K? provide quotes.\" → Answer: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, Apple identifies several main risks: 'The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs on the value of its inventory and other assets, in addition to purchase commitment cancellation risk.' The filing also notes that 'rapid technological change and competitive dynamics could materially adversely affect the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition.'\" (Provide direct quotes from chunk_text with proper citation)",
            "lineNumber": 708
          },
          {
            "text": "- Question: \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone sales?\" → Answer: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, iPhone net sales were $201.2 billion in 2024, $200.6 billion in 2023, and $205.5 billion in 2022.\" (Extract relevant data from the passage that actually mentions iPhone, not unrelated passages about inventory or IP)&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 709
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 710
          }
        ]

        "contents": "const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!\nconst SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!\n\nif (!SUPABASE_URL || !SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY) {\n  console.error('Missing required environment variables')\n  process.exit(1)\n}\n\nconst supabase = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY)\n\nconst TOOL_SELECTION_PROMPT_V2 = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool from the provided menu and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.\n\nAvailable Tools:\n\n1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Get financial metrics as NUMBERS over time\n\n   SUPPORTED METRICS (use exact names):\n   - revenue\n   - gross_profit\n   - net_income\n   - operating_income\n   - total_assets\n   - total_liabilities\n   - shareholders_equity\n   - operating_cash_flow\n   - eps\n\n   METRIC MAPPING GUIDE (handle common variations):\n   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue\n   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\" → net_income\n   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\" → eps\n   - \"P/E ratio\", \"PE ratio\", \"price to earnings\" → eps (closest available)\n   - \"assets\" → total_assets\n   - \"liabilities\", \"debt\" → total_liabilities\n   - \"equity\", \"book value\" → shareholders_equity\n   - \"cash flow\", \"operating cash\" → operating_cash_flow\n   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research\", \"development spending\" → operating_income (closest available)\n   - \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\" → operating_cash_flow (closest available)\n   - \"dividends\", \"buybacks\", \"capex\", \"margins\", \"ratios\" → operating_income (closest available)\n\n   args: {\"metric\": &lt;one from SUPPORTED METRICS&gt;, \"limit\": 1-10 (defaults to 4)}\n\n2. getPrices - Get stock PRICE history\n\n   SUPPORTED RANGES:\n   - \"7d\" - one week\n   - \"30d\" - one month\n   - \"90d\" - one quarter\n\n   RANGE MAPPING GUIDE:\n   - \"today\", \"current\", \"now\", \"latest\" → 7d\n   - \"week\", \"this week\", \"5 days\" → 7d\n   - \"month\", \"30 days\" → 30d\n   - \"quarter\", \"90 days\", \"3 months\" → 90d\n   - \"year\", \"YTD\", \"12 months\", \"long term\" → 90d (closest available)\n\n   args: {\"range\": \"7d\" | \"30d\" | \"90d\"}\n\n3. getRecentFilings - LIST recent SEC filings (metadata only: dates, types, links)\n   Use when user wants to SEE or LIST filings\n   args: {\"limit\": 1-10 (defaults to 5)}\n\n4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing CONTENT for qualitative information\n   Use when asking WHAT/WHY/HOW about:\n   - Strategy, business model, operations\n   - Risks, challenges, opportunities\n   - Management commentary, outlook\n   - Products, markets, competition\n   - Governance, compensation\n\n   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;user's question or keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}\n\nROUTING RULES:\n\n1. If question asks for NUMBERS/METRICS over time → getAaplFinancialsByMetric\n   Examples: \"revenue trend\", \"net income\", \"EPS over 5 years\"\n\n2. If question asks about STOCK PRICE → getPrices\n   Examples: \"stock price\", \"share price\", \"how's it trading\"\n\n3. If question asks to LIST/SHOW filings → getRecentFilings\n   Examples: \"recent filings\", \"last 3 10-Ks\", \"show filings\"\n\n4. If question asks WHAT/WHY/HOW about topics → searchFilings\n   Examples: \"what are the risks\", \"explain strategy\", \"tell me about competition\"\n\n5. IMPORTANT: Use metric mapping guide above - if user asks for unsupported metric, use closest available\n   Examples:\n   - \"P/E ratio\" → use eps (closest)\n   - \"free cash flow\" → use operating_cash_flow (closest)\n   - \"R&amp;D spending\" → use operating_income (closest)\n\nUser question: \"{{USER_QUESTION}}\"\n\nReturn ONLY JSON:\n\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"revenue\",\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"eps\",\"limit\":4}}\n{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"range\":\"30d\"}}\n{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":3}}\n{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}&#96;\n\nasync function addPromptV2() {\n  console.log('📝 Adding prompt v2 to database...\\n')\n}",

          },

            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "const supabase = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY)",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "const TOOL_SELECTION_PROMPT_V2 = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool from the provided menu and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "Available Tools:",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Get financial metrics as NUMBERS over time",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "   SUPPORTED METRICS (use exact names):",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "   - revenue",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "   - gross_profit",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "   - net_income",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "   - total_assets",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "   - total_liabilities",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "text": "   - shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operating_cash_flow",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "text": "   - eps",
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC MAPPING GUIDE (handle common variations):",
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\" → net_income",
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\" → eps",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/E ratio\", \"PE ratio\", \"price to earnings\" → eps (closest available)",
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"assets\" → total_assets",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"liabilities\", \"debt\" → total_liabilities",
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"equity\", \"book value\" → shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"cash flow\", \"operating cash\" → operating_cash_flow",
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research\", \"development spending\" → operating_income (closest available)",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\" → operating_cash_flow (closest available)",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"dividends\", \"buybacks\", \"capex\", \"margins\", \"ratios\" → operating_income (closest available)",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 55
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"metric\": &lt;one from SUPPORTED METRICS&gt;, \"limit\": 1-10 (defaults to 4)}",
            "lineNumber": 56
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 57
          },
          {
            "text": "2. getPrices - Get stock PRICE history",
            "lineNumber": 58
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 59
          },
          {
            "text": "   SUPPORTED RANGES:",
            "lineNumber": 60
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"7d\" - one week",
            "lineNumber": 61
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"30d\" - one month",
            "lineNumber": 62
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"90d\" - one quarter",
            "lineNumber": 63
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 64
          },
          {
            "text": "   RANGE MAPPING GUIDE:",
            "lineNumber": 65
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"today\", \"current\", \"now\", \"latest\" → 7d",
            "lineNumber": 66
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"week\", \"this week\", \"5 days\" → 7d",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"month\", \"30 days\" → 30d",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"quarter\", \"90 days\", \"3 months\" → 90d",
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"year\", \"YTD\", \"12 months\", \"long term\" → 90d (closest available)",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"range\": \"7d\" | \"30d\" | \"90d\"}",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "3. getRecentFilings - LIST recent SEC filings (metadata only: dates, types, links)",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use when user wants to SEE or LIST filings",
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"limit\": 1-10 (defaults to 5)}",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing CONTENT for qualitative information",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use when asking WHAT/WHY/HOW about:",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Strategy, business model, operations",
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Risks, challenges, opportunities",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Management commentary, outlook",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Products, markets, competition",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - Governance, compensation",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;user's question or keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "ROUTING RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "1. If question asks for NUMBERS/METRICS over time → getAaplFinancialsByMetric",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples: \"revenue trend\", \"net income\", \"EPS over 5 years\"",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "text": "2. If question asks about STOCK PRICE → getPrices",
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples: \"stock price\", \"share price\", \"how's it trading\"",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "3. If question asks to LIST/SHOW filings → getRecentFilings",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples: \"recent filings\", \"last 3 10-Ks\", \"show filings\"",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "text": "4. If question asks WHAT/WHY/HOW about topics → searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples: \"what are the risks\", \"explain strategy\", \"tell me about competition\"",
            "lineNumber": 100
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "text": "5. IMPORTANT: Use metric mapping guide above - if user asks for unsupported metric, use closest available",
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/E ratio\" → use eps (closest)",
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"free cash flow\" → use operating_cash_flow (closest)",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"R&amp;D spending\" → use operating_income (closest)",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "User question: \"{{USER_QUESTION}}\"",
            "lineNumber": 108
          },
          {

          {

        "contents": "const TOOL_SELECTION_PROMPT_V1 = &#96;\n&#96;\n\n// Answer Generation Prompt (from lib/tools.ts buildFinalAnswerPrompt)\nconst ANSWER_GENERATION_PROMPT_V1 = &#96;You are an analyst. Answer the user using ONLY the provided facts.\n\nUser question: \"{{USER_QUESTION}}\"\n\nFacts (JSON rows):\n{{FACTS_JSON}}\n\nInstructions:\n- Be concise and clear.\n- FIRST, check if you have all the data requested. If not, START your answer by explaining what data you DO have (e.g., \"I have data for the last 10 years (2015-2024), not 15 years as requested.\").\n- THEN provide your analysis using the available data.\n- If trend is relevant, describe it (e.g., increasing/decreasing/flat).\n- Do not invent numbers or sources.\n- Only say \"I don't know\" if you have ZERO relevant data.&#96;\n\nasync function seedPrompts() {\n  console.log('🌱 Seeding prompt versions...\\n')\n\n  try {\n    // Check if prompts already exist\n    const { data: existingPrompts } = await supabase\n      .from('prompt_versions')\n      .select('prompt_type, version_number')\n      .order('version_number', { ascending: false })\n\n    if (existingPrompts &amp;&amp; existingPrompts.length &gt; 0) {\n      console.log('⚠️  Existing prompts found:')\n      existingPrompts.forEach((p) =&gt; {\n        console.log(&#96;  - ${p.prompt_type} v${p.version_number}&#96;)\n      })\n      console.log('\\nSkipping seed to avoid duplicates.')\n      console.log('If you want to re-seed, delete existing prompts first.\\n')\n      return\n    }\n\n    // Insert tool selection prompt v1\n    console.log('📝 Inserting tool_selection prompt v1...')\n    const { error: toolError } = await supabase\n      .from('prompt_versions')\n      .insert({\n        prompt_type: 'tool_selection',\n        version_number: 1,\n        prompt_content: TOOL_SELECTION_PROMPT_V1,\n        change_description: 'Initial prompt version from codebase at project start',\n        is_active: true,\n        created_by: 'seed-script',\n      })\n\n    if (toolError) {\n      console.error('❌ Error inserting tool_selection prompt:', toolError)\n      throw toolError\n    }\n    console.log('✅ Tool selection prompt v1 inserted\\n')\n\n    // Insert answer generation prompt v1\n}",

'Correct tool, wrong arguments' : 'Wrong tool'}\n\nPlease provide your analysis in this format:\n\n**Verdict:** [Choose ONE: \"Golden test is correct\" | \"AI is correct\" | \"Both are reasonable\" | \"Need more context\"]\n\n**Reasoning:** [2-3 sentences explaining your verdict.         "range": {

        "contents": "# Prompt Evolution Guide: From 46% to 83% Accuracy\n\n## Table of Contents\n1. [The Problem We're Solving](#the-problem-were-solving)\n2. [How the Evaluation System Works](#how-the-evaluation-system-works)\n3. [Prompt Version History](#prompt-version-history)\n4. [How We Improve Prompts](#how-we-improve-prompts)\n5. [Results Summary](#results-summary)\n6. [How to Use This System](#how-to-use-this-system)\n\n---\n\n## The Problem We're Solving\n\n### What is \"Tool Selection\"?\n\nOur application answers user questions about Apple's financials by routing questions to one of four specialized tools:\n\n1. **getAaplFinancialsByMetric** - Gets numerical financial data (revenue, profit, cash flow, etc.)\n2. **getPrices** - Gets stock price history for different time periods\n3. **searchFilings** - Searches SEC filings for qualitative information (risks, strategy, etc.)\n4. **getRecentFilings** - Lists recent SEC filing documents\n\nWhen a user asks a question like \"What's Apple's revenue?\", the AI needs to:\n- Pick the right tool (&#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96;)\n- Choose the right arguments (&#96;metric: \"revenue\", limit: 4&#96;)\n\nIf the AI picks the wrong tool or wrong arguments, the user gets bad answers.\n\n### Why Do We Need Better Prompts?\n\nInitially, our AI was only picking the right tool + arguments **46% of the time**. That means:\n- **54% of questions got wrong answers!**\n- Users would get price data when they asked about revenue\n- Users would get 5 results when they asked for 10\n- Users asking about \"P/E ratio\" would get no useful answer\n\n**Our goal:** Improve accuracy to 85%+ by systematically improving the prompt.\n\n---\n\n## How the Evaluation System Works\n\n### Overview\n\nWe built an **offline evaluation system** that tests prompts without bothering real users. Think of it like a practice exam for the AI.\n\n### The Golden Test Set\n\nWe created 100 carefully crafted questions that represent real user queries:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"id\": 1,\n  \"question\": \"What's AAPL's revenue over the last 5 years?\",",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# Prompt Evolution Guide: From 46% to 83% Accuracy",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "text": "## Table of Contents",
            "lineNumber": 3
          },
          {
            "text": "1. [The Problem We're Solving](#the-problem-were-solving)",
            "lineNumber": 4
          },
          {
            "text": "2. [How the Evaluation System Works](#how-the-evaluation-system-works)",
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "text": "3. [Prompt Version History](#prompt-version-history)",
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "text": "4. [How We Improve Prompts](#how-we-improve-prompts)",
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "text": "5. [Results Summary](#results-summary)",
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "text": "6. [How to Use This System](#how-to-use-this-system)",
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "## The Problem We're Solving",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "### What is \"Tool Selection\"?",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "Our application answers user questions about Apple's financials by routing questions to one of four specialized tools:",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **getAaplFinancialsByMetric** - Gets numerical financial data (revenue, profit, cash flow, etc.)",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **getPrices** - Gets stock price history for different time periods",
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "3. **searchFilings** - Searches SEC filings for qualitative information (risks, strategy, etc.)",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "text": "4. **getRecentFilings** - Lists recent SEC filing documents",
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "When a user asks a question like \"What's Apple's revenue?\", the AI needs to:",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "- Pick the right tool (&#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "- Choose the right arguments (&#96;metric: \"revenue\", limit: 4&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "If the AI picks the wrong tool or wrong arguments, the user gets bad answers.",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "### Why Do We Need Better Prompts?",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "Initially, our AI was only picking the right tool + arguments **46% of the time**. That means:",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "- **54% of questions got wrong answers!**",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "- Users would get price data when they asked about revenue",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "- Users would get 5 results when they asked for 10",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "- Users asking about \"P/E ratio\" would get no useful answer",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "**Our goal:** Improve accuracy to 85%+ by systematically improving the prompt.",
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 40
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 41
          },
          {
            "text": "## How the Evaluation System Works",
            "lineNumber": 42
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 43
          },
          {
            "text": "### Overview",
            "lineNumber": 44
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 45
          },
          {
            "text": "We built an **offline evaluation system** that tests prompts without bothering real users. Think of it like a practice exam for the AI.",
            "lineNumber": 46
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 47
          },
          {
            "text": "### The Golden Test Set",
            "lineNumber": 48
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 49
          },
          {
            "text": "We created 100 carefully crafted questions that represent real user queries:",
            "lineNumber": 50
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 51
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;json",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {
            "text": "{",
            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "  \"id\": 1,",
            "lineNumber": 54
          },
          {
            "text": "  \"question\": \"What's AAPL's revenue over the last 5 years?\",",
            "lineNumber": 55
          }
        ]
      },
      "score": 0.433432012796402
    },

        "contents": "// Legacy function - kept for backwards compatibility\nexport const buildToolSelectionPrompt = (\n  userQuestion: string,\n  previousToolResults?: Array&lt;{\n    question: string\n    answer: string\n    toolData: { type: string; data: any[] } | null | undefined\n  }&gt;\n) =&gt; {\n  // Get today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format\n  const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]\n\n  // Replace the placeholder with the actual date\n  const promptWithDate = TOOL_SELECTION_STATIC_PROMPT.replace('{{TODAY_DATE}}', today)\n\n  // Add context about previous tool results if available\n  let previousDataContext = ''\n  if (previousToolResults &amp;&amp; previousToolResults.length &gt; 0) {\n    const validResults = previousToolResults.filter(r =&gt; r.toolData)\n    if (validResults.length &gt; 0) {\n      previousDataContext = &#96;\\n\\nPREVIOUS DATA AVAILABLE (for follow-up questions):\n${validResults.map((result, idx) =&gt; &#96;\nPrevious Question ${idx + 1}: \"${result.question}\"\nData Type: ${result.toolData!.type}\nData Summary: ${result.toolData!.data.length} items returned\n&#96;).join('')}\n\n⚠️ If the current question refers to the previous answer, pick the tool that produced that data so the assistant can cite it correctly.\n&#96;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return &#96;${promptWithDate}${previousDataContext}\n\nUser question: \"${userQuestion}\"&#96;\n}\n\nexport const buildFollowUpQuestionsPrompt = (\n  userQuestion: string,\n  toolUsed: string,\n  answer: string\n)",

Return ONLY valid JSON matching {\"suggestions\": string[]}.       "codeBlock": {

        "range": {

        "contents": "# Meta-Prompting Strategy for Fin Quote\n\n## Overview\n\nThis document outlines how to implement meta-prompting to improve our tool routing prompt. Meta-prompting uses AI to generate and optimize the prompts that our system uses, reducing manual prompt engineering and improving accuracy over time.\n\n---\n\n## What Problem Does This Solve?\n\n### Current Challenges\n\n1. **Manual prompt maintenance** - Every time we add a tool, we manually update the routing prompt\n2. **Tool disambiguation** - Users get confused between &#96;searchFilings&#96; (content search) vs &#96;getRecentFilings&#96; (list filings)\n3. **Limited examples** - We only have 4 example outputs, may not cover edge cases\n4. **Static prompts** - Prompts don't improve based on real user errors\n\n### What Meta-Prompting Offers\n\n- **Automatic prompt generation** when tools change\n- **Better examples** generated from tool definitions\n- **Error-driven improvement** using logged mistakes\n- **Optimized routing logic** without manual trial-and-error\n\n---\n\n## Current System Architecture\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser Question\n    ↓\n[Prompt 1: Tool Selection] ← Manually written in lib/tools.ts\n    ↓\nGPT-4 picks tool + args\n    ↓\nExecute tool (fetch data)\n    ↓\n[Prompt 2: Answer Generation] ← Manually written in lib/tools.ts\n    ↓\nGPT-4 generates answer\n    ↓\nReturn to user\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Meta-Prompting Architecture (Proposed)\n\n### Option A: One-Time Generation (Simplest)\n\nUse meta-prompting as a **development tool** to generate better prompts once.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nDeveloper runs script\n    ↓\nMeta-prompt: \"Generate optimal routing prompt for these tools: [definitions]\"\n    ↓\nAI generates improved prompt\n    ↓\nDeveloper reviews and approves\n    ↓\nManually update lib/tools.ts\n    ↓\nDeploy\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Pros:**\n- No code changes to production app\n- No added latency or cost\n- Simple to implement\n- Still use meta-prompting benefits\n\n**Cons:**\n- Manual update step\n- Doesn't auto-improve from errors\n\n---\n\n### Option B: Dynamic Generation (Advanced)\n\nGenerate prompts at **runtime** based on context.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser Question\n    ↓",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

                  "lineNumber": 4688,

On shows Reasoning Summary + Tool Trace.\\n+   - If user.isAdmin: nested “Show scratchpad (debug)” toggle; default off.\\n+ \\n+ ### Presentation\\n+ - Reasoning Summary: 2–5 short bullets, plain text. No secrets, no prompts, no identifiers.\\n+ - Tool Trace (collapsible):\\n+   - Step list with: tool name, args (redacted), durationMs, resultCount or top citations.\\n+   - For search results: show filing type/date/section and a short snippet. Avoid long payloads.\\n+ - Scratchpad (admin-only, collapsible):\\n+   - Monospace preformatted block, limited to ~200 tokens.\\n+   - Display a caution banner (“Debug view — not user facing. Not stored.”).\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## API and Data Model\\n+ \\n+ ### Response envelope (server → client)\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;json\\n+ {\\n+   \\&amp;quot;answer\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;final text\\&amp;quot;,\\n+   \\&amp;quot;reasoningSummary\\&amp;quot;: [\\&amp;quot;Selected filing content search\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;Filtered to 2024 10‑K\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;Quoted Item 1A\\&amp;quot;],\\n+   \\&amp;quot;toolTrace\\&amp;quot;: [\\n+     {\\n+       \\&amp;quot;tool\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;searchFilings\\&amp;quot;,\\n+       \\&amp;quot;args\\&amp;quot;: {\\&amp;quot;query\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;risk factors\\&amp;quot;},       // redact sensitive fields\\n+       \\&amp;quot;durationMs\\&amp;quot;: 412,\\n+       \\&amp;quot;results\\&amp;quot;: 5,\\n+       \\&amp;quot;topCitations\\&amp;quot;: [\\n+         {\\&amp;quot;filing\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;10-K\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;date\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;2024-11-01\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;section\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Item 1A\\&amp;quot;}\\n+       ]\\n+     }\\n+   ],\\n+   \\&amp;quot;scratchpad\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;&amp;lt;private notes&amp;gt;\\&amp;quot;,             // only included if admin + flag\\n+   \\&amp;quot;citations\\&amp;quot;: [\\n+     {\\&amp;quot;filing\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;10-K\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;date\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;2024-11-01\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;section\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Item 1A\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;anchor\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;#risk-factors\\&amp;quot;}\\n+   ]\\n+ }\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n+ \\n+ Notes:\\n+ - &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96; must never be persisted. It’s only added to the API response for admins when an explicit dev flag is enabled.\\n+ - &amp;#96;toolTrace.args&amp;#96; should pass through a redaction layer before returning to client (e.g., mask long strings, strip tokens/keys).\\n+ \\n+ ### Tool Trace step shape (TypeScript)\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;ts\\n+ type ToolTraceStep = {\\n+   tool: string;\\n+   args: Record&amp;lt;string, unknown&amp;gt;;\\n+   durationMs: number;\\n+   results?: number;\\n+   topCitations?: Array&amp;lt;{\\n+     filing: string;\\n+     date: string;\\n+     section?: string;\\n+     anchor?: string;\\n+   }&amp;gt;;\\n+ };\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Prompt Design\\n+ \\n+ ### Pattern\\n+ Ask the model for three sections: “Reasoning Summary”, “Final Answer”, and a private “&amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt;”. Instruct the model not to reveal scratchpad content to the user.\\n+ \\n+ Example (conceptual):\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n+ You may think step-by-step in &amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt; (max 200 tokens). Do not reveal or reference it.\\n+ Return the following sections exactly:\\n+ \\n+ Reasoning Summary:\\n+ - 2–5 short bullets explaining the approach (no prompts, no secrets)\\n+ \\n+ Final Answer:\\n+ - The answer and citations (with filing type, date, section)\\n+ \\n+ &amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt;\\n+ (Private notes for debugging: why you chose the tool, filters, edge cases considered)\\n+ &amp;lt;/scratchpad&amp;gt;\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n+ \\n+ ### Guardrails (in the prompt)\\n+ - “Do not include any content from &amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt; in the Reasoning Summary or Final Answer.”\\n+ - “Keep Reasoning Summary concise and user-safe; avoid prompt text, keys, or file paths.”\\n+ - “Cap &amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt; at ~200 tokens.”\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Backend Changes\\n+ \\n+ ### Execution flow (high level)\\n+ 1) Tool execution instrumentation\\n+    - Before each tool call, record &amp;#96;start = performance.now()&amp;#96; and sanitized &amp;#96;args&amp;#96; copy.\\n+    - After completion, compute &amp;#96;durationMs&amp;#96;; capture &amp;#96;results&amp;#96; count and &amp;#96;topCitations&amp;#96; if applicable.\\n+    - Push one &amp;#96;ToolTraceStep&amp;#96; into a &amp;#96;toolTrace&amp;#96; array on the server.\\n+ \\n+ 2) Model response parsing\\n+    - Parse the assistant output into: &amp;#96;reasoningSummary[]&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;finalAnswer&amp;#96;, and optional &amp;#96;&amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt;&amp;#96; section.\\n+    - Enforce output length limits. If missing sections, degrade gracefully (empty summary, no scratchpad).\\n+ \\n+ 3) Redaction and response assembly\\n+    - Run &amp;#96;redactArgs()&amp;#96; for &amp;#96;toolTrace.args&amp;#96; (e.g., truncate long strings, remove keys).\\n+    - If &amp;#96;user.isAdmin &amp;amp;&amp;amp; SCRATCHPAD_ADMIN_ONLY === &amp;#39;true&amp;#39; &amp;amp;&amp;amp; REASONING_SCRATCHPAD_ENABLED === &amp;#39;true&amp;#39;&amp;#96;, attach &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96;; else omit.\\n+    - Return &amp;#96;{ answer, reasoningSummary, toolTrace, citations, scratchpad? }&amp;#96;.\\n+ \\n+ 4) Persistence\\n+    - Store &amp;#96;answer&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;reasoningSummary&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;toolTrace&amp;#96;, and &amp;#96;citations&amp;#96; as part of the message or query log.\\n+    - Do not store &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96;. Avoid logging it to console or external logs.\\n+ \\n+ ### Redaction guidelines\\n+ - Remove API keys, tokens, and auth headers.\\n+ - Truncate large text fields (e.g., queries &amp;gt; 256 chars) with a suffix “…(truncated)”.\\n+ - Mask PII if present (e.g., emails → &amp;#96;u***@domain.com&amp;#96;).\\n+ - For embeddings or RPC payloads, keep only query term and counts; avoid raw vectors.\\n+ \\n+ ### Feature flags / config\\n+ - &amp;#96;REASONING_ENABLED=true&amp;#96; (default true; can disable globally).\\n+ - &amp;#96;REASONING_SHOW_SUMMARY_DEFAULT=true&amp;#96; (UI default on).\\n+ - &amp;#96;REASONING_TOOL_TRACE_DEFAULT=true&amp;#96; (UI default on).\\n+ - &amp;#96;REASONING_SCRATCHPAD_ENABLED=false&amp;#96; (default off in prod).\\n+ - &amp;#96;SCRATCHPAD_ADMIN_ONLY=true&amp;#96; (must be true in prod).\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Frontend Changes\\n+ \\n+ ### UI toggles (AssistantChat)\\n+ - Add “Show reasoning” switch (persist per-session in local state; optionally in user settings).\\n+ - If admin: show “Show scratchpad (debug)” nested switch.\\n+ \\n+ ### Rendering\\n+ - Reasoning Summary: simple bullet list under the assistant message.\\n+ - Tool Trace: collapsible section listing steps with durations and top citations; include a “Copy trace” button for debugging.\\n+ - Scratchpad: admin-only collapsible preformatted block with a warning banner.\\n+ \\n+ ### Accessibility and performance\\n+ - Ensure toggles are keyboard-accessible.\\n+ - Virtualize long histories: Reasoning/Trace should not cause message reflows that are expensive.\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Security, Privacy, and Compliance\\n+ - Never store the scratchpad; it’s transient and admin-only.\\n+ - Redact secrets/PII from tool traces and args.\\n+ - Ensure RLS prevents non-admins from seeing &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96; fields even if the API is called directly.\\n+ - Log size caps: protect logs and payloads against excessive growth (e.g., 100 KB cap per trace).\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Testing Plan\\n+ \\n+ ### Unit tests\\n+ - Prompt parser: extracts Reasoning Summary, Final Answer, and Scratchpad correctly.\\n+ - Redaction: verifies keys/PII removed; long strings truncated.\\n+ - Trace builder: correct durations, counts, and top citations propagation.\\n+ \\n+ ### Integration/E2E\\n+ - User flow: Ask filing question → Reasoning Summary + Tool Trace visible; citations match trace.\\n+ - Admin flow: Enable scratchpad → visible; disable → hidden.\\n+ - Flag behavior: Disabling &amp;#96;REASONING_ENABLED&amp;#96; hides reasoning UI entirely.\\n+ \\n+ ### Safety checks\\n+ - Ensure no scratchpad content appears in user-visible fields.\\n+ - Verify DB writes exclude scratchpad.\\n+ - Confirm large inputs do not degrade performance (load/perf checks).\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Rollout Plan\\n+ 1) Dev/staging (admins only)\\n+    - Enable all features including scratchpad.\\n+    - Collect feedback on clarity and usefulness.\\n+ 2) Limited production (users see Reasoning Summary + Trace; scratchpad off)\\n+    - &amp;#96;REASONING_ENABLED=true&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;REASONING_SCRATCHPAD_ENABLED=false&amp;#96;.\\n+ 3) Full production\\n+    - Keep scratchpad off by default; enable per-session for on-call debugging.\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Risks and Mitigations\\n+ - Risk: Prompt leakage via Reasoning Summary.\\n+   - Mitigation: Explicit prompt instructions; add tests to detect restricted phrases; manual reviews.\\n+ - Risk: Token/cost overhead.\\n+   - Mitigation: Cap scratchpad to ~200 tokens; keep reasoning bullets short; strip long fields from traces.\\n+ - Risk: Privacy leakage via traces.\\n+   - Mitigation: Redaction layer; admin-only scratchpad; RLS checks.\\n+ - Risk: Developer accidentally logs scratchpad.\\n+   - Mitigation: Lint rule / code review checklist; wrap scratchpad in a typed object only returned conditionally.\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Implementation Checklist\\n+ \\n+ Backend\\n+ - [ ] Add tool instrumentation util (&amp;#96;startTraceStep&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;endTraceStep&amp;#96;).\\n+ - [ ] Add redaction util for args and traces.\\n+ - [ ] Update answer action to request sections + parse &amp;#96;Reasoning Summary&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;Final Answer&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;&amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt;&amp;#96;.\\n+ - [ ] Assemble response envelope and exclude &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96; unless admin + flag.\\n+ - [ ] Persist answer, reasoningSummary, toolTrace, citations only.\\n+ \\n+ Frontend\\n+ - [ ] Add “Show reasoning” and admin-only “Show scratchpad” toggles.\\n+ - [ ] Render Reasoning Summary under assistant messages.\\n+ - [ ] Render collapsible Tool Trace with durations and top citations.\\n+ - [ ] Render admin-only Scratchpad with warning banner; hidden by default.\\n+ \\n+ Config &amp;amp; Testing\\n+ - [ ] Add feature flags (&amp;#96;REASONING_*&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;SCRATCHPAD_ADMIN_ONLY&amp;#96;).\\n+ - [ ] Unit tests for parser, redaction, trace builder.\\n+ - [ ] E2E tests for user/admin flows and flags.\\n+ \\n+ ---\\n+ \\n+ ## Appendix\\n+ \\n+ ### Example Tool Trace step\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;json\\n+ {\\n+   \\&amp;quot;tool\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;searchFilings\\&amp;quot;,\\n+   \\&amp;quot;args\\&amp;quot;: {\\&amp;quot;query\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;risk factors\\&amp;quot;},\\n+   \\&amp;quot;durationMs\\&amp;quot;: 387,\\n+   \\&amp;quot;results\\&amp;quot;: 5,\\n+   \\&amp;quot;topCitations\\&amp;quot;: [\\n+     {\\&amp;quot;filing\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;10-K\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;date\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;2024-11-01\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;section\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Item 1A\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;anchor\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;#risk-factors\\&amp;quot;}\\n+   ]\\n+ }\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n+ \\n+ ### Example Reasoning Summary (good)\\n+ - Selected “searchFilings” because question asks about content (not metadata).\\n+ - Filtered to the latest 10‑K results.\\n+ - Ranked by vector similarity; It’s only added to the API response for admins when an explicit dev flag is enabled.\\n- &amp;#96;toolTrace.args&amp;#96; should pass through a redaction layer before returning to client (e.g., mask long strings, strip tokens/keys).\\n\\n### Tool Trace step shape (TypeScript)\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;ts\\ntype ToolTraceStep = {\\n  tool: string;\\n  args: Record&amp;lt;string, unknown&amp;gt;;\\n  durationMs: number;\\n  results?: number;\\n  topCitations?: Array&amp;lt;{\\n    filing: string;\\n    date: string;\\n    section?: string;\\n    anchor?: string;\\n  }&amp;gt;;\\n};\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Prompt Design\\n\\n### Pattern\\nAsk the model for three sections: “Reasoning Summary”, “Final Answer”, and a private “&amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt;”. Instruct the model not to reveal scratchpad content to the user.\\n\\nExample (conceptual):\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\nYou may think step-by-step in &amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt; (max 200 tokens). Do not reveal or reference it.\\nReturn the following sections exactly:\\n\\nReasoning Summary:\\n- 2–5 short bullets explaining the approach (no prompts, no secrets)\\n\\nFinal Answer:\\n- The answer and citations (with filing type, date, section)\\n\\n&amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt;\\n(Private notes for debugging: why you chose the tool, filters, edge cases considered)\\n&amp;lt;/scratchpad&amp;gt;\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n### Guardrails (in the prompt)\\n- “Do not include any content from &amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt; in the Reasoning Summary or Final Answer.”\\n- “Keep Reasoning Summary concise and user-safe; avoid prompt text, keys, or file paths.”\\n- “Cap &amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt; at ~200 tokens.”\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Backend Changes\\n\\n### Execution flow (high level)\\n1) Tool execution instrumentation\\n   - Before each tool call, record &amp;#96;start = performance.now()&amp;#96; and sanitized &amp;#96;args&amp;#96; copy.\\n   - After completion, compute &amp;#96;durationMs&amp;#96;; capture &amp;#96;results&amp;#96; count and &amp;#96;topCitations&amp;#96; if applicable.\\n   - Push one &amp;#96;ToolTraceStep&amp;#96; into a &amp;#96;toolTrace&amp;#96; array on the server.\\n\\n2) Model response parsing\\n   - Parse the assistant output into: &amp;#96;reasoningSummary[]&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;finalAnswer&amp;#96;, and optional &amp;#96;&amp;lt;scratchpad&amp;gt;&amp;#96; section.\\n   - Enforce output length limits. If missing sections, degrade gracefully (empty summary, no scratchpad).\\n\\n3) Redaction and response assembly\\n   - Run &amp;#96;redactArgs()&amp;#96; for &amp;#96;toolTrace.args&amp;#96; (e.g., truncate long strings, remove keys).\\n   - If &amp;#96;user.isAdmin &amp;amp;&amp;amp; SCRATCHPAD_ADMIN_ONLY === &amp;#39;true&amp;#39; &amp;amp;&amp;amp; REASONING_SCRATCHPAD_ENABLED === &amp;#39;true&amp;#39;&amp;#96;, attach &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96;; else omit.\\n   - Return &amp;#96;{ answer, reasoningSummary, toolTrace, citations, scratchpad? }&amp;#96;.\\n\\n4) Persistence\\n   - Store &amp;#96;answer&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;reasoningSummary&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;toolTrace&amp;#96;, and &amp;#96;citations&amp;#96; as part of the message or query log.\\n   - Do not store &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96;. Avoid logging it to console or external logs.\\n\\n### Redaction guidelines\\n- Remove API keys, tokens, and auth headers.\\n- Truncate large text fields (e.g., queries &amp;gt; 256 chars) with a suffix “…(truncated)”.\\n- Mask PII if present (e.g., emails → &amp;#96;u***@domain.com&amp;#96;).\\n- For embeddings or RPC payloads, keep only query term and counts; avoid raw vectors.\\n\\n### Feature flags / config\\n- &amp;#96;REASONING_ENABLED=true&amp;#96; (default true; can disable globally).\\n- &amp;#96;REASONING_SHOW_SUMMARY_DEFAULT=true&amp;#96; (UI default on).\\n- &amp;#96;REASONING_TOOL_TRACE_DEFAULT=true&amp;#96; (UI default on).\\n- &amp;#96;REASONING_SCRATCHPAD_ENABLED=false&amp;#96; (default off in prod).\\n- &amp;#96;SCRATCHPAD_ADMIN_ONLY=true&amp;#96; (must be true in prod).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Frontend Changes\\n\\n### UI toggles (AssistantChat)\\n- Add “Show reasoning” switch (persist per-session in local state; include a “Copy trace” button for debugging.\\n- Scratchpad: admin-only collapsible preformatted block with a warning banner.\\n\\n### Accessibility and performance\\n- Ensure toggles are keyboard-accessible.\\n- Virtualize long histories: Reasoning/Trace should not cause message reflows that are expensive.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Security, Privacy, and Compliance\\n- Never store the scratchpad; it’s transient and admin-only.\\n- Redact secrets/PII from tool traces and args.\\n- Ensure RLS prevents non-admins from seeing &amp;#96;scratchpad&amp;#96; fields even if the API is called directly.\\n- Log size caps: protect logs and payloads against excessive growth (e.g., 100 KB cap per trace).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Testing Plan\\n\\n### Unit tests\\n- Prompt parser: extracts Reasoning Summary, Final Answer, and Scratchpad correctly.\\n- Redaction: verifies keys/PII removed; long strings truncated.\\n- Trace builder: correct durations, counts, and top citations propagation.\\n\\n### Integration/E2E\\n- User flow: Ask filing question → Reasoning Summary + Tool Trace visible; citations match trace.\\n- Admin flow: Enable scratchpad → visible; disable → hidden.\\n- Flag behavior: Disabling &amp;#96;REASONING_ENABLED&amp;#96; hides reasoning UI entirely.\\n\\n### Safety checks\\n- Ensure no scratchpad content appears in user-visible fields.\\n- Verify DB writes exclude scratchpad.\\n- Confirm large inputs do not degrade performance (load/perf checks).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Rollout Plan\\n1) Dev/staging (admins only)\\n   - Enable all features including scratchpad.\\n   - Collect feedback on clarity and usefulness.\\n2) Limited production (users see Reasoning Summary + Trace; scratchpad off)\\n   - &amp;#96;REASONING_ENABLED=true&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;REASONING_SCRATCHPAD_ENABLED=false&amp;#96;.\\n3) Full production\\n   - Keep scratchpad off by default; enable per-session for on-call debugging.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Risks and Mitigations\\n- Risk: Prompt leakage via Reasoning Summary.\\n  - Mitigation: Explicit prompt instructions; add tests to detect restricted phrases; manual reviews.\\n- Risk: Token/cost overhead.\\n  - Mitigation: Cap scratchpad to ~200 tokens; keep reasoning bullets short; strip long fields from traces.\\n- Risk: Privacy leakage via traces.\\n  - Mitigation: Redaction layer;                   "lineNumber": 1874,
                  "content": "        &amp;quot;diffString&amp;quot;: &amp;quot;- \\n+ ## Preference‑Driven Response Styling (Content Plan + Style Templates)\\n+ \\n+ This document defines how we’ll let you compare multiple answer styles side‑by‑side (A/B/n), choose a favorite, and automatically fold those preferences back into our prompts safely. It separates “what to say” (content plan) from “how to say it” (style template), and enforces quality/safety gates before promoting changes. The approach mirrors the comparative + boolean eval pattern described in Fiscal.ai’s Copilot Evals overview, which runs boolean pass/fail suites and comparative similarity checks against a production baseline to control regressions. See: How FinChat Improves AI Performance — Copilot Evals (https://fiscal.ai/blog/exploring-copilot-evals-how-finchat-improves-ai-performance/).\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ### Goals\\n+ - Offer multiple, clearly different writing styles for the same underlying facts so you can pick what reads best.\\n+ - Learn from your choices (tags/reasons) and propose minimal prompt edits that encode your preferences.\\n+ - Prevent regressions with hard gates (boolean safety/numerics) and stability checks (cross‑run similarity) before promoting prompt changes.\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ### Why separate “content plan” from “style template”?\\n+ - Content plan = what to say (facts, numbers, citations, outline) from our tools/RAG.\\n+ - Style template = how to say it (tone, structure, headings, bullets, tables, length, citation formatting).\\n+ - Keeping content fixed and only varying style makes comparisons fair (no factual drift) and makes your preferences actionable (prompt changes target style, not facts).\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ## End‑to‑End Flow\\n+ 1) Question arrives → tools run (financials, prices, filings).\\n+ 2) Build a Content Plan object (facts, key points, numbers, citations, outline).\\n+ 3) Render A/B/n drafts using:\\n+    - Style templates (deterministic rendering of the content plan), or\\n+    - A distinct “Stylist” model that rewrites only presentation (forbidden to add new facts).\\n+ 4) Show a side‑by‑side chooser (A/B/n). You pick the winner and select quick tags (e.g., “clearer”, “more numbers”, “better citations”, “shorter”).\\n+ 5) Log all metadata (question, drafts, styleId, model, tokens, tools used, your choice + tags).\\n+ 6) Analyze preferences over time and auto‑propose a small prompt/few‑shot diff for our “house style”.\\n+ 7) Run eval gates before promotion:\\n+    - Boolean suites (e.g., safety “No Advice”, numeric accuracy) → 100% pass required.\\n+    - Baseline Q&amp;amp;A (Quality + Stability): require average rubric score ≥ threshold and cross‑run similarity ≥ threshold on stability items.\\n+ 8) If gates pass, promote the prompt change; otherwise, iterate.\\n+ \\n+ This mirrors Fiscal.ai’s approach of boolean + comparative testing with production baselines to evaluate intentional vs. unintended changes (https://fiscal.ai/blog/exploring-copilot-evals-how-finchat-improves-ai-performance/).\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ## Key Concepts\\n+ \\n+ ### Content Plan (what to say)\\n+ - A neutral, factual structure produced from tool outputs.\\n+ - Includes:\\n+   - intent: high‑level goal (“Explain Apple’s segments”)\\n+   - outline: ordered sections to cover\\n+   - keyPoints: bullet points, each with a claim, numbers, and citation refs\\n+   - numbers: normalized metrics and units (e.g., USD billions)\\n+   - citations: filing passages, page refs, or dataset links\\n+   - constraints: must/not‑do (no new facts, word limits, citation rules)\\n+ \\n+ Example (schematic):\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;json\\n+ {\\n+   \\&amp;quot;intent\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Explain \\&amp;quot;Risks\\&amp;quot;],\\n+   \\&amp;quot;keyPoints\\&amp;quot;: [\\n+     { \\&amp;quot;section\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Segments\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;text\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;iPhone drives ~52% FY24 revenue\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;numbers\\&amp;quot;: [{\\&amp;quot;label\\&amp;quot;:\\&amp;quot;iPhone %\\&amp;quot;,\\&amp;quot;value\\&amp;quot;:0.52}], \\&amp;quot;citations\\&amp;quot;:[{\\&amp;quot;filing\\&amp;quot;:\\&amp;quot;10-K\\&amp;quot;,\\&amp;quot;page\\&amp;quot;:12}] },\\n+     { \\&amp;quot;section\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Drivers\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;text\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Services grew YoY with margin expansion\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;citations\\&amp;quot;:[{\\&amp;quot;filing\\&amp;quot;:\\&amp;quot;10-K\\&amp;quot;,\\&amp;quot;page\\&amp;quot;:35}] }\\n+   ],\\n+   \\&amp;quot;citations\\&amp;quot;: [{\\&amp;quot;filing\\&amp;quot;:\\&amp;quot;AAPL 10-K 2024\\&amp;quot;,\\&amp;quot;sections\\&amp;quot;:[\\&amp;quot;MD&amp;amp;A\\&amp;quot;],\\&amp;quot;pages\\&amp;quot;:[12,35]}],\\n+   \\&amp;quot;constraints\\&amp;quot;: { \\&amp;quot;noNewFacts\\&amp;quot;: true, \\&amp;quot;maxWords\\&amp;quot;: 250, \\&amp;quot;citationFormat\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;inline [source]\\&amp;quot; }\\n+ }\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ### Style Template (how to say it)\\n+ - A deterministic renderer that takes the same content plan and outputs different presentations.\\n+ - Controls: tone, structure, headings, bullets/tables, ordering, sentence rhythm, and citation formatting.\\n+ \\n+ Suggested initial templates (A/B/C):\\n+ - A) Executive Summary First\\n+   - 2‑sentence TL;DR → 3 bullets with numbers → 2 citations at end\\n+ - B) Bulleted Brief\\n+   - Heading → 5 short bullets (each with a number + citation) → “So what” line\\n+ - C) What / Why / So‑What\\n+   - What happened → Why it matters → So what for investors; cite at end of each section\\n+ \\n+ Optional: “Stylist” LLM\\n+ - Use a second model to rewrite the content plan into a specified style, with hard constraints:\\n+   - Must only use provided facts/citations\\n+   - Temperature 0 (deterministic), no new claims\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ## UI/UX\\n+ - Compare view: show A/B/C drafts side‑by‑side.\\n+ - Inputs captured: chosenDraftId, tags (checkboxes like Clearer, More numbers, Better citations, Concise, Actionable), optional comment.\\n+ - Show metadata toggle: tokens, model, latency, styleId, tool calls (for debugging).\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ## Data and Logging\\n+ Minimum fields to log per comparison:\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;json\\n+ {\\n+   \\&amp;quot;runId\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;draftId\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;A\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;styleId\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;exec-summary\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;model\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;gpt-4o-mini\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;draftId\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;B\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;styleId\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;bulleted-brief\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;model\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;gpt-4o-mini\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;temperature\\&amp;quot;: 0, \\&amp;quot;tokens\\&amp;quot;: 610, \\&amp;quot;latencyMs\\&amp;quot;: 830, \\&amp;quot;textHash\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;...\\&amp;quot; },\\n+     { \\&amp;quot;draftId\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;C\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;styleId\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;what-why-so-what\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;model\\&amp;quot;: [\\&amp;quot;Clearer\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;More numbers\\&amp;quot;], \\&amp;quot;comment\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;Fast to scan\\&amp;quot; },\\n+   \\&amp;quot;toolsUsed\\&amp;quot;: [\\&amp;quot;getAaplFinancialsByMetric\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;searchFilings\\&amp;quot;],\\n+   \\&amp;quot;version\\&amp;quot;: { \\&amp;quot;promptVersion\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;v7\\&amp;quot;, \\&amp;quot;fewShotPack\\&amp;quot;: \\&amp;quot;pack-2\\&amp;quot; }\\n+ }\\n+ &amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n+ \\n+ \\n+ ## Learning Loop (Turning Preferences into Prompt Edits)\\n+ 1) Aggregate wins by styleId and tag over N comparisons.\\n+ 2) Use an LLM to summarize “why winners win” and produce a minimal prompt diff proposal, e.g.:\\n+    - “Start with 2‑sentence summary, then 3 bullets each with a number and source; add a one‑line ‘So what’.”\\n+ 3) Open a review: show current prompt excerpt vs. proposed diff, plus recent wins/tags.\\n+ 4) If approved, run eval gates before promoting         "contents": "export async function evaluateAnswerQuality(\n  question: string,\n  answer: string,\n  sourceData: any,\n  openai: OpenAI\n): Promise&lt;AnswerQualityScore&gt; {\n  const prompt = buildJudgePrompt(question, answer, sourceData)\n\n  try {\n    const response = await openai.chat.completions.create({\n      model: 'gpt-4o',\n      messages: [\n        {\n          role: 'system',\n          content: 'You are an expert evaluator of AI-generated financial answers. Grade answers objectively and explain your reasoning.',\n        },\n        {\n          role: 'user',\n          content: prompt,\n        },\n      ],\n      response_format: { type: 'json_object' },\n      temperature: 0, // Deterministic grading\n    })\n\n    const result = JSON.parse(response.choices[0].message.content || '{}')\n\n    return {\n      accuracy: result.accuracy_score || 0,\n      relevance: result.relevance_score || 0,\n      completeness: result.completeness_score || 0,\n      insight: result.insight_score || 0,\n      overall: result.overall_score || 0,\n      reasoning: result.reasoning || 'No reasoning provided',\n    }\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('LLM-as-judge error:', error)\n    return {\n      accuracy: 0,\n      relevance: 0,\n      completeness: 0,\n      insight: 0,\n      overall: 0,\n      reasoning: &#96;Error during evaluation: ${error}&#96;,\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nfunction buildJudgePrompt(\n  question: string,\n  answer: string,\n  sourceData: any\n): string {\n  \n}",

        "contents": "async function testRouting(\n  question: TestQuestion,\n  mode: 'fast' | 'full',\n  useLLMJudge: boolean\n): Promise&lt;TestResult&gt; {\n\n    }\n\n    const baseResult: TestResult = {\n      question_id: question.id,\n      question: question.question,\n      expected_tool: question.expected_output.tool,\n      expected_args: question.expected_output.args,\n      actual_tool: parsed.tool,\n      actual_args: parsed.args,\n      tool_match: toolMatch,\n      args_match: argsMatchResult,\n      args_match_semantic: argsMatchSemResult,\n      overall_correct: toolMatch &amp;&amp;
