        "contents": "function buildJudgePrompt(\n  question: string,\n  answer: string,\n  sourceData: any\n): string {\n  return &#96;You are grading an AI's answer to a financial question.\n\nQUESTION ASKED BY USER:\n\"${question}\"\n\nDATA PROVIDED TO THE AI:\n${formatSourceData(sourceData)}\n\nAI'S ANSWER:\n\"${answer}\"\n\nGrade this answer on these criteria (1-10 scale for each):\n\n1. ACCURACY (1-10)\n   - Are all numbers, dates, and facts correct based on the source data?\n   - Any hallucinations or made-up information?\n   - Proper formatting (e.g., \"$383.3B\" not \"383300000000\")?\n\n2. RELEVANCE (1-10)\n   - Does the answer directly address what the user asked?\n   - If user asked for a \"trend\", does it describe a trend?\n   - If user asked for multiple years, does it cover them?\n\n3. COMPLETENESS (1-10)\n   - Does it use all the relevant data provided?\n   - If given 5 years of data, does it mention all 5?\n   - Are there important details missing?\n\n4. INSIGHT (1-10)\n   - Does it provide helpful context (percentages, comparisons, patterns)?\n   - Is it just a data dump, or does it interpret the data?\n   - Would this answer actually help the user?\n\n5. OVERALL (1-10)\n   - Considering all factors, how good is this answer?\n   - Would you be satisfied if you asked this question?\n\nGRADING GUIDELINES:\n- 9-10: Excellent, comprehensive, insightful answer\n- 7-8: Good answer, covers the basics well\n- 5-6: Acceptable but missing key details\n- 3-4: Poor answer, major gaps or errors\n- 1-2: Very poor, barely answers the question\n\nReturn ONLY valid JSON in this exact format:\n{\n  \"accuracy_score\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;,\n  \"relevance_score\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;,\n  \"completeness_score\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;,\n  \"insight_score\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;,\n  \"overall_score\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;,\n  \"reasoning\": \"&lt;2-3 sentence explanation of your grading&gt;\"\n}\n\nBe strict but fair. An answer that only uses 1 year when 5 were provided should score low on completeness. An answer without context or insight should score low on that dimension.&#96;\n}\n\nfunction formatSourceData(sourceData: any): string {\n  if\n}",

        "contents": "# Evaluation System: Technical Deep Dive\n\nThis document provides detailed technical explanations of how the evaluation system works under the hood.\n\n---\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n1. [Architecture Overview](#architecture-overview)\n2. [How LLM-as-Judge Works](#how-llm-as-judge-works)\n3. [Why We Test Answer Quality](#why-we-test-answer-quality)\n4. [HTML Report Generation](#html-report-generation)\n5. [Performance Optimization](#performance-optimization)\n6. [Extending the System](#extending-the-system)\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\n### The Two-Step LLM Flow\n\nYour Fin Quote system uses a two-step architecture:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nUser Question\n    ↓\n[STEP 1: Tool Selection] ← Test this with Fast Mode\n    ↓\nExecute Tool (fetch data)\n    ↓\n[STEP 2: Answer Generation] ← Test this with Full Mode\n    ↓\nFinal Answer\n    ↓\n[STEP 3: Quality Evaluation] ← Test this with LLM-as-Judge\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Evaluation Modes\n\n**Fast Mode:**\n- Tests only Step 1 (tool selection)\n- Doesn't generate answers\n- Fast: 2-3 minutes for 100 questions\n- Cheap: ~$0.02 per run\n\n**Full Mode:**\n- Tests Steps 1 AND 2 (tool selection + answer generation)\n- Generates complete answers\n- Medium speed: 8-10 minutes for 100 questions\n- Medium cost: ~$0.10 per run\n\n**Full Mode + LLM-Judge:**\n- Tests Steps 1, 2, AND 3 (tool selection + answer + quality)\n- Evaluates answer quality with GPT-4\n- Slow: 15-20 minutes for 100 questions\n- Expensive: ~$0.60 per run\n\n---\n\n## How LLM-as-Judge Works\n\n### The Problem\n\nTraditional testing can only check if the **format** is correct:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Traditional test\nassert(response.tool === \"getPrices\") // ✅ Can test this\nassert(response.args.range === \"30d\") // ✅ Can test this\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBut it CAN'T check if the **content** is good:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Can't test these automatically:\nassert(answer.isHelpful) // ❌ No way to check\nassert(answer.usesAllData) // ❌ No way to check\nassert(answer.providesInsight) // ❌ No way to check\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### The Solution: Use AI to Judge AI\n\nInstead of writing complex rules, we use GPT-4 to grade answers:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "# Prompt Evaluation &amp; Continuous Improvement System\n\n&gt; Important: The Fin Quote runtime uses the OpenAI Responses API exclusively. Any usage of Chat Completions in this document is for historical context or testing examples only.\n\n## Overview\n\nThis document outlines the complete system for evaluating and continuously improving the AI prompts used in Fin Quote. The goal is to measure prompt performance objectively, identify failure patterns, and systematically improve answer quality over time.\n\n---\n\n## Problem Statement\n\n**Current State:**\n- Prompts are hardcoded in &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;\n- No systematic way to test prompt changes before deploying\n- Can't measure if a prompt improvement actually helps or hurts\n- No visibility into which types of questions fail most often\n- Improvement is guesswork, not data-driven\n\n**Desired State:**\n- Test prompt changes against 100 representative questions in minutes\n- Objectively compare prompt versions with automated scoring\n- Deploy only improvements that show measurable gains\n- Identify and fix the most common failure patterns systematically\n- Data-driven improvement loop with &lt;1 day iteration cycles\n\n---\n\n## System Architecture\n\n### Components\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ 1. GOLDEN TEST SET                                          │\n│    - 100 representative questions                           │\n│    - Expected outputs (tool, args)                          │\n│    - Stored in: test-data/golden-test-set.json             │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n                            ↓\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ 2. PROMPT VERSIONS                                          │",

        "contents": "async function evaluate(mode: 'fast' | 'full', limit?: number, useLLMJudge = false) {\n\n  let fullyCorrectSemantic = 0\n\n  for (let i = 0; i &lt; questions.length; i++) {\n    const question = questions[i]\n    process.stdout.write(\n      &#96;[${i + 1}/${questions.length}] Testing question ${question.id}... &#96;\n    )\n\n    const result = await testRouting(question, mode, useLLMJudge)\n    results.push(result)\n\n    if (result.tool_match) correctTool++\n    if (result.args_match) correctArgs++\n    if (result.args_match_semantic) correctArgsSemantic++\n    if (result.overall_correct) fullyCorrect++\n    if (result.overall_correct_semantic) fullyCorrectSemantic++\n\n    // Print result (show semantic status)\n    if (result.overall_correct) {\n      const qualityText = result.quality_score\n        ? &#96; (quality: ${result.quality_score.overall.toFixed(1)}/10)&#96;\n        : ''\n      console.log(&#96;✅${qualityText}&#96;)\n    } else if (result.overall_correct_semantic) {\n      // Semantically correct but not exact match\n      console.log('✅ (semantic match)')\n    } else if (result.tool_match) {\n      console.log('⚠️  (wrong args)')\n    } else {\n      console.log('❌ (wrong tool)')\n    }\n\n    // Small delay to avoid rate limits\n    await new Promise((resolve) =&gt; setTimeout(resolve, useLLMJudge ? 500 : 100))\n  }\n\n  // Calculate accuracy\n  const total = questions.length\n  const accuracy = {\n    tool_selection: (correctTool / total) * 100,\n    args_selection: (correctArgs / total) * 100,\n    args_selection_semantic: (correctArgsSemantic / total) * 100,\n    overall: (fullyCorrect / total) * 100,\n    overall_semantic: (fullyCorrectSemantic / total) * 100,\n  }\n\n  // Calculate quality stats if LLM-judge was used\n  let qualityStats: EvaluationResults['quality_stats'] | undefined\n  if (useLLMJudge) {\n    const scores = results\n      .filter((r) =&gt; r.quality_score !== undefined)\n\n}",

        "contents": "async function handleBatchAnalysis(body: BatchAnalysisRequest) {\n  const { questions } = body\n\n  console.log(&#96;🔍 Analyzing ${questions.length} questions in batch...&#96;)\n\n  // Analyze all questions in parallel\n  const analysisPromises = questions.map(async (question) =&gt; {\n    const prompt = buildAnalysisPrompt(question)\n\n    const completion = await openai.chat.completions.create({\n      model: 'gpt-4o',\n      messages: [\n        {\n          role: 'system',\n          content: &#96;You are an expert evaluation assistant helping to analyze failed test cases for a financial Q&amp;A system.\n\nYour job is to:\n1. Determine if the golden test (expected output) is correct, or if the AI's actual output is better\n2. Provide clear reasoning for your opinion\n3. Recommend a specific action (fix prompt, update golden test, or accept both)\n\nBe concise but thorough. Think from the perspective of what a real user would want.&#96;,\n        },\n        {\n          role: 'user',\n          content: prompt,\n        },\n      ],\n      temperature: 0.3,\n    })\n\n    return {\n      question_id: question.question_id,\n      analysis: completion.choices[0].message.content,\n    }\n  })\n\n  const results = await Promise.all(analysisPromises)\n\n  console.log(&#96;✅ Batch analysis complete for ${results.length} questions&#96;)\n\n  return NextResponse.json({\n    analyses: results,\n  })\n}\n\nasync function handleSingleAnalysis(body: AnalysisRequest) {\n  const prompt = buildAnalysisPrompt(body)\n}",

        "contents": "---\n\n## Why We Test Answer Quality\n\n### The Hidden Problem\n\nYou can have perfect tool routing but terrible answers!\n\n**Example 1: Correct Tool, Useless Answer**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Your test passes ✅\nassert(tool === \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\")\nassert(args.metric === \"revenue\")\nassert(args.limit === 5)\n\n// But the answer is useless:\nanswer = \"Apple makes money from selling products.\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Example 2: Correct Tool, Incomplete Answer**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Your test passes ✅\nassert(tool === \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\")\nassert(args === {metric: \"revenue\", limit: 5})\n\n// But answer only uses 1 of 5 years:\nanswer = \"Revenue in 2024 was $391B.\"\n// Missing: 2020-2023 data!\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Example 3: Correct Tool, Hallucinated Answer**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Your test passes ✅\nassert(tool === \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\")\n\n// But answer contains wrong numbers:\nanswer = \"Revenue grew from $280B to $450B.\"\n// Real data: $274.5B to $391.0B\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### What Traditional Tests Miss\n\nTraditional tests check:\n- ✅ Did we pick the right tool?\n- ✅ Did we use the right arguments?\n\nTraditional tests DON'T check:\n- ❌ Does the answer actually help the user?\n- ❌ Did we use all the provided data?\n- ❌ Is the answer factually accurate?\n- ❌ Does it provide useful context/insight?\n\n### Real-World Impact\n\nWithout answer quality testing:\n\n**Scenario:** You improve tool routing from 70% → 95% ✅\n\n**Result:** Users still give thumbs down ❌\n\n**Why?** Answers are technically correct but unhelpful:\n- \"Revenue is $391B.\" (user wanted 5-year trend)\n- \"Price is $150.\" (user wanted to know if it's going up or down)\n- \"Yes.\" (user wanted detailed explanation)\n\n### The Solution\n\nLLM-as-judge catches these issues:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nTool Routing: 95% ✅\nAnswer Quality: 4.2/10 ❌ ← This is the real problem!\n\nLow Completeness Score:\n- Most answers only use 1 year when 5 are provided\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Action:** Update answer prompt to emphasize using all data.\n\n**New Results:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nTool Routing: 95% ✅\nAnswer Quality: 8.7/10 ✅ ← Much better!\n\nUsers happy ✅\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---",

        "contents": "/**\n * LLM-as-Judge: Use GPT-4 to evaluate answer quality\n *\n * This evaluates whether an AI-generated answer is actually good,\n * beyond just checking if it used the right tool.\n */\n\nimport OpenAI from 'openai'\n\nexport interface AnswerQualityScore {\n  accuracy: number // 1-10: Are numbers/facts correct?\n  relevance: number // 1-10: Does it answer the question?\n  completeness: number // 1-10: Uses all provided data?\n  insight: number // 1-10: Provides helpful context?\n  overall: number // 1-10: Overall quality\n  reasoning: string // Explanation of the scores\n}\n\nexport async function evaluateAnswerQuality(\n  question: string,\n  answer: string,\n  sourceData: any,\n  openai: OpenAI\n): Promise&lt;AnswerQualityScore&gt; {\n  \n}",

        "contents": "# Evaluation System: Complete Workflow Guide\n\nThis guide shows you how to use all three evaluation features together to improve your AI's accuracy and answer quality.\n\n---\n\n## Overview: What You Have\n\nYour evaluation system has three powerful features:\n\n1. **Fast/Full Evaluation** - Test tool selection and answer generation\n2. **LLM-as-Judge** - Automatic answer quality grading using GPT-4\n3. **HTML Reports** - Beautiful visual reports you can share\n\n---\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Fast mode (routing only) - 2-3 minutes\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast\n\n# Full mode (with answer generation) - 8-10 minutes\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode full\n\n# Full mode with LLM-as-judge - 15-20 minutes\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode full --llm-judge\n\n# Test with limited questions (faster for iteration)\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast --limit 10\n\n# Generate HTML report from results\nnpx tsx scripts/generate-html-report.ts test-data/test-results/eval-*.json\n\n# Demo LLM-as-judge\nnpx tsx scripts/test-llm-judge.ts\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Feature Comparison\n\n| Feature | Fast Mode | Full Mode | Full + LLM-Judge |\n|---------|-----------|-----------|------------------|\n| **Tests tool selection** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |\n| **Tests answer generation** | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |\n| **Evaluates answer quality** | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |\n| **Time (100 questions)** | 2-3 min | 8-10 min | 15-20 min |\n| **Cost (approx)** | $0.02 | $0.10 | $0.60 |\n| **Best for** | Daily iteration | Pre-deployment | Final validation |\n\n---\n\n## Complete Workflow Example\n\n### Scenario: You Want to Improve Your Prompts\n\n**WEEK 1: Establish Baseline**\n\n#### Step 1: Run Fast Evaluation\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Output:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n📊 EVALUATION SUMMARY\nTotal Questions: 100\nCorrect Tool: 95 (95.0%)\nCorrect Args: 83 (83.0%)\nFully Correct: 83 (83.0%)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**What this tells you:**\n- ✅ 95% tool selection accuracy (good!)\n- ⚠️ 83% overall accuracy (room for improvement in args)\n\n#### Step 2: Generate HTML Report\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Find the latest results file",

        "contents": "# Prompt Evolution Guide: From 46% to 83% Accuracy\n\n## Table of Contents\n1. [The Problem We're Solving](#the-problem-were-solving)\n2. [How the Evaluation System Works](#how-the-evaluation-system-works)\n3. [Prompt Version History](#prompt-version-history)\n4. [How We Improve Prompts](#how-we-improve-prompts)\n5. [Results Summary](#results-summary)\n6. [How to Use This System](#how-to-use-this-system)\n\n---\n\n## The Problem We're Solving\n\n### What is \"Tool Selection\"?\n\nOur application answers user questions about Apple's financials by routing questions to one of four specialized tools:\n\n1. **getAaplFinancialsByMetric** - Gets numerical financial data (revenue, profit, cash flow, etc.)\n2. **getPrices** - Gets stock price history for different time periods\n3. **searchFilings** - Searches SEC filings for qualitative information (risks, strategy, etc.)\n4. **getRecentFilings** - Lists recent SEC filing documents\n\nWhen a user asks a question like \"What's Apple's revenue?\", the AI needs to:\n- Pick the right tool (&#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96;)\n- Choose the right arguments (&#96;metric: \"revenue\", limit: 4&#96;)\n\nIf the AI picks the wrong tool or wrong arguments, the user gets bad answers.\n\n### Why Do We Need Better Prompts?\n\nInitially, our AI was only picking the right tool + arguments **46% of the time**. That means:\n- **54% of questions got wrong answers!**\n- Users would get price data when they asked about revenue\n- Users would get 5 results when they asked for 10\n- Users asking about \"P/E ratio\" would get no useful answer\n\n**Our goal:** Improve accuracy to 85%+ by systematically improving the prompt.\n\n---\n\n## How the Evaluation System Works\n\n### Overview\n\nWe built an **offline evaluation system** that tests prompts without bothering real users. Think of it like a practice exam for the AI.\n\n### The Golden Test Set\n\nWe created 100 carefully crafted questions that represent real user queries:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;json\n{\n  \"id\": 1,\n  \"question\": \"What's AAPL's revenue over the last 5 years?\",",

        "contents": "# Evaluation System - Quick Start\n\nYour Fin Quote project now has a complete evaluation system with three powerful features:\n\n1. ✅ **Fast/Full Evaluation** - Test tool selection and answer generation\n2. ✅ **LLM-as-Judge** - Automatic answer quality grading using GPT-4\n3. ✅ **HTML Reports** - Beautiful visual reports you can share\n\n---\n\n## Quick Commands\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Fast mode (2-3 min) - Test tool selection only\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast\n\n# Full mode (8-10 min) - Test tool selection + answer generation\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode full\n\n# Full mode with LLM-as-judge (15-20 min) - Test everything including answer quality\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode full --llm-judge\n\n# Test with fewer questions (faster for development)\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast --limit 10\n\n# Generate HTML report\nnpx tsx scripts/generate-html-report.ts test-data/test-results/eval-fast-*.json\n\n# Demo LLM-as-judge\nnpx tsx scripts/test-llm-judge.ts\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## What Each Mode Tests\n\n| Mode | Tests Tool Selection | Tests Answers | Evaluates Quality | Time | Cost |\n|------|---------------------|---------------|-------------------|------|------|\n| **Fast** | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | 2-3 min | $0.02 |\n| **Full** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | 8-10 min | $0.10 |\n| **Full + Judge** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | 15-20 min | $0.60 |\n\n---\n\n## Example Workflow\n\n### Day-to-Day Development\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Quick check (30 seconds)\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast --limit 10\n\n# If that looks good, run full test\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Before Deploying\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Comprehensive validation\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode full --llm-judge --limit 20\n\n# Generate report\nnpx tsx scripts/generate-html-report.ts test-data/test-results/eval-full-*.json\nopen test-data/test-results/eval-full-*.html\n\n# Review report, ensure quality score &gt;= 8.0\n# If good, deploy!\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Understanding Results\n\n### Tool Selection Accuracy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nCorrect Tool: 95 (95.0%)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- **Good:** ≥90%\n- **Needs work:** &lt;85%",

        "contents": "async function generateAnswer(\n  question: string,\n  tool: string,\n  args: Record&lt;string, any&gt;\n): Promise&lt;{ answer: string; sourceData: any; latency: number }&gt; {\n\n}\n\n// Run routing test for a single question\nasync function testRouting(\n  question: TestQuestion,\n  mode: 'fast' | 'full',\n  useLLMJudge: boolean\n): Promise&lt;TestResult&gt; {\n  const startTime = Date.now()\n\n  try {\n    // Use production prompt for accurate testing\n    const prompt = productionToolPrompt(question.question)\n\n    // Use Responses API (same as production) with system message\n    const selectionMessages: SimpleMessage[] = [\n      {\n        role: 'system',\n        content:\n          'You are Fin Quote routing assistant. Your ONLY job is to pick exactly one tool and respond with valid JSON matching {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. Do not add explanations, comments, or Markdown.',\n      },\n      { role: 'user', content: prompt },\n    ]\n    const selectionInput = toResponseInputMessages(selectionMessages)\n\n    const response = await openai.responses.create({\n      model: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-5-nano',\n      input: selectionInput,\n      ...(process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? {} : { temperature: 0 }),\n      max_output_tokens: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? 20000 : 150,\n      ...(process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? { reasoning: { effort: 'minimal' } } : {}),\n      text: { format: { type: 'json_object' } },\n    })\n\n    const latency = Date.now() - startTime\n\n    // Extract content from Responses API format\n    const content = extractResponseText(response) || ''\n\n    // Parse JSON response\n    let parsed: { tool: string; args: Record&lt;string, any&gt; } | null = null\n    try {\n      parsed = JSON.parse(content)\n    }\n}",

Not helpful.\"                         │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### The Grading Prompt\n\nHere's what we send to GPT-4 (from &#96;lib/llm-judge.ts&#96;):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nYou are grading an AI's answer to a financial question.\n\nQUESTION ASKED BY USER:\n\"What's AAPL's revenue trend over 5 years?\"\n\nDATA PROVIDED TO THE AI:\n{\n  \"metric\": \"revenue\",\n  \"data\": [\n    {\"year\": 2020, \"value\": 274515000000},\n    {\"year\": 2021, \"value\": 365817000000},\n    ...\n  ]\n}\n\nAI'S ANSWER:\n\"Apple's revenue in 2024 was $391.04 billion.\"\n\nGrade this answer on these criteria (1-10 scale):\n\n1. ACCURACY: Are all numbers correct?\n2. RELEVANCE: Does it answer what was asked?\n3. COMPLETENESS: Does it use all the data?\n4. INSIGHT: Does it provide helpful context?\n\nReturn JSON with scores and reasoning.\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Why This Works\n\n**Advantages:**\n- ✅ GPT-4 can understand nuance (is this answer helpful?)\n- ✅ Adapts to new question types automatically\n- ✅ Provides explanations (why did this score 4/10?)\n- ✅ Consistent grading (temperature=0)\n\n**Limitations:**\n- ❌ Costs money (~$0.005 per answer graded)\n- ❌ Slower (adds 3-5 seconds per question)\n- ❌ Not 100% deterministic (slight variation possible)\n- ❌ Can be wrong occasionally (need spot-checking)\n\n### Best Practices\n\n**1. Use temperature=0 for consistency:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nconst response = await openai.chat.completions.create({\n  model: 'gpt-4o',\n  messages: [{role: 'user', content: prompt}],\n  temperature: 0, // ← Makes grading more consistent\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**2. Provide clear grading rubrics:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nGRADING GUIDELINES:\n- 9-10: Excellent, comprehensive\n- 7-8: Good, covers basics\n- 5-6: Acceptable but missing details\n- 3-4: Poor, major gaps\n- 1-2: Very poor\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**3. Spot-check GPT-4's grading:**\n\nOccasionally, manually review some graded answers to ensure GPT-4 is being reasonable.\n\n---\n\n## Why We Test Answer Quality\n\n### The Hidden Problem",

        "contents": "async function evaluate(mode: 'fast' | 'full', limit?: number, useLLMJudge = false) {\n\n  if (useLLMJudge) {\n    const scores = results\n      .filter((r) =&gt; r.quality_score !== undefined)\n      .map((r) =&gt; r.quality_score!)\n    const stats = calculateQualityStats(scores)\n    qualityStats = {\n      avg_accuracy: stats.avgAccuracy,\n      avg_relevance: stats.avgRelevance,\n      avg_completeness: stats.avgCompleteness,\n      avg_insight: stats.avgInsight,\n      avg_overall: stats.avgOverall,\n      excellent_count: stats.excellentCount,\n      good_count: stats.goodCount,\n      poor_count: stats.poorCount,\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Build final results\n  const evaluationResults: EvaluationResults = {\n    mode,\n    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n    total_questions: total,\n    correct_tool: correctTool,\n    correct_args: correctArgs,\n    correct_args_semantic: correctArgsSemantic,\n    fully_correct: fullyCorrect,\n    fully_correct_semantic: fullyCorrectSemantic,\n    accuracy,\n    results,\n    llm_judge_enabled: useLLMJudge,\n    quality_stats: qualityStats,\n  }\n\n  // Save results\n  const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-')\n  const resultsPath = path.join(\n    process.cwd(),\n    'test-data',\n    'test-results',\n    &#96;eval-${mode}-${timestamp}.json&#96;\n  )\n\n  fs.writeFileSync(resultsPath, JSON.stringify(evaluationResults, null, 2))\n\n  // Print summary with three-tier accuracy (Layer 3)\n  console.log('\\n' + '='.repeat(60))\n  console.log('📊 EVALUATION SUMMARY')\n  console.log('='.repeat(60))\n  console.log(&#96;Mode: ${mode}${useLLMJudge ? ' (with LLM-as-judge)' : ''}&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;Total Questions: ${total}&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;\\n🎯 Tool Selection:&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;   ${correctTool}/${total} correct (${accuracy.tool_selection.toFixed(1)}%)&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;\\n📊 Three-Tier Accuracy:&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;   1. Exact Match:      ${fullyCorrect}/${total} (${accuracy.overall.toFixed(1)}%)&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;   2. Tool Only:        ${correctTool}/${total} (${accuracy.tool_selection.toFixed(1)}%)&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;\\n💡 Semantic matching uses:&#96;)\n}",

        "contents": "const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY })\n\nasync function testLLMJudge() {\n  console.log('🧪 Testing LLM-as-Judge\\n')\n  console.log('This shows how we can evaluate answer QUALITY, not just tool selection.\\n')\n\n  // Example scenario\n  const question = \"What's AAPL's revenue trend over 5 years?\"\n\n  const sourceData = {\n    metric: 'revenue',\n    data: [\n      { year: 2020, value: 274515000000 },\n      { year: 2021, value: 365817000000 },\n      { year: 2022, value: 394328000000 },\n      { year: 2023, value: 383285000000 },\n      { year: 2024, value: 391035000000 },\n    ],\n  }\n\n  // Bad Answer: Only mentions 1 year despite having 5 years of data\n  const badAnswer = \"Apple's revenue in 2024 was $391.04 billion.\"\n\n  // Good Answer: Uses all data, describes trend, provides insight\n  const goodAnswer =\n    \"Apple's revenue showed strong growth over the past 5 years, rising from $274.5B in 2020 to $391.0B in 2024. The company saw rapid growth from 2020-2022 (up 44%), but revenue plateaued in 2023-2024, fluctuating between $383B-$394B. Overall, revenue is up 42% over the 5-year period.\"\n\n  // Hallucinated Answer: Contains made-up numbers\n  const hallucinatedAnswer =\n    \"Apple's revenue grew from $280B in 2020 to $450B in 2024, showing consistent double-digit growth every year.\"\n\n  console.log('═'.repeat(70))\n  console.log('SCENARIO 1: Bad Answer (Only mentions 1 year)')\n  console.log('═'.repeat(70))\n  console.log(&#96;Question: \"${question}\"&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;Answer: \"${badAnswer}\"\\n&#96;)\n\n  console.log('Evaluating with GPT-4...\\n')\n\n  const score1 = await evaluateAnswerQuality(question, badAnswer, sourceData, openai)\n\n  console.log('📊 SCORES:')\n  console.log(&#96;   Accuracy:     ${score1.accuracy}/10&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;   Relevance:    ${score1.relevance}/10&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;   Completeness: ${score1.completeness}/10&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;   Insight:      ${score1.insight}/10&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;   OVERALL:      ${score1.overall}/10&#96;)\n  console.log(&#96;\\n💭 Reasoning: ${score1.reasoning}\\n&#96;)\n\n  console.log('═'.repeat(70))\n  console.log\n}",

        "contents": "export const buildFinalAnswerPrompt = \n&#96;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return &#96;You are an analyst. Answer the user using ONLY the provided facts${previousToolResults &amp;&amp; previousToolResults.length &gt; 0 ? ' and previous context' : ''}.\n\nUser question: \"${userQuestion}\"\n\nFacts (JSON rows):\n${factsJson}\n${previousContextSection}\n\nCRITICAL VALIDATION RULES - Follow These Exactly:\n\n1. NUMBERS - Use EXACT numbers from the data with proper formatting:\n   - Copy numbers precisely from the facts JSON\n   - Format large dollar amounts with B (billions) or M (millions)\n   - Example: 383285000000 → \"$383.3B\" (NOT \"$383B\" or \"around $380B\")\n   - Format ratios and percentages with 2 decimal places maximum\n   - Example: 34.092882867601105 → \"34.09\" (NOT \"34.092882867601105\")\n   - NEVER round significantly or estimate, but do round to 2 decimal places for readability\n   - If a number is 383.285B, say \"$383.3B\" not \"$383B\"\n   - For stock prices, ALWAYS add '$' before the price: \"$243.85\" not \"243.85\"\n\n2. YEARS - ONLY mention years that appear in the facts:\n   - Before mentioning any year, verify it exists in the facts JSON\n   - If asked about a year NOT in the facts, say: \"I don't have data for [year].\"\n   - DO NOT extrapolate, estimate, or guess for missing years\n   - Example: If facts have [2024, 2023, 2022, 2021] and user asks for 2020, say \"I don't have 2020 data\"\n\n3. DATES - Use EXACT dates from the data:\n   - For filings, use the exact filing_date from the facts\n   - For periods, use the exact period_end_date from the facts\n   - NEVER invent or approximate dates\n   - Example: If filing_date is \"2024-11-01\", say \"November 1, 2024\" not \"November 2024\"\n\n4. CITATIONS - Use EXACT filing information:\n   - If mentioning a filing, verify its filing_type and filing_date are in the facts\n   - Example: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024...\" (use exact date from data)\n   - NEVER reference filings not present in the facts\n\n4a. SEC FILING PASSAGES - When facts contain SEC filing content:\n   - The facts JSON contains \"chunk_text\" fields with actual text from SEC filings\n   - ⚠️ CRITICAL: READ ALL PASSAGES COMPLETELY before answering\n   - ⚠️ CRITICAL: Search through ALL passages for the information requested\n\n   When user asks about specific topics (e.g., \"iPhone sales\", \"risk factors\"):\n   1. Scan through ALL passages looking for mentions of that topic\n   2. If you find relevant data (numbers, quotes, facts), EXTRACT IT and provide it\n   3. DO NOT say \"I can provide it if you want\" - JUST PROVIDE IT\n   4. DO NOT be overly cautious - if the data is there, use it\n\n   For DATA in tables or structured format:\n   - Extract the numbers and present them clearly\n   - Example: If passage contains \"iPhone $ 201,183 $ 200,583 $ 205,489\" with headers \"2024 2023 2022\"\n   - Answer: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, iPhone net sales were $201.2 billion in 2024, $200.6 billion in 2023, and $205.5 billion in 2022.\"\n\n   For QUOTES and qualitative content:\n   - Provide direct quotes from chunk_text that are RELEVANT\n   - Use quotation marks around direct quotes\n   - Cite the source: filing type, date, and section\n   - Example: According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, \"The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs...\"\n\n   Only say \"I couldn't find information\" if:\n   - You've read ALL passages completely\n   - NONE of them contain the requested information\n   - DO NOT say this if the data exists but you're uncertain about formatting\n\n5. UNCERTAINTY - Admit when unsure:\n   - If you cannot find specific data in the facts, say so clearly\n   - Better to say \"I don't have that information\" than to guess\n   - If data seems incomplete, acknowledge it\n\n6. CALCULATIONS - You MUST calculate ratios/percentages from the data when requested:\n\n   IMPORTANT: The facts JSON often includes multiple fields per row to enable ratio calculations.\n   For example, if the metric is \"total_liabilities\", the JSON will also include \"shareholders_equity\" and \"total_assets\".\n   These additional fields are provided specifically so you can calculate ratios. USE THEM.\n\n   STOCK PRICE PERFORMANCE:\n   - If the facts include a \"percentChange\" field, USE THAT VALUE directly (it's already calculated)\n   - If percentChange is NOT provided, calculate it: ((ending_price - starting_price) / starting_price) × 100\n   - Format: \"up X%\" or \"down X%\" with 2 decimal places\n   - Example: percentChange: 790.58 → \"up 790.58%\"\n   - Example: Start: $243.85, End: $267.93 → ((267.93 - 243.85) / 243.85) × 100 = 9.88% → \"up 9.88%\"\n\n   ⚠️ REQUIRED FORMAT FOR PRICE PERFORMANCE ANSWERS (STRICTLY ENFORCE):\n\n   SENTENCE 1 (MANDATORY): \"Over the last [timeframe], AAPL stock is up (or down) X%.\"\n   SENTENCE 2 (MANDATORY): \"It has gone from $X to $X.\"\n   SENTENCE 3 (OPTIONAL): \"During this period, the stock reached a high of $X and a low of $X.\"\n\n   Example: \"Over the last 10 years, AAPL stock is up 790.58%. It has gone from $30.14 to $268.47. During this period, the stock reached a high of $271.40 and a low of $22.59.\"\n\n   ❌ WRONG (DO NOT DO THIS): \"Over the last 7 years, the data range runs from 2018-11-08 to 2025-11-07, with a start price of $52.12...\"\n   ✅ CORRECT: \"Over the last 7 years, AAPL stock is up 415.15%. It has gone from $52.12 to $268.47...\"\n\n   CRITICAL: The FIRST sentence MUST state the percentage change. Do NOT start with dates, price levels, or \"the data range runs from...\"\n\n   PROFITABILITY RATIOS:\n   - Gross Margin = (gross_profit / revenue) × 100\n   - Operating Margin = (operating_income / revenue) × 100\n   - Net Margin = (net_income / revenue) × 100\n   - ROE (Return on Equity) = (net_income / shareholders_equity) × 100\n   - ROA (Return on Assets) = (net_income / total_assets) × 100\n\n   LEVERAGE RATIOS:\n   - Debt-to-Equity = total_liabilities / shareholders_equity\n     * When asked for debt-to-equity, look for \"value\" (total_liabilities) and \"shareholders_equity\" in each row\n     * Calculate the ratio for each year: value / shareholders_equity\n     * Format as a ratio with 2 decimal places: \"3.87\" not \"3.87234...\"\n     * Show dollar amounts in B or M format, and the calculated ratio\n     * Example: \"The debt-to-equity ratio in 2025 is 3.87 (total liabilities of $285.5B divided by shareholders' equity of $73.7B).\"\n   - Debt-to-Assets = total_liabilities / total_assets\n\n   EFFICIENCY RATIOS:\n   - Asset Turnover = revenue / total_assets\n   - Cash Flow Margin = (operating_cash_flow / revenue) × 100\n\n   - If user asks for a \"margin\" or \"ratio\", calculate it from the available data\n   - Show the calculation concisely with formatted numbers\n   - For margins (profitability), show as percentage: \"Gross margin is 46.2% ($180.7B gross profit / $391.0B revenue)\"\n   - For ratios (leverage, efficiency), show as decimal: \"Debt-to-equity ratio is 3.87 ($285.5B liabilities / $73.7B equity)\"\n\n7. ⚠️ CRITICAL: EXTENDED METRICS FORMATTING (from financial_metrics table):\n   When the facts JSON contains \"metric_name\" and \"metric_value\" fields, you MUST apply these formatting rules:\n\n   PERCENTAGE METRICS - MULTIPLY BY 100 AND ADD %:\n   ❌ WRONG: \"ROE is 1.52\" or \"ROE is 1.50\"\n   ✅ CORRECT: \"ROE is 152%\" or \"ROE is 150%\"\n\n   - returnOnEquity (ROE): If data shows 1.52, write \"152%\"\n   - returnOnAssets (ROA): If data shows 0.28, write \"28%\"\n   - returnOnCapitalEmployed (ROCE): If data shows 0.35, write \"35%\"\n   - grossProfitMargin: If data shows 0.46, write \"46%\"\n   - operatingProfitMargin, netProfitMargin: Same rule\n   - All metrics ending in \"Margin\", \"Growth\", \"Yield\": multiply by 100, add %\n\n   RATIO METRICS (show as decimal, 2 places, NO multiplication):\n   - peRatio, pbRatio, priceToSalesRatio → \"P/E ratio is 28.50\"\n   - currentRatio, quickRatio, cashRatio → \"Current ratio is 1.23\"\n   - debtEquityRatio, debtToAssets → \"Debt-to-equity is 1.87\"\n\n   CURRENCY METRICS (format with $ and B/M):\n   - marketCap, enterpriseValue → \"$3.5T\" or \"$350B\"\n   - freeCashFlow, operatingCashFlow → \"$100.5B\"\n   - bookValuePerShare, cashPerShare → \"$4.25\"\n\n   DAYS METRICS (show as whole number with \"days\"):\n   - daysOfInventoryOnHand, daysPayablesOutstanding → \"45 days\"\n   - cashConversionCycle → \"-35 days\" (can be negative)\n\n   ALWAYS round to 2 decimal places maximum. NEVER show raw decimal values.\n\nGeneral Instructions:\n- Be concise and clear.\n- If the user asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (e.g., \"in 2020\", \"for 2018\"), check if that year exists in the facts:\n  * If the year IS in the facts → provide the data directly and clearly\n  * If the year is NOT in the facts → say \"I don't have data for [year].\" and stop\n- If the user asks for multiple years or a trend, show all relevant years.\n- If trend is relevant (and the user asked for it), describe it (e.g., increasing/decreasing/flat).\n- Do not invent numbers or sources.\n- Respond in plain text sentences. Do NOT use Markdown formatting (no bullet lists, bold, italics, tables, or code blocks).\n- When there is only ONE data point, provide a concise single-sentence answer with the year and value. Do NOT mention any chart or table.\n- When there are 2-4 data points AND the user did NOT explicitly ask for a chart/graph, list them briefly in your answer.\n- When there are 2-4 data points AND the user explicitly asked for a chart/graph/visualization, briefly mention the key values and direct them to check the chart below.\n- When more than four data points are relevant, do not list each one. Write at most two sentences: the first calls out the earliest year/value, latest year/value, and any notable high/low WITH the percentage change; the second describes the overall trend and tells the user to check the chart and data table below for the full yearly breakdown.\n\nExamples:\n- Question: \"What was net income in 2020?\" → Answer: \"AAPL's net income in 2020 was $57.4 billion.\" (Only 2020, exact number)\n- Question: \"What's the revenue trend?\" → Answer: \"Revenue increased from $274.5B in 2020 to $383.3B in 2024.\" (Show trend, exact numbers)\n- Question: \"Revenue in 2020 vs 2024?\" → Answer: \"Revenue was $274.5B in 2020 and $383.3B in 2024, a 40% increase.\" (Compare as requested, exact numbers)\n- Question: \"What's the gross margin?\" → Answer: \"AAPL's gross margin in 2024 is 46.2% (gross profit of $180.7B divided by revenue of $391.0B).\" (Calculate ratio from data)\n- Question: \"Chart of debt to equity ratio last 5 years\" → Answer: \"The debt-to-equity ratio decreased from 2.61 in 2022 to 0.11 in 2025; check the chart below for the full trend.\" (User asked for chart, direct them to it)\n- Question: \"Show year to date performance\" → Answer: \"AAPL is up 9.88% year-to-date, from $243.85 to $267.93 as of the latest date in the data. Check the data table below for the full yearly breakdown.\" (Calculate percentage, format prices with $, mention trend)\n- Question: \"What did AAPL say about risk factors in their latest 10-K? provide quotes.\" → Answer: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, Apple identifies several main risks: 'The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs on the value of its inventory and other assets, in addition to purchase commitment cancellation risk.' The filing also notes that 'rapid technological change and competitive dynamics could materially adversely affect the Company's business, results of operations and financial condition.'\" (Provide direct quotes from chunk_text with proper citation)\n- Question: \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone sales?\" → Answer: \"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, iPhone net sales were $201.2 billion in 2024, $200.6 billion in 2023, and $205.5 billion in 2022.\" (Extract relevant data from the passage that actually mentions iPhone, not unrelated passages about inventory or IP)&#96;\n}",

## Prompts and evaluation process

### What are prompts?

Prompts are instructions that tell the AI what to do. Your chatbot uses three main prompts:

1. Tool selection prompt — picks which data source to use
2. Answer generation prompt — writes the answer
3. Regeneration prompt — fixes mistakes

---

## The three prompts

### Prompt 1: Tool selection (`lib/tools.ts`)

What it does: Chooses which tool to use based on the question.

Example:
```
User asks: "What's AAPL's revenue in 2024?"

The prompt says:
"You are a router. Choose exactly one tool.

Available Tools:
1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - For revenue, profit, etc.
2. getPrices - For stock prices
3. searchFilings - For filing content
...

User question: 'What's AAPL's revenue in 2024?'"

AI responds: {"tool": "getAaplFinancialsByMetric", "args": {"metric": "revenue", "limit": 20}}
```

Why it matters: Routes the question to the right data source.

---

### Prompt 2: Answer generation (`lib/tools.ts`)

What it does: Writes the answer using the fetched data.

Example:
```
The prompt says:
"You are an analyst. Answer using ONLY the provided facts.

User question: 'What's AAPL's revenue in 2024?'

Facts (JSON):
[
  {year: 2024, value: 383285000000},
  {year: 2023, value: 383285000000}
]

CRITICAL RULES:
1. Use EXACT numbers from data
2. Format: $383.3B (not $383B)
3. Only mention years that exist in data
..."

AI responds: "AAPL's revenue in 2024 was $383.3 billion."
```

Why it matters: Ensures answers are accurate and formatted correctly.

---

### Prompt 3: Regeneration (`lib/regeneration.ts`)

What it does: Fixes mistakes when validation fails.

Example:
```
Validation found: Answer said "$383B" but data is "$383.3B"

The prompt says:
"⚠️ NUMBER VALIDATION ERROR:

Your answer contained: $383B
EXACT value from data: $383.3B

CRITICAL RULES:
1. Use EXACT numbers from data
2. Format: $383.3B (one decimal)
3. Do NOT round significantly

Please regenerate the answer with the correct number."

AI responds: "AAPL's revenue in 2024 was $383.3 billion." ✅
```

Why it matters: Catches and fixes errors automatically.

---

## The evaluation process

### Step 1: Create a test set

You have a "golden test set" with ~100 questions and expected answers:

```json
{
  "id": 1,
  "question": "What's AAPL's revenue in 2024?",
  "expected_output": {
    "tool": "getAaplFinancialsByMetric",
    "args": {"metric": "revenue", "limit": 20}
  }
}
```

---

### Step 2: Run evaluation

Two modes:

Fast mode (tool selection only):
```
For each question:
  1. Send question to tool selection prompt
  2. Check if AI picked the right tool
  3. Check if arguments are correct
  4. Record pass/fail

Result: "85% accuracy on tool selection"
```

Full mode (tool + answer):
```
For each question:
  1. Tool selection (same as fast mode)
  2. Fetch actual data
  3. Generate answer
  4. Check if answer is correct
  5. Record pass/fail

Result: "78% accuracy on full answers"
```

---

### Step 3: LLM-as-judge (optional)

Uses GPT-4 to grade answer quality:

```typescript
// lib/llm-judge.ts
const judgePrompt = `
Grade this answer on a 1-10 scale:

Question: "What's AAPL's revenue trend?"
Data provided: [2024: $383.3B, 2023: $383.3B, ...]
AI's answer: "Revenue increased from $274.5B in 2020 to $383.3B in 2024."

Criteria:
1. ACCURACY (1-10) - Are numbers correct?
2. RELEVANCE (1-10) - Does it answer the question?
3. COMPLETENESS (1-10) - Uses all relevant data?
4. INSIGHT (1-10) - Provides helpful context?
5. OVERALL (1-10) - How good is this answer?

Return JSON: {
  "accuracy_score": 9,
  "relevance_score": 8,
  "completeness_score": 7,
  "insight_score": 8,
  "overall_score": 8,
  "reasoning": "Good answer with correct numbers..."
}
`
```

Why it matters: Evaluates quality beyond just correctness.

---

## The complete flow

```
1. User asks question
   ↓
2. Tool Selection Prompt → Picks tool
   ↓
3. Fetch data from database
   ↓
4. Answer Generation Prompt → Writes answer
   ↓
5. Validation → Checks if answer is correct
   ↓
6. If validation fails → Regeneration Prompt → Fixes answer
   ↓
7. Final answer to user
```

---

## How prompts are improved

### Version control

Prompts are stored in the database with versions:

```typescript
// supabase/migrations/20241101000001_create_prompt_versions.sql
CREATE TABLE prompt_versions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  version VARCHAR(10),  -- "v1", "v2", "v3"
  prompt_type VARCHAR(50),  -- "tool_selection", "answer_generation"
  content TEXT,  -- The actual prompt text
  created_at TIMESTAMP
)
```

### Testing process

1. Create new prompt version (e.g., v5)
2. Run evaluation against test set
3. Compare results:
   ```
   v4: 78% accuracy
   v5: 82% accuracy ✅ (improvement!)
   ```
4. If better → Deploy v5
5. If worse → Keep v4, try again

---

## Evaluation dashboard

You have an admin page (`app/admin/evaluations/page.tsx`) that shows:

- Accuracy scores (tool selection, answer quality)
- Failed questions (what went wrong)
- Claude analysis (suggestions for fixes)
- Comparison between versions

---

## Example evaluation result

```json
{
  "question": "What's AAPL's revenue in 2024?",
  "expected_tool": "getAaplFinancialsByMetric",
  "actual_tool": "getAaplFinancialsByMetric", ✅
  "expected_args": {"metric": "revenue", "limit": 20},
  "actual_args": {"metric": "revenue", "limit": 20}, ✅
  "tool_match": true,
  "args_match": true,
  "overall_correct": true,
  "routing_latency_ms": 234
}
```

---

## Summary

1. Prompts are instructions that guide the AI
2. Three prompts: tool selection, answer generation, regeneration
3. Evaluation tests prompts against a test set
4. LLM-as-judge grades answer quality
5. Prompts are versioned and improved over time
6. Dashboard shows results and failures

The goal: measure prompt performance, find failures, and improve systematically.

## How JSON is fed into the prompt

Yes. The JSON from the database is converted to a string and inserted directly into the prompt text.

### Step-by-step process

**Step 1: Fetch data from database**
```typescript
// app/api/ask/route.ts (line 201-217)
const toolResult = await getAaplFinancialsByMetric({
  metric: "revenue",
  limit: 4
})

// Returns JavaScript objects:
// [
//   {year: 2024, value: 383285000000},
//   {year: 2023, value: 383285000000},
//   ...
// ]
```

**Step 2: Convert to JSON string**
```typescript
// Line 217
factsJson = JSON.stringify(toolResult.data, null, 2)
// Converts to formatted JSON string:
// "[\n  {\n    \"year\": 2024,\n    \"value\": 383285000000\n  },\n  ...\n]"
```

**Step 3: Insert into prompt**
```typescript
// lib/tools.ts (line 508-542)
export const buildFinalAnswerPrompt = (
  userQuestion: string,
  factsJson: string,  // ← The JSON string
  ...
) => {
  return `You are an analyst. Answer the user using ONLY the provided facts.

User question: "${userQuestion}"

Facts (JSON rows):
${factsJson}  // ← JSON is inserted here as plain text!

CRITICAL RULES:
1. Use EXACT numbers from the data
2. Format: $383.3B
...`
}
```

### What the AI sees

The AI receives a text prompt that includes the JSON as plain text:

```
You are an analyst. Answer the user using ONLY the provided facts.

User question: "What's AAPL's revenue in 2024?"

Facts (JSON rows):
[
  {
    "year": 2024,
    "value": 383285000000
  },
  {
    "year": 2023,
    "value": 383285000000
  }
]

CRITICAL RULES:
1. Use EXACT numbers from the data
...
```

The AI reads the JSON as text and uses it to write the answer.

The admin page is loading. It shows evaluation results. If no evaluation has been run yet, it will show a message to run the evaluation script.

The page displays:
- Accuracy metrics (tool selection, semantic match, etc.)

If you see "Loading evaluation..." or "No Evaluation Loaded", you'll need to run the evaluation script first:
```bash
npx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast
```

The JSON is inserted directly into the prompt as text, and the AI reads it to generate answers.

        "contents": "-- Query Logs Table\n-- Stores every user question and AI response for accuracy measurement and improvement\n\ncreate table query_logs (\n  -- Primary key\n  id uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),\n\n  -- Session tracking\n  session_id text not null,  -- Links related questions in a conversation\n\n  -- User input\n  user_question text not null,  -- The question user asked\n\n  -- LLM reasoning (Step 1: Tool selection)\n  tool_selected text not null,  -- e.g., \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\"\n  tool_args jsonb not null,  -- e.g., {\"metric\": \"revenue\", \"limit\": 5}\n  tool_selection_latency_ms integer,  -- How long tool selection took\n\n  -- Tool execution (Step 2: Data fetch)\n  data_returned jsonb,  -- Actual data from tool (or just metadata like row count)\n  data_row_count integer,  -- How many rows returned\n  tool_execution_latency_ms integer,  -- How long data fetch took\n  tool_error text,  -- If tool call failed, store error message\n\n  -- LLM response (Step 3: Answer generation)\n  answer_generated text not null,  -- The final answer shown to user\n  answer_latency_ms integer,  -- How long answer generation took\n\n  -- Metadata\n  created_at timestamp default now(),\n\n  -- Optional: User feedback (add later in Phase 2)\n  user_feedback text,  -- \"thumbs_up\", \"thumbs_down\", or null\n  user_feedback_comment text  -- Optional text feedback\n);\n\n-- Indexes for fast queries\ncreate index idx_query_logs_session on query_logs(session_id);\ncreate index idx_query_logs_created_at on query_logs(created_at desc);\ncreate index idx_query_logs_tool on query_logs(tool_selected);\n\n-- Row Level Security (RLS)\n-- For MVP: Allow all operations (adjust based on your auth setup)\nalter table query_logs enable row level security;\n\n-- Policy: Allow all operations for now (tighten in production)\ncreate policy \"Allow all operations on query_logs\"\n  on query_logs\n  for all\n  using (true)\n  with check (true);",

        "contents": "create table query_logs (\n  -- Primary key\n  id uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),\n\n  -- Session tracking\n  session_id text not null,  -- Links related questions in a conversation\n\n  -- User input\n  user_question text not null,  -- The question user asked\n\n  -- LLM reasoning (Step 1: Tool selection)\n  tool_selected text not null,  -- e.g., \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\"\n  tool_args jsonb not null,  -- e.g., {\"metric\": \"revenue\", \"limit\": 5}\n  tool_selection_latency_ms integer,  -- How long tool selection took\n\n  -- Tool execution (Step 2: Data fetch)\n  data_returned jsonb,  -- Actual data from tool (or just metadata like row count)\n  data_row_count integer,  -- How many rows returned\n  tool_execution_latency_ms integer,  -- How long data fetch took\n  tool_error text,  -- If tool call failed, store error message\n\n  -- LLM response (Step 3: Answer generation)\n  answer_generated text not null,  -- The final answer shown to user\n  answer_latency_ms integer,  -- How long answer generation took\n\n  -- Metadata\n  created_at timestamp default now(),\n\n  -- Optional: User feedback (add later)\n  user_feedback text,  -- \"thumbs_up\", \"thumbs_down\", or null\n  user_feedback_comment text  -- Optional text feedback\n);\n\n-- Indexes for fast queries\ncreate index idx_query_logs_session on query_logs(session_id);\ncreate index idx_query_logs_created_at on query_logs(created_at desc);\ncreate index idx_query_logs_tool on query_logs(tool_selected);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Why These Fields?\n\n**session_id**: Track conversations over time\n- Example: \"User asked about revenue, then net income\" → same session\n\n**user_question**: The raw question\n- Example: \"What's AAPL's revenue trend?\"\n\n**tool_selected**: Which tool the LLM chose\n- Example: \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\"\n- **Use case:** Measure tool selection accuracy\n\n**tool_args**: Arguments passed to tool\n- Example: &#96;{\"metric\": \"revenue\", \"limit\": 5}&#96;\n- **Use case:** See if LLM chose correct parameters\n\n**data_returned**: What the tool actually returned\n- **Option A (full):** Store entire dataset &#96;[{year: 2020, value: 274.5B}, ...]&#96;",

          {
            "text": "-- Indexes for fast queries",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "text": "create index idx_query_logs_session on query_logs(session_id);",
            "lineNumber": 133
          },
          {
            "text": "create index idx_query_logs_created_at on query_logs(created_at desc);",
            "lineNumber": 134
          },
          {
            "text": "create index idx_query_logs_tool on query_logs(tool_selected);",
            "lineNumber": 135
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "text": "### Why These Fields?",
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 139
          },
          {
            "text": "**session_id**: Track conversations over time",
            "lineNumber": 140
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: \"User asked about revenue, then net income\" → same session",
            "lineNumber": 141
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 142
          },
          {
            "text": "**user_question**: The raw question",
            "lineNumber": 143
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: \"What's AAPL's revenue trend?\"",
            "lineNumber": 144
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 145
          },
          {
            "text": "**tool_selected**: Which tool the LLM chose",
            "lineNumber": 146
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\"",
            "lineNumber": 147
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Use case:** Measure tool selection accuracy",
            "lineNumber": 148
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 149
          },
          {
            "text": "**tool_args**: Arguments passed to tool",
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "- Example: &#96;{\"metric\": \"revenue\", \"limit\": 5}&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 151
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Use case:** See if LLM chose correct parameters",
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "text": "**data_returned**: What the tool actually returned",
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Option A (full):** Store entire dataset &#96;[{year: 2020, value: 274.5B}, ...]&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 155
          }
        ]
      },

        "contents": "-- Create financial_metrics table for key-value metric storage\n-- This table stores ~96 financial metrics from FMP API for AAPL\n\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS financial_metrics (\n  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  symbol TEXT NOT NULL,\n  year INTEGER NOT NULL,\n  period TEXT, -- 'FY' for annual, 'Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4' for quarterly\n  metric_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  metric_value NUMERIC,\n  metric_category TEXT, -- 'Valuation', 'Profitability', 'Growth', etc.\n  data_source TEXT DEFAULT 'FMP', -- 'FMP', 'Calculated', 'SEC'\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n  -- Composite unique constraint: one value per symbol/year/period/metric\n  CONSTRAINT unique_metric_per_period UNIQUE (symbol, year, period, metric_name)\n);\n\n-- Create indexes for fast queries\nCREATE INDEX idx_financial_metrics_symbol_year ON financial_metrics(symbol, year);\nCREATE INDEX idx_financial_metrics_metric_name ON financial_metrics(metric_name);\nCREATE INDEX idx_financial_metrics_category ON financial_metrics(metric_category);\nCREATE INDEX idx_financial_metrics_symbol_year_metric ON financial_metrics(symbol, year, metric_name);\n\n-- Add RLS (Row Level Security)\nALTER TABLE financial_metrics ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\n\n-- Allow anyone to read financial metrics (public data)\nCREATE POLICY \"Allow public read access to financial metrics\"\n  ON financial_metrics\n  FOR SELECT\n  USING (true);\n\n-- Add comment\nCOMMENT ON TABLE financial_metrics IS 'Key-value storage for 96+ financial metrics from FMP API. Supports annual and quarterly data.';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN financial_metrics.metric_name IS 'Metric identifier (e.g., \"marketCap\", \"peRatio\", \"grossMargin\")';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN financial_metrics.metric_value IS 'Numeric value of the metric';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN financial_metrics.metric_category IS 'Category from stock_metrics_master.csv (e.g., \"Valuation\", \"Profitability &amp; Returns\")';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN financial_metrics.data_source IS 'Data source: FMP API endpoints, calculated from existing data, or SEC filings';",

        "contents": "# Financial Metrics System - Implementation Summary\n\n**Branch:** &#96;feature/add-financial-metrics&#96;\n**Date:** 2025-11-06\n**Status:** ✅ **Phase 1 Complete** (Database + Data Loading)\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 What We Built\n\nAdded **139 financial metrics** from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) API to the Supabase database, expanding beyond the original 9 metrics to include comprehensive valuation, profitability, growth, and leverage ratios.\n\n---\n\n## ✅ Completed\n\n### 1. Database Schema\n\n**Table:** &#96;financial_metrics&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE TABLE financial_metrics (\n  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  symbol TEXT NOT NULL,\n  year INTEGER NOT NULL,\n  period TEXT, -- 'FY', 'Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4'\n  metric_name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  metric_value NUMERIC,\n  metric_category TEXT,\n  data_source TEXT DEFAULT 'FMP',\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n  CONSTRAINT unique_metric_per_period UNIQUE (symbol, year, period, metric_name)\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Indexes:**\n- &#96;idx_financial_metrics_symbol_year&#96; - Fast lookup by company/year\n- &#96;idx_financial_metrics_metric_name&#96; - Fast lookup by metric\n- &#96;idx_financial_metrics_category&#96; - Fast category queries\n- &#96;idx_financial_metrics_symbol_year_metric&#96; - Composite for specific queries\n\n**RLS:** Public read access enabled\n\n---\n\n### 2. Data Coverage\n\n| Metric | Count | Description |\n|--------|-------|-------------|\n| **Total Records** | 2,780 | All metrics across all years |\n| **Unique Metrics** | 139 | Distinct metric types |\n| **Years Covered** | 2006-2025 | 20 years of data |\n| **Symbol** | AAPL | Apple Inc. (MVP) |\n\n---\n\n### 3. Metrics by Category\n\n| Category | Records | Example Metrics |\n|----------|---------|----------------|\n| **Valuation** | 77 | P/E Ratio, P/B Ratio, EV/EBITDA, Market Cap |\n| **Profitability &amp; Returns** | 77 | ROE, ROA, ROIC, Gross Margin, Net Margin |\n| **Growth** | 240 | Revenue Growth, EPS Growth, 3Y/5Y/10Y CAGRs |\n| **Leverage &amp; Solvency** | 67 | Debt-to-Equity, Current Ratio, Quick Ratio |\n| **Efficiency &amp; Working Capital** | 68 | Asset Turnover, Inventory Turnover, Cash Conversion Cycle |\n| **Per-Share Metrics** | 51 | Book Value per Share, FCF per Share, Revenue per Share |",

        "contents": "# Conversation Persistence Implementation Plan\n\n## Overview\nEnable users to have persistent conversations across devices by storing chat history in Supabase, linked to their authenticated user account.\n\n## Goals\n1. Store conversation history in Supabase (not just localStorage)\n2. Enable cross-device access to chat history\n3. Maintain conversation context for follow-up questions\n4. Provide conversation management (list, view, delete, rename)\n5. Preserve existing localStorage behavior for unauthenticated users\n\n---\n\n## Database Schema\n\n### 1. Create &#96;conversations&#96; table\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table public.conversations (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  user_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete cascade not null,\n  title text not null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n  updated_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n\n  constraint conversations_user_id_fkey foreign key (user_id) references auth.users(id)\n);\n\n-- Indexes\ncreate index conversations_user_id_idx on public.conversations(user_id);\ncreate index conversations_updated_at_idx on public.conversations(updated_at desc);\n\n-- RLS Policies\nalter table public.conversations enable row level security;\n\ncreate policy \"Users can view their own conversations\"\n  on public.conversations for select\n  using (auth.uid() = user_id);\n\ncreate policy \"Users can create their own conversations\"\n  on public.conversations for insert\n  with check (auth.uid() = user_id);\n\ncreate policy \"Users can update their own conversations\"\n  on public.conversations for update\n  using (auth.uid() = user_id);\n\ncreate policy \"Users can delete their own conversations\"\n  on public.conversations for delete\n  using (auth.uid() = user_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. Create &#96;messages&#96; table\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table public.messages (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),",

        "contents": "create table public.messages (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  conversation_id uuid not null,\n  role text not null check (role in ('user', 'assistant')),\n  content text not null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n\n  -- Optional metadata for rich message display\n  chart_config jsonb,\n  follow_up_questions text[],\n  data_used jsonb,\n\n  constraint messages_conversation_id_fkey foreign key (conversation_id) references public.conversations(id) on delete cascade\n);\n\n-- Composite index for optimal query performance\n-- Matches the pattern: WHERE conversation_id = ? ORDER BY created_at\ncreate index messages_conversation_id_created_at_idx on public.messages(conversation_id, created_at);\n\n-- Enable Row Level Security\nalter table public.messages enable row level security;\n\n-- RLS Policies (users can only access messages in their own conversations)\ncreate policy \"Users can view messages in their conversations\"\n  on public.messages for select\n  using (\n    exists (\n      select 1 from public.conversations\n      where conversations.id = messages.conversation_id\n      and conversations.user_id = auth.uid()\n    )\n  );\n\ncreate policy \"Users can create messages in their conversations\"\n  on public.messages for insert\n  with check (\n    exists (\n      select 1 from public.conversations\n      where conversations.id = messages.conversation_id\n      and conversations.user_id = auth.uid()\n    )\n  );\n\ncreate policy \"Users can delete messages in their conversations\"\n  on public.messages for delete\n  using (\n    exists (\n      select 1 from public.conversations\n      where conversations.id = messages.conversation_id\n      and conversations.user_id = auth.uid()\n    )\n  );\n\n-- ============================================================================\n-- 3. Create function to auto-generate conversation titles\n-- ============================================================================\n\ncreate or replace function public.generate_conversation_title(conversation_id uuid)\nreturns text\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer",

        "contents": "# Chatbot Technical Overview &amp; Improvement Ideas\n\n## Technical Architecture\n\n### High-Level Flow\n\nThe chatbot uses a **three-step LLM orchestration pattern**:\n\n1. **Tool Selection** → LLM picks which data tool to use\n2. **Tool Execution** → Fetch data from Supabase\n3. **Answer Generation** → LLM generates final answer from facts\n\n### Core Components\n\n#### 1. **Frontend Entry Points**\n- **&#96;app/page.tsx&#96;** - Home page with streaming chatbot (uses &#96;/api/ask&#96; route)\n- **&#96;app/chatbot/page.tsx&#96;** - Dedicated chatbot page (uses &#96;askQuestion&#96; server action)\n\n#### 2. **API Layer**\n- **&#96;app/api/ask/route.ts&#96;** - Streaming API endpoint (Server-Sent Events)\n  - Streams: &#96;flow&#96;, &#96;data&#96;, &#96;answer&#96;, &#96;validation&#96;, &#96;followup&#96;, &#96;complete&#96; events\n  - Real-time progress updates via Flow Visualization\n  - Edge runtime for low latency\n\n#### 3. **Server Actions**\n- **&#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96;** - Main orchestration function\n  - Non-streaming version (used by chatbot page)\n  - Handles tool selection, execution, answer generation\n  - Includes validation and regeneration logic\n\n#### 4. **Tool System** (&#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;)\nAvailable tools:\n- &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96; - Basic financial metrics (revenue, profit, assets, etc.)\n- &#96;getPrices&#96; - Stock price history with custom date ranges\n- &#96;getRecentFilings&#96; - SEC filing metadata (dates, types, URLs)\n- &#96;searchFilings&#96; - Semantic search through filing content\n- &#96;listMetrics&#96; - Browse available metrics catalog\n- &#96;getFinancialMetric&#96; - Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, 139+ metrics)\n\n#### 5. **Data Layer**\n- **Supabase** - PostgreSQL database with:\n  - &#96;financials_std&#96; - Standardized financial statements\n  - &#96;prices&#96; - Historical stock prices\n  - &#96;filings&#96; - SEC filing metadata\n  - &#96;filing_chunks&#96; - Vector embeddings for semantic search\n  - &#96;query_logs&#96; - Analytics and feedback tracking\n  - &#96;conversations&#96; / &#96;messages&#96; - Persistent chat history\n\n#### 6. **LLM Integration**\n- **OpenAI Responses API** (gpt-4o-mini or gpt-5-nano)\n- **Two-stage prompting**:\n  - Tool selection: JSON-structured output (&#96;{\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}&#96;)",

        "contents": "# Authentication Implementation Plan\n\n## Overview\n\nWe're adding user authentication to save query history per user instead of per anonymous session.\n\n---\n\n## Current State\n\n**How it works now:**\n- Anonymous sessions using &#96;localStorage&#96;\n- Each browser gets a random UUID (&#96;finquote_session_id&#96;)\n- Queries saved to &#96;query_logs&#96; table with &#96;session_id&#96;\n- **Problem:** History lost when clearing browser data or switching devices\n\n**Current schema:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nquery_logs (\n  id UUID,\n  session_id TEXT,  -- anonymous UUID from localStorage\n  question TEXT,\n  answer TEXT,\n  tool_used TEXT,\n  created_at TIMESTAMP\n)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Target State\n\n**How it will work:**\n- Users sign up/login with email + password (or OAuth)\n- Each user gets a unique &#96;user_id&#96; from Supabase Auth\n- Queries saved with &#96;user_id&#96; instead of &#96;session_id&#96;\n- **Benefit:** History persists across devices and browser clears\n\n**New schema:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nquery_logs (\n  id UUID,\n  user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id),  -- authenticated user\n  session_id TEXT,  -- keep for backward compatibility\n  question TEXT,\n  answer TEXT,\n  tool_used TEXT,\n  created_at TIMESTAMP\n)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Decisions\n\n### Where to Store User Data?\n\n**✅ Recommended: Supabase Auth**\n\n**Pros:**\n- Already using Supabase for everything\n- Built-in auth system (no extra service)\n- Free tier: 50,000 monthly active users\n- Handles password hashing, email verification, password reset\n- Works with RLS (Row Level Security) policies\n- OAuth providers (Google, GitHub, etc.) built-in\n\n**Cons:**\n- None for this use case\n\n**❌ Not Recommended: Firebase Auth**\n\n**Pros:**\n- You mentioned Firebase earlier\n- Good auth system\n\n**Cons:**\n- Adds second backend service (complexity)\n- Need to sync user_id between Firebase and Supabase\n- Extra cost\n- More moving parts\n\n### Where to Store Query History?\n\n**✅ Keep in Supabase &#96;query_logs&#96; table**\n\nJust add a &#96;user_id&#96; column to link queries to authenticated users.\n\n---\n\n## Implementation Steps\n\n### Phase 1: Database Setup (10 min)",

        "contents": "# Query Logging Implementation Plan\n\n## Overview\n\nTrack every user question and AI response to measure accuracy, improve prompts, and understand user behavior. All data stored in Supabase (our existing database).\n\n---\n\n## Why Log Queries?\n\n### 1. **Measure Accuracy**\n- Did the LLM select the correct tool?\n- Was the answer factually grounded in the data?\n- Are users getting value from responses?\n\n### 2. **Improve Over Time**\n- Identify which questions fail\n- Test new prompts and measure improvement\n- Find patterns in user needs\n\n### 3. **Debug Issues**\n- When user reports \"wrong answer,\" we have evidence\n- Can reproduce bugs\n- See exact data that was used\n\n### 4. **Product Direction**\n- Know which features users actually want\n- Prioritize new tools based on demand\n- Understand typical use cases\n\n---\n\n## Supabase vs Analytics Services\n\n### What's the Difference?\n\n**Supabase (Database Logging):**\n- **What it is:** Storing raw data in a database table\n- **Best for:** Detailed records, debugging, custom analysis, full data ownership\n- **Data storage:** You own and control all data\n- **Querying:** Write SQL to analyze anything\n- **Cost:** Free (within Supabase limits), then ~$25/month for 8GB\n- **Retention:** Keep data forever (or delete when you want)\n- **Privacy:** Full control over what you store\n\n**PostHog/Mixpanel (Analytics Services):**\n- **What it is:** Pre-built analytics platform with dashboards\n- **Best for:** User behavior tracking, funnels, cohort analysis, visualization\n- **Data storage:** They host your data (you don't own the database)\n- **Querying:** Use their UI/API, limited customization\n- **Cost:** Free tier exists, but $200-500+/month at scale\n- **Retention:** Usually 1 year max on free/cheap plans\n- **Privacy:** They process your data (more compliance concerns)\n\n### Analogy\n\n**Supabase = Your own filing cabinet**\n- You write down everything in notebooks\n- You can look up anything anytime\n- Totally customizable\n- More work to analyze\n\n**PostHog = Hiring an analyst**\n- They track everything automatically\n- Give you pretty charts and insights",

Set up RLS (Row Level Security) policies\n\n**Firebase Structure (Sunday):**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n/users/{uid}/data/watchlist\n{\n  tabs: [\n    {\n      name: string,\n      items: [\n        { type: 'stock', symbol: string, tvSymbol?: string, exchange?: string, companyName?: string, isADR?: boolean } |\n        { type: 'header', text: string }\n      ]\n    }\n  ],\n  activeTabIndex: number,\n  updatedAt: timestamp\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Supabase Schema (Fin Quote):**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Watchlist tabs table\nCREATE TABLE watchlist_tabs (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n  user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  name TEXT NOT NULL,\n  position INTEGER NOT NULL,\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Watchlist items table\nCREATE TABLE watchlist_items (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuid_generate_v4(),\n  tab_id UUID REFERENCES watchlist_tabs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('stock', 'header')),\n  position INTEGER NOT NULL,\n\n  -- Stock fields (nullable)\n  symbol TEXT,\n  tv_symbol TEXT,\n  exchange TEXT,\n  company_name TEXT,\n  is_adr BOOLEAN,\n\n  -- Header fields (nullable)\n  header_text TEXT,\n\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n  -- Validation\n  CONSTRAINT valid_stock CHECK (\n    (type = 'stock' AND symbol IS NOT NULL) OR\n    (type = 'header' AND header_text IS NOT NULL)\n  )\n);\n\n-- User settings table\nCREATE TABLE watchlist_settings (\n  user_id UUID PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n  active_tab_id UUID REFERENCES watchlist_tabs(id),\n  show_extended_hours BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW(),\n  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n\n-- Indices\nCREATE INDEX idx_watchlist_tabs_user_id ON watchlist_tabs(user_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_watchlist_tabs_position ON watchlist_tabs(user_id, position);\nCREATE INDEX idx_watchlist_items_tab_id ON watchlist_items(tab_id);\nCREATE INDEX idx_watchlist_items_position ON watchlist_items(tab_id, position);\n\n-- RLS Policies\nALTER TABLE watchlist_tabs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\nALTER TABLE watchlist_items ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;",

        "contents": "### 2. Create &#96;messages&#96; table\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate table public.messages (\n  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),\n  conversation_id uuid references public.conversations(id) on delete cascade not null,\n  role text not null check (role in ('user', 'assistant')),\n  content text not null,\n  created_at timestamptz default now() not null,\n\n  -- Optional: store metadata about the message\n  chart_config jsonb,\n  follow_up_questions text[],\n  data_used jsonb,\n\n  constraint messages_conversation_id_fkey foreign key (conversation_id) references public.conversations(id)\n);\n\n-- Indexes (composite index for optimal query performance)\ncreate index messages_conversation_id_created_at_idx on public.messages(conversation_id, created_at);\n\n-- RLS Policies\nalter table public.messages enable row level security;\n\ncreate policy \"Users can view messages in their conversations\"\n  on public.messages for select\n  using (\n    exists (\n      select 1 from public.conversations\n      where conversations.id = messages.conversation_id\n      and conversations.user_id = auth.uid()\n    )\n  );\n\ncreate policy \"Users can create messages in their conversations\"\n  on public.messages for insert\n  with check (\n    exists (\n      select 1 from public.conversations\n      where conversations.id = messages.conversation_id\n      and conversations.user_id = auth.uid()\n    )\n  );\n\ncreate policy \"Users can delete messages in their conversations\"\n  on public.messages for delete\n  using (\n    exists (\n      select 1 from public.conversations\n      where conversations.id = messages.conversation_id\n      and conversations.user_id = auth.uid()\n    )\n  );\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Create function to auto-generate conversation titles\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\ncreate or replace function public.generate_conversation_title(conversation_id uuid)\nreturns text\nlanguage plpgsql\nsecurity definer\nset search_path = public  -- Prevent search path hijacking\nas $$\ndeclare\n  first_message text;\n  title_text text;\nbegin\n  -- Get first user message\n  select content into first_message",

        "contents": "- This is our main metric - we want 85%+\n\n### Database Integration\n\nEvery prompt version is stored in Supabase:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE TABLE prompt_versions (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,\n  prompt_type TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'tool_selection' or 'answer_generation'\n  version_number INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- 1, 2, 3, 4, etc.\n  prompt_content TEXT NOT NULL,        -- The actual prompt\n  change_description TEXT,             -- What changed\n  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,     -- Currently used in production?\n  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis lets us:\n- Track every change we make\n- Compare versions side-by-side\n- Roll back if a new version performs worse\n- A/B test different prompts\n\n---\n\n## Prompt Version History\n\n### Version 1 (Baseline) - 46% Accuracy\n\n**When:** Initial production prompt\n**Results:** 46% overall, 76% tool selection, 43% args selection\n\n#### What It Looked Like\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nYou are a router. Choose exactly one tool.\n\nAvailable Tools:\n\n1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Use for questions about financial NUMBERS\n   Metrics: revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income,\n           total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity,\n           operating_cash_flow, eps\n   args: {\"metric\": &lt;one of above&gt;, \"limit\": 1-10}\n\n2. getPrices - Use for stock PRICE questions\n   args: {\"range\": \"7d\" | \"30d\" | \"90d\"}\n\n3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings\n   args: {\"limit\": 1-10}\n\n4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content\n   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 1-10}\n\nUser question: \"{question}\"\n\nReturn JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Major Problems\n\n1. **No metric mapping**: User asks \"What's the P/E ratio?\" → AI doesn't know that maps to &#96;eps&#96;\n2. **Vague limit rules**: \"Show me revenue\" → AI guesses limit randomly (sometimes 1, 5, or 10)\n3. **Ambiguous range defaults**: \"What's the price?\" → AI doesn't know if that means 7d, 30d, or 90d\n4. **No examples**: AI has to guess the right pattern\n\n**Real failure example:**\n- Question: \"What's the P/E ratio?\"\n- Expected: &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96; with &#96;metric: \"eps\"&#96;\n- Actual: &#96;searchFilings&#96; with &#96;query: \"P/E ratio\"&#96; ❌",

        "contents": "CREATE TABLE financial_metrics (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,\n  symbol TEXT,\n  year INTEGER,\n  metric_name TEXT,  -- Canonical name (e.g., 'peRatio')\n  metric_value NUMERIC,\n  metric_category TEXT,  -- Category grouping\n  data_source TEXT,\n  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Planned Table: metric_resolutions (Telemetry)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE TABLE metric_resolutions (\n  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n  user_phrase TEXT NOT NULL,\n  resolved_to TEXT,  -- NULL if failed\n  resolution_method TEXT,  -- 'canonical' | 'alias' | 'fuzzy' | NULL\n  fuzzy_match_score NUMERIC,\n  fuzzy_match_suggestion TEXT,\n  user_question TEXT,\n  timestamp TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Data Flow\n\n### Example: User asks \"What's Apple's P/E ratio?\"\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;mermaid\nUser Question\n    ↓\nTool Selection (LLM)\n    ↓\n{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\"],\"limit\":5}}\n    ↓\nMetric Resolver\n    ↓\n\"P/E\" → \"peRatio\" (via alias map)\n    ↓\nDatabase Query\n    ↓\nSELECT * FROM financial_metrics WHERE metric_name = 'peRatio'\n    ↓\nAnswer Generation (LLM)\n    ↓\n\"Apple's P/E ratio is currently 34.09 (2025). Over the past 5 years...\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Benefits\n\n### 1. Discoverability\n- LLM can explore metrics without guessing names\n- Users can ask \"What metrics do you have?\" and get real answers\n- Clear organization by category\n\n### 2. Reliability\n- Alias map handles common phrases (\"P/E\" → peRatio)\n- Fuzzy matching handles typos\n- Clear error messages when metric not found\n\n### 3. Efficiency\n- Multi-metric support reduces round-trips\n- Single database query for multiple metrics\n- Lower token costs (one tool call vs many)\n\n### 4. Maintainability\n- Adding metrics = update catalog + aliases (no prompt changes)\n- Centralized resolver logic\n- Easy to test\n\n### 5. Scalability\n- Designed to scale to 200+ metrics\n- No architectural changes needed\n- Can add semantic search over metric descriptions later\n\n---\n\n## Future Enhancements\n\n### Short Term\n1. **Complete Metadata Coverage**\n   - Add metadata for remaining 89 metrics (139 total - 50 current = 89)",
