          {
            "text": "// Static instructions that will be cached by OpenAI",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "const TOOL_SELECTION_STATIC_PROMPT = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "Available Tools:",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Financial metrics as NUMBERS over time",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "   SUPPORTED METRICS:",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "   Raw Metrics:",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "   - revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "   - total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operating_cash_flow, eps",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "   Calculated Metrics (✨ Native Support):",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debt_to_equity_ratio  (total_liabilities / shareholders_equity)",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   - gross_margin          (gross_profit / revenue × 100)",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   - roe                   (net_income / shareholders_equity × 100)",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC MAPPING (with context clues):",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "   Income/Profitability:",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\", \"profitability\" → net_income",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\" → eps",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"operating profit\", \"EBIT\" → operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "   Valuation Ratios (use getFinancialMetric tool):",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/E ratio\", \"PE ratio\", \"price to earnings\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/E\"]",
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/B ratio\", \"price to book\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/B\"]",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"PEG ratio\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"PEG\"]",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "text": "   Calculated Ratios (✨ NOW NATIVE - use directly):",
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"gross margin\", \"gross profit margin\" → gross_margin",
            "lineNumber": 100
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"ROE\", \"return on equity\" → roe",
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"debt to equity\", \"debt-to-equity\", \"D/E ratio\", \"leverage ratio\" → debt_to_equity_ratio",
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "text": "   Balance Sheet (Raw):",
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"assets\", \"total assets\" → total_assets",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"liabilities\", \"total debt\", \"debt\" → total_liabilities",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"equity\", \"book value\", \"shareholders equity\" → shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 107
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 108
          },
          {
            "text": "   Cash Flow:",
            "lineNumber": 109
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"operating cash flow\", \"cash from operations\", \"OCF\" → operating_cash_flow",
            "lineNumber": 110
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\", \"unlevered free cash flow\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool",
            "lineNumber": 111
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"capex\", \"capital expenditures\", \"buybacks\", \"dividends paid\", \"stock-based compensation\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool",
            "lineNumber": 112
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 113
          },
          {
            "text": "   Research &amp; Development:",
            "lineNumber": 114
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research and development\", \"R&amp;D spending\", \"R&amp;D expense\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"R&amp;D to revenue\"] or [\"research and development\"]",
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 116
          },
          {
            "text": "   Other (use closest available):",
            "lineNumber": 117
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"margins\", \"ratios\" (when not specific) → operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 118
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 119
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES - CRITICAL:",
            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 121
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. If question asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (2020, 2019, 2015, 2006, etc.) → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "      Why: We have 20 years (2006-2025). To find any specific year, fetch all.",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "text": "      Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"net income in 2020\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"revenue for 2018\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"What was EPS in 2006?\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 127
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If question asks for a YEAR RANGE (2008 to 2020, 2015 to present, etc.) → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 129
          },
          {
            "text": "      Why: Need all data to filter to the specific range.",
            "lineNumber": 130
          },
          {
            "text": "      Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 131
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"net income 2008 to present\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"revenue from 2015 to 2020\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 133
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"EPS between 2010 and 2018\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 134
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 135
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. If question specifies a NUMBER of years, use that EXACT number:",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last 3 years\" → limit: 3",
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"past 5 years\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last year\" or \"most recent year\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 139
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"10 years\" → limit: 10",
            "lineNumber": 140
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"20 years\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 141
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"2 years\" → limit: 2",
            "lineNumber": 142
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 143
          },
          {
            "text": "   4. If question says \"trend\", \"history\", \"over time\" WITHOUT a number → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 144
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 145
          },
          {
            "text": "   5. If question says \"all\", \"complete\", \"full history\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 146
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 147
          },
          {
            "text": "   6. If question is just asking for the metric (no time context) → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 148
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 149
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"net income in 2006\" → limit: 20 (specific year)",
            "lineNumber": 151
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"revenue over 5 years\" → limit: 5 (number specified)",
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"show me net income trend\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"EPS history\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"gross profit\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 155
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"all historical data\" → limit: 20 (all data)",
            "lineNumber": 156
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"metric\": &lt;exact name&gt;, \"limit\": &lt;number 1-20&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 159
          },
          {
            "text": "2. getPrices - Stock PRICE history",
            "lineNumber": 160
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 161
          },
          {
            "text": "   ALWAYS use custom date ranges. Calculate the \"from\" date based on the user's request.",
            "lineNumber": 162
          },
          {
            "text": "   Today's date is {{TODAY_DATE}} (use this for calculations).",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "   Date format: YYYY-MM-DD",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "text": "   \"to\" is optional (defaults to today)",
            "lineNumber": 166
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 167
          },
          {
            "text": "   CALCULATION EXAMPLES:",
            "lineNumber": 168
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 7 days\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-11-01\"} (7 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 169
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past month\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-10-08\"} (30 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 170
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 3 months\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-08-08\"} (90 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 171
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past year\" → args: {\"from\": \"2024-11-08\"} (365 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 172
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"YTD\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-01-01\"} (start of current year)",
            "lineNumber": 173
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 3 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2022-11-08\"} (3 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 174
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past 5 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-11-08\"} (5 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 175
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 7 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-11-08\"} (7 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 176
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past 10 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-11-08\"} (10 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 177
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 15 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2010-11-08\"} (15 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 178
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past 20 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 179
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"all time\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago, max available)",
            "lineNumber": 180
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 181
          },
          {
            "text": "   EXACT DATE RANGES:",
            "lineNumber": 182
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"from Jan 2020 to June 2023\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-01-01\", \"to\": \"2023-06-30\"}",
            "lineNumber": 183
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"prices between 2015 and 2020\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-01-01\", \"to\": \"2020-12-31\"}",
            "lineNumber": 184
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"from March 2018 to now\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-03-01\"}",
            "lineNumber": 185
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 186
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"from\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\", \"to\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\"}  (to is optional)",
            "lineNumber": 187
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "text": "3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings metadata ONLY",
            "lineNumber": 189
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This tool returns ONLY metadata (filing type, date, URL).",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "   It does NOT return filing CONTENT or text.",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use ONLY when:",
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHEN filings were submitted",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHICH filings exist",
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants filing dates/types/URLs",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "   DO NOT USE when:",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks WHAT the filing says",
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants content, quotes, or information FROM the filing",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks about topics like risks, strategy, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": "   → Use searchFilings instead for content questions!",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. If question specifies NUMBER of filings → use that number",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last 3 filings\" → limit: 3",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"2 years of filings\" → limit: 10 (2 years ≈ 8-10 filings)",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If question says \"recent\", \"latest\" (no number) → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 213
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. If question says \"all\", \"available\", \"history\" → limit: 10",
            "lineNumber": 214
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 215
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples (metadata questions):",
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"when was the most recent filing?\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"what filings do you have?\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"show me filing dates\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"limit\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content (for WHAT they say)",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Use this when user asks about CONTENT, not just dates!",
            "lineNumber": 225
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 226
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use for ANY question about WHAT the filings say:",
            "lineNumber": 227
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Risk factors, strategy, operations, business model",
            "lineNumber": 228
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Management commentary, outlook, quotes",
            "lineNumber": 229
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Products, markets, competition",
            "lineNumber": 230
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Governance, compensation",
            "lineNumber": 231
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ANY question asking \"what did they say\", \"provide quotes\", etc.",
            "lineNumber": 232
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 233
          },
          {
            "text": "   Even if they mention \"latest 10-K\" or specific filing:",
            "lineNumber": 234
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 235
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about AI?\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 236
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes from recent filing\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 237
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 238
          },
          {
            "text": "   QUERY RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 239
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Extract key terms from user's question",
            "lineNumber": 240
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Keep it simple (1-3 words usually best)",
            "lineNumber": 241
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Don't need full sentences",
            "lineNumber": 242
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 243
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are the risk factors?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 245
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What about risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 246
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Tell me about competition\" → {\"query\": \"competition\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 247
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes about AI strategy\" → {\"query\": \"AI strategy\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 248
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone?\" → {\"query\": \"iPhone\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 249
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 250
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 251
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 252
          },
          {
            "text": "5. listMetrics - DISCOVER available financial metrics",
            "lineNumber": 253
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 254
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use when:",
            "lineNumber": 255
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks \"what metrics do you have?\"",
            "lineNumber": 256
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to browse metrics by category",
            "lineNumber": 257
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Uncertain which metric name to use for getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 259
          },
          {
            "text": "   CATEGORY FILTER (optional):",
            "lineNumber": 260
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Valuation: P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, market cap, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 261
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Profitability &amp; Returns: ROE, ROA, ROIC, margins",
            "lineNumber": 262
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Growth: revenue growth, EPS growth, asset growth",
            "lineNumber": 263
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Leverage &amp; Solvency: debt ratios, liquidity ratios",
            "lineNumber": 264
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Efficiency &amp; Working Capital: turnover ratios, cycle days",
            "lineNumber": 265
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Capital Returns &amp; Share Data: dividend yield, payout ratio",
            "lineNumber": 266
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Per-Share Metrics: EPS, book value per share, cash per share",
            "lineNumber": 267
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Market Data: stock metrics, valuation metrics",
            "lineNumber": 268
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Other: miscellaneous metrics",
            "lineNumber": 269
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 271
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What valuation metrics do you have?\" → {\"category\": \"Valuation\"}",
            "lineNumber": 272
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me all metrics\" → {} (no category)",
            "lineNumber": 273
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What debt metrics are available?\" → {\"category\": \"Leverage &amp; Solvency\"}",
            "lineNumber": 274
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 275

          {

          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC NAME FLEXIBILITY:",
            "lineNumber": 343
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Accepts canonical names: \"peRatio\", \"returnOnEquity\", \"debtEquityRatio\"",
            "lineNumber": 344
          },

            "text": "   - Accepts common aliases: \"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"",

            "lineNumber": 346
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 347
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES (same as getAaplFinancialsByMetric):",
            "lineNumber": 348
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Specific year → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 349
          },

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"compare\" with multiple metrics → limit: 10 (show more history for comparisons)",

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 353
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 354
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's Apple's P/E ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\"], \"limit\": 5}",

          },

          },
          {
            "text": "TOOL SELECTION LOGIC:",
            "lineNumber": 368
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 369
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Basic financial metrics (revenue, assets, eps, etc.)? → getAaplFinancialsByMetric",
            "lineNumber": 370
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, etc.)? → getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 371
          },
          {
            "text": "3. User asks \"what metrics available\"? → listMetrics",
            "lineNumber": 372
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Stock price? → getPrices",
            "lineNumber": 373
          },
          {
            "text": "5. Filing metadata ONLY (when/which filings)? → getRecentFilings",
            "lineNumber": 374
          },
          {
            "text": "6. Filing CONTENT (what they say, quotes, topics)? → searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 375
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 376
          },
          {
            "text": "⚠️ KEY DISTINCTION for #6 vs #7:",

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 378
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 379
          },
          {

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 382
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 383
          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 393
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 394
          },

          },

            "lineNumber": 397
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 398
          },
          {
            "text": "CRITICAL EXAMPLES - Filing Content vs Metadata:",
            "lineNumber": 399
          },
          {

        "contents": "export async function askQuestion(\n  userQuestion: string,\n  conversationHistory: ConversationHistory = [],\n  sessionId: string = ''\n): Promise&lt;AskQuestionResponse&gt; {\n\n\n    // Step 3: Generate final answer using the fetched facts and conversation history\n    const answerGenerationStart = Date.now()\n    const answerPrompt = buildFinalAnswerPrompt(userQuestion, factsJson, previousToolResults)\n\n    // Debug logging\n    console.log('🔍 DEBUG - Question:', userQuestion)\n    console.log('🔍 DEBUG - Facts JSON LENGTH:', factsJson.length, 'characters')\n    console.log('🔍 DEBUG - Facts JSON PREVIEW:', factsJson.substring(0, 500))\n    console.log('🔍 DEBUG - Facts JSON FULL:', factsJson)\n    console.log('🔍 DEBUG - Prompt (first 800 chars):', answerPrompt.substring(0, 800))\n\n    // Build messages array with conversation history\n    const formattingInstructions = [\n      'You are Fin Quote analyst assistant.',\n      'Use only the provided facts; never guess or pull in outside data.',\n      'Respond in plain text sentences with no Markdown, bullets, bold, italics, tables, or code blocks.',\n      'If the answer covers more than four data points (years, filings, etc.), write at most two sentences: first sentence includes the earliest year/value, latest year/value, and any notable high or low; second sentence describes the overall trend and reminds the user to check the data table below for the full yearly breakdown.',\n      'Keep answers concise and follow user instructions precisely.',\n    ].join(' ')\n\n    const historyLimit = process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? 4 : 10\n    const recentHistory = conversationHistory.slice(-historyLimit)\n\n    const answerMessages: SimpleMessage[] = [\n      { role: 'system', content: formattingInstructions },\n      // Include a limited slice of prior conversation to reduce prompt size\n      ...recentHistory.map(msg =&gt; ({\n        role: msg.role as 'user' | 'assistant',\n        content: msg.content,\n      })),\n      // Add current question with facts\n      {\n        role: 'user',\n        content: answerPrompt,\n      },\n    ]\n\n    const answerInput = toResponseInputMessages(answerMessages)\n\n    const answerResponse = await openai.responses.create\n\n}",

        "contents": "export async function POST(req: NextRequest) {\nconst stream = new \nasync start(controller) {\n\n\n        try {\n          flow.startStep({\n            step: 'tool_selection',\n            group: 'planning',\n            summary: 'Selecting best tool',\n            why: 'Analyzing question and recent history',\n            details: { question },\n          })\n\n          // Step 1: Tool selection (non-streaming)\n          const toolSelectionStart = Date.now()\n\n          // Build messages with caching-friendly structure:\n          // [system: static prompt (cached)] + [conversation history] + [user: question]\n          const baseMessages = buildToolSelectionMessages(question)\n          const selectionMessages: SimpleMessage[] = [\n            baseMessages[0], // system message with static prompt (will be cached by OpenAI)\n            ...conversationHistory.slice(-10).map((msg: any) =&gt; ({\n              role: msg.role as 'user' | 'assistant',\n              content: msg.content,\n            })),\n            baseMessages[1], // user message with just the question\n          ]\n\n          const selectionResponse = await openai.responses.create({\n            model: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-4o-mini',\n            input: toResponseInputMessages(selectionMessages),\n            ...(process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? {} : { temperature: 0 }),\n            max_output_tokens: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? 20000 : 150,\n            ...(process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? { reasoning: { effort: 'minimal' } } : {}),\n            text: { format: { type: 'json_object' } },\n          })\n\n          const selectionContent = extractResponseText(selectionResponse)\n\n\n          if (!selectionContent) {\n            flow.failStep('tool_selection', {\n              summary: 'Tool selection failed',\n              why: 'No content returned from model',\n            })\n            sendEvent('error', { message: 'Failed to select tool' })\n            controller.close()\n            return\n          }\n\n          let toolSelection: { tool: string; args: any }\n          try {\n            toolSelection = JSON.parse(selectionContent.trim())\n      }\n\n}",

        "contents": "const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!\nconst SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!\n\nif (!SUPABASE_URL || !SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY) {\n  console.error('Missing required environment variables:')\n  console.error('- NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL')\n  console.error('- SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY')\n  process.exit(1)\n}\n\nconst supabase = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY)\n\n// Tool Selection Prompt (from lib/tools.ts buildToolSelectionPrompt)\nconst TOOL_SELECTION_PROMPT_V1 = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool from the provided menu and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.\n\nAvailable Tools:\n1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Use for questions about financial NUMBERS from statements\n   - Income Statement: revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income\n   - Balance Sheet: total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity\n   - Cash Flow: operating_cash_flow\n   - Per Share: eps\n   - args: {\"metric\": &lt;one of above&gt;, \"limit\": 1-10}\n\n2. getPrices - Use for questions about stock price, share price, or market price trends\n   - args: {\"range\": \"7d\" | \"30d\" | \"90d\"}\n\n3. getRecentFilings - Use to LIST recent filings (metadata: dates, types, links)\n   - args: {\"limit\": 1-10}\n\n4. searchFilings - Use to answer questions ABOUT filing content (risks, strategy, commentary, business description)\n   - Keywords: \"what risks\", \"what did\", \"describe\", \"explain\", \"strategy\", \"management said\", \"business model\"\n   - args: {\"query\": \"&lt;user question&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}\n\nRules:\n- Ticker is fixed to AAPL (MVP)\n- Choose the tool that best matches the question\n- Use searchFilings for qualitative content questions, getRecentFilings for listing filings\n- IMPORTANT: Look at conversation history to resolve references like \"that\", \"it\", \"same period\", etc.\n- If user says \"What about X?\" and previously asked about metric Y over N years, use same N years for metric X\n- If user asks for different timeframe without mentioning metric, use metric from previous question\n- Return ONLY valid JSON, no explanation\n\nConversation Context Examples:\nPrevious: \"AAPL revenue over 5 years\"\nCurrent: \"What about net income?\" → {\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"net_income\",\"limit\":5}}\n\nPrevious: \"Stock price for 30 days\"\nCurrent: \"What about 90 days?\" → {\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"range\":\"90d\"}}\n\nUser question: \"{{USER_QUESTION}}\"\n\nReturn ONLY JSON. Examples:\nFinancial metrics:\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"revenue\",\"limit\":4}}\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"eps\"}}\n\nStock prices:\n{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"range\":\"30d\"}}\n{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"range\":\"90d\"}}\n\nList filings (when asking for documents/metadata):\n{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":10}}\n\nSearch content (when asking WHAT/HOW/WHY about topics):\n{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"supply chain risks\",\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"competitive position\",\"limit\":5}}&#96;\n\n// Answer Generation Prompt (from lib/tools.ts buildFinalAnswerPrompt)\nconst ANSWER_GENERATION_PROMPT_V1 = &#96;You are an analyst. Answer the user using ONLY the provided facts.\n\nUser question: \"{{USER_QUESTION}}\"\n\nFacts (JSON rows):\n{{FACTS_JSON}}\n\nInstructions:\n- Be concise and clear.\n- FIRST, check if you have all the data requested. If not, START your answer by explaining what data you DO have (e.g., \"I have data for the last 10 years (2015-2024), not 15 years as requested.\").\n- THEN provide your analysis using the available data.\n- If trend is relevant, describe it (e.g., increasing/decreasing/flat).\n- Do not invent numbers or sources.\n- Only say \"I don't know\" if you have ZERO relevant data.&#96;",

        "contents": "const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY })\nconst supabase = createClient(\n  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL,\n  process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY\n)\n\n// Inline prompts from lib/tools.ts (using the updated Phase 0 prompts)\nconst buildToolSelectionPrompt = (userQuestion) =&gt; &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.\n\nAvailable Tools:\n\n1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Financial metrics as NUMBERS over time\n\n   SUPPORTED METRICS:\n   - revenue\n   - gross_profit\n   - net_income\n   - operating_income\n   - total_assets\n   - total_liabilities\n   - shareholders_equity\n   - operating_cash_flow\n   - eps\n\n   METRIC MAPPING (with context clues):\n\n   Income/Profitability:\n   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue\n   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\", \"profitability\" → net_income\n   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\", \"P/E ratio\", \"PE\" → eps\n   - \"operating profit\", \"EBIT\" → operating_income\n   - \"gross profit\", \"gross margin\" → gross_profit\n\n   Balance Sheet:\n   - \"assets\", \"total assets\" → total_assets\n   - \"liabilities\", \"total debt\", \"debt\", \"debt to equity\" → total_liabilities\n   - \"equity\", \"book value\", \"shareholders equity\", \"ROE\", \"return on equity\" → shareholders_equity\n   - \"cash and equivalents\", \"cash on hand\", \"cash position\" (balance sheet) → total_assets\n\n   Cash Flow:\n   - \"cash flow\", \"operating cash\", \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\" → operating_cash_flow\n\n   Other (use closest available):\n   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research\", \"development\", \"capex\", \"buybacks\", \"dividends\", \"margins\", \"ratios\" → operating_income\n\n   LIMIT RULES - CRITICAL:\n\n   1. If question asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (2020, 2019, 2015, etc.) → limit: 10\n      Why: We only have 10 years (2015-2024). To find any specific year, fetch all.\n      Examples:\n      - \"net income in 2020\" → limit: 10\n      - \"revenue for 2018\" → limit: 10\n      - \"What was EPS in 2015?\" → limit: 10\n\n   2. If question specifies a NUMBER of years, use that EXACT number:\n      \"last 3 years\" → limit: 3\n      \"past 5 years\" → limit: 5\n      \"last year\" or \"most recent year\" → limit: 1\n      \"10 years\" → limit: 10\n      \"2 years\" → limit: 2\n\n   3. If question says \"trend\", \"history\", \"over time\" WITHOUT a number → limit: 4\n\n   4. If question says \"all\", \"complete\", \"full history\" → limit: 10\n\n   5. If question is just asking for the metric (no time context) → limit: 4\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"net income in 2020\" → limit: 10 (specific year)\n   - \"revenue over 5 years\" → limit: 5 (number specified)\n   - \"show me net income trend\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"EPS history\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"gross profit\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"all historical data\" → limit: 10 (all data)\n\n   args: {\"metric\": &lt;exact name&gt;, \"limit\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;}\n\n2. getPrices - Stock PRICE history\n\n   SUPPORTED RANGES:\n   - 7d (one week)\n   - 30d (one month)\n   - 90d (one quarter)\n\n   RANGE MAPPING - CRITICAL:\n\n   For 7d (use when):\n   - \"today\", \"current price\", \"now\", \"latest\"\n   - \"this week\", \"past week\", \"5 days\"\n   - \"recent\" or \"recently\" (without other context)\n\n   For 30d (use when):\n   - \"month\", \"30 days\", \"this month\", \"past month\"\n   - \"price\" (ambiguous, default to 30d)\n   - \"how's the stock doing\" (ambiguous, default to 30d)\n\n   For 90d (use when):\n   - \"quarter\", \"Q1\", \"90 days\", \"3 months\"\n   - \"6 months\", \"half year\" (closest available)\n   - \"year\", \"YTD\", \"12 months\", \"annual\" (closest available)\n   - \"long term\", \"historical\"\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"What's the price?\" → 30d (ambiguous defaults to month)\n   - \"How's the stock doing?\" → 30d\n   - \"Price today\" → 7d\n   - \"Show me 1 year performance\" → 90d\n   - \"6 month chart\" → 90d\n\n   args: {\"range\": \"7d\" | \"30d\" | \"90d\"}\n\n3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings metadata\n\n   LIMIT RULES:\n\n   1. If question specifies NUMBER of filings → use that number\n      \"last 3 filings\" → limit: 3\n      \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1\n      \"2 years of filings\" → limit: 10 (2 years ≈ 8-10 filings)\n\n   2. If question says \"recent\", \"latest\" (no number) → limit: 5\n\n   3. If question says \"all\", \"available\", \"history\" → limit: 10\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"recent filings\" → limit: 5\n   - \"last 3 10-Ks\" → limit: 3\n   - \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1\n   - \"all available reports\" → limit: 10\n   - \"filing history\" → limit: 10\n\n   args: {\"limit\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;}\n\n4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content\n\n   Use for qualitative questions about:\n   - Risks, strategy, operations, business model\n   - Management commentary, outlook\n   - Products, markets, competition\n   - Governance, compensation\n\n   QUERY RULES:\n   - Extract key terms from user's question\n   - Keep it simple (1-3 words usually best)\n   - Don't need full sentences\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"What are the risk factors?\" → query: \"risk factors\"\n   - \"Tell me about competition\" → query: \"competition\"\n   - \"Search for AI mentions\" → query: \"AI\"\n\n   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}\n\nTOOL SELECTION LOGIC:\n\n1. Numbers/metrics over time? → getAaplFinancialsByMetric\n2. Stock price? → getPrices\n3. List filings? → getRecentFilings\n4. Qualitative content search? → searchFilings\n\nUser question: \"${userQuestion}\"\n\nReturn ONLY JSON - examples:\n\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"revenue\",\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"eps\",\"limit\":1}}\n{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"range\":\"30d\"}}\n{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":3}}\n{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}",

        "contents": "// Legacy function - kept for backwards compatibility\nexport const buildToolSelectionPrompt = (\n  userQuestion: string,\n  previousToolResults?: Array&lt;{\n    question: string\n    answer: string\n    toolData: { type: string; data: any[] } | null | undefined\n  }&gt;\n) =&gt; {\n  // Get today's date in YYYY-MM-DD format\n  const today = new Date().toISOString().split('T')[0]\n\n  // Replace the placeholder with the actual date\n  const promptWithDate = TOOL_SELECTION_STATIC_PROMPT.replace('{{TODAY_DATE}}', today)\n\n  // Add context about previous tool results if available\n  let previousDataContext = ''\n  if (previousToolResults &amp;&amp; previousToolResults.length &gt; 0) {\n    const validResults = previousToolResults.filter(r =&gt; r.toolData)\n    if (validResults.length &gt; 0) {\n      previousDataContext = &#96;\\n\\nPREVIOUS DATA AVAILABLE (for follow-up questions):\n${validResults.map((result, idx) =&gt; &#96;\nPrevious Question ${idx + 1}: \"${result.question}\"\nData Type: ${result.toolData!.type}\nData Summary: ${result.toolData!.data.length} items returned\n&#96;).join('')}\n\n⚠️ If the current question refers to the previous answer, pick the tool that produced that data so the assistant can cite it correctly.\n&#96;\n    }\n  }\n\n  return &#96;${promptWithDate}${previousDataContext}\n\nUser question: \"${userQuestion}\"&#96;\n}\n\nexport const buildFollowUpQuestionsPrompt = (\n  userQuestion: string,\n  toolUsed: string,\n  answer: string\n)",

        "contents": "# CLAUDE.md\n\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\n\n## Project Overview\n\n**Fin Quote** is a Next.js-based financial data platform with an AI-powered Q&amp;A chatbot that answers natural language questions about Apple (AAPL) stock. The system uses a two-step LLM architecture with tool selection, data execution, answer generation, and validation.\n\n**Core Design Philosophy:**\n- **Safety First**: LLMs cannot execute arbitrary database queries. Instead, they select from a whitelist of pre-built \"tools\" (server actions) with validated inputs.\n- **Server-Side Intelligence**: All LLM calls, database queries, and validation logic run server-side. The browser only handles UI.\n- **Grounded Answers**: The LLM must use only fetched data; no external knowledge or hallucinations allowed.\n- **Validation Pipeline**: All answers are validated against source data for number accuracy, year correctness, and citation validity, with auto-regeneration on failures.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Two-Step LLM Flow\n\nEvery user question follows this pattern (implemented in &#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96;):\n\n1. **Tool Selection** (lines 258-330)\n   - LLM receives question + conversation history + tool menu\n   - Returns JSON: &#96;{\"tool\": \"toolName\", \"args\": {...}}&#96;\n   - Model: Uses &#96;OPENAI_MODEL&#96; (default: &#96;gpt-5-nano&#96;)\n   - Tokens tracked for cost analysis\n\n2. **Tool Execution** (lines 332-575)\n   - Server validates tool + args\n   - Executes corresponding server action\n   - Returns structured data (financials, prices, filings, passages, or metrics)\n\n3. **Answer Generation** (lines 579-650)\n   - LLM receives question + fetched facts + conversation history\n   - Generates grounded answer using only provided data\n   - Plain text output (no Markdown, bullets, or tables)\n   - Context: Last 10 messages (tool selection) or 4 messages (answer generation for gpt-5)\n\n4. **Validation &amp; Auto-Correction** (lines 653-796)\n   - Validates numbers, years, and filing citations",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "# Chatbot Technical Overview &amp; Improvement Ideas\n\n## Technical Architecture\n\n### High-Level Flow\n\nThe chatbot uses a **three-step LLM orchestration pattern**:\n\n1. **Tool Selection** → LLM picks which data tool to use\n2. **Tool Execution** → Fetch data from Supabase\n3. **Answer Generation** → LLM generates final answer from facts\n\n### Core Components\n\n#### 1. **Frontend Entry Points**\n- **&#96;app/page.tsx&#96;** - Home page with streaming chatbot (uses &#96;/api/ask&#96; route)\n- **&#96;app/chatbot/page.tsx&#96;** - Dedicated chatbot page (uses &#96;askQuestion&#96; server action)\n\n#### 2. **API Layer**\n- **&#96;app/api/ask/route.ts&#96;** - Streaming API endpoint (Server-Sent Events)\n  - Streams: &#96;flow&#96;, &#96;data&#96;, &#96;answer&#96;, &#96;validation&#96;, &#96;followup&#96;, &#96;complete&#96; events\n  - Real-time progress updates via Flow Visualization\n  - Edge runtime for low latency\n\n#### 3. **Server Actions**\n- **&#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96;** - Main orchestration function\n  - Non-streaming version (used by chatbot page)\n  - Handles tool selection, execution, answer generation\n  - Includes validation and regeneration logic\n\n#### 4. **Tool System** (&#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;)\nAvailable tools:\n- &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96; - Basic financial metrics (revenue, profit, assets, etc.)\n- &#96;getPrices&#96; - Stock price history with custom date ranges\n- &#96;getRecentFilings&#96; - SEC filing metadata (dates, types, URLs)\n- &#96;searchFilings&#96; - Semantic search through filing content\n- &#96;listMetrics&#96; - Browse available metrics catalog\n- &#96;getFinancialMetric&#96; - Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, 139+ metrics)\n\n#### 5. **Data Layer**\n- **Supabase** - PostgreSQL database with:\n  - &#96;financials_std&#96; - Standardized financial statements\n  - &#96;prices&#96; - Historical stock prices\n  - &#96;filings&#96; - SEC filing metadata\n  - &#96;filing_chunks&#96; - Vector embeddings for semantic search\n  - &#96;query_logs&#96; - Analytics and feedback tracking\n  - &#96;conversations&#96; / &#96;messages&#96; - Persistent chat history\n\n#### 6. **LLM Integration**\n- **OpenAI Responses API** (gpt-4o-mini or gpt-5-nano)\n- **Two-stage prompting**:\n  - Tool selection: JSON-structured output (&#96;{\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}&#96;)",

        "contents": "### How It Works\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nconst tools = [{\n  type: \"function\",\n  function: {\n    name: \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\n    strict: true,  // Enforce schema\n    description: \"Get AAPL financial metrics\",\n    parameters: {\n      type: \"object\",\n      properties: {\n        metric: {\n          type: \"string\",\n          enum: [  // LLM MUST pick from this list\n            \"revenue\",\n            \"gross_profit\",\n            \"net_income\",\n            \"total_liabilities\",\n            // ... only valid metrics\n          ],\n          description: \"The financial metric to retrieve\"\n        },\n        limit: {\n          type: \"number\",\n          minimum: 1,\n          maximum: 20,\n        }\n      },\n      required: [\"metric\"]\n    }\n  }\n}]\n\n// Legacy snippet below uses Chat Completions for illustration only.\n// In Fin Quote, prefer the Responses API.\nconst response = await openai.chat.completions.create({\n  model: \"gpt-4\",\n  messages: [{role: \"user\", content: \"What's the debt to equity ratio?\"}],\n  tools: tools,\n  tool_choice: \"auto\",\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Why We Didn't Emphasize This\n\n1. **Doesn't solve the semantic problem** - still need to map \"debt to equity\" → \"total_liabilities\" somewhere\n2. **You're using Responses API** - different pattern than Chat Completions + tools\n3. **Migration complexity** - would require rewriting your existing tool selection flow\n4. **Still need mapping** - the enum just enforces it more strictly\n\n### When It's Useful\n\n✅ Use structured function calling when:\n- You want the LLM to ONLY select from valid options (strict enforcement)\n- You're using Chat Completions API (note: Fin Quote uses Responses API)\n- You need complex parameter validation (nested objects, specific formats)\n- You want the LLM to call multiple tools in sequence\n\n❌ Not helpful for:\n- Solving semantic mismatches (still need mapping)\n- Responses API workflows (different pattern)\n- Quick fixes (requires more setup)\n\n---\n\n## General Principles for LLM Integration\n\n### 1. Don't Fight the LLM's Nature\n\nLLMs are trained to:\n- Preserve semantic meaning\n- Use natural language",

        "contents": "export async function askQuestion(\n  userQuestion: string,\n  conversationHistory: ConversationHistory = [],\n  sessionId: string = ''\n): Promise&lt;AskQuestionResponse&gt; {\n\n\n    const selectionResponse = await openai.responses.create({\n      model: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL || 'gpt-4o-mini', // Fast and cheap for routing\n      input: selectionInput,\n      ...(process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? {} : { temperature: 0 }),\n      // GPT-5 models need more tokens for reasoning + output (reasoning tokens count against limit)\n      // Set to 20,000 to ensure model has enough room for complex reasoning\n      max_output_tokens: process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? 20000 : 150,\n      ...(process.env.OPENAI_MODEL?.includes('gpt-5') ? { reasoning: { effort: 'minimal' } } : {}),\n      text: { format: { type: 'json_object' } },\n    })\n\n    // Capture token usage\n    toolSelectionPromptTokens = selectionResponse.usage?.input_tokens\n    toolSelectionCompletionTokens = selectionResponse.usage?.output_tokens\n    toolSelectionTotalTokens = selectionResponse.usage?.total_tokens\n\n    console.log('🎯 TOOL SELECTION TOKENS:', {\n      input: toolSelectionPromptTokens,\n      output: toolSelectionCompletionTokens,\n      total: toolSelectionTotalTokens\n    })\n\n    // Extract content from Responses API output\n    let selectionContent: string | undefined = extractResponseText(selectionResponse as any)\n\n    if (!selectionContent) {\n      console.error('Tool selection returned empty response:', selectionResponse)\n      return { answer: '', dataUsed: null, chartConfig: null, error: 'Failed to select tool', queryLogId: null }\n    }\n\n    console.log('🔍 DEBUG - Tool selection content:', selectionContent)\n\n    // Parse the JSON response\n    let toolSelection: { tool: string; args: any }\n    try {\n      toolSelection = JSON.parse(selectionContent.trim())\n    } catch (parseError) {\n      console.error('Failed to parse tool selection:', selectionContent)\n      return {\n        answer: '',\n        dataUsed: null,\n        chartConfig: null,\n        error: 'Failed to parse tool selection',\n        queryLogId: null,\n      }\n    }\n\n    toolSelectionLatencyMs = Date.now() - toolSelectionStart\n}",

        "contents": "# CLAUDE.md\n\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\n\n## Project Overview\n\n**Fin Quote** is a Next.js-based financial Q&amp;A platform that uses LLMs to answer natural language questions about Apple (AAPL) stock data. The system uses a two-step LLM architecture: (1) tool selection and (2) answer generation with validation.\n\n**Core Design Philosophy:**\n- **Safety First**: LLMs cannot execute arbitrary database queries. Instead, they select from a whitelist of pre-built \"tools\" (server actions) with validated inputs.\n- **Server-Side Intelligence**: All LLM calls, database queries, and validation logic run server-side. The browser only handles UI.\n- **Grounded Answers**: The LLM must use only fetched data; no external knowledge or hallucinations allowed.\n- **Validation Pipeline**: All answers are validated against source data for number accuracy, year correctness, and citation validity.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Two-Step LLM Flow\n\nEvery user question follows this pattern:\n\n1. **Tool Selection** (&#96;ask-question.ts:224-313&#96;)\n   - LLM receives question + conversation history + tool menu\n   - Returns JSON: &#96;{\"tool\": \"toolName\", \"args\": {...}}&#96;\n   - Model: Uses &#96;OPENAI_MODEL&#96; (default: &#96;gpt-5-nano&#96;)\n\n2. **Tool Execution** (&#96;ask-question.ts:316-438&#96;)\n   - Server validates tool + args\n   - Executes corresponding server action\n   - Returns structured data (financials, prices, filings, or passages)\n\n3. **Answer Generation** (&#96;ask-question.ts:441-500&#96;)\n   - LLM receives question + fetched facts + conversation history\n   - Generates grounded answer using only provided data\n   - Plain text output (no Markdown)\n\n4. **Validation** (&#96;ask-question.ts:503-658&#96;)\n   - Validates numbers, years, and filing citations\n   - If validation fails with high severity, triggers auto-regeneration\n   - Logs validation results to &#96;query_logs&#96; table\n\n### Available Tools\n\nDefined in &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96; (TOOL_MENU):\n\n1. **getAaplFinancialsByMetric** - Income statement, balance sheet, cash flow metrics\n   - Core metrics: &#96;revenue&#96;, &#96;gross_profit&#96;, &#96;net_income&#96;, &#96;operating_income&#96;, &#96;total_assets&#96;, &#96;total_liabilities&#96;, &#96;shareholders_equity&#96;, &#96;operating_cash_flow&#96;, &#96;eps&#96;",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "# CLAUDE.md",
            "lineNumber": 1
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 2
          },
          {
            "text": "This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.",

          },
          {
            "text": "## Project Overview",
            "lineNumber": 5
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 6
          },
          {
            "text": "**Fin Quote** is a Next.js-based financial Q&amp;A platform that uses LLMs to answer natural language questions about Apple (AAPL) stock data. The system uses a two-step LLM architecture: (1) tool selection and (2) answer generation with validation.",
            "lineNumber": 7
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 8
          },
          {
            "text": "**Core Design Philosophy:**",
            "lineNumber": 9
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Safety First**: LLMs cannot execute arbitrary database queries. Instead, they select from a whitelist of pre-built \"tools\" (server actions) with validated inputs.",
            "lineNumber": 10
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Server-Side Intelligence**: All LLM calls, database queries, and validation logic run server-side. The browser only handles UI.",
            "lineNumber": 11
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Grounded Answers**: The LLM must use only fetched data; no external knowledge or hallucinations allowed.",
            "lineNumber": 12
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Validation Pipeline**: All answers are validated against source data for number accuracy, year correctness, and citation validity.",
            "lineNumber": 13
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 14
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 16
          },
          {
            "text": "## Architecture",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "### Two-Step LLM Flow",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "Every user question follows this pattern:",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "1. **Tool Selection** (&#96;ask-question.ts:224-313&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "   - LLM receives question + conversation history + tool menu",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Returns JSON: &#96;{\"tool\": \"toolName\", \"args\": {...}}&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },

            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "2. **Tool Execution** (&#96;ask-question.ts:316-438&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Server validates tool + args",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Executes corresponding server action",
            "lineNumber": 30

          {
            "text": "   - Returns structured data (financials, prices, filings, or passages)",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "3. **Answer Generation** (&#96;ask-question.ts:441-500&#96;)",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "   - LLM receives question + fetched facts + conversation history",
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Generates grounded answer using only provided data",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Plain text output (no Markdown)",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "text": "4. **Validation** (&#96;ask-question.ts:503-658&#96;)",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - Validates numbers, years, and filing citations",
            "lineNumber": 39

          },

## Why prompts are in `lib/` instead of `app/actions/`

### The key difference

**Server actions** (`app/actions/`):
- Fetch data from database
- Call APIs
- Use secrets
- Do the work

**Prompt builders** (`lib/tools.ts`):
- Build text strings
- Format prompts
- No database, no APIs
- Just text manipulation

---

## Where prompts are used

Prompts are used in multiple places:

```typescript
// 1. Server Action uses it
// app/actions/ask-question.ts
import { buildToolSelectionPrompt } from '@/lib/tools'  // ← Imported from lib/

export async function askQuestion() {
  const prompt = buildToolSelectionPrompt(question)  // ← Uses it
  // ... rest of code
}

// 2. API Route also uses it
// app/api/ask/route.ts
import { buildToolSelectionMessages } from '@/lib/tools'  // ← Same function!

export async function POST() {
  const messages = buildToolSelectionMessages(question)  // ← Uses it too
  // ... rest of code
}
```

If prompts were in `app/actions/`, the API route couldn't easily use them.

---

## Why `lib/` makes sense

### 1. They're reusable helper functions

```typescript
// lib/tools.ts
export function buildToolSelectionPrompt(question: string): string {
  // Just builds a string - no database, no secrets
  return `You are a router. Choose a tool...
  
  User question: "${question}"`
}
```

This is a helper function, not a server action.

### 2. They're used by multiple places

- `app/actions/ask-question.ts` (server action)
- `app/api/ask/route.ts` (API route)
- Potentially other places

If it were in `app/actions/`, you'd have to import from actions into API routes, which is awkward.

### 3. They don't need server-only features

```typescript
// lib/tools.ts - Just builds strings
export function buildFinalAnswerPrompt(question: string, factsJson: string): string {
  return `You are an analyst. Answer using ONLY these facts:
  
  ${factsJson}
  
  Question: "${question}"`
}
```

No database, no secrets, no server-only code. Works anywhere.

### 4. They're pure functions

Same input = same output. No side effects.

```typescript
// Always returns the same thing for same input
buildToolSelectionPrompt("What's revenue?")
// → Same prompt string every time
```

---

## Comparison

### If prompts were in `app/actions/`:

```typescript
// ❌ BAD: In app/actions/prompts.ts
'use server'  // ← But they don't need this!

export function buildToolSelectionPrompt() {
  // This doesn't need 'use server' - it's just string building!
}

// Now API route has to import from actions (weird)
// app/api/ask/route.ts
import { buildToolSelectionPrompt } from '@/app/actions/prompts'  // ← Awkward
```

### Current setup (in `lib/`):

```typescript
// ✅ GOOD: In lib/tools.ts
// No 'use server' needed - it's just a helper function

export function buildToolSelectionPrompt() {
  // Just builds strings
}

// Both can import easily
// app/actions/ask-question.ts
import { buildToolSelectionPrompt } from '@/lib/tools'  // ← Clean

// app/api/ask/route.ts  
import { buildToolSelectionPrompt } from '@/lib/tools'  // ← Also clean
```

---

## What's in `lib/tools.ts`

1. Tool definitions (`TOOL_MENU`) — List of available tools
2. Prompt builders — Functions that build prompt strings:
   - `buildToolSelectionPrompt()` — Builds tool selection prompt
   - `buildFinalAnswerPrompt()` — Builds answer generation prompt
   - `buildFollowUpQuestionsPrompt()` — Builds follow-up questions prompt
3. Static prompt text — The actual prompt templates

---

## Simple rule

- `app/actions/` = Functions that do work (fetch data, call APIs)
- `lib/` = Functions that help (format, calculate, build strings)

Prompts build strings, so they belong in `lib/`.

---

## Summary

Prompts are in `lib/` because:
1. They're helper functions (build strings, don't fetch data)
2. They're used by multiple places (server actions AND API routes)
3. They don't need server-only features (just text manipulation)
4. They're pure functions (same input = same output)

Think of it like:
- `app/actions/` = The workers (do the job)
- `lib/tools.ts` = The instructions (tell workers what to do)

The prompts are the instructions, so they live in `lib/` with other helper functions.

---

_**User**_

it seems like helper functions are the most important part of this code

Create &#96;app/actions/conversations.ts&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n'use server'\n\nimport { createServerComponentClient } from '@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs'\nimport { cookies } from 'next/headers'\nimport type { Database } from '@/lib/database.types'\n\nexport type ConversationWithMessageCount = {\n  id: string\n  title: string\n  created_at: string\n  updated_at: string\n  message_count: number\n}\n\n// Get all conversations for the current user\nexport async function getConversations() {\n  const supabase = createServerComponentClient&lt;Database&gt;({ cookies })\n\n  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\n  if (!user) {\n    return { data: null, error: 'Not authenticated' }\n  }\n\n  const { data, error } = await supabase\n    .from('conversations')\n    .select(&#96;\n      id,\n      title,\n      created_at,\n      updated_at,\n      messages(count)\n    &#96;)\n    .eq('user_id', user.id)\n    .order('updated_at', { ascending: false })\n\n  if (error) {\n    return { data: null, error: error.message }\n  }\n\n  const conversations: ConversationWithMessageCount[] = data.map(conv =&gt; ({\n    id: conv.id,\n    title: conv.title,\n    created_at: conv.created_at,\n    updated_at: conv.updated_at,\n    message_count: conv.messages?.[0]?.count || 0\n  }))\n\n  return { data: conversations, error: null }\n}\n\n// Get a single conversation with all messages\nexport async function getConversation(conversationId: string) {\n  const supabase = createServerComponentClient&lt;Database&gt;({ cookies })",

        "contents": "│   └── supabase/\n│       ├── client.ts           # Client-side Supabase client\n│       └── server.ts           # Server-side Supabase client\n├── .env.local.example          # Example environment variables\n└── package.json\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Features\n\n### Server Actions\n\nThe app uses Next.js Server Actions for data fetching, located in &#96;app/actions/financials.ts&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { getCompaniesWithFinancials } from '@/app/actions/financials'\n\nconst { data, error } = await getCompaniesWithFinancials()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis server action:\n- Fetches all companies with their related financial data\n- Uses Supabase's nested &#96;.select()&#96; syntax to join tables\n- Returns fully typed data using TypeScript\n- Handles errors gracefully\n- Orders companies by name and financials by year (descending)\n\n### Type Safety\n\nAll database types are defined in &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96;, providing:\n- Full TypeScript autocomplete for database queries\n- Type-safe data access throughout the application\n- Helper types like &#96;CompanyWithFinancials&#96; for joined data\n\n### Supabase Client\n\nTwo client configurations are available:\n\n1. **Server Client** (&#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&#96;)\n   - Used in Server Components and Server Actions\n   - Runs on the server only\n   - Safe for sensitive operations\n\n2. **Browser Client** (&#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&#96;)\n   - Used in Client Components\n   - Runs in the browser\n   - Uses the public anon key (safe to expose)\n\n## Usage Example\n\n### Fetching Data in a Server Component\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// app/financials/page.tsx\nimport { getCompaniesWithFinancials } from '@/app/actions/financials'\n\nexport default async function FinancialsPage() {\n  const { data: companies, error } = await getCompaniesWithFinancials()",

        "contents": "/**\n * Save a message to a conversation\n */\nexport async function saveMessage(\n  conversationId: string,\n  role: 'user' | 'assistant',\n  content: string,\n  metadata?: {\n    chart_config?: any\n    follow_up_questions?: string[]\n    data_used?: any\n  }\n): Promise&lt;{ message: Message | null; error: string | null }&gt; {\n  try {\n    console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage called for conversation:', conversationId, 'role:', role)\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    // Get current user\n    const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\n    if (authError || !user) {\n      console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage: Not authenticated')\n      return { message: null, error: 'Not authenticated' }\n    }\n\n    // Verify conversation belongs to user (RLS will also check, but this provides better error message)\n    const { data: conversation, error: convError } = await supabase\n      .from('conversations')\n      .select('id')\n      .eq('id', conversationId)\n      .eq('user_id', user.id)\n      .single()\n\n    if (convError || !conversation) {\n      console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage: Conversation not found or access denied')\n      return { message: null, error: 'Conversation not found or access denied' }\n    }\n\n    const newMessage: NewMessage = {\n      conversation_id: conversationId,\n      role,\n      content,\n      chart_config: metadata?.chart_config || null,\n      follow_up_questions: metadata?.follow_up_questions || null,\n      data_used: metadata?.data_used || null\n    }\n\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n      .from('messages')\n      .insert(newMessage)\n      .select()\n      .single()\n\n    if (error) {\n      console.error('[SERVER] Error saving message:', error)\n      return { message: null, error: error.message }\n    }\n\n    console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage: Successfully saved', role, 'message to conversation', conversationId)\n    return { message: data, error: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('[SERVER] Unexpected error in saveMessage:', err)\n    return { message: null, error: 'An unexpected error occurred' }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Update conversation title\n */\nexport async function updateConversationTitle(\n  conversationId: string,\n  title: string\n): Promise&lt;{ conversation: Conversation | null; error: string | null }&gt; {\n  \n}",

        "contents": "npm run generate:catalog                     # Generate metrics catalog with metadata\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**SEC Filings (RAG Pipeline):**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpx tsx scripts/fetch-sec-filings.ts         # Fetch metadata from SEC EDGAR\nnpx tsx scripts/ingest-filings.ts            # Load metadata into filings table\nnpx tsx scripts/download-filings.ts          # Download HTML files to storage\nnpx tsx scripts/chunk-filings.ts             # Split filings into semantic chunks\nnpx tsx scripts/embed-filings.ts             # Generate embeddings for vector search\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Data Export:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run export                               # Export financial data to Excel\nnpm run export:catalog                       # Export metrics catalog to Excel\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Testing &amp;         "contents": "'use server'\n\nimport { createServerClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'\n\n// Safe, purpose-built tool for fetching recent SEC filings for AAPL only\n// This is designed to be called by server code (e.g., an LLM routing step) and returns\n// a minimal, predictable shape for easy prompting and display.\nexport async function getRecentFilings(params: {\n  ticker?: string // AAPL only for MVP\n  limit?: number // number of most recent filings to fetch\n}): Promise&lt;{\n  data: Array&lt;{\n    filing_type: string\n    filing_date: string\n    period_end_date: string\n    fiscal_year: number\n    fiscal_quarter: number | null\n    document_url: string\n  }&gt; | null\n  error: string | null\n}&gt; {\n  const ticker = params.ticker ?? 'AAPL'\n  const requestedLimit = params.limit ?? 5\n\n  // Enforce AAPL-only for MVP\n  if (ticker !== 'AAPL') {\n    return { data: null, error: 'Only AAPL ticker is supported in MVP' }\n  }\n\n  // Limit rows to a small, safe window (1..10)\n  const safeLimit = Math.min(Math.max(requestedLimit, 1), 10)\n\n  try {\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n      .from('filings')\n      .select('filing_type, filing_date, period_end_date, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, document_url')\n      .eq('ticker', ticker)\n      .order('filing_date', { ascending: false })\n      .limit(safeLimit)\n\n    if (error) {\n      console.error('Error fetching filings:', error)\n      return { data: null, error: error.message }\n    }\n\n    return { data: data ?? [], error: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('Unexpected error (getRecentFilings):', err)\n    return {\n      data: null,\n      error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'An unexpected error occurred',\n    }\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "export async function askQuestion(\n  userQuestion: string,\n  conversationHistory: ConversationHistory = [],\n  sessionId: string = ''\n): Promise&lt;AskQuestionResponse&gt; {\n {\n      // Import at the top if not already imported\n      const { getFinancialMetrics } = await import('./get-financial-metric')\n\n      // Extract metric names (can be array or single string)\n      const metricNames = toolSelection.args.metricNames as string[]\n      const limit = toolSelection.args.limit || 5\n\n      if (!metricNames || metricNames.length === 0) {\n        return {\n          answer: '',\n          dataUsed: null,\n          chartConfig: null,\n          error: 'No metrics specified',\n          queryLogId: null,\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (limit &lt; 1 || limit &gt; 20) {\n        return {\n          answer: '',\n          dataUsed: null,\n          chartConfig: null,\n          error: 'Invalid limit (must be 1-20)',\n          queryLogId: null,\n        }\n      }\n\n      const toolResult = await getFinancialMetrics({\n        symbol: 'AAPL',\n        metricNames,\n        limit,\n      })\n\n      if (toolResult.error || !toolResult.data) {\n        toolError = toolResult.error || 'Failed to fetch financial metrics'\n        return {\n          answer: '',\n          dataUsed: null,\n          chartConfig: null,\n          error: toolError,\n          queryLogId: null,\n        }\n      }\n\n      factsJson = createFactsJson(toolResult.data)\n      dataUsed = { type: 'financial_metrics', data: toolResult.data }\n\n      // Generate chart for extended metrics (single metric queries only)\n      if (toolResult.data &amp;&amp; toolResult.data.length &gt;= 2 &amp;&amp; metricNames.length === 1) {\n        const { generateExtendedMetricChart } = await import('@/lib/chart-helpers')\n        // Use the resolved canonical metric name from the data\n        const canonicalMetricName = toolResult.data[0].metric_name\n        chartConfig = generateExtendedMetricChart(toolResult.data, canonicalMetricName, userQuestion)\n      }\n    } else {\n      return { answer: '', dataUsed: null, chartConfig: null, error: 'Unsupported tool selected', queryLogId: null }\n    }\n\n    toolExecutionLatencyMs = Date.now() - toolExecutionStart\n\n    // Step 3: Generate final answer using the fetched facts and conversation history\n}",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./docs/PROJECT_PLAN.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 16
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 49
          }
        },
        "contents": "- **RAG (Retrieval‑Augmented Generation)**: For document questions (filings/transcripts), retrieve the most relevant passages via a vector store, then answer using those passages. We’ll add this after MVP.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture overview\n\n### Frontend (browser)\n- Next.js app with a simple UI: text box + Ask button + answer display.\n- No secrets in the browser.\n- Uses &#96;createBrowserClient()&#96; only for UI‑safe tasks.\n\n### Backend (server)\n- Next.js server actions/API routes handle all sensitive work.\n- Uses &#96;createServerClient()&#96; to talk to Supabase (read‑only for MVP).\n- Two LLM steps per question:\n  1) Selection: model picks exactly one tool from our small menu and provides JSON args.\n  2) Answering: after we run the tool and get facts, the model writes the final answer using only those facts.\n\n### Data (Supabase)\n- We store standardized financials in &#96;financials_std&#96; and company metadata in &#96;company&#96;.\n- For MVP, we enforce AAPL‑only and small row limits (1–8) at the tool level.\n\n---\n\n## Current code in the repo (important files)\n- &#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&#96;: Creates the browser client (uses &#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_*&#96; env vars; no session persistence). For UI only.\n- &#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&#96;: Creates the server client (same env vars; no session persistence). For server actions and API routes.\n- &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96;: Typed Supabase schema for &#96;company&#96; and &#96;financials_std&#96;.\n- &#96;app/actions/financials.ts&#96;:\n  - &#96;getCompaniesWithFinancials()&#96;: Example server action that composes companies with financials for display.\n  - &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric({ metric, limit })&#96;: SAFE TOOL (MVP). Allowed metrics: &#96;revenue&#96; or &#96;gross_profit&#96;. Limit clamped to 1..8. Always filters to &#96;AAPL&#96;. Returns an array of &#96;{ year, value, metric }&#96;.\n- &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;:\n  - &#96;TOOL_MENU&#96;: Defines the tool(s) the model can choose from.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {
            "text": "- **RAG (Retrieval‑Augmented Generation)**: For document questions (filings/transcripts), retrieve the most relevant passages via a vector store, then answer using those passages. We’ll add this after MVP.",
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 20
          },
          {
            "text": "## Architecture overview",
            "lineNumber": 21
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 22
          },
          {
            "text": "### Frontend (browser)",
            "lineNumber": 23
          },
          {
            "text": "- Next.js app with a simple UI: text box + Ask button + answer display.",
            "lineNumber": 24
          },
          {
            "text": "- No secrets in the browser.",
            "lineNumber": 25
          },
          {
            "text": "- Uses &#96;createBrowserClient()&#96; only for UI‑safe tasks.",
            "lineNumber": 26
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 27
          },
          {
            "text": "### Backend (server)",
            "lineNumber": 28
          },
          {
            "text": "- Next.js server actions/API routes handle all sensitive work.",
            "lineNumber": 29
          },
          {
            "text": "- Uses &#96;createServerClient()&#96; to talk to Supabase (read‑only for MVP).",
            "lineNumber": 30
          },
          {
            "text": "- Two LLM steps per question:",
            "lineNumber": 31
          },
          {
            "text": "  1) Selection: model picks exactly one tool from our small menu and provides JSON args.",
            "lineNumber": 32
          },
          {
            "text": "  2) Answering: after we run the tool and get facts, the model writes the final answer using only those facts.",
            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 34
          },
          {
            "text": "### Data (Supabase)",
            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "- We store standardized financials in &#96;financials_std&#96; and company metadata in &#96;company&#96;.",
            "lineNumber": 36
          },
          {
            "text": "- For MVP, we enforce AAPL‑only and small row limits (1–8) at the tool level.",
            "lineNumber": 37
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 38
          },
          {
