        "contents": "# Chatbot Technical Overview &amp; Improvement Ideas\n\n## Technical Architecture\n\n### High-Level Flow\n\nThe chatbot uses a **three-step LLM orchestration pattern**:\n\n1. **Tool Selection** → LLM picks which data tool to use\n2. **Tool Execution** → Fetch data from Supabase\n3. **Answer Generation** → LLM generates final answer from facts\n\n### Core Components\n\n#### 1. **Frontend Entry Points**\n- **&#96;app/page.tsx&#96;** - Home page with streaming chatbot (uses &#96;/api/ask&#96; route)\n- **&#96;app/chatbot/page.tsx&#96;** - Dedicated chatbot page (uses &#96;askQuestion&#96; server action)\n\n#### 2. **API Layer**\n- **&#96;app/api/ask/route.ts&#96;** - Streaming API endpoint (Server-Sent Events)\n  - Streams: &#96;flow&#96;, &#96;data&#96;, &#96;answer&#96;, &#96;validation&#96;, &#96;followup&#96;, &#96;complete&#96; events\n  - Real-time progress updates via Flow Visualization\n  - Edge runtime for low latency\n\n#### 3. **Server Actions**\n- **&#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96;** - Main orchestration function\n  - Non-streaming version (used by chatbot page)\n  - Handles tool selection, execution, answer generation\n  - Includes validation and regeneration logic\n\n#### 4. **Tool System** (&#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;)\nAvailable tools:\n- &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96; - Basic financial metrics (revenue, profit, assets, etc.)\n- &#96;getPrices&#96; - Stock price history with custom date ranges\n- &#96;getRecentFilings&#96; - SEC filing metadata (dates, types, URLs)\n- &#96;searchFilings&#96; - Semantic search through filing content\n- &#96;listMetrics&#96; - Browse available metrics catalog\n- &#96;getFinancialMetric&#96; - Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, 139+ metrics)\n\n#### 5. **Data Layer**\n- **Supabase** - PostgreSQL database with:\n  - &#96;financials_std&#96; - Standardized financial statements\n  - &#96;prices&#96; - Historical stock prices\n  - &#96;filings&#96; - SEC filing metadata\n  - &#96;filing_chunks&#96; - Vector embeddings for semantic search\n  - &#96;query_logs&#96; - Analytics and feedback tracking\n  - &#96;conversations&#96; / &#96;messages&#96; - Persistent chat history\n\n#### 6. **LLM Integration**\n- **OpenAI Responses API** (gpt-4o-mini or gpt-5-nano)\n- **Two-stage prompting**:\n  - Tool selection: JSON-structured output (&#96;{\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}&#96;)",

        "contents": "import { cookies } from 'next/headers'\nimport { Database } from '@/lib/database.types'\n\n// Server-side Supabase client (for use in Server Actions, API Routes, Server Components)\n// This properly handles auth sessions via cookies\nexport async function createServerClient() {\n  const cookieStore = await cookies()\n\n  return createClient&lt;Database&gt;(\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!,\n    {\n      cookies: {\n        getAll() {\n          return cookieStore.getAll()\n        },\n        setAll(cookiesToSet) {\n          try {\n            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =&gt;\n              cookieStore.set(name, value, options)\n            )\n          } catch {\n            // The &#96;setAll&#96; method was called from a Server Component.\n            // This can be ignored if you have middleware refreshing\n            // user sessions.\n          }\n        },\n      },\n    }\n  )\n}",

        "contents": "'use server'\n\nimport { createServerClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'\nimport { CompanyWithFinancials, Company, Financial } from '@/lib/database.types'\n\nexport async function getCompaniesWithFinancials(): Promise&lt;{\n  data: CompanyWithFinancials[] | null\n  error: string | null\n}&gt; {\n  try {\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    // Fetch all companies\n    const { data: companies, error: companiesError } = await supabase\n      .from('company')\n      .select('*')\n      .order('name', { ascending: true })\n\n    if (companiesError) {\n      console.error('Error fetching companies:', companiesError)\n      return { data: null, error: companiesError.message }\n    }\n\n    if (!companies || companies.length === 0) {\n      return { data: [], error: null }\n    }\n\n    const companyRows: Company[] = companies as Company[]\n\n    // Fetch all financials\n    const { data: financials, error: financialsError } = await supabase\n      .from('financials_std')\n      .select('*')\n      .order('year', { ascending: false })\n\n    if (financialsError) {\n      console.error('Error fetching financials:', financialsError)\n      return { data: null, error: financialsError.message }\n    }\n\n    const financialRows: Financial[] = (financials ?? []) as Financial[]\n\n    // Manually join the data by symbol\n    const companiesWithFinancials: CompanyWithFinancials[] = companyRows.map((company) =&gt; ({\n      ...company,\n      financials_std: financialRows.filter((f) =&gt; f.symbol === company.symbol),\n    }))\n\n    return { data: companiesWithFinancials, error: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('Unexpected error:', err)\n    return {\n      data: null,\n      error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'An unexpected error occurred',\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n// Safe, purpose-built tool for fetching a specific financial metric for AAPL only (v2)",

        "contents": "'use server'\n\nimport { createServerClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'\n\nexport async function addFinancialColumns() {\n  const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n  // SQL to add new columns to financials_std table\n  const sql = &#96;\n    ALTER TABLE financials_std\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS net_income NUMERIC,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS operating_income NUMERIC,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS total_assets NUMERIC,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS total_liabilities NUMERIC,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS shareholders_equity NUMERIC,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS operating_cash_flow NUMERIC,\n    ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS eps NUMERIC;\n  &#96;\n\n  try {\n    const { data, error } = await (supabase as any).rpc('exec_sql', { sql_query: sql })\n\n    if (error) {\n      return {\n        success: false,\n        error: error.message,\n        hint: 'You may need to run this SQL manually in Supabase SQL Editor or create a custom function.'\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { success: true, error: null, hint: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    // If rpc doesn't exist, try direct query (this likely won't work but worth trying)\n    const { error } = await (supabase as any).from('_sql').insert({ query: sql })\n\n    if (error) {\n      return {\n        success: false,\n        error: error.message,\n        hint: 'Direct SQL execution not available. Please use the SQL migration approach.',\n        sqlToRun: sql\n      }\n    }\n\n    return { success: true, error: null, hint: null }\n  }\n}",

        },
        "contents": "/**\n * Get all conversations for the current user, ordered by most recent\n */\nexport async function getConversations(): Promise&lt;{ conversations: Conversation[] | null; error: string | null }&gt; {\n  try {\n    console.log('[SERVER] getConversations called')\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    // Get current user\n    const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\n    if (authError || !user) {\n      console.log('[SERVER] getConversations: Not authenticated')\n      return { conversations: null, error: 'Not authenticated' }\n    }\n\n    console.log('[SERVER] getConversations: Fetching for userId:', user.id)\n\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n      .from('conversations')\n      .select('*')\n      .eq('user_id', user.id)\n      .order('updated_at', { ascending: false })\n\n    if (error) {\n      console.error('[SERVER] Error fetching conversations:', error)\n      return { conversations: null, error: error.message }\n    }\n\n    console.log('[SERVER] getConversations: Returned', data?.length || 0, 'conversations')\n    if (data &amp;&amp; data.length &gt; 0) {\n      console.log('[SERVER] Conversation titles:', data.map(c =&gt; c.title))\n    }\n\n    return { conversations: data, error: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('[SERVER] Unexpected error in getConversations:', err)\n    return { conversations: null, error: 'An unexpected error occurred' }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Get a single conversation with all its messages\n */\nexport async function getConversation(\n  conversationId: string\n): Promise&lt;{ conversation: ConversationWithMessages | null; error: string | null }&gt; {\n  \n}",

error: string | null }&gt; {\n  try {\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    // Get current user\n    const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\n    if (authError || !user) {\n      return { title: null, error: 'Not authenticated' }\n    }\n\n    // Verify conversation belongs to user\n    const { data: conversation, error: convError } = await supabase\n      .from('conversations')\n      .select('id')\n      .eq('id', conversationId)\n      .eq('user_id', user.id)\n      .single()\n\n    if (convError || !conversation) {\n      return { title: null, error: 'Conversation not found or access denied' }\n    }\n\n    // Call the PostgreSQL function to generate title\n    const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('generate_conversation_title', {\n      conversation_id: conversationId\n    })\n\n    if (error) {\n      console.error('Error generating title:', error)\n      return { title: null, error: error.message }\n    }\n\n    // Update the conversation with the generated title\n    const { error: updateError } = await supabase\n      .from('conversations')\n      .update({ title: data })\n      .eq('id', conversationId)\n      .eq('user_id', user.id)\n\n    if (updateError) {\n      console.error('Error updating conversation with generated title:', updateError)\n      return { title: null, error: updateError.message }\n    }\n\n    return { title: data, error: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('Unexpected error in autoGenerateTitle:', err)\n    return { title: null, error: 'An unexpected error occurred' }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Migrate a conversation from localStorage to the database\n * This is a one-time operation to preserve existing conversations\n */",

---


Helper functions contain the core logic. Here's why:

## The architecture pattern

### Server actions = coordinators
### Helper functions = the actual work

Looking at your main chatbot function:

```typescript
// app/actions/ask-question.ts
export async function askQuestion() {
  // 1. Build prompt (helper function does this)
  const prompt = buildToolSelectionPrompt(question)  // ← lib/tools.ts
  
  // 2. Fetch data (server action does this)
  const data = await getAaplFinancialsByMetric()     // ← app/actions/financials.ts
  
  // 3. Generate chart (helper function does this)
  const chart = generateFinancialChart(data)         // ← lib/chart-helpers.ts
  
  // 4. Generate answer (helper function builds prompt)
  const answerPrompt = buildFinalAnswerPrompt(question, data)  // ← lib/tools.ts
  
  // 5. Validate answer (helper function does this)
  const validation = validateAnswer(answer, data)      // ← lib/validators.ts
  
  // 6. Regenerate if needed (helper function decides)
  if (shouldRegenerateAnswer(validation)) {          // ← lib/regeneration.ts
    const regenPrompt = buildRegenerationPrompt(...)  // ← lib/regeneration.ts
  }
}
```

The server action coordinates; the helpers do the work.

---

## Why helper functions are central

### 1. They contain the business logic

```typescript
// lib/validators.ts - THE LOGIC for checking if answers are correct
export function validateNumbers(answer: string, data: any[]): ValidationResult {
  // 200+ lines of logic to check if numbers match
  // This is the CORE functionality
}

// app/actions/ask-question.ts - Just calls it
const validation = validateAnswer(answer, data)  // Helper does the work
```

### 2. They're reusable

```typescript
// lib/chart-helpers.ts
export function generateFinancialChart(data) { ... }

// Used in:
// - app/actions/ask-question.ts
// - app/api/ask/route.ts
// - Potentially other places
```

If this logic were in a server action, you'd duplicate it.

### 3. They're testable

```typescript
// Easy to test helper functions
test('formatFinancialValue formats correctly', () => {
  expect(formatFinancialValue(383285000000)).toBe(383.3)
})

// Harder to test server actions (need database, API keys, etc.)
```

### 4. They contain the prompts

```typescript
// lib/tools.ts - Contains THE PROMPTS that control the AI
export function buildFinalAnswerPrompt(question, factsJson) {
  return `You are an analyst. Answer using ONLY the provided facts.
  
  ${factsJson}
  
  CRITICAL RULES:
  1. Use EXACT numbers...
  2. Format as $383.3B...
  ...`
}
```

The prompts define what the AI does.

---

## The dependency chain

```
User asks question
    ↓
app/actions/ask-question.ts (orchestrator)
    ↓
lib/tools.ts → buildToolSelectionPrompt() (THE PROMPT)
    ↓
AI picks tool
    ↓
app/actions/financials.ts → getAaplFinancialsByMetric() (fetches data)
    ↓
lib/chart-helpers.ts → generateFinancialChart() (creates chart)
    ↓
lib/tools.ts → buildFinalAnswerPrompt() (THE PROMPT)
    ↓
AI generates answer
    ↓
lib/validators.ts → validateAnswer() (checks if correct)
    ↓
lib/regeneration.ts → shouldRegenerateAnswer() (decides if fix needed)
    ↓
lib/regeneration.ts → buildRegenerationPrompt() (THE FIX PROMPT)
    ↓
Final answer
```

Most of the logic is in `lib/`.

---

## What each part does

### Server actions (`app/actions/`)
- Fetch data from database
- Call external APIs
- Coordinate the flow
- Like a manager: delegates work

### Helper functions (`lib/`)
- Build prompts (control the AI)
- Validate answers (quality control)
- Generate charts (visualization)
- Format data (presentation)
- Business logic (the rules)
- Like the workers: do the actual work

---

## Why this architecture is good

### 1. Separation of concerns

```typescript
// Server action: "Get the data"
export async function getAaplFinancialsByMetric() {
  const supabase = await createServerClient()
  return await supabase.from('financials_std').select('*')
}

// Helper function: "Format the data"
export function formatFinancialValue(value: number) {
  return `$${(value / 1_000_000_000).toFixed(1)}B`
}
```

Each does one job.

### 2. Easy to test

```typescript
// Test helper function (easy - no database needed)
test('formatFinancialValue', () => {
  expect(formatFinancialValue(383285000000)).toBe("$383.3B")
})

// Test server action (harder - needs database)
test('getAaplFinancialsByMetric', async () => {
  // Need to mock database, set up test data, etc.
})
```

### 3. Easy to change

```typescript
// Want to change how prompts work?
// Just edit lib/tools.ts

// Want to change validation rules?
// Just edit lib/validators.ts

// Server actions don't need to change!
```

### 4. Reusable

```typescript
// Same helper used everywhere
import { formatFinancialValue } from '@/lib/chart-helpers'

// In charts
const formatted = formatFinancialValue(data.value)

// In answers
const formatted = formatFinancialValue(data.value)

// In displays
const formatted = formatFinancialValue(data.value)
```

---

## The real power: prompts

The most important helpers are the prompt builders:

```typescript
// lib/tools.ts
export function buildFinalAnswerPrompt(question, factsJson) {
  return `You are an analyst. Answer using ONLY the provided facts.
  
  CRITICAL RULES:
  1. Use EXACT numbers from data
  2. Format: $383.3B (not $383B)
  3. Only mention years that exist
  ...`
}
```

This prompt controls:
- What the AI does
- How it formats answers
- What rules it follows
- The quality of answers

Change the prompt → change the AI's behavior.

---

## Visual breakdown

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│  app/actions/ask-question.ts        │
│  (The Orchestrator)                 │
│  - Coordinates the flow              │
│  - Calls helpers in order            │
│  - Handles errors                    │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘
               │
       ┌───────┴────────┐
       ↓                ↓
┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
│ lib/tools.ts │  │ lib/validators│
│ (THE PROMPTS)│  │ (THE LOGIC)  │
│              │  │              │
│ Controls AI  │  │ Checks quality│
└──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
       ↓                ↓
┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐
│lib/chart-    │  │lib/regeneration│
│helpers.ts    │  │.ts            │
│              │  │              │
│ Creates      │  │ Fixes errors │
│ charts       │  │              │
└──────────────┘  └──────────────┘
```

The helpers contain the logic; the server action coordinates.

---

## Summary

Helper functions are central because they:
1. Contain the business logic
2. Build the prompts that control the AI
3. Validate and ensure quality
4. Format and present data
5. Are reusable and testable

Server actions are coordinators that:
- Fetch data
- Call helpers in the right order
- Handle the flow

Think of it like:
- Server actions = The conductor (coordinates)
- Helper functions = The musicians (do the work)

The prompts in `lib/tools.ts` are especially important because they control what the AI does. That's why improving the chatbot often means improving the helper functions, especially the prompts.

        "contents": "### 2. LLMs Want to Help (Too Much)\n\nLLMs are trained to be helpful, which sometimes means:\n- Filling in what they think you want\n- Matching the user's language\n- Making assumptions to avoid saying \"I don't know\"\n\nThis \"helpfulness\" can work against strict schemas.\n\n**The lesson:** Design systems that work WITH the LLM's helpful nature, not against it.\n\n### 3. The 80/20 Rule Applies\n\nIn our case:\n- 80% of requests use 5 calculated metrics\n- 20% of requests use the long tail\n\n**The lesson:** Optimize for the common case, handle the long tail pragmatically.\n\n### 4. Logging Is Product Research\n\nEvery translation you log is a data point:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Logs reveal user behavior:\n\"debt_to_equity\" → total_liabilities (x450)\n\"de_ratio\" → total_liabilities (x120)\n\"leverage\" → total_liabilities (x80)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**The lesson:** Your production logs tell you what to build next.\n\n### 5. Type Safety Catches Bugs\n\nWhen we moved from normalization (strings) to native metrics (types):\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Found 3 typos that would have been runtime bugs:\n'net_incom' → ❌ TypeScript error!\n'shareholders_equty' → ❌ TypeScript error!\n'debt_to_equity_ration' → ❌ TypeScript error!\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**The lesson:** If data flows through your system, put it in the type system.\n\n### 6. Users Don't Care About Your Schema\n\nUsers ask for:\n- \"debt to equity ratio\"\n- \"D/E\"\n- \"leverage\"\n- \"debt-to-equity\"\n\nThey don't care that you store &#96;total_liabilities&#96;. That's an implementation detail.\n\n**The lesson:** Your API should speak user language, not database language.\n\n### 7. Perfect Is the Enemy of Shipped\n\nWe could have spent weeks building the perfect system upfront. Instead:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nDay 1: Ship normalization (users happy)\nWeek 2: Analyze logs (learned patterns)\nWeek 4: Implement top metrics (better performance)\nMonth 2: Full migration (production-ready)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**The lesson:** Progressive enhancement beats big-bang rewrites.\n\n---\n\n## Conclusion\n\nThe semantic impedance mismatch between user language, LLM outputs, and database schemas is a fundamental challenge in LLM application development.\n\n**The three solutions:**\n\n1. **Normalization Layer** - Quick, pragmatic, learn from production",

        "contents": "# Chatbot Technical Overview &amp; Improvement Ideas\n\n## Technical Architecture\n\n### High-Level Flow\n\nThe chatbot uses a **three-step LLM orchestration pattern**:\n\n1. **Tool Selection** → LLM picks which data tool to use\n2. **Tool Execution** → Fetch data from Supabase\n3. **Answer Generation** → LLM generates final answer from facts\n\n### Core Components\n\n#### 1. **Frontend Entry Points**\n- **&#96;app/page.tsx&#96;** - Home page with streaming chatbot (uses &#96;/api/ask&#96; route)\n- **&#96;app/chatbot/page.tsx&#96;** - Dedicated chatbot page (uses &#96;askQuestion&#96; server action)\n\n#### 2. **API Layer**\n- **&#96;app/api/ask/route.ts&#96;** - Streaming API endpoint (Server-Sent Events)\n  - Streams: &#96;flow&#96;, &#96;data&#96;, &#96;answer&#96;, &#96;validation&#96;, &#96;followup&#96;, &#96;complete&#96; events\n  - Real-time progress updates via Flow Visualization\n  - Edge runtime for low latency\n\n#### 3. **Server Actions**\n- **&#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96;** - Main orchestration function\n  - Non-streaming version (used by chatbot page)\n  - Handles tool selection, execution, answer generation\n  - Includes validation and regeneration logic\n\n#### 4. **Tool System** (&#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;)\nAvailable tools:\n- &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96; - Basic financial metrics (revenue, profit, assets, etc.)\n- &#96;getPrices&#96; - Stock price history with custom date ranges\n- &#96;getRecentFilings&#96; - SEC filing metadata (dates, types, URLs)\n- &#96;searchFilings&#96; - Semantic search through filing content\n- &#96;listMetrics&#96; - Browse available metrics catalog\n- &#96;getFinancialMetric&#96; - Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, 139+ metrics)\n\n#### 5. **Data Layer**\n- **Supabase** - PostgreSQL database with:\n  - &#96;financials_std&#96; - Standardized financial statements\n  - &#96;prices&#96; - Historical stock prices\n  - &#96;filings&#96; - SEC filing metadata\n  - &#96;filing_chunks&#96; - Vector embeddings for semantic search\n  - &#96;query_logs&#96; - Analytics and feedback tracking\n  - &#96;conversations&#96; / &#96;messages&#96; - Persistent chat history\n\n#### 6. **LLM Integration**\n- **OpenAI Responses API** (gpt-4o-mini or gpt-5-nano)\n- **Two-stage prompting**:\n  - Tool selection: JSON-structured output (&#96;{\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}&#96;)",

        "contents": "# CLAUDE.md\n\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\n\n## Project Overview\n\n**Fin Quote** is a Next.js-based financial data platform with an AI-powered Q&amp;A chatbot that answers natural language questions about Apple (AAPL) stock. The system uses a two-step LLM architecture with tool selection, data execution, answer generation, and validation.\n\n**Core Design Philosophy:**\n- **Safety First**: LLMs cannot execute arbitrary database queries. Instead, they select from a whitelist of pre-built \"tools\" (server actions) with validated inputs.\n- **Server-Side Intelligence**: All LLM calls, database queries, and validation logic run server-side. The browser only handles UI.\n- **Grounded Answers**: The LLM must use only fetched data; no external knowledge or hallucinations allowed.\n- **Validation Pipeline**: All answers are validated against source data for number accuracy, year correctness, and citation validity, with auto-regeneration on failures.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Two-Step LLM Flow\n\nEvery user question follows this pattern (implemented in &#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96;):\n\n1. **Tool Selection** (lines 258-330)\n   - LLM receives question + conversation history + tool menu\n   - Returns JSON: &#96;{\"tool\": \"toolName\", \"args\": {...}}&#96;\n   - Model: Uses &#96;OPENAI_MODEL&#96; (default: &#96;gpt-5-nano&#96;)\n   - Tokens tracked for cost analysis\n\n2. **Tool Execution** (lines 332-575)\n   - Server validates tool + args\n   - Executes corresponding server action\n   - Returns structured data (financials, prices, filings, passages, or metrics)\n\n3. **Answer Generation** (lines 579-650)\n   - LLM receives question + fetched facts + conversation history\n   - Generates grounded answer using only provided data\n   - Plain text output (no Markdown, bullets, or tables)\n   - Context: Last 10 messages (tool selection) or 4 messages (answer generation for gpt-5)\n\n4. **Validation &amp; Auto-Correction** (lines 653-796)\n   - Validates numbers, years, and filing citations",

        "contents": "# CLAUDE.md\n\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\n\n## Project Overview\n\n**Fin Quote** is a Next.js-based financial Q&amp;A platform that uses LLMs to answer natural language questions about Apple (AAPL) stock data. The system uses a two-step LLM architecture: (1) tool selection and (2) answer generation with validation.\n\n**Core Design Philosophy:**\n- **Safety First**: LLMs cannot execute arbitrary database queries. Instead, they select from a whitelist of pre-built \"tools\" (server actions) with validated inputs.\n- **Server-Side Intelligence**: All LLM calls, database queries, and validation logic run server-side. The browser only handles UI.\n- **Grounded Answers**: The LLM must use only fetched data; no external knowledge or hallucinations allowed.\n- **Validation Pipeline**: All answers are validated against source data for number accuracy, year correctness, and citation validity.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture\n\n### Two-Step LLM Flow\n\nEvery user question follows this pattern:\n\n1. **Tool Selection** (&#96;ask-question.ts:224-313&#96;)\n   - LLM receives question + conversation history + tool menu\n   - Returns JSON: &#96;{\"tool\": \"toolName\", \"args\": {...}}&#96;\n   - Model: Uses &#96;OPENAI_MODEL&#96; (default: &#96;gpt-5-nano&#96;)\n\n2. **Tool Execution** (&#96;ask-question.ts:316-438&#96;)\n   - Server validates tool + args\n   - Executes corresponding server action\n   - Returns structured data (financials, prices, filings, or passages)\n\n3. **Answer Generation** (&#96;ask-question.ts:441-500&#96;)\n   - LLM receives question + fetched facts + conversation history\n   - Generates grounded answer using only provided data\n   - Plain text output (no Markdown)\n\n4. **Validation** (&#96;ask-question.ts:503-658&#96;)\n   - Validates numbers, years, and filing citations\n   - If validation fails with high severity, triggers auto-regeneration\n   - Logs validation results to &#96;query_logs&#96; table\n\n### Available Tools\n\nDefined in &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96; (TOOL_MENU):\n\n1. **getAaplFinancialsByMetric** - Income statement, balance sheet, cash flow metrics\n   - Core metrics: &#96;revenue&#96;, &#96;gross_profit&#96;, &#96;net_income&#96;, &#96;operating_income&#96;, &#96;total_assets&#96;, &#96;total_liabilities&#96;, &#96;shareholders_equity&#96;, &#96;operating_cash_flow&#96;, &#96;eps&#96;",

        "contents": "### Trading Dashboard — Integration Brief for LLMs\n\nThis document gives another large language model the minimum-but-sufficient context to integrate this project into a different codebase or a monorepo. It focuses on architecture, dependencies, API boundaries, environment variables, build/runtime assumptions, and common pitfalls.\n\n---\n\n## 1) High-level Overview\n\n- App type: Next.js 15 (App Router) + optional PWA service worker + Electron 38 desktop wrapper.\n- Language: TypeScript for app code and scripts; CommonJS module type at root.\n- Frontend: React 19; Tailwind stack (tailwindcss, postcss, autoprefixer).\n- Packaging: &#96;electron-builder&#96; creates macOS DMG/ZIP, Windows NSIS/portable, Linux AppImage/DEB.\n- Primary domains:\n  - Stock data and charting via Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) REST and WebSocket.\n  - News ingestion and topic classification; optional OpenAI-powered summaries/classification.\n  - Watchlist, quotes, dividends, and app settings persisted in Firebase (client + admin).\n  - Subscriptions and payments via Stripe.\n\nKey entry points:\n- Web: Next.js (App Router) API routes in &#96;app/api/**&#96;.\n- Desktop: &#96;electron/main.js&#96; spawns Next server and loads &#96;http://localhost:${PORT}&#96; into an Electron &#96;BrowserWindow&#96;.\n- Optional proxy: standalone &#96;server.js&#96; Express server for TradingView symbol search (helpful when CORS blocks direct requests).\n\n---\n\n## 2) Repository Structure Signals\n\n- &#96;app/&#96;: Next.js App Router pages and API routes.\n  - &#96;app/api/**&#96;: REST endpoints for quotes, news, cron/cache jobs, Stripe, symbol search, etc.\n  - &#96;app/**/page.tsx&#96;: UI routes (watchlist, pricing, news, etc.).\n- &#96;components/TradingView/**&#96;: Chart surface using &#96;lightweight-charts&#96;, plus plugins (extended-hours overlay, trend lines) and UI controls.\n- &#96;hooks/**&#96;: Data and UI hooks (quotes, extended hours, news, symbol search, chart modal, watchlist, etc.).\n- &#96;services/fmp/**&#96;: FMP REST client, WebSocket manager, and a &#96;getFMPService()&#96; singleton.\n- &#96;lib/firebase/**&#96;: Client SDK config (&#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_*&#96;), Admin SDK bootstrap (service account or ADC), and Firestore CRUD helpers for dividends, quotes cache, news archive, settings, symbol mapping, watchlists, metrics.\n- &#96;lib/cache/simple-cache.ts&#96;: Small server-side in-memory TTL cache shared across API endpoints.",

        "contents": "## Fin Quote MVP — End‑to‑End Plan (Beginner‑Friendly)\n\n### What we’re building and why\nFin Quote is a finance Q&amp;A web app. A user asks natural‑language questions about a stock (starting with AAPL only for MVP). The server fetches the right data from Supabase and asks an LLM to produce a short, grounded answer, plus a tiny “data used” section for transparency. The goal is a safe, reliable competitor to fiscal.ai that we can ship quickly and iterate on.\n\n### Key principles (why this design)\n- **Safety first**: The LLM does not run free‑form database queries. Instead, it can only “press” a few safe, prebuilt server functions (we call these tools). This avoids bad queries, data leaks, and unpredictable costs.\n- **Predictability**: Same tool + same inputs = same query + output shape. This makes debugging and testing straightforward.\n- **Server‑side brains**: All sensitive logic (database queries, LLM calls, validation) runs on the server. The browser handles UI only.\n- **Small steps**: Start with one stock (AAPL) and a couple of tools, then add more capabilities once the loop works.\n\n### Glossary (plain English)\n- **Tool (server function)**: A tiny, safe function on the server that does one job, like “get AAPL revenue for the last N years.” The LLM can choose it and supply allowed inputs; the server validates and runs it.\n- **Function calling**: An LLM feature where the model requests a named tool + JSON arguments; your server executes it and returns results; the model continues the conversation.\n- **Reasoning**: The model deciding which tool fits and how to explain results (planning/logic). Our MVP uses single‑hop reasoning: pick one tool → fetch → answer.\n- **Multi‑hop**: Answering requires several steps (e.g., fetch AAPL, fetch peers, compare). We’ll add this later.\n- **RAG (Retrieval‑Augmented Generation)**: For document questions (filings/transcripts), retrieve the most relevant passages via a vector store, then answer using those passages. We’ll add this after MVP.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture overview\n\n### Frontend (browser)",

        "contents": "## Conclusion\n\nThe semantic impedance mismatch between user language, LLM outputs, and database schemas is a fundamental challenge in LLM application development.\n\n**The three solutions:**\n\n1. **Normalization Layer** - Quick, pragmatic, learn from production\n2. **Schema Evolution** - Correct, type-safe, maintainable long-term\n3. **Structured Functions** - Strict enforcement, different use case\n\n**The recommended path:**\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nStart → Normalization → Learn → Native Implementation → Production\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**The key insight:**\n\nDon't fight the LLM's nature. Design your system to work with how LLMs actually behave, not how you wish they would behave.\n\n**The ultimate lesson:**\n\nLLM integration is architecture, not just prompting. When prompts get complex, the problem is usually architectural.\n\n---\n\n## Additional Resources\n\n### Related Patterns\n\n- **Adapter Pattern**: Normalization is a classic adapter pattern\n- **Facade Pattern**: Schema evolution creates a domain-appropriate facade\n- **Command Pattern**: Structured function calling is the command pattern\n\n### Further Reading\n\n- [Semantic Web](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semantic_Web) - The broader problem of semantic interoperability\n- [Domain-Driven Design](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/DomainDrivenDesign.html) - Building systems that match domain language\n- [Hexagonal Architecture](https://alistair.cockburn.us/hexagonal-architecture/) - Ports and adapters pattern\n\n### Questions to Ask Your System\n\n1. Are we solving architectural problems with prompts?\n2. Do our types match our domain language?\n3. Can users ask questions naturally?\n4. Are we fighting the LLM or working with it?\n5. What do our logs tell us users actually want?\n\n---\n\n**Document Version:** 1.0\n**Last Updated:** 2025-01-04\n**Authors:** Claude Code Session\n**Status:** Living Document",

        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./docs/LLM_SEMANTIC_MISMATCH_SOLUTIONS.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {

          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 1228
          }
        },
        "contents": "LLMs are trained to:\n- Preserve semantic meaning\n- Use natural language\n- Match domain terminology\n\nWhen you find yourself writing prompts like:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\"Don't output what the user said, output this arbitrary code instead\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThat's a sign you're working against the LLM.\n\n**Better approach:** Let the LLM do what it's good at (understanding semantics), then translate in code.\n\n### 2. The Prompt vs. Code Decision\n\nUse this framework:\n\n| Task | Prompt | Code |\n|------|--------|------|\n| Understanding user intent | ✅ | ❌ |\n| Generating natural language | ✅ | ❌ |\n| Calculations | ⚠️ | ✅ |\n| Schema validation | ❌ | ✅ |\n| Business logic | ❌ | ✅ |\n| Data transformation | ❌ | ✅ |\n\n**Rule of thumb:**\n- Prompts for semantics\n- Code for mechanics\n\n### 3. The \"Dozens of Examples\" Smell\n\nIf you're adding dozens of examples to make something work:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// 🚨 CODE SMELL\nconst prompt = &#96;\nExamples:\nQ: \"debt to equity\" → {\"metric\": \"total_liabilities\"}\nQ: \"D/E ratio\" → {\"metric\": \"total_liabilities\"}\nQ: \"debt-to-equity\" → {\"metric\": \"total_liabilities\"}\nQ: \"leverage ratio\" → {\"metric\": \"total_liabilities\"}\nQ: \"debt equity\" → {\"metric\": \"total_liabilities\"}\n... 20 more examples ...\n&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis means:\n1. You're solving an architectural problem with prompts\n2. You're working against the LLM's nature\n3. There's probably a better solution in code\n\n### 4. Semantic Layers Pattern\n\nStructure your application in semantic layers:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  User Layer (Natural Language)      │\n│  \"Show me debt to equity ratio\"     │\n└──────────────┬──────────────────────┘\n               │\n               ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────┐\n│  LLM Layer (Semantic Understanding) │\n│  Intent: calculate_ratio            │",

        "contents": "// - If formula changes, update prompt\n\n// ✅ AFTER: One canonical calculation\nfunction calculateDebtToEquity(liabilities, equity) {\n  return liabilities / equity\n}\n// If formula changes, update once\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 3. Type Safety\nTypeScript knows about all metrics:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// ✅ Compile-time checking\ntype FinancialMetric = 'revenue' | 'debt_to_equity_ratio' | ...\n\nfunction getMetric(metric: FinancialMetric) {\n  if (metric === 'debt_to_equity_rati') {  // ❌ Typo caught at compile time!\n    //                            ^\n    // TypeScript Error: \"debt_to_equity_rati\" is not assignable to FinancialMetric\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 4. Better Developer Experience\nAdding a new metric is straightforward:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// 1. Add to type\ntype CalculatedFinancialMetric =\n  | 'debt_to_equity_ratio'\n  | 'current_ratio'  // ✨ New!\n\n// 2. Implement calculation\nif (metric === 'current_ratio') {\n  const data = await fetchCurrentAssetsAndLiabilities()\n  return data.map(row =&gt; ({\n    year: row.year,\n    value: row.current_assets / row.current_liabilities,\n    metric: 'current_ratio',\n  }))\n}\n\n// 3. Done! TypeScript ensures you handle it everywhere\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 5. Consistent Formatting\nData always comes back in the same shape:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Whether raw or calculated, same interface:\n{\n  year: 2025,\n  value: 3.87,\n  metric: 'debt_to_equity_ratio',\n  source: {  // Optional: show how it was calculated\n    total_liabilities: 285508000000,\n    shareholders_equity: 73733000000,\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 6. Easier Testing\nYou can test calculations directly:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Test the calculation function\ntest('debt_to_equity_ratio calculates correctly', async () =&gt; {\n  const result = await getAaplFinancialsByMetric({\n    metric: 'debt_to_equity_ratio',\n    limit: 1,\n  })\n\n  expect(result.data[0].value).toBeCloseTo(3.87, 2)\n  expect(result.data[0].source.total_liabilities).toBe(285508000000)\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Disadvantages\n\n#### 1. More Code to Write\nEvery calculated metric needs implementation:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Need to write handlers for each one\nif (metric === 'debt_to_equity_ratio') { ... }",

    {
      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./docs/PREMARKET_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 52
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 104
          }
        },
        "contents": "**Current Limitations:**\n- Only works during regular market hours (9:30 AM - 4:00 PM ET)\n- No pre-market or after-hours data\n- Shows last close data when market is closed\n\n**API Usage:**\n- ~200 API calls per day (assuming typical user traffic)\n- 2 calls per page load (gainers + losers)\n- ISR caching prevents excessive calls\n\n---\n\n## Goals\n\n1. **Add Pre-Market Scanning** - Display top 20 gainers/losers based on &#96;preMarketChangePercentage&#96; (4:00-9:30 AM ET)\n2. **Add After-Hours Scanning** - Display top 20 gainers/losers based on &#96;afterMarketChangePercentage&#96; (4:00-8:00 PM ET)\n3. **Smart Time-Based Routing** - Automatically switch data source based on current market session\n4. **Maintain ISR Caching** - Preserve efficient caching strategy, no increase in API costs\n5. **Seamless UX** - No code changes needed in homepage UI (automatic updates via polling)\n6. **Cost-Effective** - Stay within FMP free tier limits (250 calls/day)\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Design\n\n### 1. Ticker Universe Management\n\n**Source:** GitHub repository &#96;rreichel3/US-Stock-Symbols&#96;\n- Maintained and updated nightly\n- Free and public\n- Contains comprehensive list of US stocks by exchange\n\n**Implementation:**\n- Download ticker list from: &#96;https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rreichel3/US-Stock-Symbols/main/all/all_tickers.txt&#96;\n- Store in: &#96;data/us_tickers.txt&#96;\n- Filter to **~500 liquid stocks** (S&amp;P 500 constituents or equivalent)\n- Update weekly via automated script\n\n**Filtering Criteria (Automated Script):**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// scripts/filter-ticker-universe.ts\nconst filters = {\n  exchanges: ['NYSE', 'NASDAQ'],           // Only major exchanges\n  minPrice: 5,                              // Exclude penny stocks\n  minAvgVolume: 1_000_000,                  // 1M+ average daily volume\n  excludeTypes: ['ETF', 'PREFERRED', 'WARRANT', 'ADR', 'OTC'], // Common stocks only\n  maxSymbolLength: 5                        // Exclude exotic tickers\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Why 500 stocks (not 2,000)?**\n- **API Efficiency:** 500 stocks = 3 API calls per scan (vs. 10 for 2,000)",

        "contents": "# Upwork Job Posting\n\n## Job Title\n\n**Full Stack Next.js Developer for AI-Powered Financial Data Platform (Supabase, OpenAI)**\n\n---\n\n## Job Description\n\nWe're building **Fin Quote**, a financial data platform that combines AI-powered stock analysis with real-time market tracking. We're looking for an experienced full-stack developer to help extend features, improve performance, and build new functionality.\n\n### What We've Built\n\n**1. AI-Powered Stock Q&amp;A Chatbot**\n- Natural language questions about stock data (\"What was Apple's revenue in 2023?\")\n- Two-step LLM architecture: tool selection → data fetching → answer generation → validation\n- Semantic search over SEC filings using RAG (vector embeddings)\n- Auto-regeneration when answers fail validation\n- Cost tracking and query logging\n\n**2. Real-Time Stock Watchlist**\n- Live stock quotes with 10-second polling\n- Multi-source news aggregation (WSJ, NYT, Bloomberg, Yahoo)\n- TradingView-style interactive charts with candlesticks\n- Analyst ratings, earnings tracking, extended hours data\n- User authentication and data persistence\n\n### Tech Stack\n\n| Layer | Technologies |\n|-------|-------------|\n| **Frontend** | React 19, Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS |\n| **Backend** | Next.js Server Actions, API Routes |\n| **Database** | Supabase (PostgreSQL + pgvector for embeddings) |\n| **Auth** | Supabase Auth (Google OAuth, email/password) |\n| **AI/LLM** | OpenAI API (GPT-4o, GPT-5-nano), text-embedding-3-small |\n| **Charts** | Highcharts, TradingView Lightweight Charts, HTML5 Canvas |\n| **Data APIs** | Financial Modeling Prep (FMP), SEC EDGAR |\n| **Architecture** | Monorepo with npm workspaces |\n| **Testing** | Vitest, Testing Library |\n\n### What You'll Work On\n\n- Extend the AI chatbot to support additional stocks (currently Apple-only)\n- Improve LLM prompt engineering for better accuracy and lower costs\n- Build new watchlist features (alerts, portfolio tracking, screeners)\n- Optimize performance and API efficiency\n- Write tests and improve code quality\n- Debug and fix issues as they arise",

        "contents": "  // When does it stop?\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 3. Doesn't Scale to Complex Cases\nWhat if a user asks for a metric that needs THREE inputs?\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// \"Free Cash Flow\" = Operating Cash Flow - Capital Expenditures\n// But we don't have capex in our schema!\n// Can't map to a single raw metric\n'free_cash_flow': '???',  // ❌ No single mapping works\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### 4. Loses Type Safety\nTypeScript can't help you here:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// These are all strings at runtime\nconst mapping: Record&lt;string, FinancialMetric&gt; = {\n  'debt_to_equity': 'total_liabilities',  // Could have typo\n  'roe': 'net_incom',  // ❌ Typo! Won't catch until runtime\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### When to Use This Solution\n\n✅ **Good for:**\n- **Quick fixes** - need to ship today\n- **Validation** - proving the concept before bigger refactor\n- **Learning** - discovering what users actually ask for\n- **Transition** - buying time to plan proper solution\n\n❌ **Bad for:**\n- **Long-term architecture** - doesn't address root cause\n- **Complex calculations** - only works for 1-to-1 mappings\n- **Type-safe systems** - loses compile-time checking\n\n### Real-World Example\n\nOur actual implementation:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Before normalization:\nUser: \"debt to equity ratio\"\nLLM: {\"metric\": \"debt_to_equity_ratio\"}\nSystem: ❌ Error: Invalid metric\n\n// After normalization:\nUser: \"debt to equity ratio\"\nLLM: {\"metric\": \"debt_to_equity_ratio\"}\nNormalizer: debt_to_equity_ratio → total_liabilities\nSystem: ✅ Fetches total_liabilities + shareholders_equity\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**The result:** Users can ask naturally, system works reliably, and we learned that users ask for D/E ratio in 7 different ways we never anticipated.\n\n---\n\n## Solution 2: Schema Evolution (Support Calculated Metrics Natively)\n\n### Core Idea\n\n**Make your API speak the same language as your users.**\n\nInstead of forcing translation, expand your schema to support calculated metrics as first-class citizens:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// BEFORE: Schema only has raw data\ntype FinancialMetric = 'revenue' | 'total_liabilities' | ...\n\n// AFTER: Schema includes calculated metrics\ntype FinancialMetric =\n  | 'revenue'              // Raw",

        "contents": "- **RAG (Retrieval‑Augmented Generation)**: For document questions (filings/transcripts), retrieve the most relevant passages via a vector store, then answer using those passages. We’ll add this after MVP.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture overview\n\n### Frontend (browser)\n- Next.js app with a simple UI: text box + Ask button + answer display.\n- No secrets in the browser.\n- Uses &#96;createBrowserClient()&#96; only for UI‑safe tasks.\n\n### Backend (server)\n- Next.js server actions/API routes handle all sensitive work.\n- Uses &#96;createServerClient()&#96; to talk to Supabase (read‑only for MVP).\n- Two LLM steps per question:\n  1) Selection: model picks exactly one tool from our small menu and provides JSON args.\n  2) Answering: after we run the tool and get facts, the model writes the final answer using only those facts.\n\n### Data (Supabase)\n- We store standardized financials in &#96;financials_std&#96; and company metadata in &#96;company&#96;.\n- For MVP, we enforce AAPL‑only and small row limits (1–8) at the tool level.\n\n---\n\n## Current code in the repo (important files)\n- &#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&#96;: Creates the browser client (uses &#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_*&#96; env vars; no session persistence). For UI only.\n- &#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&#96;: Creates the server client (same env vars; no session persistence). For server actions and API routes.\n- &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96;: Typed Supabase schema for &#96;company&#96; and &#96;financials_std&#96;.\n- &#96;app/actions/financials.ts&#96;:\n  - &#96;getCompaniesWithFinancials()&#96;: Example server action that composes companies with financials for display.\n  - &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric({ metric, limit })&#96;: SAFE TOOL (MVP). Allowed metrics: &#96;revenue&#96; or &#96;gross_profit&#96;. Limit clamped to 1..8. Always filters to &#96;AAPL&#96;. Returns an array of &#96;{ year, value, metric }&#96;.\n- &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;:\n  - &#96;TOOL_MENU&#96;: Defines the tool(s) the model can choose from.",

        "contents": "3. **Performance**\n   - Clear old events after N questions\n   - Virtualize list for long sessions\n   - Debounce rapid events\n   - Compute rolling aggregates (avg / p95 per step, total cost) and render a summary chip under the header filters\n\n4. **Accessibility**\n   - Add ARIA labels\n   - Keyboard navigation\n   - Screen reader support\n\n### Phase 4: Advanced Features (Future)\n\n**Priority: Low**\n\n1. **Export Flow Data**\n   - Download as JSON\n   - Share flow link\n   - Copy to clipboard\n\n2. **Historical View**\n   - Show flow for previous questions\n   - Compare flows side-by-side\n   - Search through past flows\n\n3. **Metrics Dashboard**\n   - Average timing per step\n   - Success rate tracking\n   - Cost tracking over time\n\n4. **Developer Mode**\n   - Show actual SQL queries\n   - Show full LLM prompts\n   - Show raw API responses\n\n---\n\n## Streaming Event Contract\n\nTo keep the frontend and backend aligned, every flow update must conform to a shared schema.\n\n### &#96;FlowEvent&#96; Interface\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\ntype FlowEventStatus = 'pending' | 'active' | 'success' | 'warning' | 'error'\n\ninterface FlowEvent {\n  id: string                // monotonic id or UUID\n  step: string              // e.g. 'tool_selection'\n  group: 'planning' | 'data' | 'answering'\n  sequence: number          // incremental index within the flow\n  parentId?: string         // optional parent event for sub-tasks/retries\n  status: FlowEventStatus\n  startedAt: string         // ISO timestamp\n  durationMs?: number       // present when status resolves\n  why?: string              // short explanation (&lt;200 chars)\n  summary?: string          // human-readable headline\n  details?: Record&lt;string, unknown&gt; // trimmed metadata for expand panel\n  costUsd?: number          // optional incremental cost\n  inspectorRef?: {\n    type: 'query_log' | 'prompt' | 'validation_log' | 'custom'\n    id: string\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Guidelines**\n- Keep each payload under ~2 KB; strip large objects, only send IDs or counts.\n- Normalize &#96;step&#96; names so the UI can map to icons/titles.\n- Populate &#96;why&#96; directly from LLM/tool reasoning; fall back to a sensible default if none returned.",

        "contents": "# Solving Semantic Impedance Mismatch in LLM Applications\n\n## Table of Contents\n1. [Introduction](#introduction)\n2. [The Problem: Semantic Impedance Mismatch](#the-problem-semantic-impedance-mismatch)\n3. [Why This Happens](#why-this-happens)\n4. [Solution 1: Normalization Layer](#solution-1-normalization-layer-correction-mapping)\n5. [Solution 2: Schema Evolution](#solution-2-schema-evolution-support-calculated-metrics-natively)\n6. [Solution 3: Structured Function Calling](#solution-3-structured-function-calling-brief)\n7. [General Principles for LLM Integration](#general-principles-for-llm-integration)\n8. [Decision Framework](#decision-framework)\n9. [Lessons Learned](#lessons-learned)\n\n---\n\n## Introduction\n\nThis document explores a fundamental challenge when building LLM-powered applications: **the semantic impedance mismatch between user language, LLM outputs, and database schemas**.\n\n&gt; Important: Fin Quote uses the OpenAI Responses API exclusively in runtime code. Any references or snippets using Chat Completions in this document are legacy or for comparison only. Prefer the Responses API for all new work.\n\n### Our Specific Case\n\nIn our financial Q&amp;A system, users ask questions like:\n- \"What's Apple's debt to equity ratio?\"\n- \"Show me the gross margin trend\"\n- \"How's their ROE over time?\"\n\nThese are perfectly natural business questions. However, our database doesn't store \"debt to equity ratio\" or \"gross margin\" - it stores raw primitives like &#96;total_liabilities&#96;, &#96;shareholders_equity&#96;, &#96;gross_profit&#96;, and &#96;revenue&#96;.\n\n**The issue:** When we ask an LLM to select which database metric to query, it naturally wants to output &#96;debt_to_equity&#96; (matching the user's language), but our validation layer rejects it because that's not a valid database column.\n\nThis is not a bug - **it's a fundamental architectural challenge in LLM system design**.\n\n---\n\n## The Problem: Semantic Impedance Mismatch\n\n### The Three \"Languages\" That Must Align\n\n#### 1. User Language (Natural, Domain-Specific)\nUsers think in terms of **business concepts and derived metrics**:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;",

        "contents": "│   └── supabase/\n│       ├── client.ts           # Client-side Supabase client\n│       └── server.ts           # Server-side Supabase client\n├── .env.local.example          # Example environment variables\n└── package.json\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Features\n\n### Server Actions\n\nThe app uses Next.js Server Actions for data fetching, located in &#96;app/actions/financials.ts&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { getCompaniesWithFinancials } from '@/app/actions/financials'\n\nconst { data, error } = await getCompaniesWithFinancials()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis server action:\n- Fetches all companies with their related financial data\n- Uses Supabase's nested &#96;.select()&#96; syntax to join tables\n- Returns fully typed data using TypeScript\n- Handles errors gracefully\n- Orders companies by name and financials by year (descending)\n\n### Type Safety\n\nAll database types are defined in &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96;, providing:\n- Full TypeScript autocomplete for database queries\n- Type-safe data access throughout the application\n- Helper types like &#96;CompanyWithFinancials&#96; for joined data\n\n### Supabase Client\n\nTwo client configurations are available:\n\n1. **Server Client** (&#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&#96;)\n   - Used in Server Components and Server Actions\n   - Runs on the server only\n   - Safe for sensitive operations\n\n2. **Browser Client** (&#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&#96;)\n   - Used in Client Components\n   - Runs in the browser\n   - Uses the public anon key (safe to expose)\n\n## Usage Example\n\n### Fetching Data in a Server Component\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// app/financials/page.tsx\nimport { getCompaniesWithFinancials } from '@/app/actions/financials'\n\nexport default async function FinancialsPage() {\n  const { data: companies, error } = await getCompaniesWithFinancials()",

        "contents": "# Prompt Evaluation &amp; Continuous Improvement System\n\n&gt; Important: The Fin Quote runtime uses the OpenAI Responses API exclusively. Any usage of Chat Completions in this document is for historical context or testing examples only.\n\n## Overview\n\nThis document outlines the complete system for evaluating and continuously improving the AI prompts used in Fin Quote. The goal is to measure prompt performance objectively, identify failure patterns, and systematically improve answer quality over time.\n\n---\n\n## Problem Statement\n\n**Current State:**\n- Prompts are hardcoded in &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;\n- No systematic way to test prompt changes before deploying\n- Can't measure if a prompt improvement actually helps or hurts\n- No visibility into which types of questions fail most often\n- Improvement is guesswork, not data-driven\n\n**Desired State:**\n- Test prompt changes against 100 representative questions in minutes\n- Objectively compare prompt versions with automated scoring\n- Deploy only improvements that show measurable gains\n- Identify and fix the most common failure patterns systematically\n- Data-driven improvement loop with &lt;1 day iteration cycles\n\n---\n\n## System Architecture\n\n### Components\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│ 1. Tools (lib/)\n- &#96;tools.ts&#96; - Tool definitions + prompt templates for tool selection and answer generation\n- &#96;validators.ts&#96; - Answer validation (number accuracy, year correctness, filing citations)\n- &#96;regeneration.ts&#96; - Auto-correction logic when validation fails\n- &#96;chart-helpers.ts&#96; - Chart generation logic for financial data visualization\n\n### Frontend (app/)\n- &#96;app/ask/page.tsx&#96; - Main Q&amp;A interface with conversation history\n- &#96;app/admin/validation/page.tsx&#96; - Validation results dashboard\n- &#96;app/admin/costs/page.tsx&#96; - Cost tracking dashboard\n- &#96;components/FinancialChart.tsx&#96; - Highcharts visualization\n- &#96;components/RecentQueries.tsx&#96; - Recent query history\n\n### Configuration\n- &#96;.env.local&#96; - Environment variables (Supabase, OpenAI, FMP API keys)\n- &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96; - TypeScript types for Supabase schema\n- &#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&#96; - Browser client (uses NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars)\n- &#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&#96; - Server client (for server actions)\n\n---\n\n## Environment Variables\n\nRequired in &#96;.env.local&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Supabase (public, safe for browser)\nNEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co\nNEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key\n\n# OpenAI (server-only secret)\nOPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...\nOPENAI_MODEL=gpt-5-nano  # Options: gpt-4o-mini, gpt-5-nano, gpt-5-mini\n\n# Financial Modeling Prep (server-only secret)\nFMP_API_KEY=your-fmp-key\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Critical Implementation Details\n\n### Tool Selection Prompt Architecture\n\nThe tool selection prompt (&#96;lib/tools.ts:buildToolSelectionPrompt&#96;) is highly tuned:\n- **Metric Mapping**: Maps user terms like \"profit\", \"sales\", \"ROE\" to exact database metrics\n- **Limit Rules**: Special handling for specific years (limit: 10), year ranges (limit: N), trends (limit: 4)\n- **Range Mapping**: Maps user time expressions to API ranges (7d/30d/90d)\n- **Query Extraction**: Converts qualitative questions into semantic search queries\n\n### Answer Generation Validation\n\nThe answer prompt (&#96;lib/tools.ts:buildFinalAnswerPrompt&#96;) enforces strict validation rules:",

        "contents": "# Fin Quote - Company Financial Data Platform\n\nA Next.js application that displays company financial data from Supabase.\n\n## Tech Stack\n\n- **Framework**: Next.js 14 (App Router)\n- **Database**: Supabase (PostgreSQL)\n- **Authentication**: Firebase Auth (separate)\n- **Styling**: Tailwind CSS\n- **Language**: TypeScript\n\n## Database Schema\n\n### Tables\n\n1. **company**\n   - &#96;id&#96; (uuid, primary key)\n   - &#96;created_at&#96; (timestamptz)\n   - &#96;symbol&#96; (text, unique)\n   - &#96;name&#96; (text)\n   - &#96;sector&#96; (text)\n   - RLS Policy: Public read access\n\n2. **financials_std**\n   - &#96;id&#96; (uuid, primary key)\n   - &#96;created_at&#96; (timestamptz)\n   - &#96;symbol&#96; (text, foreign key → company.symbol)\n   - &#96;year&#96; (int4)\n   - &#96;revenue&#96; (int8)\n   - &#96;gross_profit&#96; (int8)\n   - RLS Policy: Public read access\n\n## Setup Instructions\n\n### 1. Install Dependencies\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm install\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. Configure Environment Variables\n\nCopy the example environment file:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\ncp .env.local.example .env.local\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThen edit &#96;.env.local&#96; with your Supabase credentials:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;env\nNEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project.supabase.co\nNEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nYou can find these values in your Supabase project:\n1. Go to [Supabase Dashboard](https://app.supabase.com)\n2. Select your project\n3. Navigate to Settings → API\n4. Copy the \"Project URL\" and \"anon/public\" key\n\n### 3. Run the Development Server\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\nnpm run dev\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOpen [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) to see the application.\n\n## Project Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n├── app/\n│   ├── actions/\n│   │   └── financials.ts       # Server action to fetch data\n│   ├── financials/\n│   │   └── page.tsx            # Financials display page\n│   ├── layout.tsx              # Root layout\n│   ├── page.tsx                # Home page\n│   └── globals.css             # Global styles\n├── lib/\n│   ├── database.types.ts       # TypeScript types for Supabase\n│   └── supabase/\n│       ├── client.ts           # Client-side Supabase client",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [

        "contents": "# Testing Setup Guide for Fin Quote\n\n## Overview\n\nThis guide explains how to add automated testing to the Fin Quote codebase. Tests will catch bugs before users see them and give you confidence to refactor code.\n\n**Time to complete**: 2-3 hours for initial setup\n**Ongoing effort**: 5-10 minutes per new feature\n\n---\n\n## Why Test This Codebase?\n\n**You're building a financial accuracy system** where wrong answers can cause:\n- Users making bad investment decisions based on incorrect data\n- Loss of trust and reputation\n- Hours debugging production issues\n\n**Three types of quality control you need**:\n1. ✅ **Validators** (you have) - Runtime checks on LLM outputs\n2. ❌ **Tests** (you need) - Verify YOUR code works correctly\n3. ✅ **Evals** (you have) - Measure overall system performance\n\n---\n\n## What to Test (Priority Order)\n\n### **Priority 1: Validators** (CRITICAL)\n- File: &#96;lib/validators.ts&#96;\n- Why: Core accuracy logic - bugs here = wrong answers to users\n- Test coverage goal: 90%+\n\n### **Priority 2: Metric Resolver** (HIGH)\n- File: &#96;lib/metric-resolver.ts&#96;\n- Why: Maps user phrases to database metrics (\"P/E\" → &#96;peRatio&#96;)\n- Test coverage goal: 90%+\n\n### **Priority 3: Server Actions** (MEDIUM)\n- Files: &#96;app/actions/*.ts&#96;\n- Why: API boundaries, database interactions\n- Test coverage goal: 60%+\n\n### **Priority 4: Chart Helpers** (LOW)\n- File: &#96;lib/chart-helpers.ts&#96;\n- Why: Data transformation for visualizations\n- Test coverage goal: 50%+\n\n---\n\n## Phase 1: Initial Setup (30 minutes)\n\n### Step 1: Install Testing Framework\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Install vitest (modern, fast test runner)\nnpm install -D vitest @vitest/ui\n\n# Install testing utilities\nnpm install -D @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom\n\n# For React component testing (optional, later)\nnpm install -D @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Step 2: Create Vitest Config\n\nCreate &#96;vitest.config.ts&#96; in project root:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'\nimport react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'\nimport path from 'path'",

        "contents": "// Static instructions that will be cached by OpenAI\nconst TOOL_SELECTION_STATIC_PROMPT = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.\n\nAvailable Tools:\n\n1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Financial metrics as NUMBERS over time\n\n   SUPPORTED METRICS:\n\n   Raw Metrics:\n   - revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income\n   - total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity\n   - operating_cash_flow, eps\n\n   Calculated Metrics (✨ Native Support):\n   - debt_to_equity_ratio  (total_liabilities / shareholders_equity)\n   - gross_margin          (gross_profit / revenue × 100)\n   - roe                   (net_income / shareholders_equity × 100)\n\n   METRIC MAPPING (with context clues):\n\n   Income/Profitability:\n   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue\n   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\", \"profitability\" → net_income\n   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\" → eps\n   - \"operating profit\", \"EBIT\" → operating_income\n\n   Valuation Ratios (use getFinancialMetric tool):\n   - \"P/E ratio\", \"PE ratio\", \"price to earnings\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/E\"]\n   - \"P/B ratio\", \"price to book\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/B\"]\n   - \"PEG ratio\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"PEG\"]\n\n   Calculated Ratios (✨ NOW NATIVE - use directly):\n   - \"gross margin\", \"gross profit margin\" → gross_margin\n   - \"ROE\", \"return on equity\" → roe\n   - \"debt to equity\", \"debt-to-equity\", \"D/E ratio\", \"leverage ratio\" → debt_to_equity_ratio\n\n   Balance Sheet (Raw):\n   - \"assets\", \"total assets\" → total_assets\n   - \"liabilities\", \"total debt\", \"debt\" → total_liabilities\n   - \"equity\", \"book value\", \"shareholders equity\" → shareholders_equity\n\n   Cash Flow:\n   - \"operating cash flow\", \"cash from operations\", \"OCF\" → operating_cash_flow\n   - \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\", \"unlevered free cash flow\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool\n   - \"capex\", \"capital expenditures\", \"buybacks\", \"dividends paid\", \"stock-based compensation\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool\n\n   Research &amp; Development:\n   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research and development\", \"R&amp;D spending\", \"R&amp;D expense\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"R&amp;D to revenue\"] or [\"research and development\"]\n\n   Other (use closest available):\n   - \"margins\", \"ratios\" (when not specific) → operating_income\n\n   LIMIT RULES - CRITICAL:\n\n   1. If question asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (2020, 2019, 2015, 2006, etc.) → limit: 20\n      Why: We have 20 years (2006-2025). To find any specific year, fetch all.\n      Examples:\n      - \"net income in 2020\" → limit: 20\n      - \"revenue for 2018\" → limit: 20\n      - \"What was EPS in 2006?\" → limit: 20\n\n   2. If question asks for a YEAR RANGE (2008 to 2020, 2015 to present, etc.) → limit: 20\n      Why: Need all data to filter to the specific range.\n      Examples:\n      - \"net income 2008 to present\" → limit: 20\n      - \"revenue from 2015 to 2020\" → limit: 20\n      - \"EPS between 2010 and 2018\" → limit: 20\n\n   3. If question specifies a NUMBER of years, use that EXACT number:\n      \"last 3 years\" → limit: 3\n      \"past 5 years\" → limit: 5\n      \"last year\" or \"most recent year\" → limit: 1\n      \"10 years\" → limit: 10\n      \"20 years\" → limit: 20\n      \"2 years\" → limit: 2\n\n   4. If question says \"trend\", \"history\", \"over time\" WITHOUT a number → limit: 4\n\n   5. If question says \"all\", \"complete\", \"full history\" → limit: 20\n\n   6. If question is just asking for the metric (no time context) → limit: 4\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"net income in 2006\" → limit: 20 (specific year)\n   - \"revenue over 5 years\" → limit: 5 (number specified)\n   - \"show me net income trend\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"EPS history\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"gross profit\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"all historical data\" → limit: 20 (all data)\n\n   args: {\"metric\": &lt;exact name&gt;, \"limit\": &lt;number 1-20&gt;}\n\n2. getPrices - Stock PRICE history\n\n   ALWAYS use custom date ranges. Calculate the \"from\" date based on the user's request.\n   Today's date is {{TODAY_DATE}} (use this for calculations).\n\n   Date format: YYYY-MM-DD\n   \"to\" is optional (defaults to today)\n\n   CALCULATION EXAMPLES:\n   - \"last 7 days\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-11-01\"} (7 days ago)\n   - \"past month\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-10-08\"} (30 days ago)\n   - \"last 3 months\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-08-08\"} (90 days ago)\n   - \"past year\" → args: {\"from\": \"2024-11-08\"} (365 days ago)\n   - \"YTD\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-01-01\"} (start of current year)\n   - \"last 3 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2022-11-08\"} (3 years ago)\n   - \"past 5 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-11-08\"} (5 years ago)\n   - \"last 7 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-11-08\"} (7 years ago)\n   - \"past 10 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-11-08\"} (10 years ago)\n   - \"last 15 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2010-11-08\"} (15 years ago)\n   - \"past 20 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago)\n   - \"all time\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago, max available)\n\n   EXACT DATE RANGES:\n   - \"from Jan 2020 to June 2023\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-01-01\", \"to\": \"2023-06-30\"}\n   - \"prices between 2015 and 2020\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-01-01\", \"to\": \"2020-12-31\"}\n   - \"from March 2018 to now\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-03-01\"}\n\n   args: {\"from\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\", \"to\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\"}  (to is optional)\n\n3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings metadata ONLY\n\n   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This tool returns ONLY metadata (filing type, date, URL).\n   It does NOT return filing CONTENT or text.\n\n   Use ONLY when:\n   - User wants to know WHEN filings were submitted\n   - User wants to know WHICH filings exist\n   - User wants filing dates/types/URLs\n\n   DO NOT USE when:\n   - User asks WHAT the filing says\n   - User wants content, quotes, or information FROM the filing\n   - User asks about topics like risks, strategy, etc.\n   → Use searchFilings instead for content questions!\n\n   LIMIT RULES:\n\n   1. If question specifies NUMBER of filings → use that number\n      \"last 3 filings\" → limit: 3\n      \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1\n      \"2 years of filings\" → limit: 10 (2 years ≈ 8-10 filings)\n\n   2. If question says \"recent\", \"latest\" (no number) → limit: 5\n\n   3. If question says \"all\", \"available\", \"history\" → limit: 10\n\n   Examples (metadata questions):\n   - \"when was the most recent filing?\" → limit: 1\n   - \"what filings do you have?\" → limit: 5\n   - \"show me filing dates\" → limit: 5\n\n   args: {\"limit\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;}\n\n4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content (for WHAT they say)\n\n   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Use this when user asks about CONTENT, not just dates!\n\n   Use for ANY question about WHAT the filings say:\n   - Risk factors, strategy, operations, business model\n   - Management commentary, outlook, quotes\n   - Products, markets, competition\n   - Governance, compensation\n   - ANY question asking \"what did they say\", \"provide quotes\", etc.\n\n   Even if they mention \"latest 10-K\" or specific filing:\n   - \"What are risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → USE searchFilings\n   - \"What does the 10-K say about AI?\" → USE searchFilings\n   - \"Provide quotes from recent filing\" → USE searchFilings\n\n   QUERY RULES:\n   - Extract key terms from user's question\n   - Keep it simple (1-3 words usually best)\n   - Don't need full sentences\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"What are the risk factors?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}\n   - \"What about risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}\n   - \"Tell me about competition\" → {\"query\": \"competition\", \"limit\": 5}\n   - \"Provide quotes about AI strategy\" → {\"query\": \"AI strategy\", \"limit\": 5}\n   - \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone?\" → {\"query\": \"iPhone\", \"limit\": 5}\n\n   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}\n\n5. listMetrics - DISCOVER available financial metrics\n\n   Use when:\n   - User asks \"what metrics do you have?\"\n   - User wants to browse metrics by category\n   - Uncertain which metric name to use for getFinancialMetric\n\n   CATEGORY FILTER (optional):\n   - Valuation: P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, market cap, etc.\n   - Profitability &amp; Returns: ROE, ROA, ROIC, margins\n   - Growth: revenue growth, EPS growth, asset growth\n   - Leverage &amp; Solvency: debt ratios, liquidity ratios\n   - Efficiency &amp; Working Capital: turnover ratios, cycle days\n   - Capital Returns &amp; Share Data: dividend yield, payout ratio\n   - Per-Share Metrics: EPS, book value per share, cash per share\n   - Market Data: stock metrics, valuation metrics\n   - Other: miscellaneous metrics\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"What valuation metrics do you have?\" → {\"category\": \"Valuation\"}\n   - \"Show me all metrics\" → {} (no category)\n   - \"What debt metrics are available?\" → {\"category\": \"Leverage &amp; Solvency\"}\n\n   args: {\"category\": \"&lt;optional category name&gt;\"}\n\n6. getFinancialMetric - GET advanced financial metrics (139 metrics available)\n\n   COMPLETE METRIC CATALOG (organized by category):\n\n   Valuation (11):\n   - peRatio, priceToBookRatio, priceToSalesRatio, priceToFreeCashFlowsRatio, earningsYield\n   - marketCap, enterpriseValue, evToSales, evToOperatingCashFlow, evToFreeCashFlow, freeCashFlowYield\n\n   Profitability &amp; Returns (12):\n   - grossProfitMargin, operatingProfitMargin, netProfitMargin, ebitPerRevenue, ebitdaMargin, pretaxProfitMargin\n   - returnOnEquity, returnOnAssets, returnOnCapitalEmployed, roic, ebtPerEbit, netIncomePerEBT\n\n   Growth (32):\n   - revenueGrowth, grossProfitGrowth, operatingIncomeGrowth, netIncomeGrowth, ebitgrowth\n   - epsgrowth, epsdilutedGrowth, operatingCashFlowGrowth, freeCashFlowGrowth\n   - assetGrowth, debtGrowth, inventoryGrowth, receivablesGrowth\n   - dividendsperShareGrowth, bookValueperShareGrowth, weightedAverageSharesGrowth, weightedAverageSharesDilutedGrowth\n   - rdexpenseGrowth, sgaexpensesGrowth\n   - threeYRevenueGrowthPerShare, threeYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, threeYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare\n   - threeYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, threeYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare\n   - fiveYRevenueGrowthPerShare, fiveYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, fiveYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare\n   - fiveYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, fiveYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare\n   - tenYRevenueGrowthPerShare, tenYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, tenYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare\n   - tenYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, tenYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare\n\n   Leverage &amp; Solvency (9):\n   - debtEquityRatio, debtRatio, currentRatio, quickRatio, cashRatio\n   - interestCoverage, longTermDebtToCapitalization, totalDebtToCapitalization, cashFlowToDebtRatio\n\n   Efficiency &amp; Working Capital (7):\n   - assetTurnover, fixedAssetTurnover, inventoryTurnover, receivablesTurnover, payablesTurnover\n   - cashConversionCycle, daysOfInventoryOutstanding, daysOfSalesOutstanding, daysOfPayablesOutstanding\n\n   Cash Flow (2):\n   - freeCashFlow, capitalExpenditure\n\n   Capital Returns &amp; Share Data (5):\n   - dividendYield, payoutRatio, dividendsPaid, commonStockRepurchased, numberOfShares\n\n   Per-Share Metrics (7):\n   - bookValuePerShare, cashPerShare, operatingCashFlowPerShare, freeCashFlowPerShare\n   - netIncomePerShare, revenuePerShare, tangibleBookValuePerShare\n\n   Market Data (1):\n   - stockPrice\n\n   Other (53):\n   - Accepts common aliases: \"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"\n   - Can handle multiple metrics in one call\n\n   LIMIT RULES (same as getAaplFinancialsByMetric):\n   - Specific year → limit: 20\n   - \"What's Apple's P/E ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\"], \"limit\": 5}\n   - \"What's the price to book ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"price to book\"], \"limit\": 5}\n   - \"Show me ROE trend\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"ROE\"], \"limit\": 4}\n   - \"Dividend yield for 2023\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"dividend yield\"], \"limit\": 20}\n\n   args: {\"metricNames\": [\"&lt;metric1&gt;\", \"&lt;metric2&gt;\"], \"limit\": &lt;number&gt;}\n\nTOOL SELECTION LOGIC:\n\n1. Basic financial metrics (revenue, assets, eps, etc.)? → getAaplFinancialsByMetric\n2. Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, etc.)? → getFinancialMetric\n3. User asks \"what metrics available\"? → listMetrics\n4. Stock price? → getPrices\n5. Filing metadata ONLY (when/which filings)? → getRecentFilings\n6. Filing CONTENT (what they say, quotes, topics)? → searchFilings\n\n⚠️ KEY DISTINCTION for #6 vs #7:\n- \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)\n- \"What does the latest 10-K say about risks?\" → searchFilings (content)\n- \"Show me recent filings\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)\n- \"What are risk factors in the latest 10-K?\" → searchFilings (content)\n- \"Provide quotes from the 10-K\" → searchFilings (content)\n\nReturn ONLY JSON - examples:\n\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"revenue\",\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"eps\",\"limit\":1}}\n{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"total_liabilities\",\"limit\":4}}\n{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2018-11-15\"}}\n{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2025-01-01\",\"to\":\"2025-11-15\"}}\n{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":3}}\n{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"AI strategy\",\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{\"category\":\"Valuation\"}}\n{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{}}\n{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\"],\"limit\":5}}\n{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"ROE\",\"debt to equity\"],\"limit\":10}}\n\nCRITICAL EXAMPLES - Filing Content vs Metadata:\nQ: \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":1}}\n\nQ: \"What about risk factors in their latest 10k? provide quotes.\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}\n\nQ: \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone sales?\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"iPhone sales\",\"limit\":5}}\n\nQ: \"Provide quotes from the latest filing about competition\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"competition\",\"limit\":5}}\n\nCRITICAL EXAMPLES - Advanced Metrics:\nQ: \"What is AAPL's debt to equity ratio?\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"debt to equity\"],\"limit\":5}}\n\nQ: \"Show me P/E ratio trend\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\"],\"limit\":4}}\n\nQ: \"What's the ROE in 2023?\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"ROE\"],\"limit\":20}}\n\nQ: \"Compare P/E and PEG ratio\"\nA: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\",\"PEG\"],\"limit\":10}}&#96;\n\n// New function that returns structured messages for caching\nexport const buildToolSelectionMessages = (userQuestion: string)",
