          {
            "text": "// Static instructions that will be cached by OpenAI",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "const TOOL_SELECTION_STATIC_PROMPT = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "Available Tools:",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Financial metrics as NUMBERS over time",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "   SUPPORTED METRICS:",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "   Raw Metrics:",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "   - revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "   - total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operating_cash_flow, eps",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "   Calculated Metrics (✨ Native Support):",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debt_to_equity_ratio  (total_liabilities / shareholders_equity)",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   - gross_margin          (gross_profit / revenue × 100)",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   - roe                   (net_income / shareholders_equity × 100)",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC MAPPING (with context clues):",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "   Income/Profitability:",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\", \"profitability\" → net_income",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\" → eps",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"operating profit\", \"EBIT\" → operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "   Valuation Ratios (use getFinancialMetric tool):",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/E ratio\", \"PE ratio\", \"price to earnings\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/E\"]",
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/B ratio\", \"price to book\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/B\"]",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"PEG ratio\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"PEG\"]",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "text": "   Calculated Ratios (✨ NOW NATIVE - use directly):",
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"gross margin\", \"gross profit margin\" → gross_margin",
            "lineNumber": 100
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"ROE\", \"return on equity\" → roe",
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"debt to equity\", \"debt-to-equity\", \"D/E ratio\", \"leverage ratio\" → debt_to_equity_ratio",
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "text": "   Balance Sheet (Raw):",
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"assets\", \"total assets\" → total_assets",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"liabilities\", \"total debt\", \"debt\" → total_liabilities",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"equity\", \"book value\", \"shareholders equity\" → shareholders_equity",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 108
          },
          {
            "text": "   Cash Flow:",
            "lineNumber": 109
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"operating cash flow\", \"cash from operations\", \"OCF\" → operating_cash_flow",
            "lineNumber": 110
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\", \"unlevered free cash flow\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool",
            "lineNumber": 111
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"capex\", \"capital expenditures\", \"buybacks\", \"dividends paid\", \"stock-based compensation\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool",
            "lineNumber": 112
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 113
          },
          {
            "text": "   Research &amp; Development:",
            "lineNumber": 114
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research and development\", \"R&amp;D spending\", \"R&amp;D expense\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"R&amp;D to revenue\"] or [\"research and development\"]",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 116
          },
          {
            "text": "   Other (use closest available):",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"margins\", \"ratios\" (when not specific) → operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 118
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 119
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES - CRITICAL:",
            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 121
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. If question asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (2020, 2019, 2015, 2006, etc.) → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "      Why: We have 20 years (2006-2025). To find any specific year, fetch all.",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "text": "      Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"net income in 2020\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"revenue for 2018\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"What was EPS in 2006?\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 127
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If question asks for a YEAR RANGE (2008 to 2020, 2015 to present, etc.) → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 129
          },
          {
            "text": "      Why: Need all data to filter to the specific range.",
            "lineNumber": 130
          },
          {
            "text": "      Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 131
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"net income 2008 to present\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"revenue from 2015 to 2020\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 133
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"EPS between 2010 and 2018\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 134
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 135
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. If question specifies a NUMBER of years, use that EXACT number:",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last 3 years\" → limit: 3",
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"past 5 years\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last year\" or \"most recent year\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 139
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"10 years\" → limit: 10",
            "lineNumber": 140
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"20 years\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 141
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"2 years\" → limit: 2",
            "lineNumber": 142
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 143
          },
          {
            "text": "   4. If question says \"trend\", \"history\", \"over time\" WITHOUT a number → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 144
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 145
          },
          {
            "text": "   5. If question says \"all\", \"complete\", \"full history\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 146
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 147
          },
          {
            "text": "   6. If question is just asking for the metric (no time context) → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 148
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 149
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"net income in 2006\" → limit: 20 (specific year)",
            "lineNumber": 151
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"revenue over 5 years\" → limit: 5 (number specified)",
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"show me net income trend\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"EPS history\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"gross profit\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 155
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"all historical data\" → limit: 20 (all data)",
            "lineNumber": 156
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"metric\": &lt;exact name&gt;, \"limit\": &lt;number 1-20&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 159
          },
          {
            "text": "2. getPrices - Stock PRICE history",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "   ALWAYS use custom date ranges. Calculate the \"from\" date based on the user's request.",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 3 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2022-11-08\"} (3 years ago)",

          },

          },

          },
          {

          },

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "text": "3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings metadata ONLY",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This tool returns ONLY metadata (filing type, date, URL).",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "   It does NOT return filing CONTENT or text.",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use ONLY when:",
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHEN filings were submitted",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHICH filings exist",
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants filing dates/types/URLs",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "   DO NOT USE when:",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks WHAT the filing says",
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants content, quotes, or information FROM the filing",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks about topics like risks, strategy, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": "   → Use searchFilings instead for content questions!",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. If question specifies NUMBER of filings → use that number",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last 3 filings\" → limit: 3",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"2 years of filings\" → limit: 10 (2 years ≈ 8-10 filings)",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If question says \"recent\", \"latest\" (no number) → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 213
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. If question says \"all\", \"available\", \"history\" → limit: 10",
            "lineNumber": 214
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 215
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples (metadata questions):",
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"when was the most recent filing?\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"what filings do you have?\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"show me filing dates\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"limit\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content (for WHAT they say)",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Use this when user asks about CONTENT, not just dates!",
            "lineNumber": 225
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 226
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use for ANY question about WHAT the filings say:",
            "lineNumber": 227
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Risk factors, strategy, operations, business model",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - Management commentary, outlook, quotes",

          {

          },
          {

          {

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "   Even if they mention \"latest 10-K\" or specific filing:",
            "lineNumber": 234
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → USE searchFilings",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about AI?\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 236
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes from recent filing\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 237
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 238
          },
          {
            "text": "   QUERY RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 239
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Extract key terms from user's question",
            "lineNumber": 240
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Keep it simple (1-3 words usually best)",
            "lineNumber": 241
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Don't need full sentences",
            "lineNumber": 242
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 243
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are the risk factors?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 245
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What about risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 246
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Tell me about competition\" → {\"query\": \"competition\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 247
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes about AI strategy\" → {\"query\": \"AI strategy\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 248
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone?\" → {\"query\": \"iPhone\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 249
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 250
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 251
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 252
          },
          {
            "text": "5. listMetrics - DISCOVER available financial metrics",
            "lineNumber": 253
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 254
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use when:",
            "lineNumber": 255
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks \"what metrics do you have?\"",
            "lineNumber": 256
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to browse metrics by category",
            "lineNumber": 257
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Uncertain which metric name to use for getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 259
          },
          {
            "text": "   CATEGORY FILTER (optional):",
            "lineNumber": 260
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Valuation: P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, market cap, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 261
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Profitability &amp; Returns: ROE, ROA, ROIC, margins",
            "lineNumber": 262
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Growth: revenue growth, EPS growth, asset growth",
            "lineNumber": 263
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Leverage &amp; Solvency: debt ratios, liquidity ratios",
            "lineNumber": 264
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Efficiency &amp; Working Capital: turnover ratios, cycle days",
            "lineNumber": 265
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Capital Returns &amp; Share Data: dividend yield, payout ratio",
            "lineNumber": 266
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Per-Share Metrics: EPS, book value per share, cash per share",
            "lineNumber": 267
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Market Data: stock metrics, valuation metrics",
            "lineNumber": 268
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Other: miscellaneous metrics",
            "lineNumber": 269
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 271
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What valuation metrics do you have?\" → {\"category\": \"Valuation\"}",
            "lineNumber": 272
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me all metrics\" → {} (no category)",
            "lineNumber": 273
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What debt metrics are available?\" → {\"category\": \"Leverage &amp; Solvency\"}",
            "lineNumber": 274
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 275
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"category\": \"&lt;optional category name&gt;\"}",
            "lineNumber": 276
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 277
          },
          {
            "text": "6. getFinancialMetric - GET advanced financial metrics (139 metrics available)",
            "lineNumber": 278
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 279
          },
          {
            "text": "   COMPLETE METRIC CATALOG (organized by category):",
            "lineNumber": 280
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 281
          },
          {
            "text": "   Valuation (11):",
            "lineNumber": 282
          },
          {
            "text": "   - peRatio, priceToBookRatio, priceToSalesRatio, priceToFreeCashFlowsRatio, earningsYield",
            "lineNumber": 283
          },
          {
            "text": "   - marketCap, enterpriseValue, evToSales, evToOperatingCashFlow, evToFreeCashFlow, freeCashFlowYield",
            "lineNumber": 284
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 285
          },
          {
            "text": "   Profitability &amp; Returns (12):",
            "lineNumber": 286
          },
          {
            "text": "   - grossProfitMargin, operatingProfitMargin, netProfitMargin, ebitPerRevenue, ebitdaMargin, pretaxProfitMargin",
            "lineNumber": 287
          },
          {
            "text": "   - returnOnEquity, returnOnAssets, returnOnCapitalEmployed, roic, ebtPerEbit, netIncomePerEBT",
            "lineNumber": 288
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 289
          },
          {
            "text": "   Growth (32):",
            "lineNumber": 290
          },
          {
            "text": "   - revenueGrowth, grossProfitGrowth, operatingIncomeGrowth, netIncomeGrowth, ebitgrowth",
            "lineNumber": 291
          },
          {
            "text": "   - epsgrowth, epsdilutedGrowth, operatingCashFlowGrowth, freeCashFlowGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 292
          },
          {
            "text": "   - assetGrowth, debtGrowth, inventoryGrowth, receivablesGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 293
          },
          {
            "text": "   - dividendsperShareGrowth, bookValueperShareGrowth, weightedAverageSharesGrowth, weightedAverageSharesDilutedGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 294
          },
          {
            "text": "   - rdexpenseGrowth, sgaexpensesGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 295
          },
          {
            "text": "   - threeYRevenueGrowthPerShare, threeYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, threeYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 296
          },
          {
            "text": "   - threeYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, threeYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 297
          },
          {
            "text": "   - fiveYRevenueGrowthPerShare, fiveYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, fiveYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 298
          },
          {
            "text": "   - fiveYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, fiveYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 299
          },
          {
            "text": "   - tenYRevenueGrowthPerShare, tenYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, tenYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 300
          },
          {
            "text": "   - tenYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, tenYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 301
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 302
          },
          {
            "text": "   Leverage &amp; Solvency (9):",
            "lineNumber": 303
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debtEquityRatio, debtRatio, currentRatio, quickRatio, cashRatio",
            "lineNumber": 304
          },
          {
            "text": "   - interestCoverage, longTermDebtToCapitalization, totalDebtToCapitalization, cashFlowToDebtRatio",
            "lineNumber": 305
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 306
          },
          {
            "text": "   Efficiency &amp; Working Capital (7):",
            "lineNumber": 307
          },
          {
            "text": "   - assetTurnover, fixedAssetTurnover, inventoryTurnover, receivablesTurnover, payablesTurnover",
            "lineNumber": 308
          },
          {
            "text": "   - cashConversionCycle, daysOfInventoryOutstanding, daysOfSalesOutstanding, daysOfPayablesOutstanding",
            "lineNumber": 309
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 310
          },
          {
            "text": "   Cash Flow (2):",
            "lineNumber": 311
          },
          {
            "text": "   - freeCashFlow, capitalExpenditure",
            "lineNumber": 312
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 313
          },
          {
            "text": "   Capital Returns &amp; Share Data (5):",
            "lineNumber": 314
          },
          {
            "text": "   - dividendYield, payoutRatio, dividendsPaid, commonStockRepurchased, numberOfShares",
            "lineNumber": 315
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 316
          },
          {
            "text": "   Per-Share Metrics (7):",
            "lineNumber": 317
          },
          {
            "text": "   - bookValuePerShare, cashPerShare, operatingCashFlowPerShare, freeCashFlowPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 318
          },
          {
            "text": "   - netIncomePerShare, revenuePerShare, tangibleBookValuePerShare",
            "lineNumber": 319
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 320
          },
          {
            "text": "   Market Data (1):",
            "lineNumber": 321
          },
          {
            "text": "   - stockPrice",
            "lineNumber": 322
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 323
          },
          {
            "text": "   Other (53):",
            "lineNumber": 324
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ebitda, stockBasedCompensation, depreciationAndAmortization, workingCapital, effectiveTaxRate",
            "lineNumber": 325
          },
          {
            "text": "   - marketCapitalization, enterpriseValueMultiple, enterpriseValueOverEBITDA",
            "lineNumber": 326
          },
          {
            "text": "   - pbRatio, pfcfRatio, pocfratio, priceBookValueRatio, priceCashFlowRatio, priceEarningsRatio",
            "lineNumber": 327
          },
          {
            "text": "   - priceEarningsToGrowthRatio, priceFairValue, priceSalesRatio, priceToOperatingCashFlowsRatio, ptbRatio",
            "lineNumber": 328
          },
          {
            "text": "   - roe, returnOnTangibleAssets",
            "lineNumber": 329
          },
          {
            "text": "   - researchAndDdevelopementToRevenue, salesGeneralAndAdministrativeToRevenue, stockBasedCompensationToRevenue",
            "lineNumber": 330
          },
          {
            "text": "   - capexPerShare, capexToDepreciation, capexToOperatingCashFlow, capexToRevenue",
            "lineNumber": 331
          },
          {
            "text": "   - shareholdersEquityPerShare, tangibleAssetValue, investedCapital",
            "lineNumber": 332
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debtToAssets, debtToEquity, netDebtToEBITDA",
            "lineNumber": 333
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operatingCashFlowSalesRatio, freeCashFlowOperatingCashFlowRatio",
            "lineNumber": 334
          },
          {
            "text": "   - cashFlowCoverageRatios, capitalExpenditureCoverageRatio, dividendPaidAndCapexCoverageRatio, shortTermCoverageRatios",
            "lineNumber": 335
          },
          {
            "text": "   - dividendPayoutRatio, interestDebtPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 336
          },
          {
            "text": "   - companyEquityMultiplier, intangiblesToTotalAssets",
            "lineNumber": 337
          },
          {
            "text": "   - daysOfInventoryOnHand, daysPayablesOutstanding, daysSalesOutstanding, operatingCycle",
            "lineNumber": 338
          },
          {
            "text": "   - incomeQuality, grahamNumber, grahamNetNet, netCurrentAssetValue",
            "lineNumber": 339
          },
          {
            "text": "   - averageInventory, averagePayables, averageReceivables",
            "lineNumber": 340
          },
          {
            "text": "   - addTotalDebt, minusCashAndCashEquivalents",
            "lineNumber": 341
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 342
          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC NAME FLEXIBILITY:",
            "lineNumber": 343
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Accepts canonical names: \"peRatio\", \"returnOnEquity\", \"debtEquityRatio\"",
            "lineNumber": 344
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Accepts common aliases: \"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"",
            "lineNumber": 345
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Can handle multiple metrics in one call",
            "lineNumber": 346
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 347
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES (same as getAaplFinancialsByMetric):",
            "lineNumber": 348
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Specific year → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 349
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Number specified → use that number",
            "lineNumber": 350
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"trend\", \"history\" → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 351
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"compare\" with multiple metrics → limit: 10 (show more history for comparisons)",
            "lineNumber": 352
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Default → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 353
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 354
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 355
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's Apple's P/E ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 356
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's the price to book ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"price to book\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 357
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me ROE trend\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"ROE\"], \"limit\": 4}",
            "lineNumber": 358
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's Apple's free cash flow?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"free cash flow\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 359
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"How much did Apple spend on buybacks?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"buybacks\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 360
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me capex trend\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"capex\"], \"limit\": 4}",
            "lineNumber": 361
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Compare P/E, ROE, and debt to equity\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"], \"limit\": 10}",
            "lineNumber": 362
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Compare P/E and ROE\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\", \"ROE\"], \"limit\": 10}",
            "lineNumber": 363
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Dividend yield for 2023\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"dividend yield\"], \"limit\": 20}",
            "lineNumber": 364
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 365
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"metricNames\": [\"&lt;metric1&gt;\", \"&lt;metric2&gt;\"], \"limit\": &lt;number&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 366
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 367
          },
          {
            "text": "TOOL SELECTION LOGIC:",
            "lineNumber": 368
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 369
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Basic financial metrics (revenue, assets, eps, etc.)? → getAaplFinancialsByMetric",
            "lineNumber": 370
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, etc.)? → getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 371
          },
          {
            "text": "3. User asks \"what metrics available\"? → listMetrics",
            "lineNumber": 372
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Stock price? → getPrices",
            "lineNumber": 373
          },
          {
            "text": "5. Filing metadata ONLY (when/which filings)? → getRecentFilings",
            "lineNumber": 374
          },
          {
            "text": "6. Filing CONTENT (what they say, quotes, topics)? → searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 375
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 376
          },
          {
            "text": "⚠️ KEY DISTINCTION for #6 vs #7:",
            "lineNumber": 377
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)",
            "lineNumber": 378
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"What does the latest 10-K say about risks?\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 379
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"Show me recent filings\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)",
            "lineNumber": 380
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"What are risk factors in the latest 10-K?\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 381
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"Provide quotes from the 10-K\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 382
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 383
          },
          {
            "text": "Return ONLY JSON - examples:",
            "lineNumber": 384
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 385
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"revenue\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 386
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"eps\",\"limit\":1}}",
            "lineNumber": 387
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"total_liabilities\",\"limit\":4}}",
            "lineNumber": 388
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2018-11-15\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 389
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2025-01-01\",\"to\":\"2025-11-15\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 390
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":3}}",
            "lineNumber": 391
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 392
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"AI strategy\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 393
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{\"category\":\"Valuation\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 394
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{}}",
            "lineNumber": 395
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\"],\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 396
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"ROE\",\"debt to equity\"],\"limit\":10}}",
            "lineNumber": 397
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 398
          },
          {
            "text": "CRITICAL EXAMPLES - Filing Content vs Metadata:",
            "lineNumber": 399
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\"",
            "lineNumber": 400
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":1}}",
            "lineNumber": 401
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 402
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"What about risk factors in their latest 10k? provide quotes.\"",
            "lineNumber": 403
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 404
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 405
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone sales?\"",
            "lineNumber": 406
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"iPhone sales\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 407
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 408
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"Provide quotes from the latest filing about competition\"",
            "lineNumber": 409
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"competition\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 410
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 411
          },
          {
            "text": "CRITICAL EXAMPLES - Advanced Metrics:",
            "lineNumber": 412
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"What is AAPL's debt to equity ratio?\"",
            "lineNumber": 413
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"debt to equity\"],\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 414
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 415
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"Show me P/E ratio trend\"",
            "lineNumber": 416
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\"],\"limit\":4}}",
            "lineNumber": 417
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 418
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"What's the ROE in 2023?\"",
            "lineNumber": 419
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"ROE\"],\"limit\":20}}",
            "lineNumber": 420
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 421
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"Compare P/E and PEG ratio\"",
            "lineNumber": 422
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\",\"PEG\"],\"limit\":10}}&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 423
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 424
          },
          {
            "text": "// New function that returns structured messages for caching",
            "lineNumber": 425
          },
          {
            "text": "export const buildToolSelectionMessages = (userQuestion: string)",
            "lineNumber": 426
          }
        ]

Created a learning roadmap. Here's what to focus on next:

## Top 4 things to learn next

### 1. Async/Await & Promises (most important)
Why: Almost everything in your codebase uses this.

```typescript
// You'll see this everywhere:
const data = await getAaplFinancialsByMetric()  // ← What does "await" mean?
const result = await askQuestion(question)       // ← Why is it needed?
```

What to learn:
- `async` functions
- `await` keyword
- `Promise.all()` for parallel operations
- How to handle errors

Time: 2-3 hours

---

### 2. TypeScript basics
Why: Your entire codebase is TypeScript.

```typescript
// You'll see types everywhere:
const [question, setQuestion] = useState<string>('')  // ← What does :string mean?
const data: MarketData | null = null                 // ← What's | null?
```

What to learn:
- Type annotations (`: string`, `: number`)
- Interfaces (defining object shapes)
- Union types (`string | null`)
- Why types help catch errors

Time: 3-4 hours

---

### 3. Error handling (try/catch)
Why: Everything can fail - you need to handle it.

```typescript
// You'll see this pattern everywhere:
try {
  const data = await fetchData()
  return { data, error: null }
} catch (err) {
  return { data: null, error: err.message }
}
```

What to learn:
- `try/catch` blocks
- How to return errors
- The `{ data, error }` pattern your codebase uses

Time: 1-2 hours

---

### 4. Database queries (Supabase)
Why: Most of your data comes from the database.

```typescript
// You'll see queries like this:
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from('financials_std')
  .select('*')
  .eq('symbol', 'AAPL')
  .limit(5)
```

What to learn:
- Supabase query syntax
- `.from()`, `.select()`, `.eq()`, `.limit()`
- How to check for errors

Time: 2-3 hours

---

## Recommended learning order

Week 1:
1. Async/Await (2-3 hours) — most critical
2. TypeScript basics (3-4 hours) — very important
3. Error handling (1-2 hours) — important

Week 2:
4. Database queries (2-3 hours) — important
5. API routes vs server actions (1-2 hours) — helpful

---

## Quick start: async/await

This is the most important one. Here's a simple example:

```typescript
// Without async/await (old way):
fetchData().then(data => {
  console.log(data)
}).catch(error => {
  console.error(error)
})

// With async/await (your codebase):
try {
  const data = await fetchData()  // Wait for it to finish
  console.log(data)
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error)
}
```

Your codebase uses async/await everywhere, so learn this first.

- Priority order

Focus on these 4 first:
1. Async/Await — everything uses it
2. TypeScript — your codebase is TypeScript

4. Database queries — how you get data

The rest (API routes, streaming, advanced TypeScript) can wait.

Explaining async/await in plain English, then showing examples from your code.

## What is async/await? (Plain English)

Some operations take time:
- Fetching data from a database
- Calling an API
- Reading a file

Without async/await, your code would freeze while waiting. With async/await, you can wait for these operations without blocking.

---

## The problem: slow operations

Imagine ordering food:
- Without async/await: you wait at the counter until it’s ready (blocking).
- With async/await: you order, do other things, then pick it up when ready (non-blocking).

---

## How it works (3 steps)

### Step 1: Mark the function as `async`
```typescript
async function fetchData() {  // ← "async" means this function can wait
  // ...
}
```

### Step 2: Use `await` before slow operations
```typescript
const data = await getDataFromDatabase()  // ← "await" means "wait here until done"
```

### Step 3: The code waits, then continues
```typescript
const data = await getDataFromDatabase()  // Wait here...
console.log(data)  // ...then continue here once data is ready
```

---

## Real example from your code

From `app/actions/ask-question.ts`:

```typescript
// Line 327: This calls OpenAI API (slow operation)
const selectionResponse = await openai.responses.create({
  model: 'gpt-4o-mini',
  input: selectionInput,
  // ...
})

// This line waits until OpenAI responds, THEN continues
toolSelectionPromptTokens = selectionResponse.usage?.input_tokens
```

What happens:
1. Code reaches `await openai.responses.create(...)`
2. It waits for OpenAI to respond (could be 1-3 seconds)
3. Once done, it stores the result in `selectionResponse`
4. Then continues to the next line

---

## Another example: parallel operations

From `app/market/page.tsx` (line 64):

```typescript
// Fetch 11 different things at the SAME TIME
const [spxResult, nasdaqResult, dowResult, ...] = await Promise.all([
  getAaplMarketData(),      // Fetch #1
  getNasdaqMarketData(),    // Fetch #2
  getDowMarketData(),       // Fetch #3
  // ... 8 more
])
```

What happens:
- `Promise.all()` runs all 11 operations at once
- `await` waits until all finish
- Then you get all results together

Without `Promise.all()`, you’d wait for each one to finish before starting the next (much slower).

---

## Error handling: try/catch

Slow operations can fail. Use try/catch:

```typescript
try {
  const data = await fetchData()  // Try to get data
  console.log(data)                // If successful, use it
} catch (error) {
  console.error('Failed!', error)  // If it fails, handle the error
}
```

From your code (line 286 in `ask-question.ts`):
```typescript
try {
  // All the slow operations here
  const selectionResponse = await openai.responses.create(...)
  // ... more await calls
} catch (err) {
  // If anything fails, handle it here
  return { error: err.message }
}
```

---

## Key takeaways

1. `async` marks a function that can wait
2. `await` pauses until a slow operation finishes
3. Use `try/catch` to handle errors
4. Use `Promise.all()` to run multiple things in parallel

---

## Why your codebase uses it everywhere

- Database queries are slow
- API calls are slow
- LLM calls are slow

Without async/await, the app would freeze during these operations. With it, the app can handle other work while waiting.

---

## Quick mental model

Think of `await` like waiting for a package:
```typescript
// Without await (wrong):
const package = orderPackage()  // You get a "promise" to deliver, not the package!
console.log(package)            // This runs immediately (package not here yet!)

// With await (correct):
const package = await orderPackage()  // Wait for delivery
console.log(package)                 // Now you have the actual package!
```

---

                  "lineNumber": 4542,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"## The Real Issue (What We Haven't Tried Yet)\\n\\n### Root Cause: Package Incompatibility\\nWe're using **&amp;#96;@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs&amp;#96;** which is **deprecated and incompatible with Next.js 15**.\\n\\nThe auth helpers package:\\n- Was designed for Next.js 13/14\\n- Doesn't properly handle cookies in Next.js 15's App Router\\n- Creates multiple client instances that don't share storage\\n- May be storing sessions in localStorage instead of cookies\\n\\n### Evidence:\\n1. **Multiple client instances**: We're creating separate Supabase clients in each component using &amp;#96;createClientComponentClient()&amp;#96;, which may not share the same storage mechanism\\n2. **Cookie storage not working**: The middleware uses &amp;#96;@supabase/ssr&amp;#96; but components use &amp;#96;@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs&amp;#96;, creating a mismatch\\n3. **Session found in auth page but lost after redirect**: Suggests the session is in memory/localStorage but not in cookies that persist across navigation\\n\\n---\\n\\n## The Solution We Need to Implement\\n\\n### Step 1: Remove &amp;#96;@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs&amp;#96;\\nUninstall the deprecated package:\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;bash\\nnpm uninstall @supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n### Step 2: Use &amp;#96;@supabase/ssr&amp;#96; Everywhere\\nCreate proper client utilities using &amp;#96;@supabase/ssr&amp;#96;:\\n\\n**File: &amp;#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&amp;#96;** (Browser Client)\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;typescript\\nimport { createBrowserClient } from '@supabase/ssr'\\nimport type { Database } from '@/lib/database.types'\\n\\nexport function createClient() {\\n  return createBrowserClient&amp;lt;Database&amp;gt;(\\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,\\n    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!\\n  )\\n}\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n**File: &amp;#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&amp;#96;** (Already using &amp;#96;@supabase/ssr&amp;#96; in middleware)\\n- Keep the current middleware implementation\\n- Update server client to use &amp;#96;@supabase/ssr&amp;#96; instead of &amp;#96;@supabase/supabase-js&amp;#96;\\n\\n### Step 3: Update All Components\\nReplace all instances of:\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;typescript\\nimport { createClientComponentClient } from '@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs'\\nconst supabase = createClientComponentClient&amp;lt;Database&amp;gt;()\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\nWith:\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;typescript\\nimport { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/client'\\nconst supabase = createClient()\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n**Files to update:**\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 5814,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"- Optimize performance and API efficiency\\n- Write tests and improve code quality\\n- Debug and fix issues as they arise\\n- Potentially integrate additional data sources\\n\\n### Project Stats\\n\\n- ~30+ server actions\\n- ~20+ API routes\\n- ~40+ React components\\n- ~130 files in the watchlist package\\n- Well-documented codebase with comprehensive CLAUDE.md\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Requirements\\n\\n### Must Have\\n\\n- **3+ years** with React and TypeScript\\n- Strong experience with **Next.js** (App Router, Server Actions, API Routes)\\n- Experience with **PostgreSQL** and Supabase (or similar like Firebase)\\n- Understanding of REST APIs and data fetching patterns\\n- Clean code practices and attention to detail\\n- Good English communication skills\\n- Available for at least **15-20 hours/week**\\n\\n### Nice to Have\\n\\n- Experience with **OpenAI API** or other LLM integrations\\n- Knowledge of **prompt engineering** and AI application development\\n- Familiarity with **vector databases** and RAG patterns\\n- Experience with **financial data** or fintech applications\\n- Experience with JavaScript charting libraries (Highcharts, TradingView Lightweight Charts, Chart.js, D3, Recharts, etc.)\\n- Knowledge of real-time data patterns (WebSockets, polling)\\n- Experience with monorepo setups (npm workspaces, Turborepo)\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Engagement Details\\n\\n| Detail | Info |\\n|--------|------|\\n| **Type** | Ongoing contract (part-time to start, potential full-time) |\\n| **Hours** | 15-20 hours/week (flexible) |\\n| **Duration** | 3+ months, ongoing |\\n| **Timezone** | Flexible, but some overlap with US Eastern preferred |\\n| **Communication** | Slack/Discord for async, weekly video calls |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## How to Apply\\n\\nPlease include in your proposal:\\n\\n1. **Brief intro** - Tell me about yourself and your relevant experience\\n\\n2. **Next.js/React experience** - Share 1-2 projects you've built with Next.js (App Router preferred). GitHub links or live demos are great.\\n\\n3. **AI/LLM experience** (if any) - Have you integrated OpenAI or other LLMs into applications? Briefly describe.\\n\\n4. **Supabase/Database experience** - What databases have you worked with? Any Supabase or Firebase experience?\","

                {
                  "lineNumber": 7489,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# CLAUDE.md\\n\\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\\n\\n## Project Overview\\n\\n**Fin Quote** is a Next.js-based financial data platform with an AI-powered Q&amp;amp;A chatbot that answers natural language questions about Apple (AAPL) stock. The system uses a two-step LLM architecture with tool selection, data execution, answer generation, and validation.\\n\\n**Core Design Philosophy:**\\n- **Safety First**: LLMs cannot execute arbitrary database queries. Instead, they select from a whitelist of pre-built \\\"tools\\\" (server actions) with validated inputs.\\n- **Server-Side Intelligence**: All LLM calls, database queries, and validation logic run server-side. The browser only handles UI.\\n- **Grounded Answers**: The LLM must use only fetched data; no external knowledge or hallucinations allowed.\\n- **Validation Pipeline**: All answers are validated against source data for number accuracy, year correctness, and citation validity, with auto-regeneration on failures.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\n### Two-Step LLM Flow\\n\\nEvery user question follows this pattern (implemented in &amp;#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&amp;#96;):\\n\\n1. **Tool Selection** (lines 258-330)\\n   - LLM receives question + conversation history + tool menu\\n   - Returns JSON: &amp;#96;{\\\"tool\\\": \\\"toolName\\\", \\\"args\\\": {...}}&amp;#96;\\n   - Model: Uses &amp;#96;OPENAI_MODEL&amp;#96; (default: &amp;#96;gpt-5-nano&amp;#96;)\\n   - Tokens tracked for cost analysis\\n\\n2. **Tool Execution** (lines 332-575)\\n   - Server validates tool + args\\n   - Executes corresponding server action\\n   - Returns structured data (financials, prices, filings, passages, or metrics)\\n\\n3. **Answer Generation** (lines 579-650)\\n   - LLM receives question + fetched facts + conversation history\\n   - Generates grounded answer using only provided data\\n   - Plain text output (no Markdown, bullets, or tables)\\n   - Context: Last 10 messages (tool selection) or 4 messages (answer generation for gpt-5)\\n\\n4. **Validation &amp;amp; Auto-Correction** (lines 653-796)\\n   - Validates numbers, years, and filing citations\","
                },
                {

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"        &amp;amp;quot;diffString&amp;amp;quot;: &amp;amp;quot;- \\\\n+ ## Reasoning Visibility Implementation Plan (Reasoning Summary, Tool Trace, Scratchpad)\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ### Why we’re adding this\\\\n+ - Improve trust and debuggability: Users (and admins) can see how an answer was produced without exposing sensitive internal prompts or raw chain-of-thought.\\\\n+ - Faster iteration: Tool traces reveal where latency comes from and which retrievals/citations drive answers.\\\\n+ - Safer transparency: Show a short Reasoning Summary to users; keep deeper internal notes (Scratchpad) behind an admin-only toggle and never persist them.\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ### Goals (what success looks like)\\\\n+ - Reasoning Summary (2–5 bullets) appears under each assistant response by default.\\\\n+ - Tool Trace shows tools executed, inputs (redacted), durations, and top citations; collapsible by default.\\\\n+ - Scratchpad (hidden chain-of-thought) is viewable only by admins, behind a toggle, and never saved to the database or logs.\\\\n+ - No PII/secrets leakage; token overhead capped; negligible latency impact (&amp;amp;lt;150 ms CPU for parsing/instrumentation).\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ### Non‑Goals\\\\n+ - Do not expose or store long chain-of-thought for non-admin users.\\\\n+ - Do not change retrieval ranking logic or embeddings configuration as part of this feature.\\\\n+ - Do not introduce new analytics dependencies; we will reuse existing logging where possible.\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ---\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ## UX and UI\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ### Surfaces\\\\n+ - Chat message detail block (beneath each assistant message):\\\\n+   - Reasoning Summary: bullet list, always visible when “Show reasoning” is on (default on).\\\\n+   - Tool Trace: collapsible details (default collapsed). Shows each step with name, duration, and high-level result info.\\\\n+   - Scratchpad: Admin-only sub-toggle “Show scratchpad (debug)”. Hidden by default; visible only if current user is admin.\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ### Controls\\\\n+ - Global toggle in chat UI header or settings pane:\\\\n+   - “Show reasoning” (on/off). On shows Reasoning Summary + Tool Trace.\\\\n+   - If user.isAdmin: nested “Show scratchpad (debug)” toggle; default off.\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ### Presentation\\\\n+ - Reasoning Summary: 2–5 short bullets, plain text. No secrets, no prompts, no identifiers.\\\\n+ - Tool Trace (collapsible):\\\\n+   - Step list with: tool name, args (redacted), durationMs, resultCount or top citations.\\\\n+   - For search results: show filing type/date/section and a short snippet. Avoid long payloads.\\\\n+ - Scratchpad (admin-only, collapsible):\\\\n+   - Monospace preformatted block, limited to ~200 tokens.\\\\n+   - Display a caution banner (“Debug view — not user facing. Not stored.”).\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ---\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ## API and Data Model\\\\n+ \\\\n+ ### Response envelope (server → client)\\\\n+ &amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;json\\\\n+ {\\\\n+   \\\\&amp;amp;quot;answer\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;final text\\\\&amp;amp;quot;,\\\\n+   \\\\&amp;amp;quot;reasoningSummary\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: [\\\\&amp;amp;quot;Selected filing content search\\\\&amp;amp;quot;, \\\\&amp;amp;quot;Filtered to 2024 10‑K\\\\&amp;amp;quot;, \\\\&amp;amp;quot;Quoted Item 1A\\\\&amp;amp;quot;],\\\\n+   \\\\&amp;amp;quot;toolTrace\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: [\\\\n+     {\\\\n+       \\\\&amp;amp;quot;tool\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;searchFilings\\\\&amp;amp;quot;,\\\\n+       \\\\&amp;amp;quot;args\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: {\\\\&amp;amp;quot;query\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;risk factors\\\\&amp;amp;quot;},       // redact sensitive fields\\\\n+       \\\\&amp;amp;quot;durationMs\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: 412,\\\\n+       \\\\&amp;amp;quot;results\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: 5,\\\\n+       \\\\&amp;amp;quot;topCitations\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: [\\\\n+         {\\\\&amp;amp;quot;filing\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;10-K\\\\&amp;amp;quot;, \\\\&amp;amp;quot;date\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;2024-11-01\\\\&amp;amp;quot;, \\\\&amp;amp;quot;section\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;Item 1A\\\\&amp;amp;quot;}\\\\n+       ]\\\\n+     }\\\\n+   ],\\\\n+   \\\\&amp;amp;quot;scratchpad\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;lt;private notes&amp;amp;gt;\\\\&amp;amp;quot;,             // only included if admin + flag\\\\n+   \\\\&amp;amp;quot;citations\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: [\\\\n+     {\\\\&amp;amp;quot;filing\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;10-K\\\\&amp;amp;quot;, \\\\&amp;amp;quot;date\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;2024-11-01\\\\&amp;amp;quot;, \\\\&amp;amp;quot;section\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;Item 1A\\\\&amp;amp;quot;, \\\\&amp;amp;quot;anchor\\\\&amp;amp;quot;: \\\\&amp;amp;quot;#risk-factors\\\\&amp;amp;quot;}\\\\n+   ]\\\\n+ }\\\\n+ &amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;&amp;amp;#96;\\\\n+ \\\\n+ Notes:\\\\n+ -                 {
                  "lineNumber": 20498,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I see that the onChange handlers call onUpdate which sets the state and schedules a save. That's great, as long as it only happens with user changes and not during rendering. The QuestionCard props use &amp;#96;annotation={annotationsData?.annotations.find(...)}&amp;#96; correctly, with no setState issues. However, in &amp;#96;loadAnnotations&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;setAnnotationsData(data)&amp;#96; expects AnnotationsFile but assigns data from &amp;#96;response.json()&amp;#96;. This might create a bug since &amp;#96;setAnnotationsData(data.annotations)&amp;#96; could lead to a type mismatch, affecting evaluationData. But I think the error mainly relates to evaluationData and not annotationsData; still, the warning could tie back.\""
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 20502,
                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I’m noticing a React warning about updating a component while rendering another one, which could stem from calling &amp;#96;setCurrentQuestionIndex&amp;#96; within the &amp;#96;handleDone&amp;#96; event handler.                   "lineNumber": 27706,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# Evaluation System: Complete Workflow Guide\\n\\nThis guide shows you how to use all three evaluation features together to improve your AI's accuracy and answer quality.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Overview: What You Have\\n\\nYour evaluation system has three powerful features:\\n\\n1. **Fast/Full Evaluation** - Test tool selection and answer generation\\n2. **LLM-as-Judge** - Automatic answer quality grading using GPT-4\\n3. **HTML Reports** - Beautiful visual reports you can share\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Quick Reference\\n\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;bash\\n# Fast mode (routing only) - 2-3 minutes\\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast\\n\\n# Full mode (with answer generation) - 8-10 minutes\\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode full\\n\\n# Full mode with LLM-as-judge - 15-20 minutes\\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode full --llm-judge\\n\\n# Test with limited questions (faster for iteration)\\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast --limit 10\\n\\n# Generate HTML report from results\\nnpx tsx scripts/generate-html-report.ts test-data/test-results/eval-*.json\\n\\n# Demo LLM-as-judge\\nnpx tsx scripts/test-llm-judge.ts\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Feature Comparison\\n\\n| Feature | Fast Mode | Full Mode | Full + LLM-Judge |\\n|---------|-----------|-----------|------------------|\\n| **Tests tool selection** | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |\\n| **Tests answer generation** | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |\\n| **Evaluates answer quality** | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ |\\n| **Time (100 questions)** | 2-3 min | 8-10 min | 15-20 min |\\n| **Cost (approx)** | $0.02 | $0.10 | $0.60 |\\n| **Best for** | Daily iteration | Pre-deployment | Final validation |\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Complete Workflow Example\\n\\n### Scenario: You Want to Improve Your Prompts\\n\\n**WEEK 1: Establish Baseline**\\n\\n#### Step 1: Run Fast Evaluation\\n\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;bash\\nnpx tsx scripts/evaluate.ts --mode fast\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n**Output:**\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n📊 EVALUATION SUMMARY\\nTotal Questions: 100\\nCorrect Tool: 95 (95.0%)\\nCorrect Args: 83 (83.0%)\\nFully Correct: 83 (83.0%)\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;\\n\\n**What this tells you:**\\n- ✅ 95% tool selection accuracy (good!)\\n- ⚠️ 83% overall accuracy (room for improvement in args)\\n\\n#### Step 2: Generate HTML Report\\n\\n&amp;#96;&amp;#96;&amp;#96;bash\\n# Find the latest results file\","

                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"async function evaluate(mode: 'fast' | 'full', limit?: number, useLLMJudge = false) {\\n\\n  if (useLLMJudge) {\\n    const scores = results\\n      .filter((r) =&amp;gt; r.quality_score !== undefined)\\n      .map((r) =&amp;gt; r.quality_score!)\\n    const stats = calculateQualityStats(scores)\\n    qualityStats = {\\n      avg_accuracy: stats.avgAccuracy,\\n      avg_relevance: stats.avgRelevance,\\n      avg_completeness: stats.avgCompleteness,\\n      avg_insight: stats.avgInsight,\\n      avg_overall: stats.avgOverall,\\n      excellent_count: stats.excellentCount,\\n      good_count: stats.goodCount,\\n      poor_count: stats.poorCount,\\n    }\\n  }\\n\\n  // Build final results\\n  const evaluationResults: EvaluationResults = {\\n    mode,\\n    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\\n    total_questions: total,\\n    correct_tool: correctTool,\\n    correct_args: correctArgs,\\n    correct_args_semantic: correctArgsSemantic,\\n    fully_correct: fullyCorrect,\\n    fully_correct_semantic: fullyCorrectSemantic,\\n    accuracy,\\n    results,\\n    llm_judge_enabled: useLLMJudge,\\n    quality_stats: qualityStats,\\n  }\\n\\n  // Save results\\n  const timestamp = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, '-')\\n  const resultsPath = path.join(\\n    process.cwd(),\\n    'test-data',\\n    'test-results',\\n    &amp;#96;eval-${mode}-${timestamp}.json&amp;#96;\\n  )\\n\\n  fs.writeFileSync(resultsPath, JSON.stringify(evaluationResults, null, 2))\\n\\n  // Print summary with three-tier accuracy (Layer 3)\\n  console.log('\\\\n' + '='.repeat(60))\\n  console.log('📊 EVALUATION SUMMARY')\\n  console.log('='.repeat(60))\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;Mode: ${mode}${useLLMJudge ? ' (with LLM-as-judge)' : ''}&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;Total Questions: ${total}&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;\\\\n🎯 Tool Selection:&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;   ${correctTool}/${total} correct (${accuracy.tool_selection.toFixed(1)}%)&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;\\\\n📊 Three-Tier Accuracy:&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;   1. Exact Match:      ${fullyCorrect}/${total} (${accuracy.overall.toFixed(1)}%)&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;   2. Semantic Match:   ${fullyCorrectSemantic}/${total} (${accuracy.overall_semantic.toFixed(1)}%) ✨&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;   3. Tool Only:        ${correctTool}/${total} (${accuracy.tool_selection.toFixed(1)}%)&amp;#96;)\\n  console.log(&amp;#96;\\\\n💡 Semantic matching uses:&amp;#96;)\\n}\","

Reporting (Week 2)\\n\\n**Goal:** Make results easy to understand and act on\\n\\n**Deliverables:**\\n\\n1. **Terminal Scorecard**\\n   - File: &amp;#96;scripts/generate-scorecard.ts&amp;#96;\\n   - Reads results JSON\\n   - Prints formatted summary to terminal\\n   - Shows overall winner and key metrics\\n\\n2. **Key Metrics Displayed:**\\n   - Tool selection accuracy (v1 vs v2)\\n   - Average answer quality (if LLM judge enabled)\\n   - Average latency\\n   - Win/loss/tie counts\\n   - Breakdown by category\\n\\n3. **Recommendations:**\\n   - Clear \\\"Deploy v2\\\" or \\\"Keep v1\\\" recommendation\\n   - List questions where v2 improved\\n   - List questions where v2 regressed\\n\\n**Time Estimate:** 3-4 hours\\n\\n**Success Criteria:**\\n- ✓ Clear, readable scorecard in terminal\\n- ✓ Easy to see which prompt is better\\n- ✓ Can identify specific improvement areas\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Phase 4: LLM-as-Judge (Week 3 - Optional)\\n\\n**Goal:** Automate answer quality evaluation\\n\\n**Deliverables:**\\n\\n1. **Judge Function**\\n   - Takes two answers + original question\\n   - Sends to GPT-4 for evaluation\\n   - Returns quality scores for both\\n\\n2. **Evaluation Criteria:**\\n   - Relevance to question\\n   - Factual accuracy\\n   - Clarity and helpfulness\\n   - Grounding in provided data\\n\\n3. **Integration:**\\n   - Optional flag: &amp;#96;--use-llm-judge&amp;#96;\","

Scan through ALL passages looking for mentions of that topic\\n   2. If you find relevant data (numbers, quotes, facts), EXTRACT IT and provide it\\n   3. DO NOT say \\\"I can provide it if you want\\\" - JUST PROVIDE IT\\n   4. DO NOT be overly cautious - if the data is there, use it\\n\\n   For DATA in tables or structured format:\\n   - Extract the numbers and present them clearly\\n   - Example: If passage contains \\\"iPhone $ 201,183 $ 200,583 $ 205,489\\\" with headers \\\"2024 2023 2022\\\"\\n   - Answer: \\\"According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, iPhone net sales were $201.2 billion in 2024, $200.6 billion in 2023, and $205.5 billion in 2022.\\\"\\n\\n   For QUOTES and qualitative content:\\n   - Provide direct quotes from chunk_text that are RELEVANT\\n   - Use quotation marks around direct quotes\\n   - Cite the source: filing type, date, and section\\n   - Example: According to the 10-K filed November 1, 2024, \\\"The Company is exposed to the risk of write-downs...\\\"\\n\\n   Only say \\\"I couldn't find information\\\" if:\\n   - You've read ALL passages completely\\n   - NONE of them contain the requested information\\n   - DO NOT say this if the data exists but you're uncertain about formatting\\n\\n5. UNCERTAINTY - Admit when unsure:\\n   - If you cannot find specific data in the facts, say so clearly\\n   - Better to say \\\"I don't have that information\\\" than to guess\\n   - If data seems incomplete, acknowledge it\\n\\n6. CALCULATIONS - You MUST calculate ratios/percentages from the data when requested:\\n\\n   IMPORTANT: The facts JSON often includes multiple fields per row to enable ratio calculations.\\n   For example, if the metric is \\\"total_liabilities\\\", the JSON will also include \\\"shareholders_equity\\\" and \\\"total_assets\\\".\\n   These additional fields are provided specifically so you can calculate ratios. USE THEM.\\n\\n   STOCK PRICE PERFORMANCE:\\n   - If the facts include a \\\"percentChange\\\" field, USE THAT VALUE directly (it's already calculated)\\n   - If percentChange is NOT provided, calculate it: ((ending_price - starting_price) / starting_price) × 100\\n   - Format: \\\"up X%\\\" or \\\"down X%\\\" with 2 decimal places\\n   - Example: percentChange: 790.58 → \\\"up 790.58%\\\"\\n   - Example: Start: $243.85, End: $267.93 → ((267.93 - 243.85) / 243.85) × 100 = 9.88% → \\\"up 9.88%\\\"\\n\\n   ⚠️ REQUIRED FORMAT FOR PRICE PERFORMANCE ANSWERS (STRICTLY ENFORCE):\\n\\n   SENTENCE 1 (MANDATORY): \\\"Over the last [timeframe], AAPL stock is up (or down) X%.\\\"\\n   SENTENCE 2 (MANDATORY): \\\"It has gone from $X to $X.\\\"\\n   SENTENCE 3 (OPTIONAL): \\\"During this period, the stock reached a high of $X and a low of $X.\\\"\\n\\n   Example: \\\"Over the last 10 years, AAPL stock is up 790.58%. It has gone from $30.14 to $268.47. During this period, the stock reached a high of $271.40 and a low of $22.59.\\\"\\n\\n   ❌ WRONG (DO NOT DO THIS): \\\"Over the last 7 years, the data range runs from 2018-11-08 to 2025-11-07, with a start price of $52.12...\\\"\\n   ✅ CORRECT: \\\"Over the last 7 years, AAPL stock is up 415.15%. It has gone from $52.12 to $268.47...\\\"\\n\\n   CRITICAL: The FIRST sentence MUST state the percentage change. Do NOT start with dates, price levels, or \\\"the data range runs from...\\\"\\n\\n   PROFITABILITY RATIOS:\\n   - Gross Margin = (gross_profit / revenue) × 100\\n   - Operating Margin = (operating_income / revenue) × 100\\n   - Net Margin = (net_income / revenue) × 100\\n   - ROE (Return on Equity) = (net_income / shareholders_equity) × 100\\n   - ROA (Return on Assets) = (net_income / total_assets) × 100\\n\\n   LEVERAGE RATIOS:\\n   - Debt-to-Equity = total_liabilities / shareholders_equity\\n     * When asked for debt-to-equity, look for \\\"value\\\" (total_liabilities) and \\\"shareholders_equity\\\" in each row\\n     * Calculate the ratio for each year: value / shareholders_equity\\n     * Format as a ratio with 2 decimal places: \\\"3.87\\\" not \\\"3.87234...\\\"\\n     * Show dollar amounts in B or M format, and the calculated ratio\\n     * Example: \\\"The debt-to-equity ratio in 2025 is 3.87 (total liabilities of $285.5B divided by shareholders' equity of $73.7B).\\\"\\n   - Debt-to-Assets = total_liabilities / total_assets\\n\\n   EFFICIENCY RATIOS:\\n   - Asset Turnover = revenue / total_assets\\n   - Cash Flow Margin = (operating_cash_flow / revenue) × 100\\n\\n   - If user asks for a \\\"margin\\\" or \\\"ratio\\\", calculate it from the available data\\n   - Show the calculation concisely with formatted numbers\\n   - For margins (profitability), show as percentage: \\\"Gross margin is 46.2% ($180.7B gross profit / $391.0B revenue)\\\"\\n   - For ratios (leverage, efficiency), show as decimal: \\\"Debt-to-equity ratio is 3.87 ($285.5B liabilities / $73.7B equity)\\\"\\n\\n7. ⚠️ CRITICAL: EXTENDED METRICS FORMATTING (from financial_metrics table):\\n   When the facts JSON contains \\\"metric_name\\\" and \\\"metric_value\\\" fields, you MUST apply these formatting rules:\\n\\n   PERCENTAGE METRICS - MULTIPLY BY 100 AND ADD %:\\n   ❌ WRONG: \\\"ROE is 1.52\\\" or \\\"ROE is 1.50\\\"\\n   ✅ CORRECT: \\\"ROE is 152%\\\" or \\\"ROE is 150%\\\"\\n\\n   - returnOnEquity (ROE): If data shows 1.52, write \\\"152%\\\"\\n   - returnOnAssets (ROA): If data shows 0.28, write \\\"28%\\\"\\n   - returnOnCapitalEmployed (ROCE): If data shows 0.35, write \\\"35%\\\"\\n   - grossProfitMargin: If data shows 0.46, write \\\"46%\\\"\\n   - operatingProfitMargin, netProfitMargin: Same rule\\n   - All metrics ending in \\\"Margin\\\", \\\"Growth\\\", \\\"Yield\\\": multiply by 100, add %\\n\\n   RATIO METRICS (show as decimal, 2 places, NO multiplication):\\n   - peRatio, pbRatio, priceToSalesRatio → \\\"P/E ratio is 28.50\\\"\\n   - currentRatio, quickRatio, cashRatio → \\\"Current ratio is 1.23\\\"\\n   - debtEquityRatio, debtToAssets → \\\"Debt-to-equity is 1.87\\\"\\n\\n   CURRENCY METRICS (format with $ and B/M):\\n   - marketCap, enterpriseValue → \\\"$3.5T\\\" or \\\"$350B\\\"\\n   - freeCashFlow, operatingCashFlow → \\\"$100.5B\\\"\\n   - bookValuePerShare, cashPerShare → \\\"$4.25\\\"\\n\\n   DAYS METRICS (show as whole number with \\\"days\\\"):\\n   - daysOfInventoryOnHand, daysPayablesOutstanding → \\\"45 days\\\"\\n   - cashConversionCycle → \\\"-35 days\\\" (can be negative)\\n\\n   ALWAYS round to 2 decimal places maximum. NEVER show raw decimal values.\\n\\nGeneral Instructions:\\n- Be concise and clear.\\n- If the user asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (e.g., \\\"in 2020\\\", \\\"for 2018\\\"), check if that year exists in the facts:\\n  * If the year IS in the facts → provide the data directly and clearly\\n  * If the year is NOT in the facts → say \\\"I don't have data for [year].\\\" and stop\\n- If the user asks for multiple years or a trend, show all relevant years.\\n- If trend is relevant (and the user asked for it), describe it (e.g., increasing/decreasing/flat).\\n- Do not invent numbers or sources.\\n- Respond in plain text sentences. \\\"Dividend yield for 2023\\\" → {\\\"metricNames\\\": [\\\"dividend yield\\\"], \\\"limit\\\": 20}\\n\\n   args: {\\\"metricNames\\\": [\\\"&amp;lt;metric1&amp;gt;\\\", \\\"&amp;lt;metric2&amp;gt;\\\"], \\\"limit\\\": &amp;lt;number&amp;gt;}\\n\\nTOOL SELECTION LOGIC:\\n\\n1. Basic financial metrics (revenue, assets, eps, etc.)? → getAaplFinancialsByMetric\\n2. Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, etc.)? → getFinancialMetric\\n3. User asks \\\"what metrics available\\\"? → listMetrics\\n4. Stock price? → getPrices\\n5. Filing metadata ONLY (when/which filings)? → getRecentFilings\\n6. Filing CONTENT (what they say, quotes, topics)? → searchFilings\\n\\n⚠️ KEY DISTINCTION for #6 vs #7:\\n- \\\"When was the latest 10-K filed?\\\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)\\n- \\\"What does the latest 10-K say about risks?\\\" → searchFilings (content)\\n- \\\"Show me recent filings\\\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)\\n- \\\"What are risk factors in the latest 10-K?\\\" → searchFilings (content)\\n- \\\"Provide quotes from the 10-K\\\" → searchFilings (content)\\n\\nReturn ONLY JSON - examples:\\n\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"metric\\\":\\\"revenue\\\",\\\"limit\\\":5}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"metric\\\":\\\"eps\\\",\\\"limit\\\":1}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"metric\\\":\\\"total_liabilities\\\",\\\"limit\\\":4}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getPrices\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"from\\\":\\\"2018-11-15\\\"}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getPrices\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"from\\\":\\\"2025-01-01\\\",\\\"to\\\":\\\"2025-11-15\\\"}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getRecentFilings\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"limit\\\":3}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"searchFilings\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"query\\\":\\\"risk factors\\\",\\\"limit\\\":5}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"searchFilings\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"query\\\":\\\"AI strategy\\\",\\\"limit\\\":5}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"listMetrics\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"category\\\":\\\"Valuation\\\"}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"listMetrics\\\",\\\"args\\\":{}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getFinancialMetric\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"metricNames\\\":[\\\"P/E\\\"],\\\"limit\\\":5}}\\n{\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getFinancialMetric\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"metricNames\\\":[\\\"ROE\\\",\\\"debt to equity\\\"],\\\"limit\\\":10}}\\n\\nCRITICAL EXAMPLES - Filing Content vs Metadata:\\nQ: \\\"When was the latest 10-K filed?\\\"\\nA: {\\\"tool\\\":\\\"getRecentFilings\\\",\\\"args\\\":{\\\"limit\\\":1}}\\n\\nQ: \\\"What about risk factors in their latest 10k?                   "lineNumber": 62419,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# CLAUDE.md\\n\\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\\n\\n## Project Overview\\n\\n**Fin Quote** is a Next.js-based financial data platform with an AI-powered Q&amp;amp;A chatbot that answers natural language questions about Apple (AAPL) stock. The system uses a two-step LLM architecture with tool selection, data execution, answer generation, and validation.\\n\\n**Core Design Philosophy:**\\n- **Safety First**: LLMs cannot execute arbitrary database queries. Instead, they select from a whitelist of pre-built \\\"tools\\\" (server actions) with validated inputs.\\n- **Server-Side Intelligence**: All LLM calls, database queries, and validation logic run server-side. The browser only handles UI.\\n- **Grounded Answers**: The LLM must use only fetched data; no external knowledge or hallucinations allowed.\\n- **Validation Pipeline**: All answers are validated against source data for number accuracy, year correctness, and citation validity, with auto-regeneration on failures.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Architecture\\n\\n### Two-Step LLM Flow\\n\\nEvery user question follows this pattern (implemented in &amp;#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&amp;#96;):\\n\\n1. **Tool Selection** (lines 258-330)\\n   - LLM receives question + conversation history + tool menu\\n   - Returns JSON: &amp;#96;{\\\"tool\\\": \\\"toolName\\\", \\\"args\\\": {...}}&amp;#96;\\n   - Model: Uses &amp;#96;OPENAI_MODEL&amp;#96; (default: &amp;#96;gpt-5-nano&amp;#96;)\\n   - Tokens tracked for cost analysis\\n\\n2. **Tool Execution** (lines 332-575)\\n   - Server validates tool + args\\n   - Executes corresponding server action\\n   - Returns structured data (financials, prices, filings, passages, or metrics)\\n\\n3. **Answer Generation** (lines 579-650)\\n   - LLM receives question + fetched facts + conversation history\\n   - Generates grounded answer using only provided data\\n   - Plain text output (no Markdown, bullets, or tables)\\n   - Context: Last 10 messages (tool selection) or 4 messages (answer generation for gpt-5)\\n\\n4. **Validation &amp;amp; Auto-Correction** (lines 653-796)\\n   - Validates numbers, years, and filing citations\","
                },
