          {
            "text": "// Static instructions that will be cached by OpenAI",
            "lineNumber": 67
          },
          {
            "text": "const TOOL_SELECTION_STATIC_PROMPT = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.",
            "lineNumber": 68
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 69
          },
          {
            "text": "Available Tools:",
            "lineNumber": 70
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 71
          },
          {
            "text": "1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Financial metrics as NUMBERS over time",
            "lineNumber": 72
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 73
          },
          {
            "text": "   SUPPORTED METRICS:",
            "lineNumber": 74
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 75
          },
          {
            "text": "   Raw Metrics:",
            "lineNumber": 76
          },
          {
            "text": "   - revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 77
          },
          {
            "text": "   - total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 78
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operating_cash_flow, eps",
            "lineNumber": 79
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 80
          },
          {
            "text": "   Calculated Metrics (✨ Native Support):",
            "lineNumber": 81
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debt_to_equity_ratio  (total_liabilities / shareholders_equity)",
            "lineNumber": 82
          },
          {
            "text": "   - gross_margin          (gross_profit / revenue × 100)",
            "lineNumber": 83
          },
          {
            "text": "   - roe                   (net_income / shareholders_equity × 100)",
            "lineNumber": 84
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 85
          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC MAPPING (with context clues):",
            "lineNumber": 86
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 87
          },
          {
            "text": "   Income/Profitability:",
            "lineNumber": 88
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue",
            "lineNumber": 89
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\", \"profitability\" → net_income",
            "lineNumber": 90
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\" → eps",
            "lineNumber": 91
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"operating profit\", \"EBIT\" → operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 92
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 93
          },
          {
            "text": "   Valuation Ratios (use getFinancialMetric tool):",
            "lineNumber": 94
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/E ratio\", \"PE ratio\", \"price to earnings\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/E\"]",
            "lineNumber": 95
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"P/B ratio\", \"price to book\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/B\"]",
            "lineNumber": 96
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"PEG ratio\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"PEG\"]",
            "lineNumber": 97
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 98
          },
          {
            "text": "   Calculated Ratios (✨ NOW NATIVE - use directly):",
            "lineNumber": 99
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"gross margin\", \"gross profit margin\" → gross_margin",
            "lineNumber": 100
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"ROE\", \"return on equity\" → roe",
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"debt to equity\", \"debt-to-equity\", \"D/E ratio\", \"leverage ratio\" → debt_to_equity_ratio",
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "text": "   Balance Sheet (Raw):",
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"assets\", \"total assets\" → total_assets",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"liabilities\", \"total debt\", \"debt\" → total_liabilities",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"equity\", \"book value\", \"shareholders equity\" → shareholders_equity",
            "lineNumber": 107
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 108
          },
          {
            "text": "   Cash Flow:",
            "lineNumber": 109
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"operating cash flow\", \"cash from operations\", \"OCF\" → operating_cash_flow",
            "lineNumber": 110
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\", \"unlevered free cash flow\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool",
            "lineNumber": 111
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"capex\", \"capital expenditures\", \"buybacks\", \"dividends paid\", \"stock-based compensation\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool",
            "lineNumber": 112
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 113
          },
          {
            "text": "   Research &amp; Development:",
            "lineNumber": 114
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research and development\", \"R&amp;D spending\", \"R&amp;D expense\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"R&amp;D to revenue\"] or [\"research and development\"]",
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 116
          },
          {
            "text": "   Other (use closest available):",
            "lineNumber": 117
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"margins\", \"ratios\" (when not specific) → operating_income",
            "lineNumber": 118
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 119
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES - CRITICAL:",
            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 121
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. If question asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (2020, 2019, 2015, 2006, etc.) → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 122
          },
          {
            "text": "      Why: We have 20 years (2006-2025). To find any specific year, fetch all.",
            "lineNumber": 123
          },
          {
            "text": "      Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 124
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"net income in 2020\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 125
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"revenue for 2018\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 126
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"What was EPS in 2006?\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 127
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 128
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If question asks for a YEAR RANGE (2008 to 2020, 2015 to present, etc.) → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 129
          },
          {
            "text": "      Why: Need all data to filter to the specific range.",
            "lineNumber": 130
          },
          {
            "text": "      Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 131
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"net income 2008 to present\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 132
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"revenue from 2015 to 2020\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 133
          },
          {
            "text": "      - \"EPS between 2010 and 2018\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 134
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 135
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. If question specifies a NUMBER of years, use that EXACT number:",
            "lineNumber": 136
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last 3 years\" → limit: 3",
            "lineNumber": 137
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"past 5 years\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 138
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last year\" or \"most recent year\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 139
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"10 years\" → limit: 10",
            "lineNumber": 140
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"20 years\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 141
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"2 years\" → limit: 2",
            "lineNumber": 142
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 143
          },
          {
            "text": "   4. If question says \"trend\", \"history\", \"over time\" WITHOUT a number → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 144
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 145
          },
          {
            "text": "   5. If question says \"all\", \"complete\", \"full history\" → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 146
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 147
          },
          {
            "text": "   6. If question is just asking for the metric (no time context) → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 148
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 149
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 150
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"net income in 2006\" → limit: 20 (specific year)",
            "lineNumber": 151
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"revenue over 5 years\" → limit: 5 (number specified)",
            "lineNumber": 152
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"show me net income trend\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 153
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"EPS history\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 154
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"gross profit\" → limit: 4 (no number)",
            "lineNumber": 155
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"all historical data\" → limit: 20 (all data)",
            "lineNumber": 156
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 157
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"metric\": &lt;exact name&gt;, \"limit\": &lt;number 1-20&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 158
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 159
          },
          {
            "text": "2. getPrices - Stock PRICE history",
            "lineNumber": 160
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 161
          },
          {
            "text": "   ALWAYS use custom date ranges. Calculate the \"from\" date based on the user's request.",
            "lineNumber": 162
          },
          {
            "text": "   Today's date is {{TODAY_DATE}} (use this for calculations).",
            "lineNumber": 163
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 164
          },
          {
            "text": "   Date format: YYYY-MM-DD",
            "lineNumber": 165
          },
          {
            "text": "   \"to\" is optional (defaults to today)",
            "lineNumber": 166
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 167
          },
          {
            "text": "   CALCULATION EXAMPLES:",
            "lineNumber": 168
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 7 days\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-11-01\"} (7 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 169
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past month\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-10-08\"} (30 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 170
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 3 months\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-08-08\"} (90 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 171
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past year\" → args: {\"from\": \"2024-11-08\"} (365 days ago)",
            "lineNumber": 172
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"YTD\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-01-01\"} (start of current year)",
            "lineNumber": 173
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 3 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2022-11-08\"} (3 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 174
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past 5 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-11-08\"} (5 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 175
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 7 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-11-08\"} (7 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 176
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past 10 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-11-08\"} (10 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 177
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"last 15 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2010-11-08\"} (15 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 178
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"past 20 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago)",
            "lineNumber": 179
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"all time\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago, max available)",
            "lineNumber": 180
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 181
          },
          {
            "text": "   EXACT DATE RANGES:",
            "lineNumber": 182
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"from Jan 2020 to June 2023\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-01-01\", \"to\": \"2023-06-30\"}",
            "lineNumber": 183
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"prices between 2015 and 2020\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-01-01\", \"to\": \"2020-12-31\"}",
            "lineNumber": 184
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"from March 2018 to now\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-03-01\"}",
            "lineNumber": 185
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 186
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"from\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\", \"to\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\"}  (to is optional)",
            "lineNumber": 187
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 188
          },
          {
            "text": "3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings metadata ONLY",
            "lineNumber": 189
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 190
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This tool returns ONLY metadata (filing type, date, URL).",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "   It does NOT return filing CONTENT or text.",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use ONLY when:",
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHEN filings were submitted",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHICH filings exist",
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants filing dates/types/URLs",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "   DO NOT USE when:",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks WHAT the filing says",
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants content, quotes, or information FROM the filing",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks about topics like risks, strategy, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": "   → Use searchFilings instead for content questions!",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. If question specifies NUMBER of filings → use that number",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last 3 filings\" → limit: 3",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"2 years of filings\" → limit: 10 (2 years ≈ 8-10 filings)",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If question says \"recent\", \"latest\" (no number) → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 213
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. If question says \"all\", \"available\", \"history\" → limit: 10",
            "lineNumber": 214
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 215
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples (metadata questions):",
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"when was the most recent filing?\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"what filings do you have?\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"show me filing dates\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"limit\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content (for WHAT they say)",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Use this when user asks about CONTENT, not just dates!",
            "lineNumber": 225
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 226
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use for ANY question about WHAT the filings say:",
            "lineNumber": 227
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Risk factors, strategy, operations, business model",
            "lineNumber": 228
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Management commentary, outlook, quotes",
            "lineNumber": 229
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Products, markets, competition",
            "lineNumber": 230
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Governance, compensation",
            "lineNumber": 231
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ANY question asking \"what did they say\", \"provide quotes\", etc.",
            "lineNumber": 232
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 233
          },
          {
            "text": "   Even if they mention \"latest 10-K\" or specific filing:",
            "lineNumber": 234
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 235
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about AI?\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 236
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes from recent filing\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 237
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 238
          },
          {
            "text": "   QUERY RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 239
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Extract key terms from user's question",
            "lineNumber": 240
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Keep it simple (1-3 words usually best)",
            "lineNumber": 241
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Don't need full sentences",
            "lineNumber": 242
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 243
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are the risk factors?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 245
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What about risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 246
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Tell me about competition\" → {\"query\": \"competition\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 247
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes about AI strategy\" → {\"query\": \"AI strategy\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 248
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone?\" → {\"query\": \"iPhone\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 249
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 250
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 251
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 252
          },
          {
            "text": "5. listMetrics - DISCOVER available financial metrics",
            "lineNumber": 253
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 254
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use when:",
            "lineNumber": 255
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks \"what metrics do you have?\"",
            "lineNumber": 256
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to browse metrics by category",
            "lineNumber": 257
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Uncertain which metric name to use for getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 259
          },
          {
            "text": "   CATEGORY FILTER (optional):",
            "lineNumber": 260
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Valuation: P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, market cap, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 261
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Profitability &amp; Returns: ROE, ROA, ROIC, margins",
            "lineNumber": 262
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Growth: revenue growth, EPS growth, asset growth",
            "lineNumber": 263
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Leverage &amp; Solvency: debt ratios, liquidity ratios",
            "lineNumber": 264
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Efficiency &amp; Working Capital: turnover ratios, cycle days",
            "lineNumber": 265
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Capital Returns &amp; Share Data: dividend yield, payout ratio",
            "lineNumber": 266
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Per-Share Metrics: EPS, book value per share, cash per share",
            "lineNumber": 267
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Market Data: stock metrics, valuation metrics",
            "lineNumber": 268
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Other: miscellaneous metrics",
            "lineNumber": 269
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 271
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What valuation metrics do you have?\" → {\"category\": \"Valuation\"}",
            "lineNumber": 272
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me all metrics\" → {} (no category)",
            "lineNumber": 273
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What debt metrics are available?\" → {\"category\": \"Leverage &amp; Solvency\"}",
            "lineNumber": 274
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 275
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 341
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 342
          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC NAME FLEXIBILITY:",
            "lineNumber": 343
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Accepts canonical names: \"peRatio\", \"returnOnEquity\", \"debtEquityRatio\"",
            "lineNumber": 344
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Accepts common aliases: \"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"",
            "lineNumber": 345
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Can handle multiple metrics in one call",
            "lineNumber": 346
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 347
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES (same as getAaplFinancialsByMetric):",
            "lineNumber": 348
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Specific year → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 349
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Number specified → use that number",
            "lineNumber": 350
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"trend\", \"history\" → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 351
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"compare\" with multiple metrics → limit: 10 (show more history for comparisons)",
            "lineNumber": 352
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Default → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 353
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 354
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 355
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's Apple's P/E ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\"], \"limit\": 5}",

          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's the price to book ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"price to book\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 357
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me ROE trend\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"ROE\"], \"limit\": 4}",
            "lineNumber": 358
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's Apple's free cash flow?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"free cash flow\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 359
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"How much did Apple spend on buybacks?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"buybacks\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 360
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me capex trend\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"capex\"], \"limit\": 4}",
            "lineNumber": 361
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Compare P/E, ROE, and debt to equity\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"], \"limit\": 10}",
            "lineNumber": 362
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Compare P/E and ROE\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\", \"ROE\"], \"limit\": 10}",
            "lineNumber": 363
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Dividend yield for 2023\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"dividend yield\"], \"limit\": 20}",
            "lineNumber": 364
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 365
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"metricNames\": [\"&lt;metric1&gt;\", \"&lt;metric2&gt;\"], \"limit\": &lt;number&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 366
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 367
          },
          {
            "text": "TOOL SELECTION LOGIC:",
            "lineNumber": 368
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 369
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Basic financial metrics (revenue, assets, eps, etc.)? → getAaplFinancialsByMetric",
            "lineNumber": 370
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, etc.)? → getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 371
          },
          {
            "text": "3. User asks \"what metrics available\"? → listMetrics",
            "lineNumber": 372
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Stock price? → getPrices",
            "lineNumber": 373
          },
          {
            "text": "5. Filing metadata ONLY (when/which filings)? → getRecentFilings",
            "lineNumber": 374
          },
          {
            "text": "6. Filing CONTENT (what they say, quotes, topics)? → searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 375
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 376
          },
          {
            "text": "⚠️ KEY DISTINCTION for #6 vs #7:",
            "lineNumber": 377
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)",
            "lineNumber": 378
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"What does the latest 10-K say about risks?\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 379
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"Show me recent filings\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)",
            "lineNumber": 380
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"What are risk factors in the latest 10-K?\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 381
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"Provide quotes from the 10-K\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 382
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 383
          },
          {
            "text": "Return ONLY JSON - examples:",
            "lineNumber": 384
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 385
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"revenue\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 386
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"eps\",\"limit\":1}}",
            "lineNumber": 387
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"total_liabilities\",\"limit\":4}}",
            "lineNumber": 388
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2018-11-15\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 389
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2025-01-01\",\"to\":\"2025-11-15\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 390
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":3}}",
            "lineNumber": 391
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 392
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"AI strategy\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 393
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{\"category\":\"Valuation\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 394
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{}}",
            "lineNumber": 395
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\"],\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 396
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"ROE\",\"debt to equity\"],\"limit\":10}}",
            "lineNumber": 397
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 398
          },
          {
            "text": "CRITICAL EXAMPLES - Filing Content vs Metadata:",
            "lineNumber": 399
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\"",
            "lineNumber": 400
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":1}}",
            "lineNumber": 401

          {
            "lineNumber": 402
          },
          {

          {

            "lineNumber": 404
          },

          },

          },

        "contents": "- OR expand to multi-ticker support\n- OR add multi-hop reasoning for complex questions\n\n---\n\n## Phase 4 — ✅ COMPLETE: RAG for SEC Filings (Semantic Document Search)\n\n### Objective\nEnable users to ask questions ABOUT the content of SEC filings using semantic search (RAG - Retrieval-Augmented Generation).\n\n### What Was Built\n\n#### 1. Database Infrastructure\n- ✅ **pgvector extension enabled** - Allows storing embeddings in Postgres\n- ✅ **&#96;filing_chunks&#96; table** - Stores text chunks with embeddings (1536-dimensional vectors)\n- ✅ **Vector search index** - IVFFlat index for fast similarity search\n- ✅ **&#96;search_filing_chunks()&#96; function** - PostgreSQL function for semantic search using cosine distance\n\n#### 2. Storage Infrastructure\n- ✅ **Supabase Storage bucket &#96;filings&#96;** - Stores original HTML files from SEC\n- ✅ **RLS policies** - Secure access control for filing documents\n- ✅ **Signed URL generation** - For secure document citations\n\n#### 3. Data Ingestion Pipeline\nThree scripts to transform SEC filings into searchable chunks:\n\n**Script 1: &#96;download-filings.ts&#96;**\n- Downloads HTML files from SEC EDGAR\n- Stores in Supabase Storage bucket\n- Respects SEC User-Agent requirements\n- Handles 10-K and 10-Q filings\n\n**Script 2: &#96;chunk-filings.ts&#96;**\n- Extracts clean text from HTML files\n- Splits into ~800-word chunks with 100-word overlap\n- Preserves section information (Risk Factors, MD&amp;A, etc.)\n- Stores chunks in &#96;filing_chunks&#96; table\n\n**Script 3: &#96;embed-filings.ts&#96;**\n- Generates embeddings using OpenAI &#96;text-embedding-3-small&#96;\n- 1,536 dimensions per embedding\n- Updates &#96;filing_chunks&#96; with vector embeddings\n- Cost: ~$0.02 per 1M tokens\n\n#### 4. Search Action\n**File:** &#96;app/actions/search-filings.ts&#96;\n- ✅ &#96;searchFilings({ query, limit })&#96; server action\n- Embeds user question using OpenAI\n- Performs vector similarity search via &#96;search_filing_chunks()&#96; RPC\n- Returns top-k most relevant passages with metadata\n- Fallback to manual query if RPC unavailable\n\n#### 5. Tool Integration\n**File:** &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;\n- ✅ Added &#96;searchFilings&#96; to tool menu",

UI Enhancement\n**File:** &#96;app/ask/page.tsx&#96;\n- ✅ Displays passage results with:\n  - Filing type and fiscal year/quarter\n  - Filing date\n  - Section name\n  - Text excerpt (first 200 characters)\n- Styled in blue table format matching other data types\n\n### How It Works (End-to-End)\n\n**User asks:** \"What supply chain risks does Apple mention?\"\n\n1. **Tool Selection** - LLM routes to &#96;searchFilings&#96; tool\n2. **Query Embedding** - Question converted to 1,536-number vector\n3. **Vector Search** - Database finds 5 most similar chunk embeddings\n4. **Passage Retrieval** - Returns relevant text passages with metadata\n5. **Answer Generation** - LLM writes answer using ONLY those passages\n6. **Citation Display** - UI shows answer + source passages\n\n### Example Questions Now Supported\n\n**Qualitative Document Questions:**\n- \"What risks does AAPL mention in their filings?\"\n- \"What did AAPL say about competition?\"\n- \"Explain AAPL's revenue recognition policy\"\n- \"What supply chain challenges does AAPL face?\"\n- \"What is AAPL's business strategy?\"\n- \"What legal issues did AAPL disclose?\"\n\n### Technical Details\n\n**Embedding Model:** OpenAI &#96;text-embedding-3-small&#96;\n- 1,536 dimensions\n- ~$0.02 per 1M tokens\n- Fast and accurate\n\n**Search Method:** Cosine similarity via pgvector\n- &#96;&lt;=&gt;&#96; operator for cosine distance\n- IVFFlat index for speed\n- Sub-second searches on thousands of chunks\n\n**Chunk Strategy:**\n- ~800 words per chunk\n- ~100 word overlap between chunks\n- Preserves context at boundaries\n- Stores section metadata\n\n### Current Data",

        "contents": "async function fetchSecFilings() {\n filings (10-K and 10-Q only)&#96;)\n\n    // Sort by filing date descending (most recent first)\n    filings.sort((a, b) =&gt; new Date(b.filing_date).getTime() - new Date(a.filing_date).getTime())\n\n    // Limit to last 10 years (approximately 40-50 filings)\n    const tenYearsAgo = new Date()\n    tenYearsAgo.setFullYear(tenYearsAgo.getFullYear() - 10)\n\n    const recentFilings10Years = filings.filter(\n      (f) =&gt; new Date(f.filing_date) &gt;= tenYearsAgo\n    )\n\n    console.log(&#96;✓ Limited to last 10 years: ${recentFilings10Years.length} filings\\n&#96;)\n\n    // Save to file\n    const fs = await import('fs/promises')\n    const path = await import('path')\n\n    const dataDir = path.join(process.cwd(), 'data')\n    await fs.mkdir(dataDir, { recursive: true })\n\n    const filePath = path.join(dataDir, 'aapl-filings.json')\n    await fs.writeFile(filePath, JSON.stringify(recentFilings10Years, null, 2))\n\n    console.log(&#96;✓ Saved ${recentFilings10Years.length} filings to data/aapl-filings.json\\n&#96;)\n\n    // Show summary by type\n    const tenKCount = recentFilings10Years.filter((f) =&gt; f.filing_type === '10-K').length\n    const tenQCount = recentFilings10Years.filter((f) =&gt; f.filing_type === '10-Q').length\n\n    console.log('Summary:')\n    console.log(&#96;  10-K (Annual): ${tenKCount}&#96;)\n    console.log(&#96;  10-Q (Quarterly): ${tenQCount}&#96;)\n    console.log('\\nSample filing (most recent):')\n    console.log(JSON.stringify(recentFilings10Years[0], null, 2))\n  } catch (error) {\n    console.error('Error fetching SEC filings:', error)\n    throw error\n  }\n}\n\nfetchSecFilings().catch(console.error)",

The `data/` folder contains static data files and database setup scripts. Here's what it's for:

## What the `data/` folder is for

### 1. Static data files (JSON)
Reference data that doesn't change often:

- `us_tickers_metadata.json` — List of stock tickers with names, prices, market caps
- `metrics-catalog.json` — Catalog of financial metrics (revenue, profit, etc.)
- `aapl-financials.json` — Apple financial data (for initial setup)
- `aapl-filings.json` — Apple SEC filing data (for initial setup)

Purpose: Reference data used by scripts to populate the database or by the app for lookups.

---

### 2. Database setup scripts (SQL)
SQL files that create tables and load initial data:

- `create-*.sql` — Create database tables
  - `create-filings-table.sql` — Creates the filings table
  - `create-query-logs-table.sql` — Creates the query logs table
- `insert-*.sql` — Load initial data
  - `insert-financials.sql` — Loads financial data
  - `insert-metrics-batch1.sql` — Loads metrics data
- `setup-and-load.sql` — Main setup script

Purpose: Used once to set up the database schema and initial data.

---

## How it's used

### Example 1: Loading metrics
From `scripts/setup-financial-metrics.ts`:
```typescript
// Script reads the JSON file
const dataPath = 'data/aapl-fmp-metrics.json'
const metrics = JSON.parse(fileContent)

// Then loads it into the database
await supabase.from('financial_metrics').insert(metrics)
```

### Example 2: Database migrations
When setting up the database:
1. Run `create-filings-table.sql` to create the table
2. Run `insert-financials.sql` to load data from JSON files

---

## Think of it like this

- `data/` = Ingredients and recipes
  - JSON files = Ingredients (the data)
  - SQL files = Recipes (how to set up the database)

---

## Summary

The `data/` folder is for:
1. Static reference data (tickers, metrics catalog)
2. Initial data to load into the database
3. SQL scripts to set up the database

It's not used by the running app; it's used by setup scripts to populate the database initially.

Here’s the importance ranking:

## Most important folders (in order)

### 1. `app/` — most important
Contains:
- Pages (what users see)
- API routes (backend endpoints)
- Server actions (server-side functions)

Why it matters: This is the core of your Next.js app. Most of your work happens here.

---

### 2. `lib/` — very important
Contains:
- Helper functions (the workhorses)
- Database clients (`supabase/`)
- Prompts (`tools.ts`)
- Validators (`validators.ts`)
- Chart helpers (`chart-helpers.ts`)

Why it matters: Your `app/` folder imports from `lib/`. Look at line 4-11 in `ask-question.ts`:
```typescript
import { createServerClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'  // ← From lib/
import { buildToolSelectionPrompt } from '@/lib/tools'      // ← From lib/
import { validateAnswer } from '@/lib/validators'            // ← From lib/
```

---

### 3. `components/` — important
Contains:
- React components (UI pieces)
- `AssistantChat.tsx`, `FinancialChart.tsx`, etc.

Why it matters: These are the building blocks for your UI.

---

### 4. `data/` — not important for day-to-day work
Contains:
- Setup files (SQL migrations, initial JSON data)
- Used once during setup, not during runtime

Why it’s less important: You rarely touch this after initial setup.

---

## How they work together

```
app/ask-question.ts
  ↓ imports from
lib/tools.ts (helper functions)
  ↓ uses
lib/supabase/server.ts (database)
  ↓ returns data to
components/AssistantChat.tsx (displays it)
```

---

## Summary

| Folder | Importance | When You Use It |
|--------|-----------|-----------------|
| **`app/`** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ | **Every day** - pages, API routes, server actions |
| **`lib/`** | ⭐⭐⭐⭐ | **Very often** - helper functions, utilities |
| **`components/`** | ⭐⭐⭐ | **Often** - building UI |
| **`data/`** | ⭐ | **Rarely** - only during initial setup |

---

## Takeaway

The most important folders are:
1. `app/` — your main work
2. `lib/` — reusable helpers used by `app/`
3. `components/` — UI building blocks

`data/` is just for setup, not day-to-day development.

Focus on `app/` and `lib/` first — that’s where most of the logic lives.

Yes. In Next.js App Router, the `app/` folder is special. Here's how it works:

## How Next.js uses the `app/` folder

### 1. Routing (pages)
Next.js uses folder structure for routing:

```
app/
  page.tsx          → http://yoursite.com/          (homepage)
  market/
    page.tsx       → http://yoursite.com/market     (market page)
  chatbot/
    page.tsx       → http://yoursite.com/chatbot    (chatbot page)
  admin/
    evaluations/
      page.tsx     → http://yoursite.com/admin/evaluations
```

Rule: A `page.tsx` file creates a route. The folder name becomes the URL path.

---

### 2. API routes
```
app/
  api/
    ask/
      route.ts      → http://yoursite.com/api/ask    (API endpoint)
    evaluations/
      latest/
        route.ts   → http://yoursite.com/api/evaluations/latest
```

Rule: A `route.ts` file creates an API endpoint. The folder path becomes the URL.

---

### 3. Server actions
```
app/
  actions/
    ask-question.ts    → Server function (not a route)
    market-data.ts    → Server function (not a route)
```

Rule: Files with `'use server'` at the top are server actions. They're functions, not routes.

---

## What Next.js doesn't require in `app/`

These folders are conventional, not required by Next.js:

- `components/` — React components (you choose where to put them)
- `lib/` — Helper functions (you choose where to put them)
- `types/` — TypeScript types (you choose where to put them)
- `data/` — Static files (you choose where to put them)

You could put components in `app/components/` if you want, but many projects keep them separate.

---

## The special files in `app/`

```
app/
  layout.tsx       → Wraps all pages (special Next.js file)
  page.tsx         → Homepage (special Next.js file)
  globals.css      → Global styles (special Next.js file)
```

These have special meaning:
- `layout.tsx` — Wraps all pages (navigation, theme, etc.)
- `page.tsx` — Creates a route
- `route.ts` — Creates an API endpoint

---

## Summary

| What | Where | Why |
|------|-------|-----|
| **Pages** | `app/` | Next.js routing requires it |
| **API Routes** | `app/api/` | Next.js routing requires it |
| **Server Actions** | `app/actions/` | Convention (could be anywhere) |
| **Components** | `components/` | Convention (could be in `app/`) |
| **Helpers** | `lib/` | Convention (could be in `app/`) |

---

## Takeaway

Next.js requires:
- Pages in `app/` (for routing)
- API routes in `app/api/` (for routing)

Everything else (`components/`, `lib/`, `types/`) is convention, not required. You could put them in `app/` if you prefer, but keeping them separate is common.

So yes — Next.js puts routing-related things in `app/`, and you organize the rest as you like.

        "contents": "'use server'\n\nimport { createServerClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'\nimport { CompanyWithFinancials, Company, Financial } from '@/lib/database.types'\n\nexport async function getCompaniesWithFinancials(): Promise&lt;{\n  data: CompanyWithFinancials[] | null\n  error: string | null\n}&gt; {\n  try {\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    // Fetch all companies\n    const { data: companies, error: companiesError } = await supabase\n      .from('company')\n      .select('*')\n      .order('name', { ascending: true })\n\n    if (companiesError) {\n      console.error('Error fetching companies:', companiesError)\n      return { data: null, error: companiesError.message }\n    }\n\n    if (!companies || companies.length === 0) {\n      return { data: [], error: null }\n    }\n\n    const companyRows: Company[] = companies as Company[]\n\n    // Fetch all financials\n    const { data: financials, error: financialsError } = await supabase\n      .from('financials_std')\n      .select('*')\n      .order('year', { ascending: false })\n\n    if (financialsError) {\n      console.error('Error fetching financials:', financialsError)\n      return { data: null, error: financialsError.message }\n    }\n\n    const financialRows: Financial[] = (financials ??         "contents": "export default function AskPage() {\nconst handleSubmit = async \n\n\n    try {\n      // Infer which tool will be called\n      const toolInfo = inferToolFromQuestion(question)\n\n      // Step 1: Analyzing question (200ms)\n      setLoadingStep('analyzing')\n      setLoadingMessage('Parsing your question...')\n      await new Promise(resolve =&gt; setTimeout(resolve, 200))\n\n      // Step 2: Selecting tool (300ms)\n      setLoadingStep('selecting')\n      setLoadingMessage('Selecting optimal tool...')\n      await new Promise(resolve =&gt; setTimeout(resolve, 300))\n\n      // Step 3: Calling tool (show actual tool)\n      setLoadingStep('calling')\n      if (toolInfo.tool === 'getAaplFinancialsByMetric' &amp;&amp; toolInfo.metric) {\n        setLoadingMessage(&#96;Calling getAaplFinancialsByMetric('${toolInfo.metric}')&#96;)\n      } else if (toolInfo.tool === 'getPrices') {\n        setLoadingMessage(&#96;Calling getPrices({ range: '${toolInfo.range}' })&#96;)\n      } else if (toolInfo.tool === 'searchFilings') {\n        setLoadingMessage('Calling searchFilings (semantic search)')\n      } else {\n        setLoadingMessage(&#96;Calling ${toolInfo.tool}()&#96;)\n      }\n      await new Promise(resolve =&gt; setTimeout(resolve, 400))\n\n      // Step 4: Fetching from database\n      setLoadingStep('fetching')\n      setLoadingMessage('Querying Supabase database...')\n      await new Promise(resolve =&gt; setTimeout(resolve, 500))\n\n      // Step 5: Calculating (if ratio)\n      const isRatio = question.toLowerCase().includes('margin') ||\n                      question.toLowerCase().includes('roe') ||\n                      question.toLowerCase().includes('roa') ||\n                      question.toLowerCase().includes('ratio')\n      if (isRatio) {\n        setLoadingStep('calculating')\n        setLoadingMessage('Computing financial ratios...')\n        await new Promise(resolve =&gt; setTimeout(resolve, 300))\n      }\n\n      // Step 6: Generating answer\n      setLoadingStep('generating')\n      setLoadingMessage('Generating answer with GPT-5-nano...')\n\n      // Send question with conversation history and session ID\n\n}",

        "contents": "export default function AskPage() {\nconst handleSubmitStreaming = async \n\n\n    try {\n      const response = await fetch('/api/ask', {\n        method: 'POST',\n        headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n        body: JSON.stringify({\n          question,\n          conversationHistory,\n          sessionId,\n        }),\n      })\n\n      if (!response.ok) {\n        throw new Error(&#96;HTTP error! status: ${response.status}&#96;)\n      }\n\n      const reader = response.body?.getReader()\n      const decoder = new TextDecoder()\n\n      if (!reader) {\n        throw new Error('No response body')\n      }\n\n      const updateFlowEvent = (incoming: FlowEvent) =&gt; {\n        setFlowEvents(prev =&gt; {\n          const existingIndex = prev.findIndex(event =&gt; event.id === incoming.id)\n          if (existingIndex === -1) {\n            return [...prev, incoming].sort((a, b) =&gt; a.sequence - b.sequence)\n          }\n\n          const next = [...prev]\n          const previous = next[existingIndex]\n          next[existingIndex] = {\n            ...previous,\n            ...incoming,\n            summary: incoming.summary ?? previous.summary,\n            why: incoming.why ?? previous.why,\n            details: incoming.details ?? previous.details,\n            durationMs: incoming.durationMs ?? previous.durationMs,\n            costUsd: incoming.costUsd ?? previous.costUsd,\n          }\n          return next.sort((a, b) =&gt; a.sequence - b.sequence)\n        })\n      }\n\n      let streamedAnswer = ''\n      let receivedData: any = null\n      let receivedChart: any = null\n      let receivedFollowUpQuestions: string[] = []\n\n      while (true) {\n        const { done, value } = await reader.read()\n      }\n\n}",

        "contents": "# Market Dashboard SSR Refactor\n\n## Goal\n\nRefactor the market dashboard (&#96;/market&#96;) from client-rendered to server-rendered, similar to how Finviz.com works.\n\n## Current State\n\nThe market page (&#96;app/market/page.tsx&#96;) is currently client-rendered:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n'use client'\n\nexport default function MarketPage() {\n  const [spxData, setSpxData] = useState(null)\n\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    fetchData()\n    setInterval(fetchData, 10000)\n  }, [])\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Current behavior:**\n1. Server sends empty HTML shell\n2. Browser downloads JavaScript\n3. Browser executes JavaScript\n4. Browser fetches market data from server actions\n5. Browser renders the page\n6. Browser polls every 10 seconds for updates\n\n**Problems with current approach:**\n- User sees \"Loading market data...\" on first visit\n- Slower perceived performance (blank → loading → content)\n- Poor SEO (Google sees empty page)\n- More work pushed to user's browser\n\n## Target State\n\nServer-rendered dashboard like Finviz.com:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// No 'use client' directive\nexport default async function MarketPage() {\n  const [spxData, nasdaqData, dowData, ...] = await Promise.all([\n    getAaplMarketData(),\n    getNasdaqMarketData(),\n    getDowMarketData(),\n    // ...\n  ])\n\n  return &lt;MarketDashboard data={...} /&gt;\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Target behavior:**\n1. Server fetches all market data\n2. Server builds complete HTML with all numbers/charts\n3. Browser receives fully-formed page (data visible immediately)\n4. Small client component handles periodic refresh\n\n## Why Finviz.com as the Model\n\nFinviz is a successful financial dashboard that uses server-rendering:\n\n- **Fast first load** - Data appears instantly, no loading spinner\n- **SEO friendly** - Search engines index all market data\n- **Works without JavaScript** - Core content visible even if JS fails\n- **Simple architecture** - Server does the heavy lifting\n\nTheir refresh strategy:\n- Page data is relatively fresh on load (server fetches on each request or uses short cache)\n- Users manually refresh for latest data, or page auto-refreshes periodically\n- Some sections use small AJAX updates without full page reload",
        "signatures": {},

        "contents": "- TypeScript Handbook: \"Basic Types\" (30 min)\n- Practice: Add types to a function you write\n\n---\n\n### 3. **API Routes vs Server Actions** ⭐ IMPORTANT\n**Why**: You have both - need to understand when to use which\n\n**What You'll See**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// API Route (app/api/ask/route.ts)\nexport async function POST(req: NextRequest) {\n  // Handles HTTP requests\n  // Can stream responses\n  // More control over response format\n}\n\n// Server Action (app/actions/ask-question.ts)\n'use server'\nexport async function askQuestion() {\n  // Called directly from components\n  // Simpler, but less control\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Key Concepts**:\n- API Routes: Full HTTP control, streaming, custom headers\n- Server Actions: Simpler, type-safe, Next.js handles the HTTP\n- Your codebase uses API route for streaming, server action for simple calls\n\n**Where to Practice**:\n- Compare &#96;app/api/ask/route.ts&#96; (streaming) vs &#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96; (non-streaming)\n- Both do the same thing, but API route streams the response\n\n**Resources**:\n- Next.js docs: \"API Routes\" vs \"Server Actions\"\n- Practice: Convert a server action to an API route (or vice versa)\n\n---\n\n### 4. **Error Handling (try/catch)** ⭐ IMPORTANT\n**Why**: Everything can fail - database, API calls, parsing JSON\n\n**What You'll See**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\ntry {\n  const data = await fetchData()\n  return { data, error: null }\n} catch (err) {\n  return { data: null, error: err.message }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Key Concepts**:\n- &#96;try&#96; - code that might fail\n- &#96;catch&#96; - what to do if it fails\n- Always return &#96;{ data, error }&#96; pattern\n- Check for errors before using data\n\n**Where to Practice**:\n- Look at any server action - they all use try/catch\n- See how errors are returned to the client\n\n**Resources**:\n- MDN: \"try/catch\" (10 min)\n- Practice: Add error handling to a function\n\n---\n\n### 5. **Database Queries (Supabase)** ⭐ IMPORTANT\n**Why**: Most of your data comes from Supabase database\n\n**What You'll See**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nconst supabase = await createServerClient()\nconst { data, error } = await supabase\n  .from('financials_std')",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 101
          },
          {
            "text": "### 4. **Error Handling (try/catch)** ⭐ IMPORTANT",
            "lineNumber": 102
          },
          {
            "text": "**Why**: Everything can fail - database, API calls, parsing JSON",
            "lineNumber": 103
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 104
          },
          {
            "text": "**What You'll See**:",
            "lineNumber": 105
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript",
            "lineNumber": 106
          },
          {
            "text": "try {",

          },
          {
            "text": "  const data = await fetchData()",
            "lineNumber": 108
          },
          {
            "text": "  return { data, error: null }",
            "lineNumber": 109
          },
          {
            "text": "} catch (err) {",
            "lineNumber": 110
          },
          {
            "text": "  return { data: null, error: err.message }",
            "lineNumber": 111
          },
          {
            "text": "}",
            "lineNumber": 112
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 113
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 114
          },
          {
            "text": "**Key Concepts**:",
            "lineNumber": 115
          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;try&#96; - code that might fail",

          },
          {
            "text": "- &#96;catch&#96; - what to do if it fails",
            "lineNumber": 117
          },
          {

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 120
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 124
          },

        "contents": "'use server'\n\nimport { createServerClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'\n\n// Safe, purpose-built tool for fetching recent SEC filings for AAPL only\n// This is designed to be called by server code (e.g., an LLM routing step) and returns\n// a minimal, predictable shape for easy prompting and display.\nexport async function getRecentFilings(params: {\n  ticker?: string // AAPL only for MVP\n  limit?: number // number of most recent filings to fetch\n}): Promise&lt;{\n  data: Array&lt;{\n    filing_type: string\n    filing_date: string\n    period_end_date: string\n    fiscal_year: number\n    fiscal_quarter: number | null\n    document_url: string\n  }&gt; | null\n  error: string | null\n}&gt; {\n  const ticker = params.ticker ?? 'AAPL'\n  const requestedLimit = params.limit ?? 5\n\n  // Enforce AAPL-only for MVP\n  if (ticker !== 'AAPL') {\n    return { data: null, error: 'Only AAPL ticker is supported in MVP' }\n  }\n\n  // Limit rows to a small, safe window (1..10)\n  const safeLimit = Math.min(Math.max(requestedLimit, 1), 10)\n\n  try {\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n      .from('filings')\n      .select('filing_type, filing_date, period_end_date, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, document_url')\n      .eq('ticker', ticker)\n      .order('filing_date', { ascending: false })\n      .limit(safeLimit)\n\n    if (error) {\n      console.error('Error fetching filings:', error)\n      return { data: null, error: error.message }\n    }\n\n    return { data: data ?? [], error: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('Unexpected error (getRecentFilings):', err)\n    return {\n      data: null,\n      error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'An unexpected error occurred',\n    }\n  }\n}",

        "contents": "export default function Home() {\nconst handleSubmitStreaming = async \nwhile (true) {\n flowEvent.step === 'tool_selection') {\n                // Capture the selected tool and show it prominently\n                const toolName = flowEvent.summary?.replace('Selected ', '') || 'tool'\n                setSelectedTool(toolName)\n                setLoadingMessage(&#96;✓ ${flowEvent.summary}&#96;)\n              }\n              break\n\n            case 'data':\n              receivedData = data.dataUsed\n              receivedChart = data.chartConfig\n              setChartConfig(data.chartConfig)\n              setDataReceived(true)\n              break\n\n            case 'answer':\n              streamedAnswer += data.content\n              setAnswer(streamedAnswer)\n              break\n\n            case 'error':\n              setChatbotError(data.message)\n              break\n          }\n        }\n      }\n\n      // Update conversation history\n      if\n\n}",

        "contents": "- **RAG (Retrieval‑Augmented Generation)**: For document questions (filings/transcripts), retrieve the most relevant passages via a vector store, then answer using those passages. We’ll add this after MVP.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture overview\n\n### Frontend (browser)\n- Next.js app with a simple UI: text box + Ask button + answer display.\n- No secrets in the browser.\n- Uses &#96;createBrowserClient()&#96; only for UI‑safe tasks.\n\n### Backend (server)\n- Next.js server actions/API routes handle all sensitive work.\n- Uses &#96;createServerClient()&#96; to talk to Supabase (read‑only for MVP).\n- Two LLM steps per question:\n  1) Selection: model picks exactly one tool from our small menu and provides JSON args.\n  2) Answering: after we run the tool and get facts, the model writes the final answer using only those facts.\n\n### Data (Supabase)\n- We store standardized financials in &#96;financials_std&#96; and company metadata in &#96;company&#96;.\n- For MVP, we enforce AAPL‑only and small row limits (1–8) at the tool level.\n\n---\n\n## Current code in the repo (important files)\n- &#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&#96;: Creates the browser client (uses &#96;NEXT_PUBLIC_*&#96; env vars; no session persistence). For UI only.\n- &#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&#96;: Creates the server client (same env vars; no session persistence). For server actions and API routes.\n- &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96;: Typed Supabase schema for &#96;company&#96; and &#96;financials_std&#96;.\n- &#96;app/actions/financials.ts&#96;:\n  - &#96;getCompaniesWithFinancials()&#96;: Example server action that composes companies with financials for display.\n  - &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric({ metric, limit })&#96;: SAFE TOOL (MVP). Allowed metrics: &#96;revenue&#96; or &#96;gross_profit&#96;. Limit clamped to 1..8. Always filters to &#96;AAPL&#96;. Returns an array of &#96;{ year, value, metric }&#96;.\n- &#96;lib/tools.ts&#96;:\n  - &#96;TOOL_MENU&#96;: Defines the tool(s) the model can choose from.",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./docs/STOCK_DETAIL_PAGE_IMPLEMENTATION.md",
        "range": {
          "startPosition": {
            "line": 585
          },
          "endPosition": {
            "line": 666
          }
        },
        "contents": "### Existing Server Actions (No Changes Needed)\n\n- &#96;getPrices()&#96; - Already supports AAPL, custom date ranges\n- &#96;getRecentFilings()&#96; - Already supports AAPL\n- &#96;searchFilings()&#96; - Already supports AAPL\n- &#96;askQuestion()&#96; - Already supports AAPL (hardcoded)\n\n---\n\n## Data Fetching Strategy\n\n### Initial Page Load (Server Component)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// app/stock/aapl/page.tsx\nexport default async function StockPage() {\n  // Parallel data fetching\n  const [overview, keyStats, financials, metrics, filings] = await Promise.all([\n    getStockOverview(),\n    getStockKeyStats(),\n    getAllFinancials(),\n    getAllMetrics(),\n    getRecentFilings('AAPL', 20) // Last 20 filings\n  ]);\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div&gt;\n      &lt;StockHeader {...overview} /&gt;\n      &lt;QuickStatsGrid stats={keyStats} /&gt;\n      &lt;StockPriceChart initialData={[]} /&gt; {/* Fetch client-side for interactivity */}\n      &lt;FinancialsSection data={financials} /&gt;\n      &lt;MetricsGrid metrics={metrics} /&gt;\n      &lt;FilingsSection filings={filings} /&gt;\n      &lt;AIInsightsPanel symbol=\"AAPL\" /&gt;\n    &lt;/div&gt;\n  );\n}\n\n// ISR with 60s revalidation\nexport const revalidate = 60;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Client-Side Data Fetching\n\n**Price Chart:**\n- Default: Load 7D data on mount\n- On timeframe change: Fetch new data via &#96;getPrices()&#96;\n\n**Real-time Price:**\n- Poll &#96;getStockOverview()&#96; every 10s during market hours\n- Update header price display\n\n**AI Chat:**\n- Fetch answers via &#96;askQuestion()&#96; on user input\n- Stream responses using existing implementation\n\n---\n\n## UI/UX Design Decisions\n\n### 1. Single Page Scroll vs Tabs\n\n**Decision**: Single scrollable page (no tabs)\n\n**Rationale:**\n- Finviz-style dense information display\n- Faster information scanning (no clicking required)\n- Better for power users who want to see everything\n- Simpler implementation (no tab state management)\n- Better SEO (all content rendered on page)\n\n**Trade-offs:**\n- Longer initial page load (more data)\n- May be overwhelming for casual users\n- Larger bundle size\n\n**Mitigations:**\n- Use ISR to pre-render server-side (fast TTFB)\n- Lazy load images and charts below fold\n- Skeleton loaders for each section",

        "contents": "│   └── supabase/\n│       ├── client.ts           # Client-side Supabase client\n│       └── server.ts           # Server-side Supabase client\n├── .env.local.example          # Example environment variables\n└── package.json\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Features\n\n### Server Actions\n\nThe app uses Next.js Server Actions for data fetching, located in &#96;app/actions/financials.ts&#96;:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { getCompaniesWithFinancials } from '@/app/actions/financials'\n\nconst { data, error } = await getCompaniesWithFinancials()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis server action:\n- Fetches all companies with their related financial data\n- Uses Supabase's nested &#96;.select()&#96; syntax to join tables\n- Returns fully typed data using TypeScript\n- Handles errors gracefully\n- Orders companies by name and financials by year (descending)\n\n### Type Safety\n\nAll database types are defined in &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96;, providing:\n- Full TypeScript autocomplete for database queries\n- Type-safe data access throughout the application\n- Helper types like &#96;CompanyWithFinancials&#96; for joined data\n\n### Supabase Client\n\nTwo client configurations are available:\n\n1. **Server Client** (&#96;lib/supabase/server.ts&#96;)\n   - Used in Server Components and Server Actions\n   - Runs on the server only\n   - Safe for sensitive operations\n\n2. **Browser Client** (&#96;lib/supabase/client.ts&#96;)\n   - Used in Client Components\n   - Runs in the browser\n   - Uses the public anon key (safe to expose)\n\n## Usage Example\n\n### Fetching Data in a Server Component\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// app/financials/page.tsx\nimport { getCompaniesWithFinancials } from '@/app/actions/financials'\n\nexport default async function FinancialsPage() {\n  const { data: companies, error } = await getCompaniesWithFinancials()",

        "contents": "export default function Home() {\nconst handleSubmitStreaming = async \nwhile (true) {\n\n          }\n        }\n      }\n\n      // Update conversation history\n      if (streamedAnswer &amp;&amp; !chatbotError) {\n        const assistantMessage: Message = {\n          role: 'assistant',\n          content: streamedAnswer,\n          timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n          chartConfig: receivedChart,\n          dataUsed: receivedData,\n        }\n\n        setConversationHistory(prev =&gt; [...prev, assistantMessage])\n\n        // Save to database if user is authenticated\n        if (user) {\n          let convId = currentConversationId\n          if (!convId) {\n            const { conversation, error: createError } = await createConversation()\n            if (!createError &amp;&amp; conversation) {\n              convId = conversation.id\n              setCurrentConversationId(convId)\n              setRefreshQueriesTrigger(prev =&gt; prev + 1)\n              await saveMessage(convId, 'user', userMessage.content)\n            }\n          } else {\n            await saveMessage(convId, 'user', userMessage.content)\n          }\n\n          if (convId) {\n            await saveMessage(convId, 'assistant', streamedAnswer, {\n              chart_config: receivedChart,\n              data_used: receivedData,\n            })\n\n            if (conversationHistory.length === 0) {\n              await autoGenerateTitle(convId)\n              setRefreshQueriesTrigger(prev =&gt; prev + 1)\n            }\n          }\n        }\n\n        setRefreshQueriesTrigger(prev =&gt; prev + 1)\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      setChatbotError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'An unexpected error occurred')\n    } finally {\n      setChatbotLoading(false)\n    }\n  }\n\n  const handleFollowUpQuestionClick = (selectedQuestion: string) =&gt; {\n    setQuestion(selectedQuestion)\n    setTimeout(() =&gt; {\n      const form = document.querySelector('form')\n      if (form) {\n        const event = new Event('submit', { bubbles: true, cancelable: true })\n        form.dispatchEvent(event)\n      }\n    }, 0)\n  }\n\n  return (\n    &lt;div className=\n}",

null)\n    })\n\n    return () =&gt; subscription.unsubscribe()\n  }, [])\n\n  // Load conversation from URL parameter or localStorage\n  useEffect(() =&gt; {\n    const loadConversation = async () =&gt; {\n      const conversationId = searchParams.get('id')\n\n      // If authenticated and conversation ID in URL, load from database\n      if (user &amp;&amp; conversationId) {\n        const { conversation, error } = await getConversation(conversationId)\n        if (error) {\n          console.error('Failed to load conversation:', error)\n          return\n        }\n\n        if (conversation) {\n          setCurrentConversationId(conversation.id)\n          // Convert database messages to conversation history format\n          const history: ConversationHistory = conversation.messages.map(msg =&gt; ({\n            role: msg.role as 'user' | 'assistant',\n            content: msg.content,\n            timestamp: msg.created_at,\n            chartConfig: msg.chart_config as ChartConfig | undefined,\n            followUpQuestions: msg.follow_up_questions || undefined,\n            dataUsed: msg.data_used as any,\n          }))\n          setConversationHistory(history)\n        }\n      }\n      // Otherwise load from localStorage for non-authenticated users\n      else if (!user) {\n        const saved = localStorage.getItem('finquote_conversation')\n        if (saved) {\n          try {\n            const parsed = JSON.parse(saved)\n            setConversationHistory(parsed)\n          } catch (err) {\n            console.error('Failed to load conversation history:', err)\n            localStorage.removeItem('finquote_conversation')\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    loadConversation()\n  }, [user, searchParams])\n\n  // Save conversation history to localStorage for non-authenticated users only\n}",

        "contents": "/**\n * Save a message to a conversation\n */\nexport async function saveMessage(\n  conversationId: string,\n  role: 'user' | 'assistant',\n  content: string,\n  metadata?: {\n    chart_config?: any\n    follow_up_questions?: string[]\n    data_used?: any\n  }\n): Promise&lt;{ message: Message | null; error: string | null }&gt; {\n  try {\n    console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage called for conversation:', conversationId, 'role:', role)\n    const supabase = await createServerClient()\n\n    // Get current user\n    const { data: { user }, error: authError } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\n    if (authError || !user) {\n      console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage: Not authenticated')\n      return { message: null, error: 'Not authenticated' }\n    }\n\n    // Verify conversation belongs to user (RLS will also check, but this provides better error message)\n    const { data: conversation, error: convError } = await supabase\n      .from('conversations')\n      .select('id')\n      .eq('id', conversationId)\n      .eq('user_id', user.id)\n      .single()\n\n    if (convError || !conversation) {\n      console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage: Conversation not found or access denied')\n      return { message: null, error: 'Conversation not found or access denied' }\n    }\n\n    const newMessage: NewMessage = {\n      conversation_id: conversationId,\n      role,\n      content,\n      chart_config: metadata?.chart_config || null,\n      follow_up_questions: metadata?.follow_up_questions || null,\n      data_used: metadata?.data_used || null\n    }\n\n    const { data, error } = await supabase\n      .from('messages')\n      .insert(newMessage)\n      .select()\n      .single()\n\n    if (error) {\n      console.error('[SERVER] Error saving message:', error)\n      return { message: null, error: error.message }\n    }\n\n    console.log('[SERVER] saveMessage: Successfully saved', role, 'message to conversation', conversationId)\n    return { message: data, error: null }\n  } catch (err) {\n    console.error('[SERVER] Unexpected error in saveMessage:', err)\n    return { message: null, error: 'An unexpected error occurred' }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Update conversation title\n */\nexport async function updateConversationTitle(\n  conversationId: string,\n  title: string\n): Promise&lt;{ conversation: Conversation | null; error: string | null }&gt; {\n  \n}",

        "contents": "export default function AskPage() {\nconst handleSubmit = async \n\n\n      // Send question with conversation history and session ID\n      const result = await askQuestion(question, conversationHistory, sessionId)\n\n      if (result.error) {\n        setError(result.error)\n      } else {\n        const formattedAnswer = summarizeAnswer(result.answer, result.chartConfig)\n        // Create assistant message\n        const assistantMessage: Message = {\n          role: 'assistant',\n          content: formattedAnswer,\n          timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),\n        }\n\n        // Update conversation history with both messages\n        setConversationHistory([...conversationHistory, userMessage, assistantMessage])\n\n        // Update UI\n        setAnswer(formattedAnswer)\n        setDataUsed(result.dataUsed)\n        setChartConfig(result.chartConfig)\n        setQueryLogId(result.queryLogId)\n\n        // Reset feedback state for new answer\n        setFeedback(null)\n        setShowCommentBox(false)\n        setFeedbackComment('')\n\n        // Refresh recent queries sidebar\n        setRefreshQueriesTrigger(prev =&gt; prev + 1)\n      }\n    } catch (err) {\n      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'An unexpected error occurred')\n    } finally {\n      setLoading(false)\n      setLoadingStep(null)\n      setLoadingMessage('')\n      setQuestion('') // Clear input after submission\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Handle feedback submission\n  const handleFeedbackClick = async (feedbackType: 'thumbs_up' | 'thumbs_down') =&gt; {\n    if (!queryLogId) return\n\n    setFeedback(feedbackType)\n    setShowCommentBox(true)\n\n    // If thumbs up and no comment needed, submit immediately\n    if (feedbackType === 'thumbs_up') {\n      setFeedbackSubmitting(true)\n      const result = await submitFeedback({\n        queryLogId,\n        feedback: feedbackType,\n      })\n      setFeedbackSubmitting(false)\n\n      if (!result.success) {\n        console.error('Failed to submit feedback:', result.error)\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // Handle comment submission\n  const handleCommentSubmit = async ()\n\n}",

        "contents": "# Learning Roadmap for Fin Quote Codebase\n\n## ✅ What You've Learned\n\n1. **Server Actions** - Functions that run on server, can access database/secrets\n2. **Helper Functions** - Reusable functions in &#96;lib/&#96; that do the actual work\n3. **useState &amp; useEffect** - React hooks for managing state and side effects\n\n---\n\n## 🎯 What to Learn Next (In Order)\n\n### 1. **Async/Await &amp; Promises** ⭐ MOST IMPORTANT\n**Why**: Almost everything in your codebase is async (database calls, API calls, etc.)\n\n**What You'll See**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Everywhere in your codebase:\nconst data = await getAaplFinancialsByMetric()  // ← await keyword\nconst result = await askQuestion(question)      // ← async function\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Key Concepts**:\n- &#96;async&#96; functions return Promises\n- &#96;await&#96; waits for Promise to finish\n- &#96;try/catch&#96; handles errors\n- &#96;Promise.all()&#96; runs things in parallel\n\n**Where to Practice**:\n- Look at &#96;app/actions/ask-question.ts&#96; - full of async/await\n- Look at &#96;app/market/page.tsx&#96; - uses &#96;Promise.all()&#96; for parallel fetching\n\n**Resources**:\n- MDN: \"Async/Await\" (15 min read)\n- Practice: Convert a callback to async/await\n\n---\n\n### 2. **TypeScript Basics** ⭐ VERY IMPORTANT\n**Why**: Your entire codebase is TypeScript - you need to understand types\n\n**What You'll See**:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// Type annotations everywhere:\nconst [question, setQuestion] = useState&lt;string&gt;('')  // ← string type\nconst data: MarketData | null = null                   // ← union type\nfunction getData(): Promise&lt;Data&gt; { ... }            // ← return type\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Key Concepts**:\n- Type annotations (&#96;: string&#96;, &#96;: number&#96;)\n- Interfaces (&#96;interface MarketData { ... }&#96;)\n- Union types (&#96;string | null&#96;)\n- Type safety (TypeScript catches errors before runtime)\n\n**Where to Practice**:\n- Look at &#96;lib/database.types.ts&#96; - see how database types are defined\n- Look at function parameters - they all have types\n- Try removing a type annotation and see the error\n\n**Resources**:\n- TypeScript Handbook: \"Basic Types\" (30 min)\n- Practice: Add types to a function you write\n\n---",

## What I created

A guide at `docs/BEGINNER_GUIDE.md` that explains:

### 15 key topics

1. How data flows — from user input → API → database → back to user
2. Error handling pattern — the `{ data, error }` pattern used everywhere
3. State management — how `useState` works in your app
4. The tool system — how the chatbot picks which function to call
5. Streaming — how answers appear word-by-word
6. Validation system — how answers are checked for accuracy
7. Common patterns — loading states, error handling, conditional rendering
8. TypeScript types — how types keep your code safe
9. Database queries — how to query Supabase
10. Component structure — how React components are organized
11. Import patterns — how imports work
12. Key files — which files to understand first
13. Common mistakes — what to avoid
14. Debugging tips — how to find problems
15. Next steps — what to learn next

---

## Top 5 concepts to focus on

### 1. Data flow
```
User → Component → API Route → Server Action → Database → Back to Component
```

### 2. Error handling pattern
```typescript
const { data, error } = await fetchData()
if (error) {
  // Handle error
} else {
  // Use data
}
```

### 3. State management
```typescript
const [data, setData] = useState(null)  // Declare
setData(newData)  // Update (triggers re-render)
```

### 4. Async/await
```typescript
const data = await fetchData()  // Wait for it
console.log(data)  // Then use it
```

### 5. The tool system
- User asks question
- AI picks a tool (function)
- Server runs the tool
- AI generates answer from the data
