          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 339
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 340
          },
          {
            "text": "### 5. Most Common Questions",
            "lineNumber": 341
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 342
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;sql",
            "lineNumber": 343
          },
          {
            "text": "-- Find similar questions (use for FAQ)",
            "lineNumber": 344
          },
          {
            "text": "select",
            "lineNumber": 345
          },
          {
            "text": "  user_question,",
            "lineNumber": 346
          },
          {
            "text": "  count(*) as times_asked",
            "lineNumber": 347
          },
          {
            "text": "from query_logs",
            "lineNumber": 348
          },
          {
            "text": "where created_at &gt; now() - interval '30 days'",
            "lineNumber": 349
          },
          {
            "text": "group by user_question",
            "lineNumber": 350
          },
          {
            "text": "order by times_asked desc",
            "lineNumber": 351
          },
          {
            "text": "limit 10;",
            "lineNumber": 352
          },
          {
            "text": "&#96;&#96;&#96;",
            "lineNumber": 353
          },

            "lineNumber": 355
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 356
          },
          {
            "text": "## Cost Estimate",
            "lineNumber": 357
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 358
          },
          {
            "text": "### Supabase Storage",
            "lineNumber": 359
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 360
          },
          {
            "text": "**Assumptions:**",
            "lineNumber": 361
          },
          {
            "text": "- 1,000 queries per day",
            "lineNumber": 362
          },
          {
            "text": "- 30,000 queries per month",
            "lineNumber": 363
          },
          {
            "text": "- Average row size: ~2KB (with full data) or ~500 bytes (metadata only)",
            "lineNumber": 364
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 365
          },
          {
            "text": "**Storage:**",
            "lineNumber": 366
          },
          {
            "text": "- With full data: 30,000 × 2KB = 60MB/month = 720MB/year",
            "lineNumber": 367
          },
          {
            "text": "- With metadata: 30,000 × 500B = 15MB/month = 180MB/year",
            "lineNumber": 368
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 369
          },
          {
            "text": "**Supabase Pricing:**",
            "lineNumber": 370
          },
          {
            "text": "- Free tier: 500MB database",
            "lineNumber": 371
          },
          {
            "text": "- Pro tier ($25/mo): 8GB database",
            "lineNumber": 372
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 373
          },
          {
            "text": "**Conclusion:** Even storing full data, we'd stay in free tier for 8+ months. At scale (10k+ queries/day), Pro tier still only $25/month.",
            "lineNumber": 374
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 375
          },
          {
            "text": "### Compare to PostHog",
            "lineNumber": 376
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 377
          },
          {
            "text": "**PostHog pricing:**",
            "lineNumber": 378
          },
          {
            "text": "- Free: 1 million events/month",
            "lineNumber": 379
          },
          {
            "text": "- But \"events\" are different from our needs",
            "lineNumber": 380
          },
          {
            "text": "- To store full Q&amp;A context: ~$200-300/month at 30k queries",
            "lineNumber": 381
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 382
          },
          {
            "text": "**Winner:** Supabase is 10x cheaper",
            "lineNumber": 383
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 384
          },
          {
            "text": "---",
            "lineNumber": 385
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 386
          },
          {
            "text": "## Implementation Code Structure",
            "lineNumber": 387
          }

        "contents": "// Static instructions that will be cached by OpenAI\nconst TOOL_SELECTION_STATIC_PROMPT = &#96;You are a router. Choose exactly one tool and return ONLY valid JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}. No prose.\n\nAvailable Tools:\n\n1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Financial metrics as NUMBERS over time\n\n   SUPPORTED METRICS:\n\n   Raw Metrics:\n   - revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income\n   - total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity\n   - operating_cash_flow, eps\n\n   Calculated Metrics (✨ Native Support):\n   - debt_to_equity_ratio  (total_liabilities / shareholders_equity)\n   - gross_margin          (gross_profit / revenue × 100)\n   - roe                   (net_income / shareholders_equity × 100)\n\n   METRIC MAPPING (with context clues):\n\n   Income/Profitability:\n   - \"sales\", \"revenue\", \"top line\" → revenue\n   - \"profit\", \"earnings\", \"bottom line\", \"profitability\" → net_income\n   - \"EPS\", \"earnings per share\" → eps\n   - \"operating profit\", \"EBIT\" → operating_income\n\n   Valuation Ratios (use getFinancialMetric tool):\n   - \"P/E ratio\", \"PE ratio\", \"price to earnings\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/E\"]\n   - \"P/B ratio\", \"price to book\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"P/B\"]\n   - \"PEG ratio\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"PEG\"]\n\n   Calculated Ratios (✨ NOW NATIVE - use directly):\n   - \"gross margin\", \"gross profit margin\" → gross_margin\n   - \"ROE\", \"return on equity\" → roe\n   - \"debt to equity\", \"debt-to-equity\", \"D/E ratio\", \"leverage ratio\" → debt_to_equity_ratio\n\n   Balance Sheet (Raw):\n   - \"assets\", \"total assets\" → total_assets\n   - \"liabilities\", \"total debt\", \"debt\" → total_liabilities\n   - \"equity\", \"book value\", \"shareholders equity\" → shareholders_equity\n\n   Cash Flow:\n   - \"operating cash flow\", \"cash from operations\", \"OCF\" → operating_cash_flow\n   - \"free cash flow\", \"FCF\", \"unlevered free cash flow\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool\n   - \"capex\", \"capital expenditures\", \"buybacks\", \"dividends paid\", \"stock-based compensation\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool\n\n   Research &amp; Development:\n   - \"R&amp;D\", \"research and development\", \"R&amp;D spending\", \"R&amp;D expense\" → Use getFinancialMetric tool with metricNames: [\"R&amp;D to revenue\"] or [\"research and development\"]\n\n   Other (use closest available):\n   - \"margins\", \"ratios\" (when not specific) → operating_income\n\n   LIMIT RULES - CRITICAL:\n\n   1. If question asks for a SPECIFIC YEAR (2020, 2019, 2015, 2006, etc.) → limit: 20\n      Why: We have 20 years (2006-2025). To find any specific year, fetch all.\n      Examples:\n      - \"net income in 2020\" → limit: 20\n      - \"revenue for 2018\" → limit: 20\n      - \"What was EPS in 2006?\" → limit: 20\n\n   2. If question asks for a YEAR RANGE (2008 to 2020, 2015 to present, etc.) → limit: 20\n      Why: Need all data to filter to the specific range.\n      Examples:\n      - \"net income 2008 to present\" → limit: 20\n      - \"revenue from 2015 to 2020\" → limit: 20\n      - \"EPS between 2010 and 2018\" → limit: 20\n\n   3. If question specifies a NUMBER of years, use that EXACT number:\n      \"last 3 years\" → limit: 3\n      \"past 5 years\" → limit: 5\n      \"last year\" or \"most recent year\" → limit: 1\n      \"10 years\" → limit: 10\n      \"20 years\" → limit: 20\n      \"2 years\" → limit: 2\n\n   4. If question says \"trend\", \"history\", \"over time\" WITHOUT a number → limit: 4\n\n   5. If question says \"all\", \"complete\", \"full history\" → limit: 20\n\n   6. If question is just asking for the metric (no time context) → limit: 4\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"net income in 2006\" → limit: 20 (specific year)\n   - \"revenue over 5 years\" → limit: 5 (number specified)\n   - \"show me net income trend\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"EPS history\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"gross profit\" → limit: 4 (no number)\n   - \"all historical data\" → limit: 20 (all data)\n\n   args: {\"metric\": &lt;exact name&gt;, \"limit\": &lt;number 1-20&gt;}\n\n2. getPrices - Stock PRICE history\n\n   ALWAYS use custom date ranges. Calculate the \"from\" date based on the user's request.\n   Today's date is {{TODAY_DATE}} (use this for calculations).\n\n   Date format: YYYY-MM-DD\n   \"to\" is optional (defaults to today)\n\n   CALCULATION EXAMPLES:\n   - \"last 7 days\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-11-01\"} (7 days ago)\n   - \"past month\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-10-08\"} (30 days ago)\n   - \"last 3 months\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-08-08\"} (90 days ago)\n   - \"past year\" → args: {\"from\": \"2024-11-08\"} (365 days ago)\n   - \"YTD\" → args: {\"from\": \"2025-01-01\"} (start of current year)\n   - \"last 3 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2022-11-08\"} (3 years ago)\n   - \"past 5 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-11-08\"} (5 years ago)\n   - \"last 7 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-11-08\"} (7 years ago)\n   - \"past 10 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-11-08\"} (10 years ago)\n   - \"last 15 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2010-11-08\"} (15 years ago)\n   - \"past 20 years\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago)\n   - \"all time\" → args: {\"from\": \"2005-11-08\"} (20 years ago, max available)\n\n   EXACT DATE RANGES:\n   - \"from Jan 2020 to June 2023\" → args: {\"from\": \"2020-01-01\", \"to\": \"2023-06-30\"}\n   - \"prices between 2015 and 2020\" → args: {\"from\": \"2015-01-01\", \"to\": \"2020-12-31\"}\n   - \"from March 2018 to now\" → args: {\"from\": \"2018-03-01\"}\n\n   args: {\"from\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\", \"to\": \"&lt;YYYY-MM-DD&gt;\"}  (to is optional)\n\n3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings metadata ONLY\n\n   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This tool returns ONLY metadata (filing type, date, URL).\n   It does NOT return filing CONTENT or text.\n\n   Use ONLY when:\n   - User wants to know WHEN filings were submitted\n   - User wants to know WHICH filings exist\n   - User wants filing dates/types/URLs\n\n   DO NOT USE when:\n   - User asks WHAT the filing says\n   - User wants content, quotes, or information FROM the filing\n   - User asks about topics like risks, strategy, etc.\n   → Use searchFilings instead for content questions!\n\n   LIMIT RULES:\n\n   1. If question specifies NUMBER of filings → use that number\n      \"last 3 filings\" → limit: 3\n      \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1\n      \"2 years of filings\" → limit: 10 (2 years ≈ 8-10 filings)\n\n   2. If question says \"recent\", \"latest\" (no number) → limit: 5\n\n   3. \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone?\" → {\"query\": \"iPhone\", \"limit\": 5}\n\n   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}\n\n5. listMetrics - DISCOVER available financial metrics\n\n   Use when:\n   - Capital Returns &amp; Share Data: dividend yield, payout ratio\n   - Per-Share Metrics: EPS, book value per share, cash per share\n   - Market Data: stock metrics, valuation metrics\n   - Other: miscellaneous metrics\n\n   Examples:\n   - \"What valuation metrics do you have?\" → {\"category\": \"Valuation\"}\n   - \"Show me all metrics\" → {} (no category)\n   - \"What debt metrics are available?\" → {\"category\": \"Leverage &amp; Solvency\"}\n\n   args: {\"category\": \"&lt;optional category name&gt;\"}\n\n6. getFinancialMetric -             "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: This tool returns ONLY metadata (filing type, date, URL).",
            "lineNumber": 191
          },
          {
            "text": "   It does NOT return filing CONTENT or text.",
            "lineNumber": 192
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 193
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use ONLY when:",
            "lineNumber": 194
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHEN filings were submitted",
            "lineNumber": 195
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to know WHICH filings exist",
            "lineNumber": 196
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants filing dates/types/URLs",
            "lineNumber": 197
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 198
          },
          {
            "text": "   DO NOT USE when:",
            "lineNumber": 199
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks WHAT the filing says",
            "lineNumber": 200
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants content, quotes, or information FROM the filing",
            "lineNumber": 201
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks about topics like risks, strategy, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 202
          },
          {
            "text": "   → Use searchFilings instead for content questions!",
            "lineNumber": 203
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 204
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 205
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 206
          },
          {
            "text": "   1. If question specifies NUMBER of filings → use that number",
            "lineNumber": 207
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"last 3 filings\" → limit: 3",
            "lineNumber": 208
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"most recent filing\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 209
          },
          {
            "text": "      \"2 years of filings\" → limit: 10 (2 years ≈ 8-10 filings)",
            "lineNumber": 210
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 211
          },
          {
            "text": "   2. If question says \"recent\", \"latest\" (no number) → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 212
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 213
          },
          {
            "text": "   3. If question says \"all\", \"available\", \"history\" → limit: 10",
            "lineNumber": 214
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 215
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples (metadata questions):",
            "lineNumber": 216
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"when was the most recent filing?\" → limit: 1",
            "lineNumber": 217
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"what filings do you have?\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 218
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"show me filing dates\" → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 219
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 220
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"limit\": &lt;number 1-10&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 221
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 222
          },
          {
            "text": "4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content (for WHAT they say)",
            "lineNumber": 223
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 224
          },
          {
            "text": "   ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Use this when user asks about CONTENT, not just dates!",
            "lineNumber": 225
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 226
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use for ANY question about WHAT the filings say:",
            "lineNumber": 227
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Risk factors, strategy, operations, business model",
            "lineNumber": 228
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Management commentary, outlook, quotes",
            "lineNumber": 229
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Products, markets, competition",
            "lineNumber": 230
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Governance, compensation",
            "lineNumber": 231
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ANY question asking \"what did they say\", \"provide quotes\", etc.",
            "lineNumber": 232
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 233
          },
          {
            "text": "   Even if they mention \"latest 10-K\" or specific filing:",
            "lineNumber": 234
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 235
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about AI?\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 236
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes from recent filing\" → USE searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 237
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 238
          },
          {
            "text": "   QUERY RULES:",
            "lineNumber": 239
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Extract key terms from user's question",
            "lineNumber": 240
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Keep it simple (1-3 words usually best)",
            "lineNumber": 241
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Don't need full sentences",
            "lineNumber": 242
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 243
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 244
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What are the risk factors?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 245
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What about risk factors in latest 10-K?\" → {\"query\": \"risk factors\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 246
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Tell me about competition\" → {\"query\": \"competition\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 247
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Provide quotes about AI strategy\" → {\"query\": \"AI strategy\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 248
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone?\" → {\"query\": \"iPhone\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 249
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 250
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 251
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 252
          },
          {
            "text": "5. listMetrics - DISCOVER available financial metrics",
            "lineNumber": 253
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 254
          },
          {
            "text": "   Use when:",
            "lineNumber": 255
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User asks \"what metrics do you have?\"",
            "lineNumber": 256
          },
          {
            "text": "   - User wants to browse metrics by category",
            "lineNumber": 257
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Uncertain which metric name to use for getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 258
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 259
          },
          {
            "text": "   CATEGORY FILTER (optional):",
            "lineNumber": 260
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Valuation: P/E, P/B, EV/EBITDA, market cap, etc.",
            "lineNumber": 261
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Profitability &amp; Returns: ROE, ROA, ROIC, margins",
            "lineNumber": 262
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Growth: revenue growth, EPS growth, asset growth",
            "lineNumber": 263
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Leverage &amp; Solvency: debt ratios, liquidity ratios",
            "lineNumber": 264
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Efficiency &amp; Working Capital: turnover ratios, cycle days",
            "lineNumber": 265
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Capital Returns &amp; Share Data: dividend yield, payout ratio",
            "lineNumber": 266
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Per-Share Metrics: EPS, book value per share, cash per share",
            "lineNumber": 267
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Market Data: stock metrics, valuation metrics",
            "lineNumber": 268
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Other: miscellaneous metrics",
            "lineNumber": 269
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 270
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 271
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What valuation metrics do you have?\" → {\"category\": \"Valuation\"}",
            "lineNumber": 272
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me all metrics\" → {} (no category)",
            "lineNumber": 273
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What debt metrics are available?\" → {\"category\": \"Leverage &amp; Solvency\"}",
            "lineNumber": 274
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 275
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"category\": \"&lt;optional category name&gt;\"}",
            "lineNumber": 276
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 277
          },
          {
            "text": "6. getFinancialMetric - GET advanced financial metrics (139 metrics available)",
            "lineNumber": 278
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 279
          },
          {
            "text": "   COMPLETE METRIC CATALOG (organized by category):",
            "lineNumber": 280
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 281
          },
          {
            "text": "   Valuation (11):",
            "lineNumber": 282
          },
          {
            "text": "   - peRatio, priceToBookRatio, priceToSalesRatio, priceToFreeCashFlowsRatio, earningsYield",
            "lineNumber": 283
          },
          {
            "text": "   - marketCap, enterpriseValue, evToSales, evToOperatingCashFlow, evToFreeCashFlow, freeCashFlowYield",
            "lineNumber": 284
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 285
          },
          {
            "text": "   Profitability &amp; Returns (12):",
            "lineNumber": 286
          },
          {
            "text": "   - grossProfitMargin, operatingProfitMargin, netProfitMargin, ebitPerRevenue, ebitdaMargin, pretaxProfitMargin",
            "lineNumber": 287
          },
          {
            "text": "   - returnOnEquity, returnOnAssets, returnOnCapitalEmployed, roic, ebtPerEbit, netIncomePerEBT",
            "lineNumber": 288
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 289
          },
          {
            "text": "   Growth (32):",
            "lineNumber": 290
          },
          {
            "text": "   - revenueGrowth, grossProfitGrowth, operatingIncomeGrowth, netIncomeGrowth, ebitgrowth",
            "lineNumber": 291
          },
          {
            "text": "   - epsgrowth, epsdilutedGrowth, operatingCashFlowGrowth, freeCashFlowGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 292
          },
          {
            "text": "   - assetGrowth, debtGrowth, inventoryGrowth, receivablesGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 293
          },
          {
            "text": "   - dividendsperShareGrowth, bookValueperShareGrowth, weightedAverageSharesGrowth, weightedAverageSharesDilutedGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 294
          },
          {
            "text": "   - rdexpenseGrowth, sgaexpensesGrowth",
            "lineNumber": 295
          },
          {
            "text": "   - threeYRevenueGrowthPerShare, threeYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, threeYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 296
          },
          {
            "text": "   - threeYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, threeYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 297
          },
          {
            "text": "   - fiveYRevenueGrowthPerShare, fiveYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, fiveYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 298
          },
          {
            "text": "   - fiveYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, fiveYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 299
          },
          {
            "text": "   - tenYRevenueGrowthPerShare, tenYNetIncomeGrowthPerShare, tenYOperatingCFGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 300
          },
          {
            "text": "   - tenYShareholdersEquityGrowthPerShare, tenYDividendperShareGrowthPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 301
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 302
          },
          {
            "text": "   Leverage &amp; Solvency (9):",
            "lineNumber": 303
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debtEquityRatio, debtRatio, currentRatio, quickRatio, cashRatio",
            "lineNumber": 304
          },
          {
            "text": "   - interestCoverage, longTermDebtToCapitalization, totalDebtToCapitalization, cashFlowToDebtRatio",
            "lineNumber": 305
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 306
          },
          {
            "text": "   Efficiency &amp; Working Capital (7):",
            "lineNumber": 307
          },
          {
            "text": "   - assetTurnover, fixedAssetTurnover, inventoryTurnover, receivablesTurnover, payablesTurnover",
            "lineNumber": 308
          },
          {
            "text": "   - cashConversionCycle, daysOfInventoryOutstanding, daysOfSalesOutstanding, daysOfPayablesOutstanding",
            "lineNumber": 309
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 310
          },
          {
            "text": "   Cash Flow (2):",
            "lineNumber": 311
          },
          {
            "text": "   - freeCashFlow, capitalExpenditure",
            "lineNumber": 312
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 313
          },
          {
            "text": "   Capital Returns &amp; Share Data (5):",
            "lineNumber": 314
          },
          {
            "text": "   - dividendYield, payoutRatio, dividendsPaid, commonStockRepurchased, numberOfShares",
            "lineNumber": 315
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 316
          },
          {
            "text": "   Per-Share Metrics (7):",
            "lineNumber": 317
          },
          {
            "text": "   - bookValuePerShare, cashPerShare, operatingCashFlowPerShare, freeCashFlowPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 318
          },
          {
            "text": "   - netIncomePerShare, revenuePerShare, tangibleBookValuePerShare",
            "lineNumber": 319
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 320
          },
          {
            "text": "   Market Data (1):",
            "lineNumber": 321
          },
          {
            "text": "   - stockPrice",
            "lineNumber": 322
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 323
          },
          {
            "text": "   Other (53):",
            "lineNumber": 324
          },
          {
            "text": "   - ebitda, stockBasedCompensation, depreciationAndAmortization, workingCapital, effectiveTaxRate",
            "lineNumber": 325
          },
          {
            "text": "   - marketCapitalization, enterpriseValueMultiple, enterpriseValueOverEBITDA",
            "lineNumber": 326
          },
          {
            "text": "   - pbRatio, pfcfRatio, pocfratio, priceBookValueRatio, priceCashFlowRatio, priceEarningsRatio",
            "lineNumber": 327
          },
          {
            "text": "   - priceEarningsToGrowthRatio, priceFairValue, priceSalesRatio, priceToOperatingCashFlowsRatio, ptbRatio",
            "lineNumber": 328
          },
          {
            "text": "   - roe, returnOnTangibleAssets",
            "lineNumber": 329
          },
          {
            "text": "   - researchAndDdevelopementToRevenue, salesGeneralAndAdministrativeToRevenue, stockBasedCompensationToRevenue",
            "lineNumber": 330
          },
          {
            "text": "   - capexPerShare, capexToDepreciation, capexToOperatingCashFlow, capexToRevenue",
            "lineNumber": 331
          },
          {
            "text": "   - shareholdersEquityPerShare, tangibleAssetValue, investedCapital",
            "lineNumber": 332
          },
          {
            "text": "   - debtToAssets, debtToEquity, netDebtToEBITDA",
            "lineNumber": 333
          },
          {
            "text": "   - operatingCashFlowSalesRatio, freeCashFlowOperatingCashFlowRatio",
            "lineNumber": 334
          },
          {
            "text": "   - cashFlowCoverageRatios, capitalExpenditureCoverageRatio, dividendPaidAndCapexCoverageRatio, shortTermCoverageRatios",
            "lineNumber": 335
          },
          {
            "text": "   - dividendPayoutRatio, interestDebtPerShare",
            "lineNumber": 336
          },
          {
            "text": "   - companyEquityMultiplier, intangiblesToTotalAssets",
            "lineNumber": 337
          },
          {
            "text": "   - daysOfInventoryOnHand, daysPayablesOutstanding, daysSalesOutstanding, operatingCycle",
            "lineNumber": 338
          },
          {
            "text": "   - incomeQuality, grahamNumber, grahamNetNet, netCurrentAssetValue",
            "lineNumber": 339
          },
          {
            "text": "   - averageInventory, averagePayables, averageReceivables",
            "lineNumber": 340
          },
          {
            "text": "   - addTotalDebt, minusCashAndCashEquivalents",
            "lineNumber": 341
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 342
          },
          {
            "text": "   METRIC NAME FLEXIBILITY:",
            "lineNumber": 343
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Accepts canonical names: \"peRatio\", \"returnOnEquity\", \"debtEquityRatio\"",
            "lineNumber": 344
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Accepts common aliases: \"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"",
            "lineNumber": 345
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Can handle multiple metrics in one call",
            "lineNumber": 346
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 347
          },
          {
            "text": "   LIMIT RULES (same as getAaplFinancialsByMetric):",
            "lineNumber": 348
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Specific year → limit: 20",
            "lineNumber": 349
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Number specified → use that number",
            "lineNumber": 350
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"trend\", \"history\" → limit: 4",
            "lineNumber": 351
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"compare\" with multiple metrics → limit: 10 (show more history for comparisons)",
            "lineNumber": 352
          },
          {
            "text": "   - Default → limit: 5",
            "lineNumber": 353
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 354
          },
          {
            "text": "   Examples:",
            "lineNumber": 355
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's Apple's P/E ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 356
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's the price to book ratio?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"price to book\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 357
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me ROE trend\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"ROE\"], \"limit\": 4}",
            "lineNumber": 358
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"What's Apple's free cash flow?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"free cash flow\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 359
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"How much did Apple spend on buybacks?\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"buybacks\"], \"limit\": 5}",
            "lineNumber": 360
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Show me capex trend\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"capex\"], \"limit\": 4}",
            "lineNumber": 361
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Compare P/E, ROE, and debt to equity\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\", \"ROE\", \"debt to equity\"], \"limit\": 10}",
            "lineNumber": 362
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Compare P/E and ROE\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"P/E\", \"ROE\"], \"limit\": 10}",
            "lineNumber": 363
          },
          {
            "text": "   - \"Dividend yield for 2023\" → {\"metricNames\": [\"dividend yield\"], \"limit\": 20}",
            "lineNumber": 364
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 365
          },
          {
            "text": "   args: {\"metricNames\": [\"&lt;metric1&gt;\", \"&lt;metric2&gt;\"], \"limit\": &lt;number&gt;}",
            "lineNumber": 366
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 367
          },
          {
            "text": "TOOL SELECTION LOGIC:",
            "lineNumber": 368
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 369
          },
          {
            "text": "1. Basic financial metrics (revenue, assets, eps, etc.)? → getAaplFinancialsByMetric",
            "lineNumber": 370
          },
          {
            "text": "2. Advanced metrics (P/E, ROE, debt ratios, etc.)? → getFinancialMetric",
            "lineNumber": 371
          },
          {
            "text": "3. User asks \"what metrics available\"? → listMetrics",
            "lineNumber": 372
          },
          {
            "text": "4. Stock price? → getPrices",
            "lineNumber": 373
          },
          {
            "text": "5. Filing metadata ONLY (when/which filings)? → getRecentFilings",
            "lineNumber": 374
          },
          {
            "text": "6. Filing CONTENT (what they say, quotes, topics)? → searchFilings",
            "lineNumber": 375
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 376
          },
          {
            "text": "⚠️ KEY DISTINCTION for #6 vs #7:",
            "lineNumber": 377
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)",
            "lineNumber": 378
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"What does the latest 10-K say about risks?\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 379
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"Show me recent filings\" → getRecentFilings (metadata)",
            "lineNumber": 380
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"What are risk factors in the latest 10-K?\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 381
          },
          {
            "text": "- \"Provide quotes from the 10-K\" → searchFilings (content)",
            "lineNumber": 382
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 383
          },
          {
            "text": "Return ONLY JSON - examples:",
            "lineNumber": 384
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 385
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"revenue\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 386
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"eps\",\"limit\":1}}",
            "lineNumber": 387
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\",\"args\":{\"metric\":\"total_liabilities\",\"limit\":4}}",
            "lineNumber": 388
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2018-11-15\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 389
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getPrices\",\"args\":{\"from\":\"2025-01-01\",\"to\":\"2025-11-15\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 390
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":3}}",
            "lineNumber": 391
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 392
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"AI strategy\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 393
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{\"category\":\"Valuation\"}}",
            "lineNumber": 394
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"listMetrics\",\"args\":{}}",
            "lineNumber": 395
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"P/E\"],\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 396
          },
          {
            "text": "{\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"ROE\",\"debt to equity\"],\"limit\":10}}",
            "lineNumber": 397
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 398
          },
          {
            "text": "CRITICAL EXAMPLES - Filing Content vs Metadata:",
            "lineNumber": 399
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"When was the latest 10-K filed?\"",
            "lineNumber": 400
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getRecentFilings\",\"args\":{\"limit\":1}}",
            "lineNumber": 401
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 402
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"What about risk factors in their latest 10k? provide quotes.\"",
            "lineNumber": 403
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"risk factors\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 404
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 405
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"What does the 10-K say about iPhone sales?\"",
            "lineNumber": 406
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"iPhone sales\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 407
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 408
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"Provide quotes from the latest filing about competition\"",
            "lineNumber": 409
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"searchFilings\",\"args\":{\"query\":\"competition\",\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 410
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 411
          },
          {
            "text": "CRITICAL EXAMPLES - Advanced Metrics:",
            "lineNumber": 412
          },
          {
            "text": "Q: \"What is AAPL's debt to equity ratio?\"",
            "lineNumber": 413
          },
          {
            "text": "A: {\"tool\":\"getFinancialMetric\",\"args\":{\"metricNames\":[\"debt to equity\"],\"limit\":5}}",
            "lineNumber": 414

        "contents": "-- Migration: Add user authentication support to query_logs\n-- Run this in Supabase SQL Editor\n\n-- Step 1: Add user_id column\nALTER TABLE query_logs\nADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS user_id UUID REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE;\n\n-- Step 2: Create indexes for performance\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_query_logs_user_id ON query_logs(user_id);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_query_logs_session_id ON query_logs(session_id);\n\n-- Step 3: Enable Row Level Security\nALTER TABLE query_logs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;\n\n-- Step 4: Drop existing policies if they exist (for re-running migration)\nDROP POLICY IF EXISTS \"Users can view own queries\" ON query_logs;\nDROP POLICY IF EXISTS \"Users can insert own queries\" ON query_logs;\nDROP POLICY IF EXISTS \"Users can update own queries\" ON query_logs;\nDROP POLICY IF EXISTS \"Users can delete own queries\" ON query_logs;\n\n-- Step 5: Create RLS policies\n\n-- Policy: Users can view their own queries (logged in) OR queries from their session (anonymous)\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can view own queries\"\n  ON query_logs FOR SELECT\n  USING (\n    -- Logged in user viewing their queries\n    (auth.uid() = user_id)\n    OR\n    -- Anonymous user viewing their session queries\n    (user_id IS NULL AND session_id IS NOT NULL)\n  );\n\n-- Policy: Users can insert queries\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can insert own queries\"\n  ON query_logs FOR INSERT\n  WITH CHECK (\n    -- Logged in user inserting with their user_id\n    (auth.uid() = user_id)\n    OR\n    -- Anonymous user inserting with session_id\n    (user_id IS NULL AND session_id IS NOT NULL)\n  );\n\n-- Policy: Users can update their own queries (for feedback)\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can update own queries\"\n  ON query_logs FOR UPDATE",

      "codeBlock": {
        "relativeWorkspacePath": "./docs/AUTH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md",

        "contents": "2. **Sign up**\n   - Click \"Sign Up\" button\n   - Enter email + password\n   - Email verification (optional)\n   - **Migrate** their anonymous session queries to user account\n\n3. **Logged in**\n   - All queries saved to their account\n   - Access history from any device\n   - Can logout and data persists\n\n### For Returning Users\n\n1. **Visit site**\n   - Auto-login if session valid\n   - Load query history from database\n   - Continue where they left off\n\n2. **New device**\n   - Login with email + password\n   - All history loads (from other devices too)\n\n---\n\n## Migration Strategy\n\n### Handling Existing Anonymous Sessions\n\nWhen a user signs up, we should migrate their anonymous queries:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nasync function migrateAnonymousQueries(userId: string, sessionId: string) {\n  // Update all queries with this session_id to have the user_id\n  await supabase\n    .from('query_logs')\n    .update({ user_id: userId })\n    .eq('session_id', sessionId)\n    .is('user_id', null)\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCall this after successful signup:\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\n// After user signs up\nconst { user } = await supabase.auth.signUp({ email, password })\nawait migrateAnonymousQueries(user.id, sessionId)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Security Considerations\n\n### Row Level Security (RLS)\n\n**Why it matters:**\n- Without RLS, users could see each other's queries\n- Even with client-side checks, anyone can call the API directly\n- RLS enforces access control at the database level\n\n**How it works:**\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\n-- Example RLS policy\nCREATE POLICY \"Users can only see own queries\"\n  ON query_logs FOR SELECT\n  USING (auth.uid() = user_id);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis means:\n- User A can only SELECT queries where &#96;user_id = User A's ID&#96;\n- Even if malicious code tries &#96;SELECT * FROM query_logs&#96;, they only get their own data\n- Enforced by Postgres, not client code\n\n### Sensitive Data\n\n**What we're storing:**\n- User questions (could contain sensitive info)\n- Financial queries (personal interest in stocks)\n- Query patterns (when/what they ask)\n\n**Protection:**\n- RLS ensures users can only see their own data\n- HTTPS for data in transit",
        "signatures": {},
        "detailedLines": [
          {

          },
          {

          },

        "contents": "create table query_logs (\n  -- Primary key\n  id uuid primary key default uuid_generate_v4(),\n\n  -- Session tracking\n  session_id text not null,  -- Links related questions in a conversation\n\n  -- User input\n  user_question text not null,  -- The question user asked\n\n  -- LLM reasoning (Step 1: Tool selection)\n  tool_selected text not null,  -- e.g., \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\"\n  tool_args jsonb not null,  -- e.g., {\"metric\": \"revenue\", \"limit\": 5}\n  tool_selection_latency_ms integer,  -- How long tool selection took\n\n  -- Tool execution (Step 2: Data fetch)\n  data_returned jsonb,  -- Actual data from tool (or just metadata like row count)\n  data_row_count integer,  -- How many rows returned\n  tool_execution_latency_ms integer,  -- How long data fetch took\n  tool_error text,  -- If tool call failed, store error message\n\n  -- LLM response (Step 3: Answer generation)\n  answer_generated text not null,  -- The final answer shown to user\n  answer_latency_ms integer,  -- How long answer generation took\n\n  -- Metadata\n  created_at timestamp default now(),\n\n  -- Optional: User feedback (add later)\n  user_feedback text,  -- \"thumbs_up\", \"thumbs_down\", or null\n  user_feedback_comment text  -- Optional text feedback\n);\n\n-- Indexes for fast queries\ncreate index idx_query_logs_session on query_logs(session_id);\ncreate index idx_query_logs_created_at on query_logs(created_at desc);\ncreate index idx_query_logs_tool on query_logs(tool_selected);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Why These Fields?\n\n**session_id**: Track conversations over time\n- Example: \"User asked about revenue, then net income\" → same session\n\n**user_question**: The raw question\n- Example: \"What's AAPL's revenue trend?\"\n\n**tool_selected**: Which tool the LLM chose\n- Example: \"getAaplFinancialsByMetric\"\n- **Use case:** Measure tool selection accuracy\n\n**tool_args**: Arguments passed to tool\n- Example: &#96;{\"metric\": \"revenue\", \"limit\": 5}&#96;\n- **Use case:** See if LLM chose correct parameters\n\n**data_returned**: What the tool actually returned\n- **Option A (full):** Store entire dataset &#96;[{year: 2020, value: 274.5B}, ...]&#96;",

        "contents": "- This is our main metric - we want 85%+\n\n### Database Integration\n\nEvery prompt version is stored in Supabase:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;sql\nCREATE TABLE prompt_versions (\n  id UUID PRIMARY KEY,\n  prompt_type TEXT NOT NULL,           -- 'tool_selection' or 'answer_generation'\n  version_number INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- 1, 2, 3, 4, etc.\n  prompt_content TEXT NOT NULL,        -- The actual prompt\n  change_description TEXT,             -- What changed\n  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,     -- Currently used in production?\n  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThis lets us:\n- Track every change we make\n- Compare versions side-by-side\n- Roll back if a new version performs worse\n- A/B test different prompts\n\n---\n\n## Prompt Version History\n\n### Version 1 (Baseline) - 46% Accuracy\n\n**When:** Initial production prompt\n**Results:** 46% overall, 76% tool selection, 43% args selection\n\n#### What It Looked Like\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nYou are a router. Choose exactly one tool.\n\nAvailable Tools:\n\n1. getAaplFinancialsByMetric - Use for questions about financial NUMBERS\n   Metrics: revenue, gross_profit, net_income, operating_income,\n           total_assets, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity,\n           operating_cash_flow, eps\n   args: {\"metric\": &lt;one of above&gt;, \"limit\": 1-10}\n\n2. getPrices - Use for stock PRICE questions\n   args: {\"range\": \"7d\" | \"30d\" | \"90d\"}\n\n3. getRecentFilings - LIST SEC filings\n   args: {\"limit\": 1-10}\n\n4. searchFilings - SEARCH filing content\n   args: {\"query\": \"&lt;keywords&gt;\", \"limit\": 1-10}\n\nUser question: \"{question}\"\n\nReturn JSON: {\"tool\": string, \"args\": object}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#### Major Problems\n\n1. **No metric mapping**: User asks \"What's the P/E ratio?\" → AI doesn't know that maps to &#96;eps&#96;\n2. **Vague limit rules**: \"Show me revenue\" → AI guesses limit randomly (sometimes 1, 5, or 10)\n3. **Ambiguous range defaults**: \"What's the price?\" → AI doesn't know if that means 7d, 30d, or 90d\n4. **No examples**: AI has to guess the right pattern\n\n**Real failure example:**\n- Question: \"What's the P/E ratio?\"\n- Expected: &#96;getAaplFinancialsByMetric&#96; with &#96;metric: \"eps\"&#96;\n- Actual: &#96;searchFilings&#96; with &#96;query: \"P/E ratio\"&#96; ❌",

## Quick answer

You're writing queries in TypeScript using Supabase's query builder (not raw SQL).

---

## The two types of SQL in your codebase

### 1. Raw SQL (only for setup)
- Where: `.sql` files in `data/` and `supabase/migrations/`
- Purpose: Creating tables, indexes (one-time setup)
- Example: `CREATE TABLE financials_std (...)`

### 2. TypeScript query builder (for data queries)
- Where: Your actual code (`app/actions/`, etc.)
- Purpose: Getting data, inserting, updating (runs every time)
- Example: `supabase.from('table').select('*')`

---

## How you write queries

### TypeScript with Supabase query builder

Real example from your code (`app/actions/financials.ts` line 123):

```typescript
const { data, error } = await supabase
  .from('financials_std')           // Which table
  .select('year, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity')  // Which columns
  .eq('symbol', 'AAPL')             // Filter: symbol = 'AAPL'
  .order('year', { ascending: false })  // Sort by year, descending
  .limit(safeLimit)                 // Only get 10 rows
```

This is TypeScript, not SQL.

---

## What this translates to

The TypeScript above becomes this SQL:

```sql
SELECT year, total_liabilities, shareholders_equity
FROM financials_std
WHERE symbol = 'AAPL'
ORDER BY year DESC
LIMIT 10
```

You don't write the SQL directly. Supabase converts your TypeScript to SQL.

---

## Common query methods

```typescript
supabase
  .from('table')           // Which table
  .select('*')             // Which columns
  .eq('column', value)     // Filter: WHERE column = value
  .order('column')          // Sort
  .limit(10)               // Only get 10 rows
```

---

## Summary

| What | Language | Where | When |
|------|----------|-------|------|
| **Data Queries** | **TypeScript** | `app/actions/` | Every time app runs |
| **Table Setup** | **SQL** | `.sql` files | Once during setup |

---

## What you need to learn

1. Supabase query builder methods
   - `.from()`, `.select()`, `.eq()`, `.order()`, `.limit()`
   - Time: 1-2 hours

2. Error handling
   - Always check `error` before using `data`
   - Time: 30 minutes

3. Method chaining
   - How to chain methods together
   - Time: 30 minutes

Total: ~2-3 hours to master database queries.

---

## Full guide

I created a guide at `docs/DATABASE_QUERIES_GUIDE.md` with:
- Detailed explanations of each method
- Real examples from your codebase
- Common patterns
- Practice exercises

Bottom line: You're writing TypeScript queries, not SQL. Supabase handles the SQL conversion.

_**Agent (model default, mode Agent)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Explaining const clearly**

I need to give a concise explanation of `const`, focusing on its differences from `let`, especially for beginners. I should clarify that `const` affects the immutability of the binding, not the value itself. 

In React, it's common to see `const` used with hooks like `useState`. I’ll touch on specific examples such as `searchParams`, `router`, and `supabase`. My goal is to keep the explanation clear and not overly verbose!</details></think>

---

### Plain English answer

`const` means: **“this variable name will always point to the same thing; I won’t reassign it later.”**

It does **not** mean the value can never change internally (objects/arrays/state can still change), it just means you can’t do `variable = somethingElse` later.

---

### In your specific lines

```ts
const searchParams = useSearchParams()
const router = useRouter()
const supabase = createClientComponentClient<Database>()

const [user, setUser] = useState<User | null>(null)
const [sessionId, setSessionId] = useState<string>('')
const [sidebarOpen, setSidebarOpen] = useState(false)
const [refreshQueriesTrigger, setRefreshQueriesTrigger] = useState(0)
```

- **We use `const` because these bindings never change to a different thing:**
  - `searchParams` will always be “the search params object” for this render.
  - `router` will always be “the router object”.
  - `supabase` will always be “the Supabase client”.
  - For state, the **pair** `[user, setUser]` is fixed; React wants this to stay in the same order and shape.

- When you do `setUser(...)`, you’re **changing the state value React stores internally**, not reassigning `user` or `setUser`:
  - You never do `user = something` or `setUser = something` (that would be illegal with `const`).
  - Instead you call `setUser(newValue)`; React handles the change and re-renders.

---

### Why `const` is good here

1. **Prevents bugs** – you can’t accidentally reassign important things like `router`, `supabase`, or your state setters.
2. **Matches React patterns** – hooks (like `useState`) are always used with `const [value, setValue] = ...`.
3. **Makes code easier to reason about** – you know these names won’t be pointed at something totally different later in the function.

If you want, next we can compare `const` vs `let` with a tiny example and where you’d use each.

## What is useEffect? (Plain English)

`useEffect` runs code after the component renders. It’s for side effects like:
- Fetching data when the page loads
- Setting up timers
- Listening to events
- Saving to localStorage

Think of it as: “Do this after the component shows up on screen.”

---

## Basic Pattern

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  // This code runs AFTER the component renders
  console.log('Component rendered!')
}, [])  // Empty array = run only once
```

**Breaking it down:**
- `useEffect` = React hook
- `() => { ... }` = function that runs
- `[]` = dependency array (controls when it runs)

---

## Real Examples from Your Code

### Example 1: Set Session ID (Run Once)

**From `app/page.tsx` lines 63-70:**

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  let id = localStorage.getItem('finquote_session_id')
  if (!id) {
    id = crypto.randomUUID()
    localStorage.setItem('finquote_session_id', id)
  }
  setSessionId(id)
}, [])  // Empty array = run only ONCE when component first loads
```

**What it does:**
1. After the component renders, check localStorage for a session ID
2. If none exists, create one
3. Save it and set it in state
4. The `[]` means this runs once on mount

---

### Example 2: Listen to Auth Changes (Run Once, Then Clean Up)

**From `app/page.tsx` lines 127-141:**

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  // Get current user on mount
  supabase.auth.getUser().then(({ data: { user } }) => {
    setUser(user)
  })

  // Listen for auth state changes
  const {
    data: { subscription },
  } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((_event, session) => {
    setUser(session?.user ?? null)
  })

  return () => subscription.unsubscribe()  // Cleanup: stop listening when component unmounts
}, [])  // Run once on mount
```

**What it does:**
1. On mount, get the current user
2. Start listening for auth changes (login/logout)
3. When the component unmounts, stop listening (cleanup)

**The `return () => { ... }` is cleanup** — React calls it when the component is removed.

---

### Example 3: Run When Data Changes

**From `app/page.tsx` lines 73-77:**

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  if (conversationHistory.length > 0) {
    setShowTypedHints(false)
  }
}, [conversationHistory.length])  // Run when conversationHistory.length changes
```

**What it does:**
- When `conversationHistory.length` changes, hide the typed hints
- The dependency array `[conversationHistory.length]` means: “run this effect whenever this value changes”

---

## The Dependency Array Rules

### Empty Array `[]` = Run Once

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  // Runs ONCE when component first loads
}, [])
```

**Use for:** Setup that happens once (session ID, initial data fetch, event listeners)

---

### With Dependencies `[value]` = Run When Value Changes

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  // Runs when 'value' changes
}, [value])
```

**Use for:** Reacting to state changes (hide hints when conversation starts, update UI when data changes)

---

### No Array = Run Every Render (usually avoid)

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  // Runs EVERY TIME component renders (usually bad!)
})
```

**Avoid this** — it can cause infinite loops.

---

## Common Patterns in Your Code

### Pattern 1: Fetch Data on Mount

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  async function fetchData() {
    const data = await getData()
    setData(data)
  }
  fetchData()
}, [])  // Run once on mount
```

---

### Pattern 2: Cleanup (Stop Listeners/Timers)

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  const subscription = listenToSomething()
  
  return () => {
    subscription.unsubscribe()  // Cleanup when component unmounts
  }
}, [])
```

---

### Pattern 3: React to State Changes

```typescript
useEffect(() => {
  // Do something when 'count' changes
  console.log('Count changed:', count)
}, [count])  // Run when count changes
```

---

## Quick Mental Model

Think of `useEffect` like this:

```
Component Renders
    ↓
useEffect Runs (if dependencies match)
    ↓
Do the side effect (fetch data, listen, etc.)
    ↓
If component unmounts → Run cleanup
```

---

## Summary

- `useEffect` = “Do this after render”
- Empty `[]` = run once on mount
- `[value]` = run when `value` changes
- `return () => { ... }` = cleanup when unmounting
- Use for: fetching data, setting up listeners, timers, localStorage

---

## In Your Codebase

You have 6 `useEffect` hooks in `app/page.tsx`:
1. Session ID setup (once)
2. Hide hints when conversation starts (when history changes)
3. Typed.js hints setup (when hints toggle)
4. Auth listener (once, with cleanup)
5. Auto-focus on typing (once)
6. Auto-scroll to messages (when conversation updates)

Each one follows the patterns above. Want me to walk through any specific one in more detail?

## What is Cursor's Visual Editor/Composer?

Cursor's Composer is a chat interface that can:
- Edit multiple files at once
- Understand your codebase context
- Generate code based on your instructions
- Show you what it's going to change before you accept

---

## How to Access It

### Method 1: Keyboard Shortcut
- Press `Cmd+I` (Mac) or `Ctrl+I` (Windows/Linux)
- Opens the Composer panel

### Method 2: Command Palette
- Press `Cmd+Shift+P` (Mac) or `Ctrl+Shift+P` (Windows/Linux)
- Type "Composer" and select it

### Method 3: Menu
- Look for "Composer" or "AI" in the top menu

---

## Basic Usage

### 1. Ask for Changes
Type what you want, for example:
- "Add error handling to the fetchData function"
- "Create a new component called UserProfile"
- "Refactor this function to use async/await"

### 2. Review the Changes
- Cursor shows a diff of what will change
- Green = additions, red = deletions
- You can see which files will be modified

### 3. Accept or Reject
- Accept All: Apply all changes
- Accept Individual: Accept specific changes
- Reject: Cancel

---

## Tips for Better Results

### 1. Be Specific
❌ Bad: "Fix the bug"
✅ Good: "Add error handling to the handleSubmitStreaming function in app/page.tsx"

### 2. Reference Your Code
- Mention specific files: "In app/actions/financials.ts..."
- Reference line numbers: "Around line 123..."
- Use @ mentions: "@app/page.tsx add a comment here"

### 3. Break Down Big Tasks
Instead of: "Refactor the entire chatbot"
Try: "First, extract the streaming logic into a separate function"

---

## Common Use Cases

### Adding a Feature
```
"Add a loading spinner component that shows when chatbotLoading is true"
```

### Fixing Bugs
```
"In app/page.tsx line 310, add a check to handle when reader is null"
```

### Refactoring
```
"Extract the streaming logic from handleSubmitStreaming into a separate function called processStream"
```

### Adding Comments
```
"Add comments explaining what each useEffect does in app/page.tsx"
```

---

## Advanced Features

### Multi-File Edits
You can ask for changes across multiple files:
```
"Update all components to use the new User type from types/user.ts"
```

### Code Generation
```
"Create a new server action called getStockPrice that queries the prices table"
```

### Code Explanation
```
"Explain how the streaming logic works in app/page.tsx"
```

---

## What I Can Help With

Since you're talking to me (the AI assistant), I can:
- Explain code (like we've been doing)
- Suggest changes
- Help you understand concepts
- Answer questions about your codebase

But I can't directly:
- Click buttons in Cursor's UI
- See your screen
- Control the visual editor interface

---

## Quick Start Guide

1. Open a file you want to edit (e.g., `app/page.tsx`)
2. Press `Cmd+I` to open Composer
3. Type: "Add a console.log at the start of handleSubmitStreaming to debug"
4. Review the diff
5. Click "Accept" if it looks good

---

## Pro Tips

1. Use @ mentions to reference files:
   - `@app/page.tsx` - references that file
   - `@components/` - references that folder

2. Be conversational:
   - "Can you help me understand..."
   - "I want to add..."
   - "How do I..."

3. Iterate:
   - If the first result isn't perfect, refine your request
   - "Actually, make it async" or "Add error handling too"

4. Learn from the diffs:
   - See what changed to understand patterns
   - Use it as a learning tool

---

## Common Issues

### "It changed too much"
- Be more specific about what to change
- Use line numbers or function names

### "It didn't understand"
- Reference specific files with @
- Show an example of what you want

### "It broke something"
- Use Cursor's undo (`Cmd+Z`)
- Ask me to explain what went wrong

---

## Practice Exercise

Try this:
1. Open `app/page.tsx`
2. Press `Cmd+I`
3. Type: "Add a comment above the handleSubmitStreaming function explaining what it does"
4. Review the change
5. Accept it

This helps you get comfortable with the workflow.

## What I see

### Strengths

1. Well-organized layout
   - Top: Major indices (SPX, NASDAQ, DOW, Russell 2000) with dates and changes
   - Middle: Gainers/Losers tables with clear columns
   - Bottom: VIX, sector performance, futures, economic calendar

2. Data density
   - Shows a lot of information without feeling cluttered
   - Tables are scannable (Symbol, Last, Change, Change %, Volume)

3. Visual hierarchy
   - Clear sections
   - Color coding for gains/losses (green/red implied)
   - VIX card with trend indicator

4. Useful features
   - Sector performance buttons (clickable)
   - Economic calendar with dates/times
   - Futures data (Crude Oil, Gold, etc.)

---

### Potential issues

1. Missing charts
   - The snapshot shows text data, but no visible price charts for the indices
   - Expected: SPX, NASDAQ, DOW should have mini charts

2. Data freshness
   - Dates show "Dec 15" — verify this is current
   - Some economic events show "null" values (e.g., "Prev: -0.12null")

3. Float column
   - Many rows show "—" in the Float column
   - Consider hiding the column if data isn't available

4. Responsive layout
   - On smaller screens, the tables may be hard to read
   - Consider horizontal scrolling or stacking

---

### Specific observations

- Gainers table: XBP up 922.69% (likely a small-cap mover)
- Losers table: IRBT down 72.34% (significant drop)
- VIX: 16.36 (relatively low, suggesting low volatility)
- Sector performance: Consumer Defensive down most (-2.32%), Consumer Cyclical up most (+0.65%)

---

### Recommendations

1. Add mini charts
   - Small sparklines for each index showing the day's trend

2. Fix data issues
   - Address "null" values in economic events
   - Populate or hide the Float column

3. Add tooltips
   - Hover explanations for terms like "VIX" or "Futures"

4. Loading states
   - Show skeleton loaders while data fetches

5. Auto-refresh indicator
   - Show when data was last updated

---

## Overall assessment

Rating: 7.5/10

- Good: Information density, organization, useful data
- Needs work: Missing charts, some null values, could use more visual polish

The page is functional and informative. Adding charts and fixing data issues would improve it.

## Assessment of the market page

### What works well

1. Information density
   - Major indices (SPX, NASDAQ, DOW, Russell 2000) at the top
   - Gainers/Losers tables with clear columns
   - VIX card with trend indicator
   - Sector performance buttons
   - Futures data
   - Economic calendar

2. Data organization
   - Clear sections
   - Tables are scannable (Symbol, Last, Change, Change %, Volume)
   - Color coding implied (gains/losses)

3. Useful features
   - Clickable sector buttons
   - Economic events with dates/times
   - VIX range display
   - Top stocks table (TSLA, META, NVDA, etc.)

---

### Issues to fix

1. Data quality
   - Economic events show "null" values: "Prev: -0.12null", "Est: -0.4null"
   - Float column shows "—" for most rows (consider hiding if not available)

2. Missing visual elements
   - No charts for the major indices (SPX, NASDAQ, DOW)
   - Expected: mini sparklines or price charts

3. Date display
   - Shows "Dec 15" — verify this is current/accurate

---

### Specific observations

- Market status: All major indices down slightly (SPX -0.04%, NASDAQ -0.41%)
- VIX: 16.37 (low, suggesting low volatility)
- Biggest gainer: XBP +922.69% (likely a small-cap mover)
- Biggest loser: IRBT -72.34% (significant drop)
- Sector performance: Consumer Cyclical leading (+0.71%), Technology lagging (-1.24%)

---

### Recommendations

1. Fix data issues
   - Remove "null" from economic event displays
   - Format numbers properly (e.g., "-0.12" instead of "-0.12null")

2. Add visual elements
   - Mini charts for each index
   - Sparklines for top gainers/losers

3. Improve UX
   - Add "Last updated" timestamp
   - Tooltips for terms like "VIX" or "Futures"
   - Loading states while data fetches

4. Responsive design
   - Ensure tables scroll horizontally on mobile
   - Consider stacking on smaller screens

---

## Overall rating: 7.5/10

- Strengths: Good information density, clear organization, useful data
- Needs work: Data formatting issues, missing charts, some polish

The page is functional and informative. Fixing the "null" values and adding charts would improve it.

## Design improvement ideas for the financials page

### Current state
- Header: Company name, price ($273.17), change (-1.84%), market status
- Key Statistics: Grid of metrics (Valuation, Performance, Profitability, etc.)
- Price Chart: "Coming soon..." placeholder
- Financial Statements: "Financial data loaded: 5 years" (no visible data)
- Financial Metrics: "Metrics loaded..." (no visible data)
- SEC Filings: "Recent filings:" (no visible data)

---

## Design improvements

### 1. Visual hierarchy and spacing

Problem: The Key Statistics grid is dense and hard to scan.

Solution:
- Group related metrics with subtle borders or background colors
- Add icons for each category (Valuation, Performance, Profitability)
- Use larger font for important metrics (Market Cap, P/E Ratio)
- Add hover states to show definitions

Example:
```
┌─ Valuation ─────────────┐
│ Market Cap: $4.04T      │
│ P/E Ratio: 36.62        │
└─────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Price display enhancement

Problem: Price is plain text.

Solution:
- Make price larger and prominent (e.g., 48px)
- Add a mini sparkline showing today's movement
- Color-code the change (green/red)
- Show price range for the day (High/Low)

Example:
```
$273.17  [small chart]  -$5.11 (-1.84%)
         ↑ Today's range: $272.50 - $278.20
```

---

### 3. Data visualization

Problem: "Coming soon..." for charts, and no visual data.

Solution:
- Add a price chart (1D, 5D, 1M, 3M, 1Y, 5Y)
- Add trend indicators (↑↓) next to metrics
- Use progress bars for ratios (e.g., P/E vs industry average)
- Mini charts for revenue/income trends

---

### 4. Key Statistics organization

Problem: Too many metrics in one grid.

Solution:
- Use tabs or accordions: "Valuation" | "Performance" | "Profitability" | "Financial Health"
- Show top 3–5 metrics by default, expand for more
- Add comparison badges (e.g., "Above Industry Avg")

---

### 5. Missing data handling

Problem: Many values show "0.00" (Forward P/E, PEG, Returns, Beta, Margins).

Solution:
- Show "N/A" or "—" instead of "0.00" when data is unavailable
- Add tooltips explaining why data might be missing
- Use a different visual style (grayed out) for unavailable data

---

### 6. Financial statements section

Problem: Only shows "Financial data loaded: 5 years" with no visible data.

Solution:
- Add expandable tables for Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow
- Include year-over-year change indicators
- Add a "View Full Statement" link
- Show key line items (Revenue, Net Income, etc.) prominently

---

### 7. SEC Filings section

Problem: Only shows "Recent filings:" with no list.

Solution:
- List recent filings (10-K, 10-Q) with dates
- Add icons for filing types
- Include "View" links to SEC website
- Show filing dates and highlight recent ones

---

### 8. Interactive elements

Problem: Page feels static.

Solution:
- Add a "Compare" button to compare with other stocks
- Add a "Watchlist" button
- Add export options (CSV, PDF)
- Add a "Share" button

---

### 9. Mobile responsiveness

Problem: Grid layout may not work well on mobile.

Solution:
- Stack metrics vertically on mobile
- Use a card-based layout for each metric group
- Make tables horizontally scrollable
- Collapse less important sections

---

### 10. Color and typography

Problem: Needs clearer visual distinction.

Solution:
- Use color coding:
  - Green for positive/good metrics
  - Red for negative/warning metrics
  - Blue for neutral/informational
- Use font weights: Bold for labels, regular for values
- Add subtle backgrounds to separate sections

---

## Quick wins (easy to implement)

1. Replace "0.00" with "N/A" for missing data
2. Make the price larger and more prominent
3. Add color to the price change (green/red)
4. Show actual financial statements data (if available)
5. List SEC filings with dates and links
6. Add tooltips explaining what each metric means

---

## Priority order

1. High priority: Show actual data (Financial Statements, SEC Filings)
2. Medium priority: Fix "0.00" values, add price chart
3. Low priority: Visual polish, animations, comparisons

---

## Example layout

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Apple Inc. (AAPL)                   │
│ $273.17  -$5.11 (-1.84%)  [chart]   │
└─────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─ Key Metrics (Top 6) ───────────────┐
│ Market Cap | P/E | Revenue | ROE     │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─ Price Chart ────────────────────────┐
│ [Interactive chart with timeframes]  │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─ Financial Statements ────────────────┐
│ [Expandable tables]                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

Overall, the page has good data but needs better presentation and to show the actual data sections. Should I help implement any of these improvements?

Opened the financials page in the Cursor browser. Here are design improvements based on the code and what I see:

## Design improvement ideas

### 1. Fix "0.00" values — high priority

**Problem:** Many metrics show "0.00" when data is missing (Forward P/E, PEG, Returns, Beta, Margins).

**Solution:** Show "N/A" or "—" instead of "0.00".

```typescript
// Instead of:
{keyStats.forwardPE.toFixed(2)}

// Use:
{keyStats.forwardPE > 0 ? keyStats.forwardPE.toFixed(2) : 'N/A'}
```

---

### 2. Add visual grouping to Key Statistics

**Problem:** The 4-column grid is dense and hard to scan.

**Solution:** Add section headers and subtle backgrounds:

```typescript
// Add headers above each column:
<div className="space-y-2">
  <h3 className="text-xs font-semibold uppercase text-gray-500 mb-2">
    Valuation
  </h3>
  {/* metrics */}
</div>
```

---

### 3. Add color coding for metrics

**Problem:** All metrics look the same; hard to spot good/bad values.

**Solution:** Color-code based on value ranges:

```typescript
// For P/E Ratio - show if high/low
<span className={`font-medium ${
  keyStats.peRatio > 30 ? 'text-orange-600' : 
  keyStats.peRatio < 15 ? 'text-green-600' : 
  'text-gray-900'
}`}>
```

---

### 4. Make price more prominent

**Problem:** Price is in the header but could be more eye-catching.

**Solution:** Increase size and add a mini trend indicator:

```typescript
<div className="text-5xl font-bold">  {/* Bigger */}
  ${overview.currentPrice.toFixed(2)}
</div>
// Add a small up/down arrow icon next to change
```

---

### 5. Show actual Financial Statements data

**Problem:** Line 327 only shows "Financial data loaded: 5 years" — no actual data.

**Solution:** Display the data in expandable tables:

```typescript
// Add expandable Income Statement table
<div className="mt-4">
  <button>Income Statement ▼</button>
  <table>
    {/* Show revenue, expenses, net income by year */}
  </table>
</div>
```

---

### 6. Show actual SEC Filings list

**Problem:** Line 350 only shows "Recent filings: 20" — no list.

**Solution:** Display the filings:

```typescript
<div className="mt-4 space-y-2">
  {filings.map(filing => (
    <div key={filing.id} className="flex justify-between">
      <span>{filing.filing_type} - {filing.fiscal_year}</span>
      <a href={filing.url}>View →</a>
    </div>
  ))}
</div>
```

---

### 7. Add tooltips for metrics

**Problem:** Users may not know what "PEG Ratio" or "ROIC" means.

**Solution:** Add hover tooltips:

```typescript
<div className="group relative">
  <span>P/E Ratio</span>
  <div className="hidden group-hover:block absolute ...">
    Price-to-Earnings ratio. Lower is generally better.
  </div>
</div>
```

---

### 8. Add comparison indicators

**Problem:** No context for whether metrics are good or bad.

**Solution:** Add industry comparison badges:

```typescript
<span className="text-sm">
  {keyStats.peRatio.toFixed(2)}
  <span className="ml-2 text-xs text-green-600">↓ vs Industry</span>
</span>
```

---

### 9. Improve mobile layout

**Problem:** 4-column grid may be too cramped on mobile.

**Solution:** Stack columns on small screens:

```typescript
// Change grid-cols-4 to:
className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4"
```

---

### 10. Add loading states

**Problem:** No indication while data is loading.

**Solution:** Add skeleton loaders:

```typescript
<Suspense fallback={<SkeletonLoader />}>
  {/* content */}
</Suspense>
```

---

## Quick wins (easy to implement)

1. Replace "0.00" with "N/A" (5 minutes)
2. Add section headers to Key Statistics (10 minutes)
3. Show actual SEC filings list (15 minutes)
4. Show actual Financial Statements data (30 minutes)
5. Add color coding to important metrics (20 minutes)

---

## Priority order

1. High: Show actual data (Financial Statements, SEC Filings)
2. Medium: Fix "0.00" values, add section headers
3. Low: Tooltips, comparisons, visual polish

The page structure is solid; the main gap is displaying the data that's already loaded. Should I help implement any of these?

          {

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 15
          },
          {
            "text": "## Raw Financial Metrics (Primitives)",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 17
          },
          {
            "text": "These metrics are stored directly in the database and fetched from the Financial Modeling Prep API.",
            "lineNumber": 18
          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 19
          },
          {
            "text": "### Income Statement Metrics",
            "lineNumber": 20

          {

          },

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 26

          {
            "text": "| **Net Income** | &#96;net_income&#96; | Bottom line profit after all expenses and taxes | USD |",

          },
          {
            "text": "| **EPS** | &#96;eps&#96; | Earnings per share (diluted) | USD per share |",

          {

          {
            "text": "### Balance Sheet Metrics",

          {

          },
          {

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 33
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Total Assets** | &#96;total_assets&#96; | Sum of all assets owned by the company | USD |",

          {

            "lineNumber": 35
          },
          {
            "text": "| **Shareholders' Equity** | &#96;shareholders_equity&#96; | Net worth of the company (Assets - Liabilities) | USD |",

          },
          {

          },

            "text": "### Cash Flow Statement Metrics",

          },
          {
            "lineNumber": 39
          },
          {

          },
          {

          {

          {
            "text": "### Profitability Ratios",

          },
          {

          },
          {
            "text": "#### Gross Margin",
            "lineNumber": 52
          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 53
          },
          {
            "text": "- **Unit**: Percentage (%)",

          },
          {

            "lineNumber": 55
          },

        "contents": "/**\n * Get key statistics for stock detail page\n * Combines data from financial_metrics table and FMP API\n * Currently hardcoded to AAPL\n */\nexport async function getStockKeyStats(): Promise&lt;StockKeyStats&gt; {\n  const symbol = 'AAPL';\n  const apiKey = process.env.FMP_API_KEY;\n\n  if (!apiKey) {\n    throw new Error('FMP_API_KEY is not set');\n  }\n\n  try {\n    const supabase = await createServerClient();\n\n    // Fetch latest metrics from financial_metrics table (key-value format)\n    const { data: metricsData, error: metricsError } = await supabase\n      .from('financial_metrics')\n      .select('metric_name, metric_value, year')\n      .eq('symbol', symbol)\n      .order('year', { ascending: false })\n      .limit(200); // Get enough rows to cover all metrics for the latest year\n\n    if (metricsError) {\n      console.error('Error fetching financial metrics:', metricsError);\n    }\n\n    // Transform key-value rows into an object with metric names as keys\n    const latestMetrics: Record&lt;string, number&gt; = {};\n    metricsData?.forEach((row) =&gt; {\n      if (!latestMetrics[row.metric_name]) {\n        latestMetrics[row.metric_name] = row.metric_value;\n      }\n    });\n\n    // Fetch key metrics from FMP API for real-time data\n    const [quoteRes, keyMetricsRes] = await Promise.all([\n      fetch(\n        &#96;https://financialmodelingprep.com/api/v3/quote/${symbol}?apikey=${apiKey}&#96;,\n        { next: { revalidate: 60 } }\n      ),\n      fetch(\n        &#96;https://financialmodelingprep.com/api/v3/key-metrics/${symbol}?limit=1&amp;apikey=${apiKey}&#96;,\n        { next: { revalidate: 3600 } } // Cache for 1 hour\n      ),\n    ]);\n\n    const quoteData = await quoteRes.json();\n    const keyMetricsData = await keyMetricsRes.json();\n\n    const quote = quoteData?.[0] || {};\n    const keyMetrics = keyMetricsData?.[0] || {};\n\n    // Fetch latest financials for TTM data\n    const { data: financialsData } = await supabase\n      .from('financials_std')\n      .select('*')\n      .order('year', { ascending: false })\n      .limit(1);\n\n    const latestFinancials = financialsData?.[0] || {};\n}",
